records.qtitle: Steps to make bureaucracy accountable and transparent
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) 	how many officers of All India Services-IAS/IPS/Customs/Income Tax etc.have been found corrupt and dishonest, State-wise, during the last three years;<br/><br/>(b) 	what measures are being contemplated to identify and punish tainted officers; and<br/><br/>(c) 	the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government for making the bureaucracy more accountable and transparent?<br/>
records.ans_text: Minister of State in the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office. (DR. JITENDRA SINGH)<br/><br/>(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/> <br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (A) TO (C) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 182 FOR 06.08.2015<br/>(a): 	As per information provided by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), during the last three years i.e. 2012,2013, 2014 and 2015 (up to 30.06.2015), the details regarding number of officers of Group ‘A’ Services i.e. Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Police Service (IPS)and the officers of  Indian Revenue Service(Customs& Central Excise) and Indian Revenue Service (Income Tax)against whom cases under the Prevention of Corruption(PC) Act, 1988 have been registered is as follows:-<br/><br/>Service	2012	2013	2014	2015 (up to June, 2015<br/>IAS	8	2	2	0<br/>IPS	1	0	0	0<br/>IRS<br/>(Customs& Central Excise)	21	37	10	2<br/>IRS(Income Tax) 	17	7	9	5<br/><br/>	However, this information is not maintained centrally service-wise and category-wise but has been culled out from the case records available at different stations.<br/><br/>	The number of officers against whom cases have been registered and belonging to All India Service – IAS and IPSfor the above mentioned period, consolidated State-wise, is given as under:-<br/><br/>	IAS	IPS<br/>2012	Uttar Pradesh-2 <br/>West Bengal-1<br/>AGMUT*-2<br/>Assam Meghalaya-2<br/>Maharashtra-1<br/>Others-NIL	AGMUT*-1<br/>Others-NIL<br/><br/><br/>2013	Tamilnadu-1<br/>Andhra Pradesh-1<br/>Others-NIL	NIL<br/>2014	Tamilnadu-1<br/>AGMUT*-1<br/>Others-NIL	NIL<br/>2015 (upto June)	NIL	NIL<br/>•	AGMUT: Arunachal, Goa, Mizoram, Union Territories.	<br/><br/> <br/>(b)&(c): The Central Government has already taken several measures to make the bureaucracy more accountable and transparent. These include:<br/><br/>(i)	Vigilance Clearance is being denied to the officers, who do not file Immovable Property Return (IPR) within the stipulated time. <br/>(ii)	Placing of details of immovable property returns of all members of the All India Services and other Group'' A'' officers of the Central Government in <br/>the public domain.<br/>(iii)	Thirteen principles of ethics have been added to All India Service(Conduct) Rules, 1968.<br/>(iv)	Cases of prosecution pending in various Ministries/Departments are monitored by Department of Personnel & Training regularly. <br/>(v)	Introduction of e-Governance for improving the service delivery to citizens and enhancing transparency.<br/>(vi)	Simplification of procedures including abolition of affidavit and promotion of self-certification.<br/>(vii)	Advertisements campaigns to make the citizens aware about various Information Technology-based simplified procedures like e-filing of various tax returns.<br/>(viii)	The State Governments/Union Territory Administrations and various Ministries/Departments in Government of India have been asked to undertake regular screening exercise to weed out officers of doubtful integrity and also those who are non-productive.<br/>(ix)	Government has sanctioned 92 additional Special Courts across the Country to dispose of PC Act cases expeditiously. Of these, 86 Courts have become functional.<br/><br/>Following additional measures have also been undertaken to achieve the objectives of making the bureaucracy more accountable and transparent. <br/>		<br/>(i)	Issue of comprehensive instructions on transparency in tendering and contracting process by the CVC; <br/>(ii)	Issue of instructions by the CVC asking the organizations to adopt Integrity Pact in major procurement activities; State Governments have also been advised to adopt Integrity Pact in majorprocurements; <br/>(iii)	The Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988;<br/>(iv)     Enactment of Right to Information Act, 2005; <br/>(v) 	Enactment of Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013; <br/>(vi)     Enactment of Whistle-blowers Protection Act, 2011;<br/>(vii)    Issue of Citizen Charters; <br/>(viii)   Ratification of United Nations Convention against Corruption (UNCAC) in 2011.<br/><br/>*************<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Long standing demand of CPMFs
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether the Central Para-military Forces like CRPF, CISF, BSF, SSB etc. have requested Government to consider their long standing demands;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details of their long standing demands; and<br/><br/>(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government to fulfil their demands?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):	Following are some long standing demands of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) are:-<br/><br/>(i)	Grant  of  Organised  Group ‘A’ Service  (OGAS)  status  and <br/>Non-functional upgradation (NFU) as applicable to OGAS.<br/>(ii)     Para Military Service Pay to  CAPFs personnel.<br/>(iii)	Enhanced rate of Detachment Allowance (DA) to CAPFs `      personnel deployed in LWE at par with J&K.<br/>(iv)	Payment  of  Risk/Hardship  Allowance  during  Earned  Leave <br/>(60 days).<br/>(v)   Grant of 20 days Casual Leave to Officers and 30 Days to Other <br/>        ranks at par with Army.<br/><br/>(c):	 With respect to item (i) the Government has rejected the demand for OGAS and NFU.  However, the matter is presently subjudice in Hon’ble High Court of Delhi. The items (ii) to (v)   have been referred to the 7th Central Pay Commission.<br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Blocking of DTH overspill services
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that many India-based Direct-to-Home(DTH)overspill services such as Dish TV IndiaAirtel Digital TV, Sun Directand Tata Sky are unlicensed and unauthorised to operate theirservices particularly in the Middle East and North Africa region and inPakistan; if so, Government’s response thereto;<br/><br/>(b) whether Government is considering to block the DTH signals reaching out tothe consumers in such countries, where the operators are not givenlicenses; and<br/><br/>(c) if so, by when and if not, the reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING {COL RAJYAVARDHAN RATHORE (Retd.)}<br/><br/>(a) to (c):   This Ministry has granted license to six private companies viz. M/s Dish TV India Ltd, M/s Tata Sky Ltd, M/s Reliance BIG TV, M/s Videocon d2h Ltd, M/s Sun Direct TV Pvt Ltd and M/s BharatiTelemediaLtd to provide Direct to Home (DTH) Broadcasting service in India under DTH policy guidelines. All private DTH operators are required to comply with the provisions of these guidelines. Detailed guidelines are available at www.mib.nic.in<br/>

records.qtitle: Purchase of energy from solar power plants
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)	whether many State Governments have signed agreements/contracts with many industrial houses to purchase energy from solar power plants in various parts of the country without competitive bidding;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof indicating the cost of power purchase agreements;<br/><br/>(c)	whether recent bids for solar projects under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission  attracted bids as low as ? 7 per unit and if so, details thereof; and <br/><br/>(d)	the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government to purchase energy from solar power plants at lower cost?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR POWER, COAL & NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY <br/>(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) (SHRI PIYUSH GOYAL)<br/><br/>(a)&(b):	Information is being collected and will be laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/>(c):	Under Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission (JNNSM), the latest invited tariff-based bid for solar power by MNRE was in August 2011, wherein the least tariff selected was Rs. 7.49 per unit. Thereafter MNRE had invited bids wherein a fixed tariff of Rs. 5.45 per unit was offered and the bidding was for the amount of Viability Gap Funding (VGF) required. However, in the latest bids invited by Madhya Pradesh for setting up of 300 MW solar power, the least tariff selected is Rs. 5.05 per unit.<br/>(d):	The Government of India has taken following steps to purchase energy from solar power at lower cost:<br/>A.	Inviting competitive bidding including International Competitive Bidding (ICB) & reverse auction to ensure lowest possible tariffs.<br/>B.	Reducing the cost of financing by way of following :<br/>•	Award of Priority Sector status to Renewable Energy Sector for lending upto certain limit.<br/>•	Roof-top Solar PV systems have been made eligible for home loans.<br/>•	Issuance of tax free green bonds of Rs. 5,000 crore.<br/>•	Long term Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) to ensure low cost financing.<br/>•	Waiver of wheeling charges on Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS).<br/>•	Fiscal incentives like custom duty concessions, excise duty exemptions, 10 year income tax holiday and incentives from States like stamp duty waiver, reduced/nil wheeling charges, etc. to enable solar power developers to offer lower tariffs.<br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Fraud cases in education sector
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has detected many fraud cases in education sector during the last two years and if so, the details thereof; <br/>(b) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government against the culprit; and <br/>(c) whether Government is planning to bring more transparent and responsive policy in education sector?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SMT. SMRITI ZUBIN IRANI)<br/><br/>(a) to (c): As per information made available by the University Grants Commission (UGC), 21 Fake Universities have been listed in the UGC list of Fake Universities.  The details of such Fake Universities are available on the UGC website www.ugc.ac.in. In addition, the UGC has also informed that Bhartiya Shiksha Parishad, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh and Indian Institute of Planning and Management (IIPM), Qutub Enclave, Phase-II, New Delhi are also unrecognized and functioning in violation of Section 2(f) and Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956. The High Court of Delhi has given the final decision against the IIPM and advised that acts of the IIPM, Arindam Chaudhari and Malay Chaudhari, constitute a criminal offence of cheating punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code. To comply with the Court decision, the UGC has lodged FIR against IIPM in the Police Station.<br/>All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) has informed that various fraud cases have been detected during the last two years in several States, which is enclosed at Annexure-I. AICTE has further informed that presently 343 technical institutes which do not have AICTE approval are running in the Country. The details of such Institutes are available on AICTE web portal at http://www.aicte-india.org/misapproved institutions.php. <br/>The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has informed that sporadic incidents of candidates using fake Mark-sheets and Certificates for obtaining job or admission in Higher Educational Institutions as well as incidents of schools sponsoring ineligible candidates in the examinations conducted by the Board have been reported.<br/>UGC, AICTE and CBSE have taken several steps to check the menace of these Fake Universities/Institutions/Schools. UGC has written to all the Chief Secretaries, Home Secretaries and Education Secretaries of all states including Union Territories to check the menace of fake universities and initiate a drive against institutions offering degrees without approval of the Statutory Authorities viz. UGC, AICTE and Distance Education Council (DEC) in the States/Union Territories. UGC also issues ‘Public Notice’, ‘Press Release’ and paid advertisements for the awareness of the general public/students in the leading daily newspapers at the beginning of academic session, cautioning aspiring students not to seek admission in such institutions.<br/>In order to avoid irregularities, to ensure availability of qualified faculty and basic infrastructure, AICTE has published an approval Process Handbook as per the AICTE (Grant of Approvals for Technical Institutions) Regulations, 2012. Institutions violating these norms and standards are liable for punitive action per the Approval Process Handbook. AICTE has introduced e-governance in all the processes to bring transparency, accountability, flexibility by integrating the entire system. Besides above, AICTE has also taken few steps viz. sending letters to Principal Secretary/ Director, Technical Education/ concerned State authorities for taking appropriate action. Public Notices have also been issued by AICTE in newspapers cautioning the students not to take admission in such unapproved institutions for the benefit of Stakeholders. <br/>CBSE has also displayed the list of affiliated or disaffiliated schools as well as the results of Class X and Class XII and other entrance examinations conducted by the Board on its website for ensuring the genuineness of the mark sheets. Public notices are also issued as and when the Board withdraws affiliation of any school. <br/>	The Ministry vide its D.O. letter No.12-3/2015/U3(A) dated 21st July, 2015 requested the Chief Secretaries of several State Governments where these Fake Universities/Institutions are situated, to investigate the matter and register complaints in the Police Station. Prosecution may also be initiated against those involved in defrauding and cheating students by misrepresenting themselves as “Universities” awarding degrees with their name.<br/>*********<br/>

records.qtitle: Farmers not getting production cost of agricultural crops
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether there has been a rise in the production cost of several agricultural crops in various parts of the country during the last three years, if so, details thereof;<br/><br/>(b) 	whether farming community is not getting their production cost; <br/><br/>(c)	 if so, Government''s response thereto and details of steps taken for the overall enhancement in farm earning; <br/><br/>(d) 	whether Government is considering to bring in any new policy to pay farmers according to their actual agri-production cost like in USA; and<br/><br/>(e) 	if so, Government''s stands thereon and if not, the reasons therefor?	<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE <br/><br/>(SHRI MOHANBHAI  KUNDARIA)<br/><br/>(a) to (c): 	Yes, Sir.   There has been a rise in the cost of production of several agricultural crops during the last three years. The Minimum Support Price (MSP) fixed by the government on the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) takes into account the cost of production of agricultural crops along with other important factors. MSPs have also increased over the  years. MSP is in the nature of a minimum price offered by the Government to the farmers for their produce in case the market prices fall below that level. Farmers are free to sell their produce to government agencies at MSP or in the open market, as is advantageous to them. The details of the All India weighted  average Cost of Production(paid-out cost and family labour) of major agricultural commodities and Minimum Support Price (MSP) declared by the Government during the last three years is Annexed. <br/><br/>(d) & (e):	No, Sir.   The Government has initiated several steps to bring down cost of production of agricultural commodities by promoting increase in productivity through efficient use of inputs like fertilizers, irrigation, quality seeds, machinery, etc. Government is promoting Integrated Nutrient Management (INM) for balanced and judicious use of chemical fertilizers, bio-fertilizers and locally available organic manures like farmyard manure, compost, vermin-compost and green manure based on soil testing to maintain soil health and productivity etc. 	<br/> <br/>

records.qtitle: Early marriages of female population
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)     		whether it is a fact that the nearly 102.61 million women, roughly a sixth of India''s female population of 587.58 million, were married before they had turned 18, according to the recent Census data; and <br/>(b)      if so, details thereof and Government''s reaction thereto?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRIMATI MANEKA SANJAY GANDHI)<br/><br/><br/>(a) 	& (b):  Government of India is seized of the matter and has put in place necessary legislation viz. Prohibition of Child Marriage Act (PCMA) 2006 to tackle the problem. The States/UTs from time to time are being regularly pursued for effective implementation of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006. Further, State Governments are requested to take special initiative to delay marriage by coordinated efforts on Akha Teej—the traditional day for such marriages; Advertisements in the press and electronic media educating peoples about the issue of Child Marriage etc also being taken up. Platforms such as the International Women’s Day and the National Girl Child Day are used to create awareness on issues related to women and to bring to the centre stage issues such as child marriage. Through the Sabla programme of this Ministry, adolescent girls in the age group of 11 to 18 years are imparted training with regard to legal rights of women which also includes the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006. <br/><br/><br/>********<br/>

records.qtitle: Transfer of DDA and Anti Corruption Branch under Delhi Government
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether Delhi Government has requested to transfer the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) and Anti- Corruption Branch under the jurisdiction of the Delhi Government;<br/><br/>(b) if so, Government''s response thereto; and<br/><br/>(c) what are the basic concerns and reasons of Delhi Government for making such demands?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI HARIBHAI PARATHIBHAI CHAUDHARY)<br/><br/>(a):	No, Sir.<br/><br/>(b) & (c):	Do not arise in view of (a) above.<br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Quality test of imported Chinese rice
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: a)	whether it is a fact that the large quantity of rice is being imported from China without any quality check, if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>b)	whether Government''s attention has been drawn towards recent reports of the  plastic rice being sold by mixing it with real rice in the country;<br/><br/>c)	if so, Government''s reaction thereto; and<br/><br/>d)	the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government to carry out the quality test, particularly on imported Chinese rice?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY<br/>(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) (SMT. NIRMALA SITHARAMAN)<br/><br/>(a)	Import of rice is allowed only through the State Trading Enterprises (STE), as per India’s Import Policy under Chapter 10 of Indian Trade Classification (Harmonised System), 2012, Schedule – I (Import Policy) and it is subject to clearance by Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI). No import of rice under ITC(HS) code-1006 from China has been reported during 2014-15 and 2015-16 (April-May).  No adulteration in import consignments of rice cleared by FSSAI has been reported in any laboratory tests.<br/><br/>(b)	& (c): On the basis of alert from International Network of Food Safety Authorities (INFOSAN), FSSAI had taken up the issue with the Governments of Kerala and Gujarat and these states have confirmed that no incidence of imported plastic rice has been reported in the respective states.<br/><br/>(d): To ensure against import of any adulterated food products from any country, including China, FSSAI has put in place a mechanism for drawing of samples from each of the food import consignments and their testing at authorised laboratories.   		<br/>                                                              <br/>                                                                  **********<br/>

records.qtitle: Fraud cases and NPAs with PSU Banks
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)	whether PSU banks have reported more than 2100 fraud cases involving a sum of  11,022 crore during 2014-15; if so, Government’s response thereto;<br/><br/>(b)	whether it is a fact that most of the NPA of the banks and their loss is mainly due to corruption and mismanagement of the banks; and<br/><br/>(c)	if so, the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government to check all the NPA loans and fix responsibilities by punishing the culprits?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/>(SHRI JAYANT SINHA)<br/><br/>(a)	Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reported that for frauds of   1 lakh and above, a total of 3134 cases have been reported by PSU banks during 2014-15, involving a total amount of  16,828 crore.  <br/><br/>Following measures have been taken by RBI and Department of Financial Services (DFS) in this regard: -<br/><br/>i.	RBI has issued Master Circular on “Frauds – Classification and reporting” vide RBI DBS.CFMC.BC.No.1 / 23.04.001/2015-16 dated July 01, 2015 containing all the details / aspects relating to frauds.  The same is also available on the website of RBI i.e. www.rbi.org.in.  On receipt of fraud reports from banks, various aspect related to the frauds are examined and concerned banks are advised to report the case to CBI / Police / SFIO, examine staff accountability, complete proceedings against the erring staff expeditiously, take steps to recover the amount involved in the fraud, claim insurance wherever applicable and streamline the system as also procedures so that frauds do not recur. To compress the time taken in detection of fraud, a new framework for handling loan frauds has been put in place.  The framework stipulates continuous monitoring of loan accounts, time bound action at each stage of loan’s life cycle and commencement of investigations on observing early warning signal in an account.  Further the framework also prohibited banks from extending bank finance to borrowers who have defaulted and also committed a fraud for five years from the date of full payment of the defrauded amount.<br/>ii.	DFS vide its letter dated 13.05.2015 has also issued instructions laying down framework to facilitate timely detection, reporting, investigation, etc. relating to large value bank frauds”.<br/><br/>(b)	Main reasons for increase in NPAs of banks, inter-alia, are stalled projects, sluggishness in the domestic growth in the last few years, slowdown in recovery in the global economy and aggressive lending by the banks. <br/><br/>(c)	To improve asset quality of banks, and to prevent slippages, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued instructions to have a Board approved loan policy, loan recovery policy, put in place an effective mechanism for information sharing for sanction of fresh loans/ad-hoc loans/renewal of loans to new or existing borrowers, have a robust mechanism for early detection of signs of distress including prompt restructuring in the case of all viable accounts, taking recourse to legal mechanisms like SARFAESI Act, 2002, DRTs and LokAdalats.  <br/><br/>In January, 2014, RBI has released a comprehensive ‘Framework for Revitalising Distressed Assets in the Economy’.  The Framework outlines a corrective action plan that will incentivise early identification of problem cases, timely restructuring of accounts which are considered to be viable, and taking prompt steps by banks for recovery or sale of unviable accounts. <br/><br/>The Government has advised PSBs to constitute a Board level Committee for monitoring of NPAs and recovery, banks to give more focussed monitoring in coordination with other members of consortium, assigning the responsibility at the Executive Director level, hiring best lawyers and monitoring their performance in defending bank’s interest in the Debt Recovery Tribunals (DRTs) and High Courts.  <br/><br/>The Government has decided to establish six new Debt Recovery Tribunals (DRT) (at Chandigarh, Bengaluru, Ernakulum, Dehradun, Siliguri, Hyderabad) to speed up the recovery of bad loans of the banking sector.<br/><br/>Banks examine staff accountability and staff involvement in all cases of NPA and fraud.On completion of investigation, the Bank takes action against erring officials as per the applicable disciplinary rules.<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Rain water harvesting
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.min_name: WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government''s attention has been drawn towards recently study report, while looking at NASA satellite data on rain water harvesting concept and its benefits;<br/>(b) if so, the details thereof and Government''s response thereto; and<br/>(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government for encouraging rain water harvesting concept, particularly in dense population areas in the country?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/><br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION<br/>(PROF. SHRI SANWAR LAL JAT)<br/>(a) & (b)  The study, published in the June, 2015 issue of Urban Water Journal, is based on precipitation data from the Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM), a joint mission between NASA and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, which provided observations of rainfall over the tropics and sub-tropics from the year 1997 to 2015.  The study advocated direct collection of rain water and put it into use instead of recharge to ground water.  <br/>The optimum strategy for artificial recharge / rain water harvesting is dependent upon topography and hydro-meteorological conditions.  Direct collection of rain water is useful in  areas where sufficient rainfall takes place throughout the year and evaporation losses are less.  In other areas, schemes for rain water harvesting dovetailed with artificial recharge to ground water are suitable and thus promoted.<br/><br/><br/>Contd…p/2<br/><br/><br/><br/>//2//<br/><br/>(c) 	The National Water Policy (2012) formulated by this Ministry, inter-alia, advocates rain water harvesting and conservation of water and also, highlights the need for augmenting the availability of water through direct use of rainfall.  A Model Bill has also been circulated to all the States/UTs to enable them to enact suitable ground water legislation for its regulation and development, which includes provisions for rain water harvesting.  So far, 15 States/UTs have adopted and implemented the ground water legislation on the lines of Model bill.  Further, 31 States/UTs have made rain water harvesting mandatory by enacting laws or by formulating rules & regulations or by including provisions in building bye-laws or through suitable Government Orders.  Also, CGWB has prepared a conceptual document entitled “Master Plan for Artificial Recharge to Ground Water in India” during the year 2013, which envisages construction of 1.11 crore rain water harvesting and artificial recharge structures in the Country, at an estimated cost of Rs. 79,178 crores to harness 85 BCM (Billion Cubic Metre) of water, to augment ground water resources.  The Master Plan has also been circulated to all State Governments for implementation.<br/><br/>Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) has implemented demonstrative projects on direct collection of rain water and their use during IX Plan for North Eastern States and coastal areas.<br/><br/>Further, Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) has also issued directives to the Chief Secretaries of all States and the Administrators of all UTs to take measures to promote/adopt artificial recharge to ground water / rain water harvesting.  Besides, CGWA has also taken up the matter with various Central and State government organizations for adopting rain water harvesting and recharge to the ground water.  CGWB has been organizing mass awareness programmes in the Country to promote rain water harvesting and artificial recharge to ground water.<br/><br/>*****<br/><br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Achievement of National Electricity Fund
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) 	the details of funds sanctioned under the National Electricity Fund (NEF) to various State power utilities for improving the power distribution network during the last three years, particularly in Maharashtra; and<br/><br/>(b) 	what are the outcome in the power distribution by the companies since the implementation of NEF?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR POWER, <br/>COAL AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY<br/><br/>( SHRI  PIYUSH GOYAL )<br/><br/>(a)  :		Government of India launched the National Electricity Fund (Interest Subsidy Scheme) in July 2012 to provide Interest Subsidy on loans raised by both Public and Private Distribution Companies (DISCOMS), for capital works sanctioned by financial institutions to improve the infrastructure in distribution sector during the financial year 2012-13 and 2013-14.  For the State of Maharashtra, project loan worth Rs.7940 crore (both for MSEDCL and BEST) for 254 Nos. of projects have been approved for coverage under NEF.  State/Discoms-wise details are annexed.  <br/>(b) :   		Distribution utilities are trying to improve the operational efficiency by way of reducing AT&C loss and Revenue gap to get the interest subsidy under NEF. The NEF Scheme is acting as one of the enablers towards improvement of performance parameters of Discoms.  The benefit of interest subsidy would finally be passed on to the consumer through reflecting the same in the ARR of the respective utilities.<br/><br/>*************<br/>

records.qtitle: Farm subsidy to farming community
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)	 how much farm subsidies and grants have been allocated by Government to the farming community since the last five years; <br/><br/>(b) 	whether the poor and marginal farmers are not being benefited by the subsidy, if so, Government''s reaction thereto; and <br/><br/>(c) 	whether Government is considering any method to introduce new schemes/ programmes to provide direct benefit to the farming community, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE <br/><br/>(DR. SANJEEV KUMAR BALYAN)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):	 Farm subsidy/ financial assistance is provided to farm community including poor and marginal farmers for farm inputs and farm machinery etc. under some Centrally Sponsored Schemes of the Department of Agriculture & Cooperation (DAC). A statement indicating allocation made during last five years under various schemes / missions of DAC is attached (Annexure-I).<br/>       <br/> 	Subsidy on Urea and 22 grades of Phosphatic & Potassic (P&K) fertilizers is passed on to farmers through fertilizer companies in the form of lower MRP, which is much below the delivered cost. While Urea is provided at Government fixed price of Rs. 5360/- MT (excluding taxes etc.), the P&K fertilizers are provided to farmers at subsidized prices based on the nutrient content on each grade of P&K fertilizer. The fertilizers subsidy paid during the last five year is attached (Annexure-II).<br/><br/>(c):	 Under National Food Security Mission (NFSM) of DAC, Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) programme is being implemented from 2015-16 for resource conservation technologies / tools; efficient water application tools; acquiring assets under local initiatives & marketing support components. States may also include such components as per feasibility.<br/><br/>    	  Department of Fertilizer (DoF) is planning to introduce direct transfer of fertilizer subsidy to farmers on the basis of recommendations made by a High Level Committee (HLC) formed under the Department of Food and Public Distribution, which has suggested to move from product based subsidy to direct subsidy transfer linked to size of land of the farmer at flat rate of INR 7000/-per ha. However, implementation of this proposal requires resolution on decontrol of Urea, identification of beneficiaries and scale of entitlements which have also been communicated to the HLC.<br/>

records.qtitle: Metro projects in Maharashtra
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a)	how much amount have been sanctioned and utilised for Pune, Nagpur and Mumbai Metro projects since last three years;<br/>(b)	whether Government has requested for the sanctioning the metro projects and demanded financial assistance for the early completion of Pune, Nagpur and Mumbai metro projects; and<br/>(c)	if so, details thereof and Government’s response thereof ?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT<br/><br/>(SHRI BABUL SUPRIYO)<br/><br/>(a)	:Amount sanctioned and utilized for Pune, Nagpur and Mumbai Metro projects since last three years is as under:<br/><br/><pre><br/><br/><br/>S.No.	Metro Rail Projects	Amount sanctioned and utilized (Rs in crores)<br/>		2012-13	2013-14	2014-15	2015-16<br/> (till 30.06.2015)<br/>1	Pune Metro	0	0	0	0<br/>2.	Nagpur Metro	0	0	0.50	0<br/>3.	Mumbai Metro Line-III	0	0	    0	78.20<br/><br/><br/></pre><br/><br/><br/>(b)	 & (c): Yes, Sir. Government of India (GoI) has accorded ‘in-principle’ approval to the proposal of Government of Maharashtra (GoM) for Pune Metro Rail Project Phase-1 covering a length of 31.51 km along two corridors at a completion cost of Rs. 11,802 crores. The final/revised Detailed Project Report (DPR) of the said project has not been received in this Ministry from GoM. GoI has already sanctioned Nagpur Metro Rail Project covering a length of 38.215 km along two corridors at a completion cost of Rs. 8,680 crores and Mumbai Metro Rail Project Line-III covering a length of 33.5 km (fully underground) at a completion cost of Rs. 23,136 crores.<br/>                  *******<br/>

records.qtitle: Steps to motivate CBI officers
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether CBI says that its officers are not serious about pursuing their investigations in 	courts and they deliberately seek adjournments time and again, if so, details thereof and 	Government''s response thereto; and<br/>(b) 	the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken to motivate CBI officers in pursuing 	court cases and in disposing of cases?<br/>
records.ans_text: Minister of State in the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office. (DR. JITENDRA SINGH)<br/><br/>(a):  	CBI officers pursue all pending cases in courts sincerely for their expeditious and timely disposal and adjournment is not sought from the court without any justified reason.<br/><br/>(b):  	CBI has instituted Gold Medal award for the best Investigating Officer and the Prosecuting Officer of CBI, CBI Day award etc. to reward selected officers to motivate them to  pursue excellence in their areas of work.  Special Incentive Allowance is also given to CBI officers to attract officers of proven competence and integrity.  Further, specialised training is imparted to CBI officers at CBI Academy as well as at IIM Bengaluru to improve their capabilities and efficiency.<br/><br/>***********<br/>

records.qtitle: Expansion of Vanbandhu Kalyan Yojana
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government is considering to expand the programme Vanbandhu Kalyan Yojna (VKY) for the development of tribal people in the country;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the details of the scheme and its salient features thereof; and <br/><br/>(c)	how much amount has been allocated to various parts of the country during the last one year, particularly in Maharashtra?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI MANSUKHBHAI DHANJIBHAI VASAVA)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):	The Scheme ‘VKY’ has been adopted as a strategic process, which aims at creating enabling environment for need based and outcome oriented holistic development of the tribal people across the country by convergence of resources through appropriate institutional mechanism. Thematic areas covered under VKY are given below:<br/><br/>I.	Qualitative and sustainable employment.<br/>II.	Quality education and higher education.<br/>III.	Accelerated economic development of tribal areas.<br/>IV.	Health for all.<br/>V.	Housing for all.<br/>VI.	Safe drinking water for all.<br/>VII.	Irrigation facilities suited to the terrain.<br/>VIII.	All weather roads with connectivity to the nearby town/cities.<br/>IX.	Universal availability of electricity.<br/>X.	Urban development.<br/>XI.	Promotion of sports in the tribal areas<br/>XII.	Promotion and preservation of tribal culture and heritage<br/>XIII.	Robust institutional mechanism. <br/>XIV.	Security. <br/><br/>The strategies under VKY are as under:<br/>(i)	Strengthening of institutions meant for delivery of goods and services with adequate administrative, technical and financial powers such as Tribal Welfare Departments as nodal Department, Integrated Tribal Development Agency (ITDA), Integrated Tribal Development Projects (ITDPs) and creation of new ones where they do not exist etc. <br/>(ii)	Convergence of scattered resources and activities being undertaken under various components.<br/>(iii)	Preparation of perspective plan with outcome oriented and monitorable targets.<br/>(iv)	Gender responsiveness. <br/>(v)	To  ensure that Tribal Sub Plan (TSP) components of Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) and State Plan (SP) are actually spent for tribal people and areas inhabited by tribal people.<br/>(vi)	Implementation of interventions primarily through ITDAs/ITDPs, with Public Private Partnership (PPP) support wherever needed and feasible.<br/>(vii)	Services of Academic Institutions, Research Organizations, Tribal Research Institutes and professional agencies for monitoring of outcomes.<br/>(viii)	In NE States where panchayats do not exist, institutions of decentralized governance at village / town level to be created.<br/>	<br/>(c):	During the year 2014-15, an amount of Rs 10.00 crore was earmarked to each of the ten States having Schedule V Areas including Maharashtra for undertaking initiatives for development of one Block in each State. <br/>

records.qtitle: NGOs registered under FCRA and blacklisted
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) the names of the NGOs registered under the Foreign Contributions Regulation Act, 1976 (FCRA) and blacklisted along with the reasons during the last three years, particularly in Maharashtra;<br/><br/>(b) the names of the NGOs which applied for permission along with the letter of sanction received from the foreign funding agency for collecting foreign funds under FCRA;<br/><br/>(c) whether the activities of the foreign funding agencies have been found to be against the national interest;<br/><br/>(d) if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(e) the steps and action taken by Government against foreign funding agencies working against the national interest?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU)<br/>(a):  The list of  NGOs registered under Foreign Contribution Regulation Act, 2010 (FCRA) is available on the website of the Ministry of Home Affairs http://mha1.nic.in/fcra.htm. Instances of non-Government Organisations violating provisions of the FCRA and FCRR have come to Government’s notice. FCRA and Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Rule, 2011 (FCRR) came into force with effect from 01.05.2011. Since then, FCRA registration of 1296 NGOs have been cancelled in the State of Maharashtra,   after issue of Show Cause  Notices  to  such associations and giving them adequate opportunity.<br/><br/>--2/-<br/><br/>-2-<br/>R.S. U.S.Q. No. 227 for 22.07.2015<br/><br/>After inspections and scrutiny of accounts, 3 cases were referred to CBI and 2 associations have been prohibited from receiving foreign contribution in State of Maharashtra.  <br/><br/> (b) to (e):	The names of the associations who have applied for prior permission under FCRA, 2010 is  annexed.  Foreign funding agencies don’t  come directly  under the purview of FCRA, 2010.  However, since 2011, whenever it has come to the notice of Central Government that certain associations  who are not authorized or entitled  to receive foreign contribution are getting funds from these foreign  donors, 16  donor agencies were placed under prior approval category under Section 46 of FCRA, 2010.  This ensures that any funding from these agencies will require prior approval from the Ministry of Home Affairs. <br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Flights to Leh and Ladakh
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that Flights to Leh-Ladakh almost never meet all the safety requirements, as set by Directorate General of Civil aviation (DGCA) and this is one of the worst kept secrets of Indian aviation;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof and Government''s response thereto;<br/><br/>(c) whether the Indian Commercial Pilots'' Association (ICPA) has raised questions to fly towards Leh-Ladakh airport; and<br/><br/>(d) if so, the Government''s reaction thereto?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION<br/><br/>(Dr Mahesh Sharma)<br/><br/>(a) & (b) No, Sir. Flights to Leh-Ladakh meet all the safety requirements, as set by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA). However, in the recent DGCA inspection certain deficiencies were observed. The same has been communicated to all the airlines operating to Leh-Ladakh.<br/><br/>(c) to (d) ICPA has recently sought certain clarifications on performance and technical issues regarding day to day Leh operations. The matter was discussed with ICPA and it stands addressed.

records.qtitle: Action plan for Yoga promotion
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has prepared any ambitious action plan on the promotion of Yoga and for tapping the ancient form of exercise in various parts of the country, if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(b) the details of fund allocated for the promotion of Yoga programmes in the country during the last one year; and <br/><br/>(c) the details of Goverment programmes and schemes currently in operation for the promotion of Yoga in the country?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYURVEDA,<br/>YOGA & NATUROPATHY, UNANI, SIDDHA AND HOMOEOPATHY<br/>(SHRI SHRIPAD YESSO NAIK)<br/>(a): The Ministry under its Central Sector Schemes of Information Education and Communication (IEC) and International Co-operation (IC) extends financial assistance to State Governments and other reputed Government/ Non Governmental Organizations/ Universities for conducting National/ International seminars/ workshops/ symposiums to promote Yoga. <br/><br/>      The Government also carries out print and electronic media campaigns for development, promotion and creation of awareness among the people about health promotive, disease preventive and curative potentials of Yoga in the country. AROGYA fairs at National and State level are organized to make public aware of the benefits of AYUSH systems including Yoga.  <br/><br/>        The Ministry of AYUSH has recently initiated a Scheme for Voluntary Certification of Yoga Professionals. First phase of the Scheme to certify Yoga teachers was launched on 22nd June 2015. The Scheme is being operated by the Quality Council of India (QCI), India’s apex quality facilitation and accreditation body, under Ministry of Commerce and Industry.<br/><br/>(b): During 2014-15, under the Central Sector Scheme of Information, Education and Communication (IEC) and International Cooperation (IC) of the Ministry of AYUSH, funds to the tune of Rs. 17.50 Crore  and Rs.  8 Crore were allocated respectively for promotion of AYUSH systems including Yoga.<br/><br/>       In addition, Central Council for Research in  Yoga and Naturopathy (CCRYN) and Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga (MDNIY) were allocated Rs. 13.70 Crore and Rs. 9 Crore under Plan and Rs. 2.24 Crore and Rs. 4.20 Crore under Non-Plan respectively. <br/><br/>(c): Details of programmes and schemes currently in operation for the promotion of Yoga in the country are as follows:-<br/> <br/>(i) Under the Central Sector Schemes of Information Education and Communication (IEC) and International Co-operation (IC) as mentioned in the reply of part (a) of the question, the Ministry of AYUSH has been undertaking many activities to promote Yoga.<br/><br/>(ii) 	   The Ministry of AYUSH has recently initiated a Scheme for Voluntary Certification of Yoga Professionals. (Details mentioned in reply of part (a) of the question).<br/><br/>(iii) 	  A scheme titled “Yoga Training for Police Personnel” has been formulated by the Ministry.  Financial assistance in the form of recurring grant of Rs. 7.00 lakh and non-recurring grant of Rs. 1.00 lakh (one time) will be provided to each district of the State/UT.<br/><br/><br/>(iv)  MDNIY has started B.Sc. (Yoga Science), a regular course of three years duration, Diploma in Yogic Science of One year duration and Certificate courses in Yogic Science for specified Target groups like Delhi Police.<br/><br/>(v)  NIN, Pune provides treatment facility to the patients. It also conducts two years Nursing Diploma in Naturopathy & Yoga Therapy Course.  It has set up a state of the art new pathology lab in its premises with fully equipped automated analyzers for all the routine tests and special tests like CD4 counter for AIDS, Tridot, Spirometry etc. <br/><br/>(vi) CCRYN has established a Central Research Institute (CRI) in Rohini, Delhi.  First phase construction work of two more CRIs in Nagmangala, Karnataka and Jhajjar, Haryana is almost complete. The Council is running 08 Yoga and Naturopathy OPDs in Govt. Hospitals of Delhi and Haryana.<br/><br/>(vii)    The Government of India has approved the National AYUSH Mission which, inter alia, envisages better access to AYUSH services including Yoga and strengthening of AYUSH educational institutions. The Mission provides for a) Co-location of AYUSH facilities at Health Centers/Hospitals including Yoga facilities b) Upgradation of exclusive State AYUSH Hospitals & dispensaries including hospitals with Yoga  centers  c) Upgradation of State Government teaching  institutions including those of Yoga d) Yoga and Naturopathy Wellness Centres  as per guidelines as deemed appropriate by the States under the flexible component. The proposals are sanctioned under the AYUSH Mission on receipt of the same from the State/UT Governments.

records.qtitle: Identification of extractable reserves of shale gas
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether Indian scientists have identified 28 blocks (sedimentary basins, including Damodar), which have an extractable reserve of 260 trillion cubic feet of shale gas, which can meet India’s energy requirement for the next 200 years;  <br/><br/>(b) if so, Government’s response thereto; <br/><br/>(c) whether Government is preparing for the further exploration of shale   gas for fulfillment of energy demands of our country; and  <br/><br/>(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? <br/>_____________
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI DHARMENDRA PRADHAN)<br/><br/>(a): Various agencies have estimated the shale gas and oil resource potential in selected sedimentary basins/ sub basins in India as per the details below:<br/>i.	M/s Schlumberger: 300 to 2100 tcf of shale gas in the country (as available in public domain);<br/>ii.	Energy Information Administration (EIA), USA in 2011: 290 tcf of shale gas in four basins namely, Cambay, KG, Cauvery and Damodar;<br/>iii.	United States Geological Survey (USGS) in Jan’12:  6.1 tcf of technically recoverable shale gas in 3 basins, namely, Cambay, KG & Cauvery.<br/>iv.	EIA, USA in 2013: 584 tcf of sale gas and 87 Billion barrel of shale oil in 4 basins namely,  Cambay, KG, Cauvery and Damodar;<br/>v.	ONGC in 2013: 187.5 tcf of shale gas in 5 basins namely, Cambay, KG, Cauvery, Ganga & Assam and Assam - Arakan;<br/>vi.	Central Mine Planning and Design Institute (CMPDI) in Jul’13:  45 tcf of Shale Gas in Gondwana basin (including Damodar);<br/><br/>(b): The Government has, on 14.10.2013, notified policy guidelines for exploration and exploitation of shale gas and oil by National Oil Companies (NOCs) in their onland PEL (Petroleum Exploration Lease) /PML (Petroleum Mining Lease) blocks awarded under the nomination regimes.<br/>(c) and (d): Under the above policy, there are three Phases,  each of 3 years duration.  Under the Phase I of Assessment, permission has been granted for 55 PEL/PML blocks (ONGC - 50, and OIL – 5)   for carrying out Shale gas /oil exploration and exploitation activities. These blocks are located in the states of Assam (6 blocks), Arunachal Pradesh (1 block), Gujarat (28 blocks), Rajasthan (1 block), Andhra Pradesh (10 blocks) and Tamil Nadu (9 blocks). <br/><br/>Under the Phase-II of the Assessment, ONGC and OIL have to identify an additional 75 and 5 blocks respectively.  Further in Phase III, ONGC and OIL have to identify 50 and 5 blocks to carry out shale gas exploration and exploitation.<br/>______________

records.qtitle: Transfer of salt pan lands in Mumbai
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government has received  any substantive proposal from the Government of Maharashtra for transfer of salt pan lands in Mumbai Metropolitan Region to the State Government for Affordable Housing project;<br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the details thereof and Government''s response thereto; and<br/><br/>(c) 	whether there are rules and regulations for transferring salt pan lands and if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE)<br/>OF THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY<br/>(SHRIMATI  NIRMALA  SITHARAMAN)<br/><br/>(a):	No, Sir. <br/><br/>(b):	Does not arise.   <br/><br/>(c):	Transfer of Central Government land, in general, is regulated by Rule 278 and 279 of the General Financial Rules (GFR) which provides for transfer of land surplus to the requirement of the Union Government to the concerned State Government on payment of market values of the land at the date of transfer.  However, the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion (DIPP) has adopted Internal Policy Guidelines for transfer of salt pan lands owned by the Government of India through the Salt Commissioner’s Organisation, at places other than Mumbai and its suburbs, for public purposes. These guidelines were issued on 24th January, 2012.  As per the approved guidelines, land declared surplus shall be considered for transfer and land under active salt production shall be considered for transfer for public purposes only in exceptional cases.  The transfer shall be in exchange for alternative land of equivalent value suitable for salt production, failing which, on payment of market value. Such identified land shall be offered first to other Central Government Ministries / Departments, next to Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs), failing which the Government of the State in which the land is situated and lastly to the State Public Sector Enterprises (SPSEs).  The transfer of land will be on free hold basis. There shall be no transfer of land to private sector agencies.  A token value of Re.1/- (Rupee One) will be charged for transferring land to Central Government Ministries/Departments after obtaining the approval of the Minister in charge of DIPP.  For cases pertaining to CPSEs, State Governments and their SPSEs, market value will be charged for the land. The market value of the land and its transfer shall be approved by the Minister in charge of DIPP.  <br/>******* <br/>

records.qtitle: Gold  jewellery lying idle with religious places
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)	Whether it is a fact that gold/jewellery worth more than Rs. one lakh crores is lying idle in the lockers of temples, churches, mosques, Gurudwaras etc;<br/><br/>(b)	If so, what are Government’s observation thereon;<br/><br/>(c)	The details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government for reducing India’s dependence on imported gold and narrowing its current account deficit by making use of this idle gold;<br/><br/>(d)	Whether Government is considering to make proper utilization of these gold/jewellery in infrastructure and social development sector; and<br/><br/>(e)	If so, the details thereof and if not, reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a)	to (e):  A statement is laid on the table of the House.<br/><br/>                              ********<br/><br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 175 RAISED BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT, HON’BLE MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT FOR REPLY ON 12TH MAY, 2015<br/><br/>(a)	 As per estimates, the stocks of gold in India are over 20,000 tonnes.<br/><br/>(b)	 to (e) In order to mobilize this gold. The Government has announced the Gold Monetisation Scheme in the Budget 2015-16. The Scheme will allow the depositors of gold to earn interest in their metal accounts and the jewelers to obtain loans in their metal accounts. It is expected that making use of idle gold in this manner will help in reducing India’s dependence on imported gold and in narrowing its current account deficit. The details of the scheme are being finalized.<br/>

records.qtitle: Affordable drugs for Hepatitis C
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that around 2 crore Indians affected with Hepatitis C could not afford the medical treatment for this disease due to costly affairs;<br/><br/>(b) if so, Government''s response thereto; and<br/><br/>(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government for encouraging private pharmaceuticals companies for providing effective drugs at nominal rates?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI JAGAT PRAKASH NADDA)<br/>(a) & (b):	The figures of Hepatitis C affected Indians who could not afford medical treatment are not collected centrally. However, the cost of treatment for Hepatitis C is high for the cases which require treatment.<br/><br/>The Government of India has launched a National Programme for prevention and control of viral Hepatitis during 12th Five Year Plan period under which the activities undertaken, inter alia, are:  <br/><br/>1.	Laboratory network for laboratory based surveillance of viral hepatitis in different geographical locations of India, in a phased manner.<br/>2.	Setting up of one Reference Laboratory at National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), Delhi.<br/>3.	Training and capacity building of professionals in relevant sectors, like Microbiologists, Laboratory Technicians, data Managers and Field Workers. <br/>4.	Laboratory support for outbreak investigation of hepatitis through established network of laboratories. <br/>5.	Development of guidelines and creating awareness for prevention and control and treatment of blood borne and water borne hepatitis.<br/>6.	Information Education and communications (IEC) for dissemination of information about prevention and control of viral hepatitis.<br/><br/>(c):	Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) has granted import and marketing permission on 13th January, 2015 for Sofosubuvir 400 mg tablet (brand name Sovaldi)  manufactured by M/s Gilead Science Ltd., to M/s Mylan Pharma Pvt. Ltd. for treatment of chronic Hepatitis C in adults. <br/> <br/>Subsequently, CDSCO has also granted permission to manufacture and market Sofosubuvir 400 mg tablet in March, 2015 to Indian manufacturers namely, M/s Hetero Labs. and Natco Pharma.  CDSCO has no information about cost of the drug.<br/>

records.qtitle: Ban on old vehicles in Delhi and NCR
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has decided to ban diesel vehicles older than 10 years and all petrol vehicles older than 15 years and they would be taken off the capital''s roads to curb the air pollution in Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR), if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(b) whether Government is considering any scheme to provide incentives for the owners of old vehicles to purchase new and more fuel-efficient vehicles; and <br/><br/>(c) if so, the details thereof, and if not, the reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE<br/>MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI PON. RADHAKRISHNAN)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c)	A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/><br/>	<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 156 ANSWERED ON 11TH MAY, 2015 ASKED BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT REGARDING BAN ON OLD VEHICLES IN DELHI AND NCR <br/><br/><br/>(a)	The National Green Tribunal (NGT) vide its order dated 26-11-2014 has banned all vehicles that are more than 15 years of age to ply in NCT of Delhi and vide its order dated 07-04-2015 banned all diesel vehicles that are more than 10 years of age to ply in NCT of Delhi. In compliance of the Hon’ble NGT orders, plying of 15 years old petrol driven vehicles and 10 years old diesel driven vehicles have been banned by the Delhi Government. Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has filed an application in the NGT for stay of operation of the orders dated 26.11.2014 and 07.04.2015 and give reasonable time of 6 months  for suggesting measures for addressing pollution concerns. NGT has asked Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Ministry of Environment and Forests, Ministry of Urban Development, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, NCT of Delhi to submit within two weeks vies on various states aspects.<br/><br/>(b) & (c) No Sir, There is no such proposal to provide incentives for the owners of old vehicles to purchase new vehicles.<br/><br/>***** <br/>

records.qtitle: Refund of fees by private schools
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government''s attention has been drawn towards the recent direction by the Delhi High Court to implement recommendations of a panel on the unaided private schools fee structure and also asked nearly 250 institutions to return the excess amount to parents with nine per cent interest; <br/><br/>(b) if so, Government''s response and reaction thereto; <br/><br/>(c) whether Government is preparing any new guidelines or rules for the fixing of fee structures of unaided private schools in the country; and <br/><br/>(d) if so, details in this regard and if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SMT. SMRITI ZUBIN IRANI) <br/><br/>(a) to (d):	Fee structures of unaided private schools do not come under the purview of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act 2009, but are in the ambit of respective State Governments.<br/><br/>	However, Government of Delhi has informed that in compliance with the recent direction by the Delhi High Court, all the identified unaided recognized public schools were directed to comply with the recommendations of the Justice Anil Dev Singh Committee.<br/><br/>****

records.qtitle: Restricting profits on sale of medicines
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: <br/>Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a)	whether it is a fact that some companies, are earning huge profit on medicines and medical equipments produced by them as there seems huge price difference between production cost and selling price as Maximum Retail Price (MRP) of different brands of the same medicine varies by as much as 1,700-1,800 per cent in the country; <br/>(b)	if so, Government''s reaction thereto; and <br/>(c)	the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government for restricting profit on medicines?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI HANSRAJ GANGARAM AHIR)<br/><br/>(a) to (c): Pursuant to announcement of National Pharmaceutical Pricing Policy, 2012 (NPPP,2012), the Government has notified Drugs (Price Control) Order, 2013 (DPCO, 2013) on 15.05.2013.  Under DPCO, 2013, methodology for price fixation of drugs is ‘Market based pricing’ instead of ‘Cost based pricing’ provided earlier in the DPCO, 1995.  NPPA has already fixed the ceiling prices in respect of 521 medicines till date out of 680 medicines (628 net medicines) included in the First Schedule of DPCO, 2013 on the basis of market based price data under provisions of said order.<br/><br/>                                                       …2/-<br/> <br/><br/>                      -2-<br/><br/>Maximum Retail Price of different brands of the same molecules / medicines varies for both scheduled and non-scheduled formulations.  However, in respect of scheduled formulations, no person is authorized to sell any scheduled formulation (medicine) to a consumer at a price exceeding the price notified by the NPPA.  In respect of medicines not under price control, manufacturers are allowed to increase maximum retail price (MRP) by 10% annually.  The NPPP, 2012 and DPCO 2013 does not regulate the production cost of medicines and medical equipments and the profit earned by the respective companies.<br/><br/>                   xxxxxxx<br/>

records.qtitle: Misuse of scholarship amount
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) the amount disbursed and spent for providing scholarships to SC/ST communities for their upliftment during the last five years, category-wise; <br/><br/>(b) whether it is a fact that many educational institutes have misused the scholarship amount, if so, number of complaints received by Government during the last five years, State-wise; and <br/><br/>(c) the details of action taken by Government against such erring educational institutes in the country so far?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT<br/><br/>(SHRI VIJAY SAMPLA)<br/><br/>(a) The details of the amount disbursed as Central assistance for providing scholarships to SC/ST communities for their upliftment during the last five years are given in the Annexure. The amount disbursed is utilized and unspent balance, if any, is adjusted in the succeeding year before the release of funds for the year.<br/><br/>(b) & (c) No such complaint regarding misuse of funds by educational institute has been reported to the Government during the last five years. <br/>

records.qtitle: Work related to Aadhaar Card in Maharashtra
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that 95 percent work related to Aadhaar Cards has been completed in Maharashtra;<br/><br/>(b) 	if so, whether Aadhaar cards have been distributed to all the 95 per cent people; and<br/><br/>(c)   	if not, the reasons therefor and by when the Aadhaar cards would be distributed to everyone? <br/>
