records.qtitle: Role of State Governments in matters of universities
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether there is a clear law defining the role of State Governments in matter of universities;<br/><br/>(b) 	whether their role is to only give grants to universities and bear its sundry  expenses and not raise questions about irregularities and malpractices; and<br/><br/>(c) 	if so, the response of the Ministry?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>	(DR. SHASHI THAROOR)<br/><br/>(a):	The Universities are established either by Central legislation or by State legislation. The role of the appropriate Government is clearly defined in the Act governing the University. The State Universities established by the State Legislatures are under the control of the State Governments. In addition, the University Grants Commission (UGC) lays down, from time to time, the minimum standards concerning teaching, examination and research in universities.<br/>(b) & (c):	The grants are given to the State Universities by the State Governments and also by the UGC if they are covered under Section 2(f) and 12B of the UGC Act, 1956. The role of the State Government is not limited to grants giving alone and it can exercise powers of issuing policy directions and regulating the functioning of the State Universities subject to provisions of Acts and Statutes governing the universities and regulations issued by statutory regulatory authorities. The Central Government has introduced the Prohibition of Unfair Practices in Technical Educational Institutions, Medical Educational Institutions and Universities Bill, 2010 in order to prohibit certain unfair practices in technical educational institutions, medical educational institutions and universities and to protect the interests of students.<br/>****

records.qtitle: Annual Status of Education Report
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that Pratham, an NGO, has done stellar work and brought out its latest Annual Status of Education Report on primary education;<br/><br/>(b)	whether the said NGO has provoked policymakers to urgently assess and tackle the crisis in India''s primary school education;<br/><br/>(c)	if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(d)	the corrective measures Government is taking to address the problem?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(DR. SHASHI THAROOR)<br/><br/>(a) to (d):	The latest Annual Status of Education Report (ASER), brought out annually by PRATHAM, a non-governmental organization, presents certain positive findings, including that more than 96% children in the 6-14 years age group are enrolled in schools in rural areas, while the percentage of out-of-school children in the 6-14 years age group has dropped from 4% in 2009 to 3.5% in 2012.  The report expresses concern regarding the learning levels of children in schools in rural areas. It is indeed a valuable input, along with other material, into the work of policy-makers. <br/><br/>Under the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), which specially focuses on rural and backward areas, the State Governments and UT Administrations are supported on several interventions to improve the quality of elementary education, including the provision of 20-day in-service teacher training, the distribution of free and improved textbooks, the recruitment of additional teachers for better pupil-teacher ratios, academic support for school and teachers through block and cluster resource centres, a continuous and comprehensive evaluation system, teacher and school grants for development of appropriate teaching- learning material, etc. <br/><br/>*****

records.qtitle: Reconstitution of body for regualting GM crops
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government will reconstitute the body to regulate Genetically Modified (GM) crops;<br/>(b) whether applications seeking nod for field trials of GM crops are piling up ;<br/>(c) whether Supreme Court’s  appointed technical expert committee called  for a  ten year ban on GM crops; and <br/>(d) if so, the reasons for Government’s decision to reconstitute the body?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRIMATI JAYANTHI NATARAJAN)<br/><br/>(a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN THE REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 101 BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT REGARDING RECONSTITUTION OF BODY FOR REGULATING  GM CROPS  DUE FOR REPLY ON 05.3.2013<br/><br/>(a) Yes Sir; there is a proposal to establish an independent ‘Biotechnology Regulatory Authority of India (BRAI)’ for the regulation of GM Crops through an Act of Parliament, and the BRAI Bill has been submitted to Lok Sabha Secretariat for introduction by the Department of Biotechnology, Ministry of Science and Technology. Currently, the regulation of GM crops is being carried out by the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee (GEAC) a statutory body constituted by the Ministry of Environment and Forests (MoEF) notified under the ''Rules for Manufacture, Use, Import, Export and Storage of Hazardous Microorganisms/Genetically Engineered Organisms or Cells 1989'', of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.<br/><br/>(b) Permission for conduct of confined Biosafety Research Level (BRL) trials by the  GEAC is subject to recommendations from the Review Committee on Genetic Manipulation (RCGM) constituted under Rules 1989 and ‘No Objection’ from the State Government.  At present about 70 applications recommended by RCGM are pending consideration of the GEAC.  In addition about 50 applications for BRL trials approved by the GEAC are awaiting consent of the State Government.<br/><br/>(c) & d) As per the directions of Hon’ble Supreme Court Order dated 10.5.2012, in Writ Petition (Civil) No. 260/2005 of Aruna Rodrigues & Others vs Union of India & Others a Technical Expert Committee (TEC) was constituted to address issues related to genetically modified (GM) crop field trials. The TEC in its interim report has recommended (i) 10-year moratorium on field trials of Bt food crops used for human consumption on the basis of review of Bt cotton and Bt brinjal biosafety data; (ii) Ban on field trials of herbicide tolerant (HT) crops till an independent committee of experts has examined the potential impact of the HT technology including livelihood issues; and (iii) Ban on GM crop field trials in the centers of origin and centers of diversity.  The other key recommendations of the TEC include need assessment, strengthening and restructuring of the current regulatory system, reassessment of the biosafety data on Bt cotton and other data that is generated by all field trials; ensuring there is no conflict of interest; a ban on outsourcing or subcontracting field trials; designation of sites for field trials, and requirement of preliminary bio-safety tests etc; as a prerequisite to all GM crop field trials. <br/><br/>The Union of India has not accepted the recommendations on the ground that  the interim report does not address the terms of reference (TOR) and has not only exceeded the mandate assigned to TEC but are also outside the scope of the Writ Petition itself. A  Joint Affidavit in this regard has been filed by the Ministry of Agriculture on behalf of Union of India. The Hon’ble Supreme Court vide Order dated 9.11.2012 has directed the TEC to consider the objections filed by all  respondents, interested parties and the Union of India and submit its report within six weeks. The TEC has sought extension of time till March, 2013 for submission of the final report.  The matter is now listed for 1.4.2013.   <br/><br/><br/>*******

records.qtitle: Illegal clinical drug trials
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: 867. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: <br/><br/>Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether clinical trials for drugs are being used on gullible human beings in<br/>Maharashtra and other States; and<br/><br/>(b) if so, the number of people died or rendered immobile in these clinical trials?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD)<br/><br/> (a)  & (b):	Although the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation has not received any such report that clinical trial for drugs are being used on gullible human beings in Maharashtra, six cases of alleged irregularities in the conduct of clinical trials have been reported in the country during the last two years.  As per the available data, the number of Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) of deaths during clinical trials reported during the last two years viz. 2011 and 2012 were 438 and 436, respectively.  But SAEs of death attributable to clinical trials during these two years were 32.  The Government of India has recently taken a number of steps to ensure that safety, rights and well-being of clinical trial participants  are protected by strengthening the approval procedures and monitoring mechanism of clinical trials in the country.  Necessary amendments have been incorporated in the Drugs & Cosmetics Rules to strengthen the regulatory framework including the payment of compensation in case of clinical trial related deaths.<br/>

records.qtitle: Mandatory set top boxes for viewing TV Channels
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government has made set top boxes mandatory for viewing TV channels across the country;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, how many metro cities have been covered in the first phase and how many would be covered in the second phase;<br/><br/>(c)	how much revenue Government has earned on each set top box; and<br/><br/>(d)	whether Government is mulling to provide subsidy to the families who can’t afford to install set top boxes and pay monthly subscription?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING (SHRI  MANISH TEWARI)<br/>(a)	to (d):  A statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/>****<br/> <br/><br/><br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. *88 FOR ANSWER ON 4.3.2013.<br/><br/>Ans. (a) & (b): Section 4A(1) of the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995, makes it obligatory for every cable operator to transmit or re-transmit programmes of any channel in an encrypted form through a digital addressable system with effect from such date as notified by the Central Government.  Accordingly, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, vide its notification dated 11.11.2011, has notified dates for implementing Digital Addressable System (DAS) in the Cable TV sector in four phases.  In the digital addressable systems, Cable TV subscribers require Set Top Box (STB) to watch television.  For viewing Doordarshan channels available in terrestrial mode, no STB is required.  Implementation of DAS was substantially completed in 3 out of the planned 4 metros of Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata by the mandated timeline of 31st October, 2012.  In Chennai, the matter is sub judice in the High Court of Madras.  In second phase of DAS, 38 cities with a population more than one million are included.<br/><br/>(c) : The procurement and distribution of Set Top Boxes (STBs) is done by the industry. <br/><br/>(d) : There is no such proposal under the consideration of the Government.  Multi System Operators (MSOs) are, however, mandated to offer STBs on outright purchase, rental or hire purchase as per the convenience of the consumers.<br/>*****

records.qtitle: Acquiring coal blocks by private firms
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: a) the number of private firms which misrepresented their net worth to secure coal blocks; and<br/><br/>(b) the action taken by CBI against them and officials of the Ministries of Coal, Power and Steel who have colluded with private firms to allocate coal blocks?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL<br/>(SHRI PRATIK PRAKASH BAPU PATIL)<br/><br/><br/>(a) & (b): The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has registered 3 Preliminary Enquiry cases regarding alleged irregularities in allocation of coal blocks – relating to allocation of coal blocks to private companies during the period 2006-09, relating to allocation of coal blocks to private companies during the period 1993-2004 and relating to allocation of coal blocks to Government companies. records.qtitle: Prices of cancer drugs
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: <br/><br/>(a)	whether Government is mulling over reducing the prices of cancer drugs for the common man; and<br/>(b)	if so, by when, as it will not just benefit Indians but also bring down cancer drug prices in countries where the pharma market is not controlled by the US and Western European nations?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/><br/>MINISTER OF STATE(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI SRIKANT KUMAR JENA)<br/><br/><br/>(a) & (b):	A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. <br/>                    xxxxxxx <br/><br/>STATEMENT REFERRED IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) & (b) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 71FOR ANSWER ON 01.03.2013 REGARDING PRICES OF CANCER DRUGS<br/><br/><br/>(a)& (b):	Cancer Drugs are non- scheduled drugs and therefore, prices of cancer drugs are not fixed under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 1995(DPCO,95).  Prices of non-scheduled drugs are fixed by the respective manufacturers themselves without seeking the approval of Government / National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA). There is no control on the launch price of non-scheduled medicines under DPCO, 95.  <br/><br/>However, as a part of price-monitoring activity, NPPA regularly examines the movement in prices of non-scheduled formulations.  The monthly reports of IMS Health and the information furnished by individual manufacturers are utilized for the purpose of monitoring prices of non-scheduled formulations.  Wherever a price increase beyond 10% per annum is noticed, the manufacturer is asked to bring down the price voluntarily failing which, subject to prescribed conditions, action is initiated under paragraph 10(b) of the DPCO, 95 for fixing the price of the formulation in public interest. <br/><br/>	National Pharmaceutical Pricing Policy, 2012 (NPPP,2012) notified by the Government on 7th Dec,2012 has the provisions of bringing the medicines under National List of Essential Medicines-2011(NLEM-2011) under price control.  NLEM-2011 also contains anti-cancer drugs of the specified strengths and dosage forms.As envisaged in the NPPP,2012 prices of these specified anti-cancer drugs under NLEM-2011 would be fixed after promulgation of the new Drugs Prices Control Order by the Government.<br/><br/>                xxxxxxx<br/>

records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(DR. The Government of Maharashtra has reported an expenditure of Rs. 1534.29 crores till December, 2012, which also includes the State share. <br/><br/>(c) & (d):  The State Government of Maharashtra has reported 92% expenditure against funds available in 2009-10, 96% in 2010-11 and 95% in 2011-12. records.qtitle: Funds for education sector
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government intends to provide more funds to education sector which at present hovers around 2.5 per cent of the GDP;<br/><br/>(b)	whether since the recommendations of the Kothari Commission, academicians have advocated for funds up to 6 per cent of GDP; and<br/><br/>(c)	by when Government would meet the expectations of the academicians?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(DR. SHASHI THAROOR)<br/><br/><br/><br/>(a): 	The public expenditure on education as a percentage of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is 3.80 % (Provisional) during 2010-11 (Budget Estimates).<br/><br/>(b):	The Education Commission, 1964-66, under the Chairmanship of Dr. D.S Kothari, projected that the educational expenditure in the country as a whole should rise to 6 per cent of the Gross National Product by 1985-86.  The National Policy on Education 1986, as modified in 1992, had also laid down that the investment on education be gradually increased to reach a level of 6% of the National Income as early as possible.<br/><br/>(c):	The outlay of the Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD) for the XII Five Year Plan is Rs.453728 crore (Rs.343028 crore for the Department of School Education & Literacy and Rs.110700 crore for the Department of Higher Education).  As compared to the outlay of XI Plan, which was Rs.269873 crore, (Rs.184930 crore for the Department of School Education & Literacy and Rs.84943 crore for Department of Higher Education), this is an increase of 68%.  This increase in central plan outlay for education represents a determined effort on the part of the Central Government for raising public spending on education towards the national goal of spending 6% of GDP for education.  Overall progress towards this goal, would also depend to a great extent on the investment made by the States on education.  It should be noted that the overall target of 6% of GDP would include private sector spending on education as well.<br/>**********

records.qtitle: Economic relation with ASEAN nations
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)	whether India is forging deeper economic relations with Association of South East 	Asian Nations (ASEAN) countries;  <br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the details of sectors therein;  <br/><br/>(c) 	whether for any economic cooperation to become meaningful, the geographical barrier between India and the region must be erased; and <br/><br/>(d)	if so, the steps Government is taking to erase the barrier?  <br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS <br/>(SHRI SALMAN KHURSHID)<br/>(a) to (d) A statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/>*****<br/><br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (A) TO (D) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 397 REGARDING "ECONOMIC RELATION WITH ASEAN NATIONS"<br/><br/>(a) & (b) Yes, Sir. India and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) countries are forging deeper economic relations across multiple sectors covering trade, investment and services.   <br/><br/>(c) & (d) Yes, Sir. Efforts are being made to strengthen air, road, rail and maritime connectivity with ASEAN and an Inter-Ministerial Group on ASEAN Transport Connectivity, chaired by Ministry of Road Transport & Highways has been constituted.  <br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Merging of Janashree Bima Yojana and Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)	 whether Government is planning to merge Janashree Bima Yojana and Aam aadmi Bima Yojana to streamline expenditure and to ensure better delivery of the schemes;<br/>(b)	whether it is a fact that convergence of the schemes is essential due to overlapping and to cater to similar categories of population; and<br/>(c)	whether merger of the scheme would lead to savings? <br/>
records.ans_text: (a) and (b) : The Government has merged Janashree Bima Yojana (JBY) and Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana(AABY) into one scheme, since both the schemes have similar structure of benefits, premium and target group and are being implemented through Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC). The schemes were merged for better administration and services in providing life insurance cover to the economically backward sections of the society. It will also avoid any duplication of coverage of lives under the two schemes and thus allow more accurate claim experience. <br/>(c ): The objective of the merger of the two schemes is not to increase the savings but to ensure better administration and services under the Schemes and also avoid any duplication of coverage of lives under the two existing schemes.<br/>

records.qtitle: Top scientists of DRDO working on extended tenures
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)  whether it is a fact that dozens of top scientists at the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) are working on extended tenures;<br/><br/>(b)  whether it is also a fact that Government disfavours the policy of retaining officers or specialists after their retirement; and<br/><br/>(c) if so, the reasons for retaining them and the steps taken to impart training to the new scientists as specialists?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF DEFENCE<br/>(SHRI A.K. ANTONY)<br/><br/>(a)  Presently, only 11 Distinguished (top) Scientists are working in Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) on extended tenures.<br/><br/>(b)  Extension in service of scientists and technologists is granted by the Government on         a selective basis only for which provisions exist.<br/><br/>(c)  This extension is granted keeping in view their knowledge and merit in the concerned fields.  DRDO is thus able to utilize rich experience and knowledge of these scientists in on-going research works.  DRDO has also been giving due importance to training.  The Organization has dedicated training institutes, such as Targeted Training Centre at Bangalore, Institute of Technology Management (ITM) at Mussoorie, Training Institute at Jodhpur, Military Institute of Training (MILIT) at Pune.  DRDO has a well established training policy, whereby training programmes for scientists are organized / sponsored in technical and techno-managerial areas through renowned academic institutes / universities / other organizations from India and abroad.<br/><br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Vacancies in national grid operator
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether the national grid operator continues to be grossly understaffed;<br/><br/>(b) 	whether lack of adequate and timely interventions to curb overdrawing by northern region States was cited as one of the reasons for the consecutive grid failures that took place on 30 and 31 July, 2012; and<br/><br/>(c) 	if so, the steps Government is taking to fill up the vacancies in the national grid operator?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF POWER<br/><br/>( SHRI JYOTIRADITYA M. SCINDIA  )<br/> <br/>(a) :		At present, there is no shortage of manpower for important Grid Operation function being done by the National Grid Operator, i.e. Power System Operation Corporation (POSOCO).  POSOCO has adequate manpower at each Regional Load Despatch Centre (RLDC) & National Load Despatch Centre (NLDC).  However, additional manpower is required in other functions of POSOCO like Market Operation, Regulatory and Legal functions.<br/><br/>(b) :		No, Sir.  The Enquiry Committee constituted by the Ministry of Power after the grid disturbances on 30th and 31st July 2012 has found that disturbances were due to a combination of factors, inter-alia, weak inter-regional corridors due to multiple outages, high loading on some inter-regional links due to overdrwal by Northern Region (NR) Utilities and under drawal by WR Utilities, inadequate protection system and inadequate response by State Load Despatch Centres (SLDCs) to the instructions of RLDCs, etc.<br/><br/>(c) :		Suitable action has already been taken to fill up vacancies in the National Grid Operator, i.e. POSOCO.<br/>********<br/>

records.qtitle: Impact of SSA and other schemes
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)	whether the impact of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) is dismal in States across the country; <br/><br/>(b)	whether it is a fact that funds provided under the scheme are not being utilized fully;<br/><br/>(c)	whether it is also a fact that schemes have failed to control students’ drop-out rate in Government schools; and  <br/><br/>(d)	if so, whether Government would formulate annual action plans according to requirement?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(DR. SHASHI THAROOR)<br/><br/>(a):	No, Sir. The Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) programme is being implemented effectively in all the States/UTs.  Since the inception of the SSA, 1,81,522 schools have been opened, 12,34,016 teachers have been recruited, and 5,30,212 toilets and 2,13,617 drinking water facilities have been constructed in schools.  <br/><br/>(b):	The SSA has a good track record of fund utilisation.  Expenditure in 2009-10 was 97.91% of Budget Estimates (BE), in 2010-11 it was 98.38%, in 2011-12 it was 99.36% of BE and in 2012-13 till date it is 80.41% of BE. <br/><br/>(c)&(d):	No Sir, the drop out rates have declined from 39.03% at the primary level and 54.65% at the elementary level to 27% at the primary & 40.6% at the elementary level in    2010-11. <br/><br/>	The Annual Work Plan & Budgets by States/UTs are prepared every year based on their requirement of funds to meet the objectives of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009.

records.qtitle: Steps to check frauds
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: GOVERNMENT OF INDIA<br/>MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/>DEPARTMENT OF FINA.NCIAL SERVICES<br/>RAJYA SABHA<br/>STARRED QUESTION NO.-292<br/>TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 13rH DECEMBER, 20121AGRAHAYANA 22,1934 (SA11,q)<br/>STEPS TO CHECK FRAUDS<br/>QUESTION<br/>*292 : SHRI SANJAY RAUT:<br/>Willthe Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:<br/>(a) whether Ernst and Young financial agency has reported that different<br/>types of frauds have caused Rs. 6600 crore loss to lndian economy and banks in<br/>the last fiscal ;<br/>(b) if so, the reasons therefor and details thereof ; and<br/>(c) the effective steps that Government is taking to check these frauds ?<br/>ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF FINANCE<br/>(sHRl P. CHIDAMBARAM)<br/>(a) to (c) : A statement is laid on the table of the House.<br/>*******Statement as<br/>Question No"<br/>referred<br/>*292 for<br/>in reply to<br/>answer on<br/>part (a) to<br/>13.12.2012<br/>(c) of Rajya<br/>regarding<br/>Sabha Starred<br/>steps to check<br/>tab Shri , ber bha<br/>Part (a) & (b):-<br/>As per the report of Ernst and Young total number of fraud cases during<br/>the FY 2A11-12 stood at 204 involving an amount of Rs 6600 crore for the<br/>financial services sector.<br/>However, as per Reserve Bank of India''s record, the incidents of frauds<br/>reported by the Banks during FY 2011-12 was 5569 cases involving an amount<br/>of Rs.4448 crore.<br/>As reported by RBl, the reasons for frauds in banks are broadly as under:<br/>a) The banks had released the loan amount in lump sum which was not<br/>used for the purpose/s for which the loan was sanctioned.<br/>b) The banks had not carried out the pre sanction inspection of property for<br/>the acquisition of which the loan was being sanctioned to ascertain if the<br/>uniU proPertY reallY existed''<br/>c) The loans were sourced through Direct Sales Agents (DSAs) and the<br/>banks did not carry out any due diligence on their part before sanctioning<br/>the loan.<br/>d) The borrowers submitted fake title deeds of the collateral security which<br/>could not be detected through the process of search reports.<br/>e) The borrowers submitted fake documents related to ''Know your<br/>Customer'' (KYC) compliance and could not be found at the given<br/>addresses after release of loan amount.<br/>f) The borrowers submitted fake and fabricated financial statements/ salary<br/>slips to show improved financial position of the borrowers.<br/>g) The assets created out of the loan amount were sold without the<br/>knowledge of the financing banks before the loan is paid in full.<br/>Part (c)<br/>The steps taken by RBI are as under:-<br/>Reserve Bank of India has issued detailed instructions vide Master Circular dated<br/>Jufy 01 ,2A12 on "Frauds - Classification and Reporting" containing all the details<br/>/aspects relating to frauds. On receipt of fraud reports from banks, various<br/>aspects related to the frauds are examined and concerned banks are advised to<br/>report the case to CBI/Police/Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO), examine<br/>staff accountability, complete proceedings against the erring staff expeditiously,<br/>take steps to recover the amount involved in the fraud, claim insurance wherever<br/>applicable and streamline the system & also procedures so that frauds do not<br/>recur.Reserve Bank of lndia as a part of its supervisory process also takes the<br/>following measures to prevent /reduce the incidence of frauds:<br/>i)Sensitizesbanksfromtimetotimeaboutcommonfraudproneareas<br/>through issuance of modus operandi circulars on various types of<br/>frauds and the measures to be taken by them''<br/>ii) lssues caution advises in respect of borrowers who have defaulted the<br/>banks.<br/>In the past considering various concerns arising out of bank''s operations''<br/>including incidence of frauds, RBI has advised banks to:<br/>a) Introduce a system of concurrent audit ;<br/>b) Review working of internal inspection and audit machinery in<br/>banks by the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors;<br/>c) constitute a specral committee of the Board to exclusively<br/>monitor frauds of Rs'' 1 crore and above; and<br/>d) In order to make third parties and professionals accountable''<br/>who have played a vital role in credit sanction/disbursement or<br/>facilitated the''perpetration of frauds, banks have been advised<br/>vide circular dated, March 16, 2009 to report to lndian Banks''<br/>Association (lBA). IBA in turn will prepare caution lists of such<br/>parties for circulation among the banks

records.qtitle: Reduction in commission of PPF agents
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: <br/>(a)   whether recommendation of Shyamala Gopinath Committee for  abolishing 	one per cent commission of agents of PPF schemes and to reduce<br/>	commission on postal small saving schemes have victimised the agents 	across the country;<br/><br/>(b)	whether Small Savings Agents’ Welfare Association, Mumbai has 	represented to the Ministry to reconsider the Committee’s 	recommendation; 	and<br/>						<br/>(c)	if so, the action that the Ministry is taking to reconsider the ‘one-sided 	report’?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a):   The recommendation of Shyamala Gopinath Committee regarding agents’ commission was to reduce commission of 0.5% on Senior Citizens Saving Scheme (SCSS) and 1% on Public Provident Fund (PPF) to zero, reduce 4% commission under Mahila Pradhan Kshetriya Bachat Yojana (MPKBY) to 1% in a phased manner and to  reduce 1% commission for all other schemes under Standardised Agency System (SAS) to 0.5%.  The Government, after consulting all the stakeholders and the representations received, has decided to reduce the commission under PPF and SCSS to zero and under SAS to 0.5%.  However, commission under MPKBY continues to be at 4% for the time being.<br/>    The main intention of these recommendations is to make these schemes more investor<br/>centric than agent centric.  <br/><br/> (b) & (c):    Representations of Small Savings Agents’ Association from various states including Mumbai were received in the past.  Taking into account of large number of   representations received from Small Savings Agent’s Associations, Members of Parliament, other dignitaries and others, the Government accepted most of the recommendations of the Committee.<br/><br/><br/>

records.qtitle: (clubbed) Shortfalls of goals in ICDS scheme
records.name: VASANTHI STANLEY
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) Scheme falls way short of the goals;<br/>(b)	whether it is a fact that recent UN reports have shown that under five child mortality rate in India is worse than even Nepal and Bangladesh; and<br/>(c)	if so, what effective steps Government is taking to spend heavily on health to check mortality rate in India?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT <br/>(SHRIMATI KRISHNA TIRATH)<br/><br/>(a):   	The Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) Scheme is a well-conceived programme to address health, nutrition and developmental needs of under-six children as well as pregnant and lactating women.<br/><br/>Over 35 years of its operation, ICDS has expanded from 33 community development blocks and 4891 Anganwadi Centres (AWCs) selected in 1975 to become universal through 7076 approved projects and 14 lakh AWCs across the country with final phase of unversalization approved in 2008-09.  However, the larger part of such expansion (more than 50%) has taken place post-2005. Given even this limitation, there has been decline in the prevalence of malnutrition from 42.7% in 1998-99 (NFHS-2) to 40.4% in 2005-06 (NFHS-3). Several studies including National Family Health Survey-3 (NFHS-3) have revealed that the programme has contributed positively towards achieving some of the key programme objectives such as reduction of child malnutrition, improvement in caring practices and improved early child hood development outcomes including quality pre-school education.<br/><br/>(b):  	As per Sample Registration System (SRS-2010), the under-five mortality rate in India is 59.  As per the ‘Levels and Trends in Child Mortality’ Report 2012 by UN Inter-agency group for Child Mortality Estimation, India’s Under-five mortality rate-2011 is 61 where as that of Nepal and Bangladesh are 48 and 46 respectively.<br/><br/>(c):  	Apart from ICDS which has been approved for strengthening and restructuring, various interventions under RCH progamme of National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) of Ministry of Health and Family Welfare are being implemented by the Government to reduce the child mortality. These include Janani Shishu Suraksha Yojna, Navjaat Shishu Suraksha Karyakaram, along with Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI), Special New Born Care Units (SNCU), Nutrition Rehabilitation Centres (NRC) etc. <br/><br/>The High Level Expert Group (HLEG) on Universal Health Coverage has recommended increasing public spending on health to at least 2.5% by the end of the 12th Plan and to at least 3% of GDP by 2022. The recommendations of the High Level Expert Group (HLEG) are considered by the Planning Commission during formulation of the 12th Five Year Plan. <br/><br/>                                                                             ******<br/>

records.qtitle: Investment by EPFO in equities
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)whether the Employees'' Provident Fund Organisation is considering<br/>     investment in equities as funds earning 12 per cent annually in the National Pension System do;<br/>(b)how much EPFO has invested in private sector, blue chip manufacturing companies; and<br/>(c)how Government would ensure that 5 crore subscribers are not punished with low returns for no fault of theirs?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT<br/>(SHRI KODIKUNNIL SURESH)<br/>(a):	No, Sir.<br/>(b):	As on 31.10.2012, the total of Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) corpus invested in private sector is Rs. 26,896.54 Crore including Rs. 4.05 Crore investments in blue chip manufacturing companies.<br/>(c):	Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) ensure security of the capital contributed by the beneficiaries with risk free, consistent return on the same.<br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: Monopoly of cable TV sector
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)	whether the Ministry has asked the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) to suggest measures to check monopoly of cable TV sector;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(c)	whether the Ministry would clip the wings of certain players who are dominating in the Multi System Operators in various States;<br/><br/>(d)	whether any time-frame has been set for TRAI to submit the report; and<br/><br/>(e)	if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING (SHRI  MANISH TEWARI)<br/><br/>(a) to(e) : The Ministry is seized of the issue of monopolistic practices in the various segments of broadcasting sector and accordingly a reference to the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) was made on 16.5.2012 to examine the entire gamut of media ownership issues. The Ministry has requested TRAI to provide  recommendations on specific issues of vertical integration within the various segments in the Broadcasting Sector as in the present scenario more and more broadcasting companies owning television channels are venturing into various distribution platforms, namely cable TV distribution, DTH, and IPTV etc. and similarly many companies owning distribution platforms are also entering into television broadcasting. TRAI has also been asked to look into the issue of horizontal integration wherein companies have controls/ownerships across print, TV and Radio. TRAI recommendations are awaited. The Ministry is also in the process of making a reference to the TRAI to examine the spectre of alleged monopolistic practices in the distribution segment of the Broadcasting Sector.<br/><br/>******

records.qtitle: Cancellation of coal blocks
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether the Ministry has cancelled coal blocks to various private/public sector companies during the last three months;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; and   <br/><br/>(c) what penalty has been imposed against them?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL<br/>(SHRI PRATIK PRAKASHBAPU PATIL)<br/><br/>(a) to (c) During the period of last three months Government has cancelled allocation of 15 coal blocks and issued orders for deduction/forfeiture/introduction of bank guarantee in respect of 13 other coal blocks as per the details given at Annexure. <br/><br/>*****<br/> <br/>

records.qtitle: (clubbed) Leasing out of vacant railway land
records.name: VASANTHI STANLEY
records.qn_text: (a) whether Railways plan to lease out vast railway land lying vacant across the country;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details of the sites; and <br/><br/>(c) the amount Government is going to realise out of this lease?  <br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI KOTLA JAYA SURYA PRAKASH REDDY)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/><br/> <br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1685 BY SHRIMATI VASANTHI STANLEY & SHRI SANJAY RAUT TO BE ANSWERED IN RAJYA SABHA ON 07.12.2012 REGARDING LEASING OUT OF VACANT RAILWAY LAND.<br/><br/>(a) to (c):  Indian Railway network occupies a land area measuring about 10.65 lakh acres.  Ninety per cent of this land is directly under railway tracks, yards, workshops and allied infrastructure.  The vacant land, measuring about 1.13 lakh acres is mostly in the form of a narrow strip along tracks which railways have been utilizing, or plan to utilize, for its expansion in the form of doubling, third line, quadrupling, gauge conversion, freight corridors, yard remodelling, traffic facility works, workshops, etc. for servicing and maintenance of track and other rail related  infrastructure. Vacant railway land/air-space not required by Railways for its immediate future operational needs is utilized for commercial development through Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA), wherever feasible.  So far, 55 sites having area of 154 hectare amenable for commercial development have been identified. As the commercial development is a market driven activity, to be undertaken with the approval of the State Governments/local authorities, assessment of revenue generation can only be done when specific schemes are taken up for development.<br/><br/>***<br/>

records.qtitle: Bangalore Police crack down on alleged terror modules
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that the Bangalore Police recently has cracked down on alleged terror modules in the State;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(c) whether Government has found similar modules running in other parts of<br/>the country; and<br/><br/>(d) what effective steps Government is taking to check rise of terror links in the country?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI R.P.N. SINGH)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):  Yes, Sir.  Bangaluru Central Crime Branch and ATS, Aurangabad, Maharashtra busted a terror module in the Karnataka State with the arrest of 18 persons.  The group was planning to target political leaders and Media persons.  They were also planning to commit robberies in Hubli for raising funds for carrying out terrorist activities.<br/><br/>(c):  No, Sir.<br/><br/>(d):  There exists a very close and effective coordination amongst intelligence agencies at the Center and the State levels.  Intelligence inputs about possible designs and threats are shared with the State Governments concerned on a regular basis.  The Multi Agency Center (MAC) has been strengthened and re-organized to enable it to function on 24x7 basis for real time collation and sharing of intelligence with other intelligence agencies and security intelligence inputs are shared with the concerned States through the established mechanism, which ensures close coordination and sharing of intelligence and seamless flow of information between the States and the Central Security and Law Enforcement Agency.  This has resulted in busting of terrorist modules.<br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: High toll rates
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether it is a fact that according to the All India Motor Transport Congress, the current toll policy lacks transparency, accountability and affordability;<br/><br/>(b) 	whether it is also a fact that toll charges are pinching the transport community and the common man very dearly;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether the toll policy is highly in favour of private builders; and<br/><br/>(d) 	what steps Government is taking to revisit the toll policy?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE<br/>IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS<br/>(SHRI SARVEY SATHYANARAYANA)<br/>(a)	No, Sir.  However All India Motor Transport Congress (AIMTC) have been raising some issues in the meetings held in the Ministry.  In one such meeting AIMTC was requested to submit a detailed proposal with statistics on reforms and alternatives in taxation and toll policy for augmenting the funding requirement for the Government for the construction/maintenance of national highways.  The same is still awaited.<br/><br/>(b)	 No, Sir<br/><br/>(c)	No, Sir.  <br/>(d)	Sir, as and when need arises user Fee Rules are amended in public interest.<br/><br/>*******<br/> <br/>

records.qtitle: Statutory Audit Report of NRHM
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: 1124. SHRI SANJAY RAUT:<br/><br/>Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WLEFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether the Minsitry has made it mandatory for the State Governments to<br/>disclose several important aspects of the Mission on the State''s National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) website;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details of those important aspects;<br/><br/>(c) whether the Ministry has made Statutory Audit Report a must for release<br/>of the second tranche of funds; and<br/><br/>(d) the number of States which have compiled with audit report; and how many<br/>have not?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI ABU HASEM KHAN CHOUDHURY)<br/><br/>(a)&(b) :  Funds are made available to States for implementing the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) and the primary responsibility for proper financial management lies with the States. However, while  approving the State Programme Implementation Plan for the year 2012-13, the States have been directed to ensure mandatory disclosure on the State NRHM website of the following: <br/><br/>i)	Facility wise deployment of all contractual staff engaged under NRHM with name and designation,<br/>ii)	MMUs-total number of MMUs, registration numbers, operating agency, monthly schedule and service delivery data on a monthly basis,<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>iii)	Patient Transport ambulances and emergency response ambulances- total number of vehicles, types of vehicle, registration number of vehicles, service delivery data including clients served and kilometres logged on a monthly basis. <br/>iv)	All procurements- including details of equipments procured.<br/>v)	Buildings under construction/renovation –total number, name of the facility/hospital along with costs, executing agency and execution charges (if any), date of start & expected date of completion.<br/><br/>(c)	Yes. <br/><br/>(d)	Out of 35 States/UTs, only 17 (Seventeen) States/UTs have submitted the Audit Report and 18 (Eighteen) States /UTs have not yet submitted the Audit Report for the F.Y. 2011-12.    <br/>--<br/>

records.qtitle: Free channels
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that Government is offering free channels through its own Direct-to-Home (DTH) without any monthly subscription fee;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(c) the reasons for which Government is not popularizing its DTH facility with set-top boxes in an aggressive way for the poor people who cannot afford to pay monthly subscription fee to the private companies like Tata Sky, Dish TV, Airtel, Reliance, etc.?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING (SHRI MANISH TEWARI)<br/><br/>(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. <br/>                                       *****************<br/><br/> <br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION No. 129 FOR ANSWER ON 03.12.2012<br/><br/>(a) to (c) Yes, Sir. Doordarshan currently has provision for 59 DTH channels as per details given in Annexure-I. These channels are free to air with no monthly subscription fee.<br/>Promos are shown frequently on all Doordarshan channels and publicity through the press is also being done to popularize its DTH facility. A Scheme for upgradation of Doordarshan’s DTH platform to 97 TV channels (from existing 59) has been approved. Also, as part of the above scheme, distribution of 30,000 DTH sets in remote, tribal and border areas of the country has been approved. Besides 10,000 DTH sets have been installed by Doordarshan in uncovered areas, as part of the DTH project and another 55,000 DTH sets under various other schemes have been provided to the State Governments, for uncovered areas like the North-East Region, J&K, Lakshadweep Islands and Pondicherry etc.<br/>***

records.qtitle: Irregularities in MGNREGA
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) 	whether it is a fact that large scale irregularities are taking place in the implementation of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) in various States;<br/>(b) 	if so, the names of such States;<br/>(c) 	whether the Ministry is mulling to use technology like electronic  system for generation and clearance of bills using Global Positioning System to curb the misuse of MGNREGA funds; and<br/>(d) 	if so, by when?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI PRADEEP JAIN ‘ADITYA’)<br/>	<br/>(a)&(b): The Ministry receives a large number of complaints about implementation of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) in the country. The complaints mainly relate to cases of job cards not provided, misappropriation of funds, engagement of contractors, forgery of muster roll, manipulation in job cards, under payment of wages, non-payment of wages, corruption and other irregularities, use of machinery, delay in payments etc. As implementation of the Act is done by the State Governments in accordance with the Schemes formulated by them as per the provisions of the Act, all complaints received in the Ministry are forwarded to the concerned State Governments for taking appropriate action, including investigation, as per law. The state-wise details of such complaints received, disposed of and pending are given in Annexure.<br/><br/>(c)&(d): The Ministry has piloted a proposal for electronic management of musters and material bills to reduce delays in payment and to capture information on real time  basis.    The solution has been offered to all States/UTs.<br/><br/>********

records.qtitle: Leveraging CSR to expand sanitation coverage
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether it is a fact that a conference of State Ministers in-charge of rural sanitation discussed leveraging Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) to augment expansion of sanitation coverage in the country;<br/>(b) 	whether it is a fact that the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation is planning to explore the potential to assist India in sanitation sector;<br/>(c) 	if so, the details of the discussions held by the Ministry with the Foundation on the subject;<br/>(d) 	whether India has asked its scientists to come up with a design of low cost toilets that doesn''t require use of water; and<br/>(e) 	if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a):	Yes sir. <br/><br/>(b)&(c): As per record of this Ministry, no specific plan has been submitted by this Ministry to the Foundation. <br/><br/>(d)&(e): All toilets require a minimum amount of water. However , under NBA guidelines, Research Institutes, organizations and NGOs with proven track record in the area of sanitation and National/ State level institutions involved in sanitation can take up, among others, the design and implementation of environment friendly , self-sustaining sanitation systems, including designs of low water use toilets / ecological sanitary units.  <br/>

records.qtitle: Recommendations of the Sam Pitroda and the Anil Kakodkar Committee
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government is mulling to consider the recommendations of the Sam Pitroda and the Anil Kakodkar Committees on modernization and safety of Railways;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; and <br/><br/>(c) how many recommendations of these Committees have been accepted by Government?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF RAILWAYS<br/><br/><br/>( SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL )<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/><br/>***********<br/><br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF STARRED QUESTION NO. 119 BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT TO BE ANSWERED IN RAJYA SABHA ON 30.11.2012 REGARDING RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE SAM PITRODA AND THE ANIL KAKODKAR COMMITTEES.<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c): The recommendations of the Expert Group for modernization of Indian Railways chaired by Sam Pitroda and of the High level Safety Review Committee chaired by Dr. Anil Kakodkar have been received.<br/><br/>The recommendations of the Expert Group for Modernisation of Indian Railways include those pertaining to modernisation of tracks and bridges, signalling systems, rolling stock, stations and terminals, PPP initiatives, utilisation of land and airspace, construction of Dedicated Freight Corridors, High-speed Passenger Corridors, expeditious implementation of ‘priority’ projects, harnessing Information & Communication Technology, indigenous development and safety. It has recommended mobilisation of resources for the aforesaid purposes along with Human Resource Development to increase specialisation and some organisational changes. It has also provided a blue print for next five years for modernization of Indian Railways.<br/><br/>The High Level Safety Review Committee has made recommendations including general safety matters, organizational structure, empowerment at working level, safety related works and issues, manpower planning issues, shortage of critical safety spares, external interference-encroachment and sabotage, signalling, telecommunication and train protection, modernisation of rolling stock, tracks and bridges, level crossings, fire prevention of trains, road and level crossings and funding issues, human resource development with emphasis on education and training, training institutes on Indian Railways, research eco-system on Indian Railways and  safety architecture on Indian Railways.<br/><br/>Both sets of recommendations are under examination in the Ministry of Railways.<br/><br/>*******<br/><br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Poor condition of railway stations
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that there are many railway stations in Maharashtra that are in a dilapidated condition due to poor maintenance;<br/><br/>(b) whether it is also a fact that shelters on the platform are breaking apart and during rains, water leaks and flows onto the platforms;<br/><br/>(c) if so, the corrective measures Railways would take to improve conditions at the stations; and <br/><br/>(d) if so, the names of those railway stations?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS<br/><br/><br/>(SHRI KOTLA JAYA SURYA PRAKASH REDDY)<br/><br/>(a) to (d): No railway station in Maharashtra is in dilapidated condition. However, repair and maintenance of infrastructure including platform shelters is a continuous process.  Corrective action is taken for repairs / rectification whenever deficiencies are noticed either as a result of regular inspections or through public complaints.<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Scarcity of packaged water
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) whether scarcity of packaged water has added to the miseries of the vendors at railway stations;<br/><br/>(b) whether vendors have complained that IRCTC is not supplying bottles of ‘Rail Neer’ according to demand;<br/><br/>(c) whether vendors claim that for inadequate supply, they are neither able to meet the demand nor can sell bottles of other companies not allowed by IRCTC;<br/><br/>(d) if so, the steps Government is taking to ensure adequate supply of Rail Neer bottles or permit vendors to sell bottles of other brands; and <br/><br/>(e) the steps taken by Railways to curtail price of packaged Rail Neer?	<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS<br/>(SHRI KOTLA JAYA SURYA PRAKASH REDDY)<br/><br/>(a) to (d): As per extant policy guidelines wherever Rail Neer packaged drinking water bottles (PDW) is not adequately available, other BIS (Bureau of Indian Standard)  approved packaged drinking water bottles having requisite laid down standards, are shortlisted by zonal Railways  and permitted for sale over the Railways.  To ensure adequate availability of Rail Neer, Indian Railway Catering  and  Tourism   Corporation   (IRCTC)   has   set    up    three drinking water plants at Nangloi (Delhi) and Danapur (Bihar) and Palur (Tamil Nadu) for production of 1 litre packaged drinking water bottles.  Apart from this, six bottling plants are to be set up by IRCTC at Ambala, Amethi, Mal, Nasik, Farakka and Trivandrum as announced in Railway Budget 2010-11. <br/><br/>(e): The sale price of Rail Neer is based on the cost of production and distribution.  <br/><br/>*******<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Loss to economy due to frauds
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:<br/>(a)	whether Ernst and Young financial agency has reported that different types of frauds have caused Rs.6,600 crore loss to Indian economy and banks in the last fiscal year;<br/>(b)	if so, the reasons therefor and the details thereof; and<br/>(c)	the effective steps that Government is taking to check these frauds?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: (a) & (b) : As per the report submitted by Ernst and Young total number of fraud cases during the FY 2011-12 stood at 204 involving an amount of Rs. 6600 crore for the financial services sector. The exposure of banking sector in this regard stood at Rs.3505.50 crore.<br/>However, as per Reserve Bank of India’s record the incidents of frauds reported by banks along with amount involved therein during 2011-12 was 5569 cases involving an amount of Rs. 4448 crore.<br/>As reported by RBI, reasons for frauds are broadly as under:-<br/>1.        Use of loan not for the purpose/s for   which it was sanctioned.<br/>2.         Improper pre-sanction inspection.<br/>3.        Lack of due diligence before sanction of loan.<br/>4.        Submission of fake title deeds, fake KYC documents by the borrowers.<br/>5.        Submission of fake and fabricated financial statement by the borrowers. <br/>6.        Sale of asset created out of loan without the knowledge of the Bank.  <br/>(c): The measures initiated by RBI are as under:-<br/>Reserve Bank of India has issued detailed instructions vide Master Circular dated July 01, 2012 on “Frauds – Classification and Reporting” containing all the details/aspects relating to frauds.  On receipt of fraud reports from banks, various aspect related to the frauds are examined and concerned banks are advised to report the case to CBI/Police/SFIO, examine staff accountability, complete proceedings against the erring staff expeditiously, take steps to recover the amount involved in this fraud, claim insurance wherever applicable and streamline the system and also procedures so that frauds do not recur.<br/>Reserve Bank of India as a part of its supervisory process also takes the following measures to prevent/reduce the incidence of frauds.<br/> <br/>i)   Sensitizes banks from time to time about common fraud prone areas through issuance of modus operandi circulars on various types of frauds and the measures to be taken by them.<br/> <br/>ii)    Issues caution advises in respect of borrowers who have defaulted the banks.<br/>In the past considering various concerns arising out of bank’s operations, including incidence of frauds, RBI has advised banks to:<br/>      a) Introduce a system of concurrent audit;.<br/>     b)  Review working of internal inspection and audit machinery in banks by the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors;<br/>     c)  Constitute a Special Committee of the Board to exclusively monitor frauds of Rs. 1 crore and above.<br/> <br/>iii)  In order to make third parties and professionals accountable, who have played a vital role in credit sanction/disbursement or facilitated the perpetration of frauds, banks have been advised vide circular dated March 16, 2009 to report to Indian Banks’ Association (IBA). IBA in turn will prepare caution lists of such parties for circulation among the banks.      <br/><br/><br/>*********<br/><br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Vijay Kelkar Committee on elimination of inequitable subsidies
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: Will the MINISTER OF FINANCE be pleased to state:<br/>(a)	whether it is a fact that Vijay Kelkar Committee has suggested elimination of inequitable subsidies;<br/>(b)	if so, the details of items on which elimination of subsidies was suggested; and <br/>(c)	whether it would not affect UPA Government’s welfare programmes?
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/> THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/>(Shri Namo Narain Meena)<br/><br/><br/>(a & b)	Relating to subsidies Vijay Kelkar Committee has mainly emphasized on adjusting the price of petroleum products on regular basis in incremental steps towards eventual deregulation of diesel and an affordable level of subsidy on LPG and kerosene, increase the Marked Retail Price (MRP) of Urea etc. and linking Central Issue Price (CIP) increases to Minimum Support Price (MSP)  increases.<br/><br/>(c)  	Government has broadly accepted the recommendations but with some reservations.  Government is of the view that in country like ours, certain level of subsidies targeted towards poor is necessary and Government is committed to its commitment towards welfare programmes.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) stolen during transit
records.name: VASANTHI STANLEY
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that an Indian diplomatic bag with a visa stickers was stolen during 	transit from the airport to the Indian High Commission;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(c)	the steps taken to retrieve the same?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI E. AHAMED)<br/>(a)	Yes.<br/><br/>(b) 	On 3 September 2012, the High Commission of India, London was informed that 4 Diplomatic Bags, including 3 Bags containing 6000 visa stickers, were stolen in transit from Heathrow Airport to the High Commission. The lost visa stickers were part of a consignment of 50,000 visa stickers sent to the High Commission.<br/><br/>(c)	A case was registered at the police station concerned in London. The High Commission has been closely following with UK authorities. In addition, as soon as the incident came to notice, all authorities concerned in India were informed. Suitable action was taken by the authorities to prevent any misuse of visa stickers. <br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Inequity in medicines access
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: *78. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: <br/><br/>Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether it is a fact that drug access for poor communities in the country has not improved;<br/><br/>(b) whether it is also a fact that since the introduction of Drug Price Control Orders, access to medicines in class II to IV towns has actually declined;<br/><br/>(c) whether it is also a fact that the inequity in medicine access is widely 23 perceived as symptomatic of weaknesses in the healthcare system and represents a failure on the part of Government to fulfil its obligations towards the citizens in terms of their right to health; and<br/><br/>(d) if so, the steps Government is taking to address these concerns?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD)<br/><br/><br/>(a)to(d):	A statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/> <br/><br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 78 FOR 27TH NOVEMBER,  2012<br/>.....<br/><br/><br/>(a)&(b) Access to quality health care is a challenge in a developing country like India. According to an estimate, upto 79% cost of health care in rural areas is due to cost of medicines. There is no report to the effect that since the introduction of Drug Price Control Orders, access to medicines in class II to IV towns has declined. <br/><br/>(c)&(d) Government of India has been supplying various types of vaccines, anti-malarial and anti-tuberculosis drugs free of cost to all at the public health facilities. In addition, Government launched Janani Sishu Suraksha Karyakaram in June 2011, under which all pregnant mothers and sick neonets upto 30 days are entitled to free treatment which includes free drugs and consummables, free blood, diagnostics, free diet and free transport. The 12th Five Year Plan envisages supply of free generic medicines to all accessing public health institutions. <br/><br/> <br/>

records.qtitle: Black marketing of LPG cylinders
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)  whether it is a fact that following the restriction on subsidized LPG cylinders, the capital city of India and neighbouring areas have seen the black market price of the essential commodity almost double from ` 600-700 to ` 1,200-1,300;<br/><br/>(b) whether it is also a fact that the absence of a system to prove that a customer has finished his quota of rationed cylinders is posing a great problem and tampering of seals has aggravated the situation; <br/><br/>(c) whether it is also a fact that rationing of LPG has led to further rise in LPG mafia as it prevails in the case of kerosene; and <br/><br/>(d) If so, the steps Government is taking to check this trend ?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS <br/>(SMT PANABAAKA LAKSHMI)<br/>(a) (c) & (d) : Public sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), namely Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOC), Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) have reported that some cases of overcharging, diversion and supply of under-weight cylinders have been reported in Delhi & National Capital Region between 15.09.2012 & 30.10.2012. As far as irregularities such as diversion of cylinders for unauthorized use or tempering etc. are detected and any cases of irregularities/ malpractices by the distributors/ delivery staff are established, action under provisions of Marketing Discipline Guidelines/ Distributorship agreement is taken against such erring distributors.<br/> (b) : OMCs have a system in vogue for the customer to know the number of subsidized LPG cylinders supplied to him. The system is as under :-<br/>- In each refill voucher for subsidized LPG cylinder of each customer, the sequential number against entitlement is printed. For balance part of current year’s entitlement of 3 cylinders (post capping), 1/3, 2/3 and 3/3 shall be printed on the refill voucher to denote the number of subsidized cylinders supplied to the customer.<br/>- The distributor/ delivery man is required to record each refill delivery in the Domestic Gas Consumer Card (DGCC/ Blue Book). The customer is required to acknowledge receipt of refill in the refill voucher.<br/>- Particulars of subsidized LPG cylinder supplied by the OMCs distributors to the customers are available in the ‘Transparency Portal’ hosted by the corresponding OMCs on the internet and are in public domain.<br/>******<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Problems faced by LPG customers in Maharashtra
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)  whether it a fact that the new guidelines for LPG cylinders has added to the woes of customers in Maharashtra;<br/>(b) whether it is also a fact that customers have to wait for several hours to book gas cylinders; and<br/>(c) if so, the steps the Ministry is taking to provide hassle free booking of LPG cylinders for the customers ?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS <br/>(SMT PANABAAKA LAKSHMI)<br/><br/>(a) to (b) : No established complaint have been reported by any public sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) distributorships regarding implementation of new guidelines for LPG cylinders or for refill booking w.e.f. 14.09.2012.<br/>	Though there are no established complaints, since the new guidelines have come into effect, certain procedural difficulties are being faced by the customers, which are being addressed on priority. Constant efforts are also being made to communicate various provisions to the public at large, through web site, press release, advertisements etc.<br/><br/>(c)   OMCs are having facility of refill booking on telephone. In some of the select cities Short Messaging Service (SMS) and Interactive Voice Response System (IVRS) are also active and booking through the company website is also provided.<br/>	The complaints received by the OMCs are investigated and in all the established cases,  disciplinary action is initiated under the Marketing Discipline Guidelines.<br/>*********<br/>

records.qtitle: Cooling off period for post retirement jobs by judges
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that there is a clamour for post-retirement jobs among judges of High Courts and the Supreme Court: <br/><br/>(b)	if so, the details of judges appointed to various Commissions or Tribunals: and<br/><br/>(c)	whether Government is considering to have a two year cooling-off period after retirement to become eligible for appointments to Commissions or Tribunals?
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/><br/>MINISTER OF LAW & JUSTICE<br/>(DR. ASHWANI KUMAR)<br/><br/><br/>(a) and (b) :   As per information available, there are sixty two (62) Tribunals, Commissions and Authorities constituted under the provisions of Articles 323A and 323B of the Constitution of India.  These Tribunals, Commissions and Authorities have been set up under various legislations and are under the administrative control of twenty four (24) Ministries and Departments of the Government of India. The Chairpersons and Members in many of these Tribunals, Commissions and Authorities are required to be appointed from amongst the retired judges of the High Courts/Supreme Court or by judges retired from the State Judicial Services. Details of Tribunals, Commissions and Authorities in which judges of High Courts and Supreme Court are appointed will be collected and laid on the table of the house. <br/><br/>(c)  :  There is no such proposal.

records.qtitle: Recommendation of Expert Committee on modernization of Railways
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to refer to reply to Unstarred Question No. 1357 given in Rajya Sabha on 2 December, 2011 and state:<br/><br/>(a)   the details of the Expert Committee’s final report; and  <br/><br/><br/>(b) how many recommendations have been accepted and how many are still under  consideration?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS<br/><br/><br/>( SHRI KOTLA JAYA SURYA PRAKASH REDDY )<br/><br/><br/>(a): The Ministry of Railways constituted an Expert Group for Modernization of Indian Railways on 21.09.2011 under the Chairmanship of Shri Sam Pitroda to, inter alia, recommend ways and means to modernize Indian Railways. <br/><br/>The Group has submitted its report on 27.02.2012.<br/><br/>The Group has made recommendations pertaining to modernisation of tracks and bridges, signalling systems, rolling stock, stations and terminals, PPP initiatives, utilisation of land and airspace, construction of Dedicated Freight Corridors, High-speed Passenger Corridors, expeditious implementation of ‘priority’ projects, harnessing Information & Communication Technology, indigenous development and safety. It has recommended mobilisation of resources for the aforesaid purposes along with Human Resource Development to increase specialisation and some organisational changes.<br/><br/>(b): The recommendations are presently under examination in the Ministry of Railways.<br/><br/>*******<br/> <br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Shortfall in Kharif crops due to delayed monsoon
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether the delayed monsoon is all set to adversely affect the Kharif crop output this year;<br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the details of Kharif rice, pulses and coarse cereals output; and<br/><br/>(c) 	the concrete steps Government is taking to make up Kharif shortfall of these produces?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES<br/><br/>(SHRI TARIQ ANWAR)   <br/><br/>(a) & (b):	Yes, Sir.  As per available estimates (First Advance Estimates, 2012-13), Kharif food grain production for 2012-13 is 117.18 million tonnes which is 12.76 million tonnes less compared to that of 2011-12.<br/><br/>(c):	Steps have been taken for enhancing coverage and productivity of rabi crops through initiatives like, early sowing, extending the enhanced ceiling on seed subsidy for rabi crops, fast tracking of releases under the schemes/programmes etc.  Further to compensate the losses of kharif pulses production, a programme on Additional Area Coverage of Pulses during Rabi/Summer 2012-13 has been sanctioned with an allocation of Rs.100.00 crore.  It is reported that as on 16.11.2012, the Rabi coverage is 19.58 million hectare which is about 0.9 million hectare more compared to the normal crop coverage during the corresponding period. <br/><br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: Misuse of RTI Act
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: (a) 	the instances where the misuse of RTI Acts has infringed on individual privacy in the last five years;<br/><br/>(b)	 the number of RTI queries rejected which are not in public interest during the last five years; and<br/><br/>(c) 	whether Government is mulling to amend the RTI Act?<br/>
records.ans_text: Minister of State in the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office. (SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY)<br/>(a):    A Public Information Officer is not obliged under the RTI Act, 2005 to give any citizen information which relates to personal information the disclosure of which has no relationship to any public activity, or interest, or which would cause unwarranted invasion of the privacy of the individual unless the Public Information Officers or the appellate authority, is satisfied that the larger public interest justifies the disclosure of such information.<br/>(b):    The Central Inforamation Commission does not maintain such data.<br/>(c):    Privacy of individual is adequately protected under the RTI Act, 2005 and there is no proposal to amend the Act with respect to that.<br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Reduction in fiscal deficit by increased tax collection
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: Will the MINISTER OF FINANCE be pleased to state:<br/>(a)	whether Vijay Kelkar’s report on fiscal consolidation has painted grim pictures of Government finances;<br/>(b)	If so, the details thereof; and<br/>(c)	the steps that are being taken by the Ministry to mobilise resources and to increase tax collection both direct and indirect in order to reduce fiscal deficit?
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/> THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/>(Shri Namo Narain Meena)<br/><br/><br/>(a)<br/>   	No Sir/ Madam.  <br/><br/>(b)	Does not arise.  <br/><br/>(c)  	The following steps are being taken by the Ministry to mobilise resources to increase tax collection in order to reduce fiscal deficit: -<br/><br/>(A)	      Direct Taxes:<br/><br/>(i)	Monitoring of Advance Tax payment especially by top taxpayers; Emphasis is also given to monitor Advance tax payers that have to pay Alternate Minimum Tax applicable from the Financial Year; <br/><br/>(ii)          Conducting surveys for detection of concealment of income and for compliance of TDS provisions. Detection of new areas of violation/avoidance of the provisions of TDS and taking action for proper deduction and deposit of TDS; <br/>(iii)        Organizing training programmes for senior management as well as for DDOs (particularly of Government departments and PSUs)  to spreading awareness about TDS& TCS provisions; <br/>(iv)         Emphasis on collection out of arrear demand and monitoring of high default cases;<br/>(v)         Detailed strategy for making quality assessments has also been devised; <br/>(vi)        Cross-verification of data collected through Annual Information Return with the return of income and issuance of notices in suitable cases. Using the data collected through Transaction statements for better quality assessments as well as recovery of demand; and<br/>(vii)        Multi–media campaign to encourage voluntary compliance of tax laws.<br/><br/>(B)	      Indirect Taxes:<br/><br/>(i)        To broaden the tax base and limit exemptions, negative list based comprehensive approach to service tax has been introduced with effect from the 1st of July, 2012.<br/>(ii)      From 1st of October, 2012, service tax on transport of goods and passengers (in air-conditioned class and first class) by rail has been brought into effect.<br/>(iii)    In addition, other steps including monitoring of revenue, strengthening of anti-evasion and audit mechanism, conduct of targeted audits and search operations, adjudication of pending show cause cum demand notices, realization of arrears, steps to curb undervaluation of import, disposal of confiscated bullion and precious stones, administrative steps like redeployment of human power to service tax field formations which have more potential for augmentation of revenue.
