A High Level Central Team of the Department of Agriculture & Cooperation has visited Bihar and advised the State Government about suitable agricultural crops/activities and agricultural inputs i.e. appropriate crop varieties and seeds.

records.qtitle: ALTERATION ADDITIONS IN DDA FLATS NO.
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that free hold title holders and hire purchase allottees are entitled to carry out alterations/additions in the DDA flats after approval by the DDA;

(b) whether it is permissible to add another floor at the top of DDA flats as fifth floor;

(c) whether it has come to the notice of Government about unauthorised constructions going on in DDA flats particularly in some pockets of Mayur Vihar Phase-I; and

(d) the action Government is going to take against the erring allottees for indulging in unauthorized constructions?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )


(a): Lease deed/ Conveyance deed holders of Delhi Development Authority (DDA) flats are allowed to carry out alterations/ additions to their flats as per the approved guidelines.

(b): No, Sir.

(c): DDA has informed that cases of unauthorized construction have come to its notice in Mayur Vihar Phase-I.

(d): Action against the unauthorized construction is an ongoing process and includes demolition as well as sealing.

records.qtitle: FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE FOR DEVELOPMENT OF FORESTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government provides some financial assistance to State Governments for the development of Forests in their territory;

(b) the amount of funds so released to State Governments, particularly to State Government of Maharashtra for the purpose during the last three years;

(c) the works undertaken by the State Government of Maharashtra using the aforesaid funds;

(d) whether there is a delay in releasing the funds by Government; and

(e) if so, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI S. REGUPATHY)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) The National Afforestation and Eco-development Board, Ministry of Environment and Forests is implementing the National Afforestation Programme aimed at regeneration of degraded forests and fringe areas, through a two tier institutional set-up of Forest Development Agencies (FDAs) at the district level and Joint Forest Management Committees at the village level. The State-wise details of funds released by the National Afforestation and Eco-development Board to the FDAs, including those in Maharashtra, during the last three years, are given in the annexure

(c) The FDAs have undertaken Afforestation as well as related activities like soil and moisture conservation, fencing, Entry Point Activities, monitoring and evaluation, utilizing the fund.

(d) & (e) Funds are released to FDA projects on receipt of appropriate proposals along-with satisfactory utilization of the funds released earlier and other requisite documents like progress report, audit report etc. The release is further subject to availability of fund with National Afforestation and Eco-Development Board during the financial year.

records.qtitle: FOREIGN FUNDING AGENCIES WORKING AGAINST NATIONAL INTEREST .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the names of the NGOs registered under the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) 1976 blacklisted alongwith the reasons during each of the last three years, till date, State-wise;

(b) the names of the NGOs applied for permission alongwith the letter of sanction received from the Foreign Funding Agency for collecting Foreign Funds under FCRA;

(c) whether the activities of foreign funding agencies have been found to be against the national interest;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) the action taken by Government against foreign funding agencies working against the national interest?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a) to (e): A statement is laid on the table of the House.

STATEMENT IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 528 FOR ANSWER ON 22ND OCTOBER, 2008

(a) There is no blacklist of association registered under Foreign Contribution Regulation act (FCRA), 1976. However, as and when, complaints relating to the violation of provisions of FCRA against associations come to the notice of the Government, appropriate action is taken against such associations under the Act. Such actions may include
(i) prohibiting the association from receiving foreign contribution,
(ii) placing the association in the Prior Permission category,
(iii) prosecuting the association in a court of law and
(iv) freezing the bank accounts of the association. In case, associations are found to be indulging in serious violations such as misappropriation or diversion of foreign contribution for purposes other than the stated objectives of the association, the case is referred to Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) for a detailed investigation and prosecution, if necessary. Violations which are unintentional and not of a serious nature are condoned under the previsions of Section 31 of the Act.
On the basis of various complaints received and inquiries made, 44 associations have been prohibited from receiving foreign contribution, 26 Associations have been placed in Prior Permission category and bank accounts of 11 Associations have been frozen. A list of associations against which action has been taken for violation of various provisions of the Act, is available on Ministry’s website: http://mha.nic.in/fcra.htm. Cases of 17 associations have been referred to CBI for detailed investigation.

(b)to(e): Associations seeking prior Permission for receiving foreign contribution from a foreign source are required to submit a commitment letter from the donor agency specifying the amount of the foreign contribution to be received and the purpose for which it is proposed to be utilized. Such permission is granted after carrying out a verification of the antecedents and activities of the recipient organization. In case, the amount of foreign contribution proposed to be received is above a certain threshold limit, a detailed verification of the antecedents of the donor agency is also carried out. If after due verification, substantive inputs are received against a particular donor agency suggesting its involvement in activities prejudicial to the national interest or its funding NGOs indulging in anti-India propaganda/activities abroad, prior permission for receipt of foreign contribution from such donor agencies is denied. The State-wise list of NGO’s granted prior permission under the FCRA is available on Ministry’s website: http:www.mha.nic.in/fcra.htm.

records.qtitle: INDUSTRIAL UNITS SET UP WITH CENTRALLY SPONSORED SCHEME .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of industrial units set up with the help of centrally sponsored scheme in the country particularly in the Maharashtra during the last three years; and

(b) the details of investment made in these units during the above period, State-wise and Union Territory-wise?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY

(SHRI ASHWANI KUMAR)


(a)&(b): Under the liberalized Industrial Policy, the decision to set up an industry is based on the techno economic considerations of the entrepreneurs, which in turn depend on the initiatives of the State Governments in creating conducive environment by way of providing infrastructure facilities and other incentives. Central Government supplements their efforts to the extent possible. Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion is implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme i.e., Package for Special Category States, in the states of

(ii) Himachal Pradesh and
(iii) Uttarakhand (w.e.f. 7.1.2003). Under this scheme, Capital Investment Subsidy, Interest Subsidy, Comprehensive Insurance and Transport Subsidy are provided to industrial units. The Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion does not implement such a scheme for Maharashtra. The details of plan funds released to the three states in the last three years is provided in Annexure –I. The details of Industrial units set up and investment made in the three states is provided in Annexure-II.
The Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion is also implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme i.e., North East Industrial and Investment Promotion Policy (NEIIPP) in the states of North East including Sikkim w.e.f. records.qtitle: REVIVAL OF PSES
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of unviable Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs) registered with the Board of Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) upto September, 2008, PSE-wise and location-wise; and

(b) the steps taken to revive them ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES & PUBLIC ENTERPRISES

(SHRI SONTOSH MOHAN DEV)

(a) & (b) A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

Statement in reply to Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 57 for reply on 21.10.2008. regarding revival of PSEs by Shri Sanjay Raut.

(a): As per available information as on 30.6.2008, total 66 Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) were registered with the Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction(BIFR). The status-wise, PSE-wise and location-wise details are annexed.

(b) : Enterprise specific steps for revival of CPSEs are taken by the concerned administrative Ministries/Departments and the CPSEs as well, which may include financial and business restructuring such as waiver of lean and interest including penal interest, conversion of loan into equity, Government guarantee, grant of moratorium on payment of interest/loan, formation of jo,int ventures, merger/closure, modernization, improved marketing strategies, rationalization of manpower, change of management, fresh cash infusion, etc. in addition, the Government constituted the Board for Reconstruction of Public Sector Enterprises(BRPSE) in December, 2004 in pursuance to the stipulations made in the National Common Minimum Programme(NCMP) for inter alia examination of the cases for revival of CPSEs and to make appropriate recommendations to the Government.

records.qtitle: SCAMS IN PRIVATE AND FOREIGN BANKS QUESTION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has taken any decision to introduce any special scheme to unearth the irregularities and scares in private and foreign banks;

(b) if so, the salient features of the scheme; and

(c) by when the above scheme is likely to be implemented?
records.ans_text:
The Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance

(Shri Pawan Kumar Bansal)

(a) to (c): As a proactive measure for strengthening financial stability and with a view to enhancing public confidence in the robustness of the financial sector, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has, vide its circular dated 18.04.2007, implemented a scheme called `Protected Disclosures Scheme for Private Sector and Foreign Banks`. The salient features of the Scheme include the areas of complaints such as corruption, misuse of office, criminal offences, suspected / actual fraud, failure to comply with existing rules and regulations such as Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, Banking Regulation Act 1949, etc. and acts resulting in financial loss / operational risk, loss of reputation, etc. detrimental to depositors` interest / public interest. The Scheme also provides the procedure for lodging complaints under the Scheme, framing protected disclosure policy by banks, etc. As per the Scheme, employees of the bank concerned (private sector and foreign banks operating in India), customers, stake holders, Non-government Organisations (NGOs) and members of public can lodge complaints. The detailed Scheme is available at RBI website www.rbi.org.in.

records.qtitle: HELICOPTER SERVICES IN THE COUNTRY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the infrastructure requirements for helicopter operations in India;

(b) whether there is any proposal under consideration of Government to import helicopters for commercial operations in India;

(c) whether civilian air routes have been chalked out for the purpose;

(d) if so, the details thereof;

(e) the certification and licensing procedures for building helipads;

(f) whether there is a tariff regulating authority for commercial operations of helicopters in India; and (g) whether the commercial operators are free to charge any fare to cover cost of operations and make profit?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )
(a):- At present dedicated infrastructure for operation of helicopters does not exist. The helicopters are operated from normal airports. However, at Mumbai, Juhu airport is being predominantly used for helicopter operations for off - shore flights. (b):- There is no proposal under consideration of Government to import helicopters. However, Pawan Hans Helicopters Limited has plans to buy 16 helicopters. (c):- No, Sir. (d):- Does not arise. (e):- The procedures exist in the form of Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR) Section 4 Series B Parts II and III. (f) :- No, Sir. (g):- Government does not regulate air fare.

records.qtitle: GOVERNMENT AND PRIVATE COLLEGES IN THE COUNTRY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of Government and private colleges, as on date, in the country, State-wise;

(b) the number of private colleges getting grant from the UGC;

(c) the criterion for giving grant to private colleges ; and

(d) the steps taken by Government for promoting quality education in these private and Government colleges?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SMT. D. PURANDESWARI)

(a): As on 30.09.2008, there are 4961 Private Colleges and 2038 Government owned Colleges recognized by the University Grants Commission (UGC). A State-wised List of colleges is at Annexure I.

(b): As on 30.09.2008, 3904 private colleges were eligible to receive grants from the UGC.

(c): Private Colleges that are permanently affiliated to State universities and which get maintenance grants (under Salary head) from the State government concerned are eligible for grants from the UGC.

(d): Eligible colleges are provided development grants and also grants for improvement of quality of education under the UGC’s scheme of `Colleges with Potential for Excellence`.

Annexure referred to in reply to part (a)of Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question No.212 for answer on 20.10.2008 asked by Shri Sanjay Rout, Member of Parliament, regarding Government and private colleges in the country.
No. of Colleges Govt./Non Govt. state-wise under Section 2 (f) & 12 (B) of the UGC Act, 1956 as on 30.9,2008.

records.qtitle: TWO SHIFT KENDRIYA VIDYALAYAS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of Kendriya Vidyalayas functioning in the country, having two shifts at present;

(b) whether Government is planning to start two shifts in all the Kendriya Vidyalayas, with a view to accommodate more students;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) if not, the alternative arrangements made or proposed to be made by Government to accommodate more students in Kendriya Vidyalayas?
records.ans_text:
MIINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M. A. A. FATMI)

(a) There are 42 Kendriya Vidyalayas in the country having two shifts at present.

(b) & (c) No, Sir.

(d) The mandate of the Kendriya Vidyalayas is primarily to cater to the educational needs of` the wards of transferable Central Government employees including defence personnel and para-military forces. In many Kendriya Vidyalayas, the available seats are being offered to the applicants of other categories in order of priority.

records.qtitle: INVESTMENT IN URBAN INFRASTRUCTURE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the country needs more than Rs. 120,000 cr of investment in urban infrastructure over the next seven years;

(b) If so, Government`s response thereto;

(c) The details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for providing adequate fund towards urban infrastructure development;

(d) Whether Government`s attention have been drawn towards demand of evolved municipal bonds as an option for financing urban infrastructure in the country; and

(e) If so, Government`s view and reaction thereto?
records.ans_text:
Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance

(SHRI P.K BANSAL)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b)& (c): Government of India has launched the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) on 3ra December, 2005 to give focused attention to integrated development of urban infrastructure and services in cities with emphasis on provision of basic services to the urban poor including housing, water supply, sanitation, road network, urban transport, development of inner (old) city areas etc. The Mission envisages central assistance of Rs. 50,000 crore as reform linked central assistance over the Mission period of seven years beginning from 2005-06.

(d)& (e): In 2000-01, the Government inserted a new clause
(vii) in Section 10(15) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, exempting interest income from bonds issued by local authorities. Funds raised from Tax Free Municipal Bonds are to be used only for capital investments in urban infrastructure for providing one or more of the following:-
i.Potable Water Supply ii. Sewerage or Sanitation iii. Drainage iv. Solid Waste Management v. Roads, Bridges and Flyovers; and vi. Urban Transport (if this is a municipal function under respective state legislation)

records.qtitle: HVDC LINE BETWEEN INDIA AND SRI LANKA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is considering any proposal to lay an under-sea High- Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission line between India and Sri Lanka;

(b) if so, the details thereof and what are the salient features thereof;

(c) whether Government is considering such power transmission projects with other neighbouring countries also; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )

(a) to (d) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF STARRED QUESTION NO. 545 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 05.05.2008 REGARDING HVDC LINE BETWEEN INDIA AND SRI LANKA.

(a) & (b) : A feasibility study is being proposed for establishing a High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission system of 1000 MW capacity using overhead and submarine cables between India and Sri Lanka. The system will have two HVDC terminal stations at both sides of the link. According to preliminary estimates, the length of the HVDC line may be approximately 350-400 kms. This would consist of about 200-250 kms overhead HVDC line in India and between 30 to 50 kms undersea cables and finally about 125-150 kms of overhead line in Sri Lanka. The study would facilitate estimation of capital cost based on route survey and would also examine the techno-economic feasibility of the interconnection.

(c) & (d) : India is already having cross-border AC transmission links with Bhutan and Nepal. Further interconnection with Bhutan is proposed with Punatsangchu-I HEP in Bhutan. Existing transmission lines between India and Nepal are at 132 kV and below and are operated in radial mode. A 400 kV D/C transmission line between Muzaffarpur (India) and Dhalkebar (Nepal) interconnection through a joint venture of ILFS, Nepal Electricity Authority, PTC India Limited and Powergrid is also under consideration.

records.qtitle: DEVELOPMENT OF BIO GAS PLANTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government to promote bio-gas plants in the country ;

(b) whether Government has set any target for bio-gas plants during the next five years; (

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) whether there is any scheme for community-based bio-gas plants in the urban and rural areas and if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY

(SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR)

(a),(b)&(c): The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy is implementing National Biogas and Manure Management Programme for the promotion of biogas plants in the country. For the 11th Five Year Plan (2007-12), a physical target for the installation of an aggregated capacity of two million cubic meter biogas plants has been proposed.

(d): Presently, there is no scheme for installation of community-based biogas plants in the urban and rural areas of the country.

records.qtitle: ENERGY FUEL PRODUCTION THROUGH PLASTIC WASTE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is aware that there is a successful commercial energy/fuel production through plastic waste in Nagpur, and such projects are proposed to be set up in other major cities of the country;

(b) if so, the details thereof and Government’s response thereto;

(c) whether Government proposes to produce such environment-friendly energy production project in the country; and

(d) if so, the details of steps taken, so far, by Government in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY

(SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR)

(a)&(b): Yes, Sir. A 5 tonnes per day capacity plant for producing fuel from plastic waste has been set up at Nagpur. The plant is based on a process invented by a private company in Nagpur for conversion of waste plastic into liquid hydrocarbon fuel. Municipal Corporations in Maharashtra were informed by Maharashtra Energy Development Agency about this project. A few other private companies have also indicated interest for taking up such projects in other cities in the country.

(c)&(d): There is no such proposal.

records.qtitle: SCHEMES FOR HIGHER SECONDARY EDUCATION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of the Centrally sponsored schemes for higher secondary education being implemented through the State Governments; and

(b) the details of proposals sanctioned during the last three years, particularly for Maharashtra? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M.A.A. FATMI)

(a) & (b) At present the following centrally sponsored schemes are being implemented through State Governments at the higher secondary stage.

i) “ICT in schools” for providing assistance to State Governments for computer education and computer aided education in secondary and higher secondary schools.
ii) Integrated Education for Disabled Children (IEDC) for assisting State Governments and NGOs in mainstreaming the disabled children in schools.

Details of financial assistance extended to the State/UT Governments, including the Government of Maharashtra, under the above schemes during the last three years are annexed.

records.qtitle: E LEARNING PROGRAMME IN HIGHER EDUCATION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is considering any proposal of e- learning programme in higher education, with the help of Information and Communication TechnologiesBSNL;

(b) if so, the details of the proposals and programmes likely to be taken up and taught to the common man; and

(c) by when this e-learning programme would be started throughout the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SMT. D. PURANDESWARI)

(a) to (c): The Government is considering to launch National Mission in Education through Information and Communication Technology (ICT). The proposal is for making use of ICT in teaching and learning process in higher education sector as also to provide connectivity to the institutions of higher education in collaboration with Department of Telecommunications among others.

records.qtitle: UNCLAIMED DEPOSITS IN EPFO .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the amount of unclaimed deposits that has accumulated so far in the Employees Provident Fund Organization (EPFO);

(b) the number of such cases, State-wise;

(c) the reasons attributed to such accumulation;

(d) whether efforts are being made to trace out the bonafide subscribers; and

(e) if so, the details of the bonafide subscriber with respective amount?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT

(SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES)

(a): The amount lying in the Inoperative Account (earlier known as Unclaimed Deposit Account) as on 31.03.2007 was Rs.1,624.69 crore.

(b): The details of inoperative accounts as on 31.03.2007 in respect of 21 regions is given at Annexure.

(c): Accumulations in the inoperative account can be attributed to the following factors:

(i) EPF deposits earn better yield and is also exempt from Income Tax.

(ii) Deposits are relatively safe and also free from attachment by any authority/courts.

(iii) Subscribers sometimes have multiple accounts as they do not transfer their accounts upon change in employment.

(iv) It is not mandatory for members to withdraw money even after superannuation.

(d): Regular efforts are made by the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation to trace out the beneficiaries through advertisements in newspapers, interaction with trade unions/employer, etc.

(e): The desired information is not maintained separately.

records.qtitle: FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO SIMI BY FOREIGN AGENCIES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) how many activists of Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) were arrested by special task forces of Madhya Pradesh Government in March, 2008;

(b) whether his Ministry is having information that some foreign agencies are helping SIMI organization financially to the tune of Rs. 90 crores every year;

(c) if so, the names of foreign agencies with total amount spent by them on these terrorists and anti-national outfits; and

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a): 20 (twenty) activists of Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) have been arrested.

(b) & (c): SIMI has been raising funds in a clandestine manner from well-wishers and sympathizers in foreign countries.

(d): The activities of SIMI are under constant watch of law enforcement agencies.

records.qtitle: PROTECTION OF HISTORICAL MONUMENTS IN MAHARASHTRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has received any proposals from the State Government of Maharashtra for financial assistance for the protection of historical monuments there;

(b) if so, the details thereof indicating the location-wise details of each project; and

(c) what is the status of these proposals and the funds allocated for these monuments during last two years?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF TOURISM AND CULTURE

(SMT. AMBIKA SONI)

(a) to (c) A statement is laid on the table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (a) TO (c) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.514 FOR 29.04.2008 REGARDING PROTECTION OF HISTORICAL MONUMENTS IN MAHARASHTRA

(a) to (c) Archaeological Survey of India has no scheme for grant of financial assistance to State Governments for protection of historical monuments and has not received any such proposal from the Government of Maharashtra.

There is a Scheme for financial assistance for preservation of monuments less than 100 years old. Only registered Societies/public trusts are eligible for the assistance. State Governments/Union Territories/local authorities are not entitled for assistance under this scheme.

records.qtitle: GAS FROM PANNA MUKTA TAPTI FIELDS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Power Ministry has demanded for nearly half the quantity of gas from Panna-Mukta-Tapti fields for producing more power to meet countrywide power shortage;

(b) if so, what is Government’s reaction thereto; and

(c) what are the barriers for accepting power Ministry’s legitimate demand?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS

(SHRI DINSHA PATEL)

(a) to (c): The demand for natural gas in the country is more than the availability. However, priority is being given to supply of natural gas to power plants, including from PMT fields. The power plants located along Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur/ex-Hazira (HVJ/ex-Hazira) are being supplied a total quantity of 2.25 million standard cubic meters per day (mmscmd) natural gas from PMT fields at Administered Price Mechanism (APM) price. Further, 1.5 mmscmd is being supplied to Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Utpadan Nigam Limited (RRVUNL). 0.90 mmscmd would be supplied to Torrent Power Limited. So total supply to power sector from PMT fields would be 4.65 mmscmd.

records.qtitle: SHORTAGE OF LPG .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is aware of LPG shortage in various parts of the country during the last six months;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor, by indicating by when the problem of LPG shortage will put to an end;

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government for fulfilment of LPG demand in the country;

(d) whether there is any proposal to hike LPG prices on demand of second cylinder within a month time limit; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS

(SHRI DINSHA PATEL)

(a) to (c): Public Sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have reported that at present, there is no overall shortage of LPG in the country and LPG supplies to distributors are being made by the OMCs through indigenous production and imports in accordance with the genuine demand of customers registered with the LPG distributors. OMCs have further reported that they have supplied 9394 Thousand Metric Tonnes (TMTs) of domestic LPG in the country during the year April, 2007- February, 2008 as against 8863 TMTs during the corresponding period of 2006-07.

However, OMCs had reported backlog in LPG supplies in certain States in the country due to a combination of factors viz., reduction in supply of bulk LPG compared to the target by Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) & Essar Oil Limited in January-February, 2008, delay in movement of bulk LPG by rail from Jamnagar to the Northern Region, increased demand in the States due to severe cold which resulted in panic booking by the customers, strikes by contract labour, agitational activities, delays in berthing of vessels at Haldia Port due to reduced draft, bandhs etc.

Government had advised OMCs to liquidate the backlog in the country by operating the bottling plants on holidays and during extended hours. Increased bottling is also done during the working days for early clearance of backlog.

At present, OMCs have not reported any backlog in supply of LPG in the country. OMCs are monitoring the situation on a day to day basis and corrective action is being taken whenever required.

(d): No, Sir.

(e): Does not arise in view of (d) above.

records.qtitle: SINGLE WINDOW CLEARANCE SYSTEM FOR AIRPORTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a)whether it has been decided to allow airports within 150 kilometer if the existing ones in future under the single window clearance policy, while seeking potential to have more than 500 airports in the country;

(b)if so, what are the salient features of the Single Window clearance policy; and

(c)the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken on single Window Clearing System policy so far by the Government?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )

(a),(b) & (c): Government has approved a new policy for greenfield airport which allows for setting up of a new airport within 150 Km of an existing airport on a case to case basis. The new policy would streamline the process for setting up of new airports. Its salient features are:
(i) Terms and conditions of all the concerned agencies like DGCA, Security, Defence etc. would be prescribed up-front.
(ii) DGCA can clear a proposal if it meets all the prescribed terms and conditions.
(iii) If the proposal is to set up a new airport within an aerial distance of 150 kms from an existing airport, it would be considered by a Steering Committee of the Ministry of Civil Aviation on whose advice, the Ministry can clear it.
(iv) In case the proposal seeks any exemption from any of the prescribed conditions, it would require approval of the Union Cabinet.
(v) All reserved activities to be performed at the airport by central agencies like immigration, customs etc. would be on cost recovery basis.

records.qtitle: AIR TRAFFIC JAM AT MUMBAI AIRPORT .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Mumbai Airport is suffering from air-traffic jam during the take-off and landing of domestic and international flights everyday;

(b) if so, how many domestic and international flights take-off and land every day at Mumbai Airport, also indicating average delay due to traffic jam;

(c) the number of runways available at Mumbai Airport and how many of them are in actual working condition; and

(d) the steps taken/being taken to get rid of air traffic jam at Mumbai Airport?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )

(a) & (b) Approximately 750 flights take off and land daily at Mumbai airport. Sometimes when there is bunching of traffic, congestion occurs leading to delays of about 15 minutes to 30 minutes. (c) Two runways which are crossing each other at mid point are avilable at Mumbai airport and both are being used. (d) Important measures taken for air traffic management at Mumbai airport are: construction of a new exit taxi-way, straightening of taxi-way D, simultaneous use of both the runways during peak hours,joining of runways `32` and `27` through a new taxi-track to reduce runway occupancy time, introduction of improved ATC procedures, ban on general aviation during peak hours, scientific allocation of schedules in order to avoid of bunching of aircrafts, etc.

records.qtitle: MDR TB PATIENTS IN THE COUNTRY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a facat that daily 4400 TB patients die and number of MDR-TB patients is increasing in the country;

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto;

(c) whether it is also a fact that around 20 per cent of TB patients, who are presently having TB, are actually availing re-treatment after having failed to comply with treatment regiments earlier; and

(d) if so, the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government to tackle this deadly disease?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE

(DR. ANBUMANI RAMADOSS)



(a)to(d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.


STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 470 FOR 25TH APRIL, 2008.
……


As per the latest estimates the number of deaths attributable to TB daily is ~900. Revised National TB Control Programme (RNTCP), by implementation of internationally recommended DOTS strategy and consistent efforts, has been able to bring down the number of deaths from ~1400 per day in the pre-RNTCP days to the current level. WHO global report 2008 estimates a decline in the deaths due to TB from 42/lakh population per year in 1990 to 28/lakh population per year in 2006.


Drug resistance surveillance studies undertaken in the past by premier institutes like Tuberculosis Research Centre (TRC), Chennai and National Tuberculosis Institute (NTI), Bangalore and the State level studies undertaken in Gujarat and Maharashtra recently have shown that the prevalence of multi-drug resistant TB has not increased over the past several years and is estimated to be ~3% in new cases and 12-17% in re-treatment cases. The ongoing drug resistance surveillance undertaken by TRC in its study area, from 1999 to 2004, has actually shown a decrease in the prevalence of MDR-TB.


About 18% of all patients registered for treatment under RNTCP are re-treatment cases. However, large numbers of re-treatment cases are those who have taken non-standardized/inadequate/irregular treatment outside the programme in the past.


The Revised National TB Control Programme (RNTCP), which is based on WHO recommended DOTS strategy, is being implemented in the entire country. Under the programme, diagnosis and treatment facilities including the supply of anti TB drugs are provided free of cost to all TB patients. For quality diagnosis, more than 12000 microscopy centres have been established in the country. Treatment centres (DOT centres) have been established near to residence of patients to the extent possible. All government hospitals, Community Health Centres (CHC), Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Sub-centres are DOT Centres, in addition, NGOs, Private Practitioners (PPs) involved under the RNTCP, Community Volunteers, Anganwadi workers, Women Self Groups etc. also function as DOT Providers/DOT Centres. Drugs are provided under direct observation and the patients are monitored so that they complete their treatment.


To increase accessibility to the facilities provided under the Programme, special emphasis is laid on the IEC activities, involvement of NGOs, private sector and medical colleges under the programme.


The programme is in the process of establishing a network of accredited Culture and Drug Susceptibility testing Intermediate Reference Laboratories (IRL) across the country, at least one in each state, in a phased manner for diagnosis and follow up of MDR TB patients. The IRL at Gujarat and Maharashtra have been accredited recently. Another 10 IRLs are under the accreditation process and are expected to be accredited in 2008. The remaining IRLs will be established and accredited by 2009-10.


The diagnosed MDR cases will be treated as per the DOTS Plus guidelines developed by the programme, in line with the international recommendations. The treatment will be provided at the DOTS Plus sites at least one in each state, with qualified staff to manage the patients, and have a system to deliver ambulatory DOT after an initial short period of in-patient care. The DOTS plus services have been rolled out in the states of Gujarat and Maharashtra in 2007. Remaining states will be covered under DOTS Plus by 2009-10.

records.qtitle: AUTISM CASES IN THE COUNTRY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that around 4 million people have been suffering from Autism in the country and cases of such people are increasing day by day;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken to provide proper treatment and facilities to the suffering children in the country; and

(d) the details of names and number of organizations working for the autism suffered children in the country?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) to (c) :Data on the Persons with Autism in the country is not maintained. The National Trust Act, 1999 is particularly meant for the welfare of persons with Autism and other developmental disabilities. Under the Act, a host of activities are undertaken like caregivers courses, training and public awareness programmes etc. There is no definite treatment for Autism. However, early diagnosis and intervention leads to limitation of disability. Pediatric & Psychiatry departments of Government hospitals provide such services. Government of India is providing support for upgradation of Psychiatry Wings of Govt. Medical Colleges/General Hospitals and modernization State-run Mental Health Institutes under the National Mental Health Programme (NMHP). District Mental Health Programme under NMHP also provides for proper intervention of mental disorders including Autism.

(d) A list of organizations working with support of National Trust in the area of developmental disabilities including Autism is Annexed.

records.qtitle: NEED TO REVOKE THE BAN ON LAKHODI DAL .
records.name: Sanjay Raut

(a) whether the Government of Maharashtra has requested for revoking the ban on lakhodi dal by codnucting proper tests on the effects of consumption of lakhodi dal (Lathyrus sativus) through Hyderabad- based National Institute for Nutrition (NIN);

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto indicating by when the reports from NIN is expected;

(c) whether it is a fact that there are large quantity cultivation and consumption of lakhodi dal is happening in various parts of the country;

(d) if so, the details thereof;

(e) whether it is also a fact that there will be no need of import of pulses if ban is revoked and allowed to bulk cultivation, particularly in Maharashtra; and

(f) if so, Government`s response thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)


(a) & (b): A request has been received in the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India from the Government of Maharashtra for lifting ban on the sale of Khesari Dal (Lathyrus sativus) imposed under Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. National Institute of Nutrition, Hyderabad has submitted a proposal for conducting a study using goats as animal model for approval of the Committee for the Purpose of Control and Supervision on Experiments on Animals (CPCSEA). The study would commence after the receipt of the approval of CPCSEA and may take about 2 years time to complete. However, initial data from the study would be available after 6 months.

(c) & (d): Lakhodi dal is cultivated and consumed in various parts of the country. The area under lakhodi dal (Lathyrus sativus) in the country during 2003-04, 2004-05 and 2005-06 has been as under:- 
		Year		        Area
			              (in Lakh ha)
		2003-04	         7.09
		2004-05	         6.41
		2005-06	         6.26


(e) & (f): The production of lakhodi dal in the country particularly in Maharashtra may not be sufficient to bridge the gap between the demand and domestic production of pulses as the current production of lakhodi dal is far less than the total import of pulses. Further, the import of pulses in the country is mainly of tur, lentil, gram and urd.

records.qtitle: PAYMENT OF TOLL ON NHS BY STATE ROADWAYS BUSES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that State roadways buses have been made to pay expressway toll, which are being used mostly by the poor; and

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

(SHRI T.R. BAALU)

(a) & (b) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.


STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) & (b) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.458 FOR ANSWER ON 24.4.2008 ASKED BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT REGARDING PAYMENT OF TOLL ON NHS BY STATE ROADWAYS BUSES.

records.qtitle: SHORTAGE OF HOUSES NO.
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a shortage of more than 25 million housing units in urban cities and over 95 per cent housing shortage is related to the economically weaker sections of the country;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government is considering to bring any comprehensive scheme with the consultation of Planning Commission for housing to the urban poor in the country;

(d) if so, the details of such housing scheme; and

(e) the target fixed under the scheme and by when it would be started?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING & URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION

( KUMARI SELJA )

(a)&(b): According to the estimation of a Technical Group constituted by this Ministry for assessment of the urban housing shortage at the end of the Tenth Five Year Plan, the total housing shortage in the country is 24.71 million dwelling units. Out of this, the shortage in respect of Economically Weaker Section (EWS) accounts for 21.78 million dwelling units.

(c)to(e): A provision of Rs.95 crores has been made for an Interest Subsidy Scheme for housing the urban poor in the current financial year 2008-09. The scheme envisages to provide interest rate subsidy for loans taken by beneficiaries from the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and Low Income Group (LIG) from public lending institutions and it is expected to cover 4 lakh beneficiaries during the remaining period of the Eleventh Five Year Plan (2007-2012).

records.qtitle: CRITERIA FOR FORMING OF SHGS UNDER SGSY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the criteria being followed while forming of Self-Help-Groups (SHGs) under Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY); and

(b) how many Self Help Groups are currently under the SGSY working, particularly in Maharashtra and the details of works undertaken by such SHGs?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRIMATI SURYAKANTA PATIL)

(a): The objective of the Swarnjayanti Gram Swarojgar Yojana (SGSY) is to bring the assisted families above the poverty line by ensuring appreciable increase in incomes over a period of time. The criteria being followed while forming the Self-Help Groups are as below:

1. A self help group may consist of 10 to 20 persons. However, in difficult areas like desserts, hills and areas with scattered and sparse population and in case of minor irrigation and disabled persons, this number may be from 5-20.

2. Generally all members of the group should belong to families below the poverty line. However, if necessary, a maximum of 20% and in exceptional cases, where essentially required, upto a maximum of 30% of the members in a group may be taken from families marginally above the poverty line living contiguously with BPL families and if they are acceptable to the BPL members of the group.

3. The group should actively participate in the management and decision-making, such as devising a code of conduct, holding regular meetings, building up a corpus through regular savings, evolving financial management norms, interest rates and procedures for sanctioning of the loans etc.

4. The members in the group meetings should take all the loaning decisions through a participatory decision making process.

5. The group should operate a group account preferably in their service area bank branch. 6. The group should maintain simple basic records such as Minutes book, Attendance register, Loan ledger, General ledger, Cash book, Bank passbook and individual passbooks.

(b): In the State of Maharashtra, under SGSY, since inception of the scheme from

1.4.1999, 1,71,368 Self-Help Groups have been formed, out of which 1,05,875 SHGs have passed Grade-I , 55, 001 SHGs have passed Grade-II and 38,198 SHGs have taken up economic activities. During 2007-08 (upto February, 2008) the corresponding figures are: 26, 246 SHGs formed, 18, 700 SHGs passed Grade – I, 10,112 SHGs passed Grade – II and 6, 807 SHGs taken up economic activities. The Sector – wise details of 6,807 SHGs that have taken up economic activities in the year 2007-08 (upto February, 2008) are as follows: 


Sector	        Activities 	               					Total

records.qtitle: VOCATIONAL AND PRODUCTIVITY TRAINING TO RESCUED CHILD LABOURERS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of the steps taken by Government for providing vocational and productivity training to the rescued child labourers during the last three years; and

(b) the number of child labourers benefited during this period, particularly in Maharashtra State?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT

(SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES)

(a): Government is implementing the National Child Labour Projects (NCLP) Scheme in 250 districts of 20 States of the country. Under the Scheme, children working in identified hazardous occupations and processes are withdrawn from work and put in Special Schools where they are provided with vocational training, accelerated bridging education, nutrition, stipend and healthcare facilities etc. In addition, another project, namely INDUS Child Labour Project is being implemented in collaboration with the US Department of Labour since 2004 in 21 Districts of the country. Under the project, vocational training is also being provided to the adolescents in the age group of 14-17 years.

(b): Under the NCLP and INDUS Schemes, 7,214 and 1,914 children have been mainstreamed into regular system respectively in Maharashtra State. These children have been provided with vocational training under the Schemes. In addition, 17,118 adolescents in the age group of 14-17 years have been provided vocational training under INDUS Project in the State.

records.qtitle: SURVEY TO ASSESS THE REASONS OF UNEMPLOYMENT
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of educated and uneducated rural and urban persons registered with employment exchanges in the country during 2007-08, State-wise ;

(b) whether Government has made any study/survey to assess the reasons of unemployment in the country;

(c) if so, the details thereof and the steps taken by Government to create additional avenues/opportunities for employment; and

(d) the number of rural and urban unemployed persons targeted to be provided employment during 2008-09?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT

(SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES)

(a) State-wise number of educated and uneducated job seekers and also number of rural and urban job seekers registered with employment exchanges as on 31.12.2005 is given in Annex-I.



(b) National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO), Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation, conducts quinquennial labour force surveys to assess employment and unemployment situation in the country. The surveys also ascertain reasons for becoming unemployed for those only who were employed in the past. Apart from the quinquennial surveys on employment and unemployment, NSSO also conducts an all India survey on employment and unemployment from a limited set of households as a part of the annual series of rounds.

(c) Details of reasons for becoming unemployed for those who had worked in the past as revealed by 61st round of NSSO during 2004-05 are given in Annex. II. The Government has been implementing various employment generation schemes such as Prime Minister’s Rozgar Yojana (PMRY); Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY); Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY); Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY); Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP) and National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 (NREGA) etc. for generating gainful employment opportunities in the country.

(d) The 11th Plan document approved by National Development Council has projected that 58 million job opportunities are likely to be created during the 11th Plan period at an average rate of 11.6 million job opportunities per annum.

records.qtitle: REQUEST OF USA TO CHANGE M A REGULATION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that USA has requested for changing the new regulations on governing Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) under the amended Competition Act, including those taking place outside the country;

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto; and

(c) the reasons behind such opposition towards Competition Act, particularly M&A rules?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY

(SHRI ASHWANI KUMAR)

(a): The Ministry of Corporate Affairs is the nodal Ministry for the Competition Act, 2002. No request from USA Government has been received by Ministry of Corporate Affairs for changing any regulations governing mergers and acquisitions under the amended Competition Act, 2002.

(b) & (c): Does not arise.

records.qtitle: MOBILE BANKING SYSTEM .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government ho, s received any proposal to operate mobile phone banking system, in which customers avail of deposit and withdrawal facility as well as transfer money to other account through mobile telephone without the customer ever having to visit the bank-branch or ATM;

(b) if so, the details thereof and the salient features thereof, indicating how many banks have got nod for using such mobile phone banking system in the country by Reserve Bank of India (RBI)

(c) what are the pros and cons towards such customer friendly system?
records.ans_text:
Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) & (b): Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has informed that they have received a few proposals from banks to provide mobile phone based payment / money transfer services to their existing account holders/credit card customers. Most of these services involve making payments at select merchant outlets, remittance of money to bank customers of the same bank. These proposals do not involve direct deposit or withdrawal of currency from any location other than a bran branch. RBI is in the process of framing regulatory guidelines for mobile payments, The experiments being conducted by a few banks are limited both in terms of customers anti the type of payment transactions.


(c): Mobile phone based payment systems provide an alternate, cheap and efficient mode of payment system to the public. They facilitate micro payments as well and would help in bringing about financial inclusion.

records.qtitle: CORRECT VALUATION OF IPOS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that most of Initial Public Offerings (IPOs) since last two years are quoting below the offer price and some of the IPOs are trading below 40 to 60 per cent in the market presently and retail/small investors in-particular have been badly hit;

(b) if so, the response of Government thereto; and

(c) what steps Securities and exchange Board of India (SEBI) would take in future to arrive at correct valuation of the companies to prevent such situation of IPOs so that small investor’s money could not be affected badly?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a)As informed by SEBI, the details of IPOs listed during the period April 1, 2006 to March 31, 2008 are as follows: 
							NSE	BSE 

(i)No. of IPOs listed					150	162


(ii) No. of IPOs trading at a discount 			86	88
	(as on April 11, 2008).	 

(iii) Of 
(ii), number of IPOs trading at a discount	36	38
of more than 40% to issue price 

(as on April 11, 2008).


(b) & (c): The authorities do not try to manage or control prices. They endeavour to build systems and practices to deepen and broaden markets which can withstand volatility. The Government has put in place systems and practices to promote a safe, transparent and efficient market and to protect market integrity. The systems instituted include advanced risk management mechanisms comprising on-line monitoring and surveillance, various limits on positions, margin requirements, circuit filters, etc. Measures taken to broaden and deepen markets include: screen based trading system, dematerialization of securities, corporatization and demutualization of exchanges, settlement through clearing corporation, trading in derivatives, etc.

Under the current regulatory regime, the price is discovered by the market through book building mechanism, while the authorities endeavour to make all relevant information available to market participants including issuers and investors for making informed investment decisions.

records.qtitle: FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO MAHARASHTRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of financial assistance provided to Maharashtra by the Central Government during the last three years;

(b) whether the Central Government has received any request from the State Government of Maharashtra for more financial assistance to fund its developmental projects

(c) if so, the details there of ; and

(d) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by the Central Government for providing financial assistance to Maharashtra ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL

(a): A statement containing details of Central Assistance (plan and non-plan) released by Ministry of Finance to the state of Maharashtra during the last three years is placed at Annexure.

(b) to (d): Ministry of Finance has not received any request from the State Government of Maharashtra for more financial assistance to fund its developmental projects for 2008-09.
Planning Commission also has not received any fresh proposal from the State of Maharashtra for consideration with respect to financial assistance under annual plan 2008-09. However, during Deputy Chairman, Planning Commission and Chief Minister, Maharashtra level discussions for finalizing the Annual Plan of the State for 2007-08, Central Assistance to the tune of Rs.110 crates for development of infrastructure for Commonwealth Youth Games in Pune was agreed to. Subsequently, Additional Central Assistance of Rs.150 crores was released to Maharashtra in 2007-08 taking into account the cost escalation of creating the necessary infrastructure.

records.qtitle: POWER SHORTAGE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that domestic industrial production would be hampered by upto thirty-five per cent in the coming months due to power shortage;

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto; and

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government for generation of more power in the country, to fulfil the industry`s demand?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE, MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER

( SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH )

(a) to (c): There is a continuing shortage of power in the country. The quantum of shortage varies from State to State, on day to day and hour to hour depending on demand and supply of power. The energy and peak shortage in the country during the year 2007-08 was 9.8% and 16.6% respectively.

There is no representation from the domestic industries about the impact of power shortage or its impact degree in terms on the domestic production in the coming months. Electricity being a concurrent subject under the Constitution, the supply and distribution of electricity to different areas and different categories of consumers in a State is within the purview of the concerned State Government/State Power Utilities. The Government of India supplements the efforts of the State Government(s) by establishing power generation plants in the Central Sector through Central Public Sector Undertakings.

The steps taken/being taken to improve the power supply position in the country include augmentation of generating capacity by over 78,500 MW during the 11th Plan, development of Ultra Mega Power Projects of 4,000 MW capacity each, improving performance of existing power stations, renovation, modernization and life extension of old and inefficient generating units, harnessing surplus captive power into the grid, strengthening inter-state and inter-regional transmission capacity for optimum utilization of available power, promoting demand side management, energy efficiency and energy conservation measures and import of power from Bhutan.

records.qtitle: ALLOCATION OF GAS FROM PANNA MUKTA TAPTI FIELDS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Ministry has approached the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas for getting nearly half the quantity of gas from Panna-Mukta-Tapti fields for producing more power to meet countrywide power shortage;

(b) if so, the response of the latter thereto; and

(c) what are the barriers in accepting the Ministry`s legitimate demand?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE, MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER

( SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH )

(a) : Yes, Sir. Keeping in view the prevailing shortage of gas at NTPC power plants, Ministry of Power has requested Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas to advise Gas Authority of India Ltd. (GAIL) to allocate 7 Million Standard Cubic Meter per day (MMSCMD) of gas from Panna-Mukta-Tapti (PMT) field to NTPC Ltd.

(b) & (c) : Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas has intimated that the demand of natural gas in the country is more than the availability. However, priority is being given to supply of natural gas to power plants, including from PMT fields. The power plants located along Hazira- Bijapur-Jagdishpur (HBJ)/ex-Hazira are being supplied a total quantity of 2.25 MMSCMD natural gas from PMT fields at Administered Pricing Mechanism (APM) price. Further, 1.5 MMSCMD is being supplied to Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Utpadan Nigam Limited (RRVUNL). 0.90 MMSCMD would be supplied to Torrent Power Limited. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has informed that the total supply to power sector from PMT fields would be 4.65 MMSCMD.

records.qtitle: ONLINE CAT EXAMINATION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether there is any move to permit online CAT examinations similar to US examinations like GMAT and GRE, etc., which may help in handling the huge number of students appearing for the test every year;

(b) if so, what would be the modus operandi of the scheme with regard to ensuring the transparency; and

(c) whether Government proposes to extend this scheme to all other all India basis exams like Staff Selection Board exams, Railway Recruitment Board exams, etc.?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SMT. D. PURANDESWARI)


(a) & (b): Yes Sir. The Committee of Chairpersons of the Admissions Committees of the Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs) – CAT Group had recommended to the Institute to explore the possibility of conducting CAT on-lines of GMAT/GRE, etc. The information is being collected and will be laid on the Table of the House.

(c): At present, Staff Selection Commission (SSC) has no such scheme. In so far as Railway Recruitment Board (RRB) exams are concerned, they have already introduced On-line examinations where number of candidates is small/limited.

records.qtitle: FOREST COVER AREA IN INDIA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the “Open Forest” is increasing and “dense forest cover” has been decreasing in the country, particularly in Maharashtra;

(b) if so, details of statistics of past ten years about open forest cover and dense forest cover in the country, State-wise; and

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken to increase the dense forest cover percentage in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI S.REGUPATHY)


(a) No, Sir. As per remote sensing based biennial assessments made by Forest Survey of India presented in tables given in Annexure 1 & 2, the open forest and dense forest cover for the country have remained between 7.95% to 8.82% and 11.32% to 11.78% respectively of total geographic area, between 1997 and 2005.
In Maharashtra the forest cover in open forest and dense forest categories has remained between 7.28% to 6.2% and 7.72% to 9.22% respectively of total geographic area, between 1997and 2005.

(b) The requisite statistics have been given in Annexure 1 & 2.

(c) The Government of India is implementing National Afforestation Programme, Integrated Forest Protection Scheme, Assistance for Development of National Parks and Sanctuaries for afforestation, regeneration and protection of forests for improving the quality of forest and increasing its density.

records.qtitle: FOREIGN COMPANIES BUYING LAND NO.
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is aware that a large number of foreign companies are buying land through builders at various parts of the country, particularly around metropolitan cities and border areas;

(b) if so, the details thereof and Government`s response thereto;

(c) whether Government has taken any cautious approach towards land grabbing by foreign companies, particularly some important and sensitive areas of border;

(d) whether it is also a fact that huge lands have been purchased unlawfully by some companies in Badmer and Jaisalmer districts of Rajasthan; and

(e) if so, Government`s views and reaction thereto?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )


(a): No, Sir. Government of India in this Ministry is not aware of any such specific instances since Land is a State Subject.

(b)to(e): Question does not arise in view of (a) above.

records.qtitle: LAND GRABBING BY FOREIGN COMPANIES IN BORDER AREAS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is aware that a large number of foreign companies are buying land through builder at various parts of the country, particularly around metropolitan cities and border areas;

(b) if so, the details thereof and Government`s response thereto;

(c) whether Government has taken any cautious approach towards land grabbing by foreign companies, particularly some important and sensitive areas of border;

(d) whether it is also a fact that huge land have been purchased unlawfully by some companies in Barmer and Jaisalmer districts of Rajasthan; and

(e) if so, Government`s views and reaction thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a) to (c): Relevant information are being collected from various States/UTs etc.

(d) & (e): Government is aware that large scale land transactions have taken place in the border areas of Rajasthan. The Rajasthan Government has initiated a detailed inquiry into these transactions with the intention of identifying the purchasers and ascertaining the motives behind such transactions. A definitive conclusion/analysis would be possible only after completion of the detailed enquiry being undertaken by the Government of Rajasthan with the support of the Central Government agencies. A high level review on the subject matter has also been taken in the Ministry of Home Affairs and the issue is being closely monitored in coordination with the State Government from time to time.

records.qtitle: PACKAGE FOR INDUSTRIES IN MAHARASHTRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has identified the industries where the growth rate is on decline;

(b) if so, what measure are being taken to improve the situation; and

(c) is the Central Government devising any package for the benefit of States like Maharashtra where the industries are suffering due to several problems?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI ASWANI KUMAR)

(a): Yes Sir. The Government has identified some group of industries where the growth rate is on decline as per Annexure enclosed.

(b): The Government has put in place various policies to promote broad based industrial growth, which includes, inter-alia, delicensing of industrial capacity, liberalization of foreign trade regime to provide better access to inputs at competitive prices, rationalization and reduction of duty rates of customs and central excise, better infrastructure support, and liberal FDI regime, etc. In the Budget 2008-09, the Government has also reduced the excise duty across the board from 16% to 14%, reduction of excise duty from 16% to 12% for Small Cars, Motorcycles and Three Wheelers, reduction of excise duty on Buses and their Chasis, reduction of customs duty on certain raw materials for Tyres, Sports goods, Fertilizers, etc. to boost the domestic demand for the manufacturing industry. In addition, Government has also announced several measures to assist and promote for export oriented industries affected by the rupee appreciation, which includes enhancement of the Duty Entitlement Pass Book (DEPB); reduction in Export Credit Guarantee Corporation (ECGC) premium by 10%; enhancement of the rates of duty drawback; interest subvention of pre-shipment and post-shipment credit, refund of service tax; raising the revenue ceiling for Vishesh Krishi and Gram Udyog Yojana etc.

(c) : The Government had announced a New Industrial Policy and other concessions for the North-Eastern States, Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, since these States are hilly, geographically isolated, remote to large markets and have poor infrastructure & poor resource base. Under this policy package, various concessions have been allowed to industrial units in the State which include excise and income tax exemption and subsidies under various Schemes like Central Capital Investment Subsidy Scheme, Central Interest Subsidy Scheme and Central Comprehensive Insurance Scheme. As the State of Maharashtra do not face such geographical adversities, there is no proposal at the moment to extend any incentives for industries in Maharashtra.
