records.qtitle: RAILWAY CROSSING .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of manned and unmanned railway crossings in the country, separately, State-wise and zone-wise;

(b) the number of railway accidents that have occurred during the last three years at such level crossing; (

(c) whether many of these accidents have occurred due to the unmanned level crossings;

(d) if so, the steps being taken to prevent the recurrence of such accidents and to convert unmanned level crossings to manned level crossings;

(e) whether it is proposed to entrust the unmanned level crossings to private sector; and

(f) if so, the details thereof alongwith terms and references thereon?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R.VELU)

(a) As on 01.04.2007, there were 16,778 manned and 17,966 unmanned level crossings (Excluding `D` Class cattle crossings and canal crossings) in the country. State-wise and Zone-wise number is given in appendix..

(b) The number of railway accidents that have occurred at level crossings during the last three years is as under: 
YEAR			NUMBER OF ACCIDENTS
		MANNED		UNMANNED


2004-05		05		65
2005-06		10		65
2006-07		07		72


(c ) & (d) No, Sir. Accidents take place at unmanned level crossings due to failure of road users in terms of the provisions of Motor Vehicle Act, 1931. However, in order to prevent unmanned level crossing accidents, public awareness programmes and publicity campaigns are undertaken regularly for educating road users for observing safe practices while negotiating unmanned level crossings. Joint ambush checks with the involvement of civil authorities are also conducted. Level crossings, on reaching the laid down traffic volume criteria of manning, are also progressively manned. As a special measure to reduce the number of level crossings, Zonal Railways have been given power to consider and sanction ‘Limited Use Subways’ wherever technically feasible. Efforts are also being made to close down as many of unmanned level crossings as possible, suggesting their merger with another level crossing in the close vicinity.

(f) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: FUNDS FOR URBAN INFRASTRUCTURE
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the country needs more than Rs.1,20,000 crores of investment in urban infrastructure over the next seven year?

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto;

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for providing adequate funds towards urban infrastructure development;

(d) whether Government`s attention has been drawn towards demand for evolved municipal bonds as an option for financing urban infrastructure in the country; and

(e) if so, Government`s view and reaction thereto?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b)&(c): Government of India has launched the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) on 3rd December, 2005 to give focused attention to integrated development of urban infrastructure and services in cities with emphasis on provision of basic services to the urban poor including housing, water supply, sanitation, road network, urban transport, development of inner (Old) city areas etc. The Mission envisages central assistance of Rs.50,000 crore as reform linked Central assistance over the Mission period of seven years beginning from 2005-06.

(d)&(e): In 2000-01, the Government inserted a new clause
(vii) in Section 10(15)of the Income Tax Act, 1961, exempting interest income from bonds issued by local authorities. Funds raised from Tax Free Municipal Bonds are to be used only for capital investments in urban infrastructure for providing one or more of the following:-

i. Potable Water Supply
ii. Sewerage or Sanitation
iii. Drainage
iv. Solid Waste Management
v. Roads, Bridges and Flyovers; and
vi. Urban Transport (if this is a municipal function under respective state legislation)

records.qtitle: DIRECT FERTILIZER SUBSIDY TO FARMERS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is considering any proposal to provide direct fertilizer subsidy to farmers;

(b) if so, by when it will be implemented this in all over the country; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS

(SHRI B.K. HANDIQUE)

(a) to (c) A Group of Ministers (GOM) constituted to looked into sustainable use of fertilizers and pertinent subsidy and pricing issues has looked into various issues relating to fertilizer sector including the option of direct fertilizer subsidy to farmers. The same has not been recommended by the GOM in its final recommendations.

records.qtitle: PRICES OF MILK .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the production of milk and milk products, indicating demands and supply, State-wise during last three years;

(b) whether prices of milk has also been increased in all States with the increase in its production;

(c) if so, the average price of milk in the country at present;

(d) whether the price of milk is beyond the reach of most of the people, particularly poor and below poverty line segments;

(e) if so, Government’s response thereto and whether Government has any proposal for setting up innovative dairy projects;

(f) if so, the details thereof; and (g) the steps being taken by Government for modernization of dairy units in the country?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI TASLIMUDDIN)

(a): The production of milk and milk products at National level is by and large sufficient to meet the domestic demand. Since major quantity of milk is handled in unorganized sector, no authentic data on production of milk products in the country is available. State-wise estimates of milk production in last three years is enclosed at Annex-I.

(b)&(c): Price of milk has increased in last few years mainly due to increase in the costs of production, procurement, processing and marketing. A list of average prices of milk in various cities in the country is enclosed at Annex-II.

(d)to(f): The Government does not have any report of any difficulty faced by poor & below poverty line segments in regard to milk price. However, Government is regularly monitoring the availability of milk and milk products to ensure availability at reasonable price in the country and takes necessary action as and when situation demands. Further, the Government is implementing various dairy development schemes, including those which provide scope for innovative dairy projects to enhance milk production.

(g): The government of India supplements efforts of the State Governments to modernize dairy units in the country through the following schemes:

(i) National Project for Cattle and Buffalo Breeding.

(ii) Strengthening Infrastructure for Quality and Clean Milk Production.

(iii) Intensive Dairy Development Programme.

(iv) Assistance to Cooperatives.

(v) Dairy/Poultry Venture Capital Fund.

(vi) Rastriya Krishi Vikas Yojana.

records.qtitle: EFFECT OF STRENGTHENING OF RUPEE AGAINST DOLLAR ON THE TEXTILE SECTOR .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the textile sector is facing problems due to the strengthening of rupee more than 13 per cent against the dollar in the last year;

(b) if so, whether the Indian Textile Industry Federation has made certain suggestions to avoid the loss being suffered by the textile sector;

(c) if so, the steps taken by Government to promote the textile industry based on these suggestions; and

(d) the steps taken by Government to ensure that this sector being the second largest employment provider after agriculture does not face such problems in future?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES

(SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN)

(a) to (d): The Government is seized of the submissions of textiles export promotion councils and other associations, which attribute the decline in India`s textiles exports to the recent appreciation of the Indian rupee vis-à-vis the US dollar. The Indian textiles industry has been demanding various concessions, which include refund of State and local levies, higher rates of Duty Entitlement Pass Book (DEPB) and Duty Drawback, etc., to cope with the adverse situation. The Government has, in response, introduced certain measures to provide relief to the affected exporters. These include increase in Duty Entitlement Pass Book and Duty Drawback rates, exemption from service tax on select services, reduction in interest rates of pre-shipment and post-shipment credit, and faster clearance of arrears of terminal excise duties and Central Sales Tax.

records.qtitle: NEW LICENSING POLICY FOR OIL AND GAS EXPLORATION
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the production of oil and gas in the oil and gas reserves found in Krishna Godavari basin, Tapti Gas area and Bikaner region of Rajasthan will be started in the year 2008;

(b) if so, the total quantum of oil and gas to be made available from these areas;

(c) whether Government has prepared any new licensing policy for the exploration of oil and gas; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI MURLI DEORA)


(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.87 BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT AND SHRI DATTA MEGHE TO BE ANSWERED ON 4.3.2008 REGARDING NEW LICENSING POLICY FOR OIL AND GAS EXPLORATION

a) : In Krishna Godavari basin, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) started commercial oil and gas production in October 1998. In 2006-07, production by ONGC in onland areas of KG basin was about 602 tonnes per day of crude oil and 4 million metric standard cubic metres per day (MMSCMD) of natural gas. In June 2008, additional natural gas of 40 MMSCMD from Krishna Godavari deepwater areas is likely to be produced by Reliance Industries Limited and NIKO Resources Limited Joint Venture.

In Rajasthan, ONGC and Oil India Limited are producing natural gas at the rate of 0.75 MMSCMD from Jaisalmer Basin. In second quarter of 2009, crude oil peak production of 6 million metric tonnes per annum is likely to be produced by Cairn Energy India Pty. Ltd.

12 MMSCMD of natural gas is produced from Tapti field by British Gas Exploration Production India Limited (BGEPIL).

b) : As on 1.4.2007, in KG basin, initially in place oil and gas reserves of 970.52 million metric tonnes of oil equivalent (MMTOE) have been established. In Rajasthan, initially in place oil and gas reserves 330.36 MMTOE have been established. In Tapti field, initially in place oil and gas reserves of 114.96 MMTOE have been established.

c&d) : Government of India approved the New Exploration & Licensing Policy (NELP) in 1997 and it became effective in February, 1999 Since then licenses for exploration are being awarded only through a competitive bidding system and National Oil Companies (NOCs) are required to compete on an equal footing with Indian and foreign companies to secure Petroleum Exploration Licences (PELs). Six rounds of bids have so far been concluded under NELP, in which production sharing contracts for 162 exploration blocks have been signed. Under NELP, 56 oil and gas discoveries in 17 blocks have already been made in Cambay onland, North East Coast and Krishna-Godaveri deepwater areas, for which, development plans by the operators, viz., Cairn, RIL and Niko are in progress.

With Exploration and development efforts made under NELP, Natural Gas production in the country is likely to be doubled by end of 11th Five Year Plan from the present level of gas production of about 90 million standard cubic metres per day (MMSCMD).

Under seventh round of NELP which was launched on 13th December 2007, Government is offering 57 exploration blocks. The offered blocks include - 19 deepwater blocks, 9 shallow water blocks and 29 onland blocks. Exploration blocks in onland areas are located in the states of Assam (1), Bihar (3), Chattisgarh (1), Gujarat (11), Madhya Pradesh (2), Rajasthan (3), Tamil Nadu (2) and West Bengal (6). Out of 19 deepwater blocks, 15 exploration blocks are in western offshore areas and 3 exploration blocks are in eastern offshore areas. One deepwater exploration block is in Andaman Nicobar basin. Amongst shallow water blocks, 6 blocks are in Mumbai basin in western offshore, while 3 blocks are in KG basin in eastern offshore.

records.qtitle: MALNUTRITION IN VIDARBHA REGION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has prepared any project to save thousands of tribal and other category children of Vidarbha region in Maharashtra from malnutrition;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether it is a fact that, on many occasions, young children have even died due to malnutrition; and

(d) if so, the effective steps taken by Government to avoid recurrence of such incidents?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT

(SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY)


(a),(b),(c)&(d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (a),(b),(c)&(d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.74 FOR 03.03.2008 BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT AND SHRI DATTA MEGHE REGARDING MALNUTRITION IN VIDARBHA REGION

(a) & (b) Ministry of Women & Child Development is administering a Centrally-sponsored Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) Scheme which is implemented through State Governments. ICDS provides a package of services comprising supplementary nutrition, immunization, health check-up, referral services, pre-school non-formal education and nutrition and health education. ICDS Scheme has been expanded twice in 2005-2006 and 2006-2007, increasing the number of ICDS Projects, Anganwadi Centres (AWCs) and Mini-AWCs to 6284, 10.53 lakhs and 36829, respectively. For Maharashtra, 79 additional Projects, 22741 AWCs and 7490 Mini-AWCs have been sanctioned during the year 2005-2006 and 2006-2007. However, no area specific project has been framed for Vidarbha Region.

(c) The malnutrition is not a direct cause of death although it can increase the

(d) Malnutrition is a multifaceted problem, the determinants of which vary from food insecurity, female illiteracy, poor access to health-care, safe drinking water, sanitation and poor purchasing power. Early marriages of girls, teenage pregnancies resulting in low birth weight of the new borns, poor breastfeeding and complementary feeding practices, ignorance about nutritional needs of infants and young children and repeated infections further aggravate the situation.
The Government is seized of the problem of malnutrition and is implementing a number of schemes through out the country, which directly or indirectly improve the nutritional status of women & children. Some of these are as under:

(i) Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) Scheme (Ministry of Women & Child Development); The steps taken in the recent past to increase the effectiveness of the delivery of services under ICDS includes: Ø The scheme has been expanded twice in the year 2005-2006 and 2006-2007 during the Tenth Five Year Plan.
Ø The Government has doubled the financial norms for supplementary nutrition from Re.1 to Rs.2/- per beneficiary per day.
Ø From the year 2005-06, 50% cost of supplementary nutrition is also being shared with the States/UTs.
Ø Constant emphasis on States to: § Ensure regular supply of supplementary nutrition as per schematic norms. § Ensure effective convergence of health, nutrition, education and safe drinking water services under various programmes.

(ii) National Programme for Nutritional Support to Primary Education (Mid Day Meal Scheme) [Department of School Education & Literacy);

(iii) Nutrition Programme for Adolescent Girls in 51 districts to provide free foodgrains to undernourished adolescent girls (Ministry of Women & Child Development);

(iv) Nutrition Education and Training Programmes of Food and Nutrition Board (Ministry of Women & Child Development);

(v) Reproductive and Child Health (RCH-II) Programme under National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) including:
Ø Maternal Health by promoting institutional deliveries, improved coverage and quality of ante natal care (ANC), skilled care to pregnant women, Post-partum care at Community level. Ø Immunization. Ø Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illnesses and malnutrition. Ø Emphasis on Infant & Young Child Feeding. Ø Specific Programmes to prevent and combat micronutrient deficiencies of Vitamin A and Iron & Folic Acid through Vitamin A Supplementation for children till the age of 5 years and Iron & Folic Acid Supplementation for preschool children, pregnant and lactating women. (Ministry of Health & Family Welfare);

(vi) National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme (Ministry of Health & Family Welfare);s

(vii) Targetted Public Distribution System (Department of Food & Public Distribution).

(viii) Accelerated Rural Water Supply Programme/ Swajaldhara and Total Sanitation Campaign; National Rural Employment Guarantee Programme (Ministry of Rural Development).

records.qtitle: HYDRO AND WIND POWER GENERATION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a vast potential in hydro power resources and wind power generation in the country;

(b) if so, Government’s response to tap these natural resources in the country;

(c) whether Government is encouraging community based mini hydro projects in the country so that power generation targets are achieved, particularly in rural and tribal areas of the country; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY

(SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR)

(a): The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is responsible for the subject of small hydro up to 25 MW. As per the Central Electricity Authority (CEA), the total hydroelectric power potential in the country is assessed at about 150,000 MW equivalent to 84,000 MW at 60 per cent load factor. The potential of small hydropower projects (up to 25 MW) is estimated at 15,000 MW and that of wind power is 45,000 MW in the country.

(b): The Ministry is encouraging development of both small hydro power (SHP) and wind power in the country through various fiscal and financial incentives. So far, SHP projects of 2061 MW and wind power projects of 7940 MW (as on 31.1.2008) have been set up in the country.

(c) & (d): Yes, Sir. The Ministry is providing central financial assistance (CFA) for the setting up of small / mini hydro power projects both in public and private sector. The CFA is also given to community / individual watermill owners for development and upgradation of watermills for mechanical as well as electricity generation (3-5 KW). The CFA is to meet 75 per cent of the project cost limited to Rs. 30,000/- per water mill for mechanical application and Rs. 1.0 lakh per water mill for mechanical and electrical applications.

records.qtitle: NCERT S RECOMMENDATION ON OPTIONAL EXAMINATION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that NCERT’s revised National Curriculum Framework has recommended to make class X examination optional, together with earlier recommendations on eliminating pass/fail terminology for reducing students’ mental stress;

(b) if so, the details of recommendations made by NCF on curriculum and Government’s response thereto;

(c) whether Government is considering those suggestions to implement in the country; and

(d) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for making education practical and professional?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M.A.A. FATMI)

(a) to (c) Yes, Sir. The National Curriculum Framework

(NCF) – 2005 prepared by National Council of Educational Research & Training (NCERT) has suggested ways to reduce exam related stress, such as, no board or state level examinations at other stages of schooling, such as class V, VIII or XI, as a long – term measure, making the class X examination optional, thus permitting students continuing in the same school to take an internal school examination and elimination of the terminology of ‘pass’ / ‘fail’. The other key features of the recommendations are:

(i) Flexibility in examination time,

(ii) Flexibility in choice of subject,

(iii) Continuous and comprehensive evaluation and internal assessment,

(iv) Differential levels of the difficulty in subjects.
However, NCERT has only an advisory role in the matter. It is upto the School Education Boards to adopt the recommendations.
Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has taken up following steps towards examination reforms:

(i) Provision of 15 minutes extra time for candidates to read the question paper and to plan their answer in Class X & XII board examinations,

(ii) Restructuring question papers that can be answered by all the students within the allowed time period,

(iii) Publication of support materials such as sample question papers,

(iv) Publication of Performance Analysis,

(v) Providing counseling facility.
In addition CBSE has already implemented Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation from Classes I to VIII.

(d) Vocational streams at the higher secondary stage provides for diversification of educational opportunities so as to enhance individual employability, for enhancement of supply of skilled manpower and is an alternative for those pursuing higher education.

records.qtitle: CHALLENGES OF EDUCATION SECTOR .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government is facing problems in meeting the challenges of the education sector on its own;

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto and the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for enhancing competitiveness of the Indian education system in the global market;

(c) whether Government has strategically decided to adopt public private participation route in education sector; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and the policy made in this regard? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SMT. D. PURANDESWARI)

(a) & (b): No, Sir. Public investment on all sectors of education is sought to be increased several fold during the XIth Five Year Plan for enhancing capacity and improving quality thereof.

(c) & (d): There is already private not-for-profit participation in all sectors of education. The Eleventh Plan envisages the setting up of several new institutions mainly in the public sector, while also exploring possibilities of private participation in some of them.

records.qtitle: IMPLEMENTATION OF NREG SCHEME IN THE WHOLE COUNTRY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has proposed to implement the National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREGS) from April, 2008 in the whole country;

(b) if so, the steps taken for successful implementation of this scheme;

(c) whether complaints have also been received that irregularities are being committed in the implementation of this scheme; and

(d) if so, the steps taken by Government to check irregularities in the implementation of this scheme?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(DR. RAGHUVANSH PRASAD SINGH)

(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

Statement referred to in reply to part (a) to (d) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No.26 to be answered on 27.02.2008

(a): Yes, Sir. National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREGS) was launched in 200 districts in the country in the first phase on 2.2.2006. It was extended to 130 additional districts in its second phase in the current financial year. All the remaining rural areas in the country have been notified for coverage under the Act with effect from 1.4.2008.

(b)&(d) : Ministry has taken the following measures for successful implementation of the Scheme and to check irregularities in its implementation.

(i) Generating Awareness Various steps have been taken to generate awareness about NREGA. Gram Sabhas and one day orientation of all Sarpanches at the Block level have been held. Local vernacular newspapers, radio, TV, films and cultural forms are being used for the purpose. Leaflets and brochures in local language are being provided. Village camps have been organized by the District teams and NGOs and Self help Groups are being associated in the awareness generation.

(ii) Staffing/Training Capacity building for rural development functionaries and Panchayati Raj functionaries is an essential pre-requisite for better implementation of rural development programmes. NREGA guidelines provide that a dedicated Gram Rojgar Sahayak(GRS) should be appointed in each Gram Panchayat and a dedicated Programme officer should be appointed at Block level for NREGA works besides other technical and non-technical staff. So far 79249 GRS and 1685 Programme Officers have been recruited. Besides, 11464 technical staff and 10109 other non- technical staff has also been recruited for NREGA. Regarding training, so far 927766 Panchayati Raj functionaries, 177031 Government functionaries and 246655 Members of Vigilance and Monitoring Committees (VMC) have been trained under NREGA.

(iii) People`s Participation

(i) Village level monitoring committees have been set up and trained.

(ii) Non Governmental Organisations are being involved for awareness generation under NREGA.

(iii) Gram Sabhas are held.

(iv) Vigilance and Monitoring

(i) Implementation of NREG Act is monitored on regular basis. Vigilance and Monitoring Committees have been set up at State as well as district levels. Local MPs are the members of the district Vigilance and Monitoring Committees. Village level Vigilance and Monitoring Committees have also been set up for local monitoring. Members of the Central Employment Guarantee Council also undertake field visits to various districts. National level Monitors (NLMs) and Area Officers visit various districts to oversee the progress of the Act.

(ii) Muster Roll verification has to be done in a campaign mode and consolidated reports sent to the Ministry.

(v) Transparency

(i) States have been directed to conduct social audit of each and every work of NREGA within three months. Members of the Central Employment Guarantee Council are actively participating in the Social audit. Social Audit has been done in 53911 Gram Panchayats.

(ii) A Citizen Information Board has been introduced. This board is to be displayed at all prominent places. This will enable the local community to know the works being undertaken under NREGA and would also facilitate the process of spreading awareness about the programme.

(vi) MIS A comprehensive Web-based MIS www.nrega.nic.in has been implemented which places all data in public domain. This data pertains to workers` entitlements like registration, Job cards, muster rolls, employment demanded and provided; work data like sanctioned shelf of works, work estimates, work in progress, measurement; Financial indicators like funds available/spent, amount paid as wages, materials and administrative expenses. Data software has been engineered for cross verification of records and for report generation.

(c): Yes, Sir. Some complaints have been received regarding implementation of NREGA. These have been forwarded to the concerned State Governments for appropriate action.

records.qtitle: WITHDRAWAL OF PRIVATE CHANNELS FROM DD DIRECT PLUS .

records.qtitle: MOSQUITO COIL FORMULATION BASED ON AGRICULTURAL PESTICIDES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether his Ministry has received any applications on proposals for sanctioning household mosquito coil formulation based on agricultural pesticides like Bifenthrin, DDT, Cyperperthrin and deltamethrin;

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto in view of health hazards to users by such agricultural insecticides; and

(c) whether Government has fixed any formula-rules for manufacturing household mosquito coils in the country so that users health could not be hampered?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(SHRI TASLIMUDDIN)

(a) to (c): It has been informed by the Ministry of Agriculture, Department of Agriculture and Cooperation, that the Central Insecticide Board and Registration Committee has received an application for registration of Bifenthrin 0.05% Mosquito Coil. The Registration Committee constituted under the Insecticides Act, 1968 (Under Section 5) registers pesticides only after satisfying itself their bio-efficacy and safety to human beings and animals after scrutinizing their formulae and verifying claims made by the importer or the manufacturer. The Committee has formulated the guidelines for registration of pesticides for use in household purposes, which includes mosquito coils also.
Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has also formulated an Indian Standards on “Allethrin- Mosquito Coils” (IS13438:1992). This standard is voluntary in nature and prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for mosquito coils containing allethrin. There is no BIS licencee presently on mosquito coil.

records.qtitle: DATABASE OF COMPANIES MAINTAINED BY REGISTRARS OF COMPANIES
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:

(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

(c) whether it is also a fact that there is no control system over such erring companies;

(d) whether it is also a fact that many companies are not submitting their balance sheet, annual returns and profit/ loss accounts to Registrars of Companies; and

(e) if so, Government’s response thereto and the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken against such erring companies by bringing in more transparent systems?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS

(SHRI PREM CHAND GUPTA)

(a)&(b) No, Sir. The records of companies maintained by the Registrars in physical document form prior to the implementation of e-Governance programme are complete and accurate. The documents filed in the electronic mode are secure and intact as maintained in the electronic Registry. Some problems were identified on accuracy of data resulting from digitisation of the physical records and migration to the electronic registry, which are being verified and corrected.

(c) No, Sir.

(d)&(e) Yes, Sir. However, the rate of compliance in filing of Annual Returns, Balance Sheets and Profit & Loss Accounts has registered significant improvement with the introduction of e-Governance system. An Action Plan has been prepared to focus on compliance management and monitoring, according to which, the order of prioritisation follows from the public interest involved and the size of the company with authorised capital as the base. Top priority has been accorded to the public limited companies including the listed companies. Action has also been initiated for striking off the names of defunct companies from the Registry. - - - - - - -

records.qtitle: POWER SUPPLY SITUATION IN MAHARASHTRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the present consumption of electricity in Maharashtra and how much electricity would be made available during the next one-year by Government, to fulfill the requirement of electricity of the State;

(b) from where it would be generated and how many districts and villages would enjoy the benefit of electricity in the State;

(c) whether Government is planning to establish power generation projects, as well as producing more equipments/machineries, for the purpose of power generation companies in Maharashtra, particularly in Sholapur district; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and by when it would be set up?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )

(a) to (b) : The availability of electricity in Maharashtra from its own generating stations and allocation from Central Sector Generating Stations was 8,301 Million Units (MU) during October, 2007 and 53,662 MUs during the period April, 2007 to October, 2007. Central Electricity Authority has estimated that during the remaining period of 2007-08 i.e. November, 2007 to March, 2008 availability of electricity is expected to be 38,996 MU from the state`s own generating stations and entitlement from Central Sector generating stations. Furthermore, the availability of electricity in Maharashtra at the end of 2008-09 is anticipated to be 100,009 MU. Electricity is a concurrent subject and distribution is within the purview of the States. Therefore, from the available supply of electricity, the quantum of electricity that is to be provided to various districts and villages in Maharashtra is to be decided by the State Distribution Utilities.

(c) & (d) : The details of power projects envisaged to be developed under State and Private sector in Maharashtra during the 11th Plan are at Annex. In addition, Maharashtra will inter alia have a share from the generation of Central Sector projects proposed to be developed in Western region during the course of 11th Plan. In the Western region, out of the proposed capacity addition of 7813 MW in Central Sector, as on 26.11.2007, generation capacity to the tune of 1760 MW has been commissioned and projects aggregating 3480 MW are under construction. Regarding production of more equipments/machineries for the purpose of power generation, the leading power equipment manufacturer Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd. (BHEL) has intimated that it envisages to fabricate power house structures, parts of boiler structures and ducts at MAHAGENCO sites where projects are being executed by BHEL.

records.qtitle: POLICY FOR NON CONVENTIONAL ENERGY RESOURCES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is considering to make any comprehensive policy for compulsory use of renewable energy resources through biomass, hydropower, wind, solar and municipal waste in the country, particularly for commercial establishments, as well as Government establishment;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) the current capacity of renewable and non-conventional energy sources in the country; and

(d) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for increasing the use of renewable and non-conventional energy sources in the country ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY

(SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR)

(a) & (b): Under the Electricity Act 2003, National Electricity Policy 2005 and Tariff Policy 2006 it is obligatory upon State Electricity Regulatory Commissions to fix certain percentage for purchase of power from renewable energy sources in the area of a distribution licensee and to fix preferential tariffs for the same

(c): Grid-interactive renewable power installed capacity in the country has reached 11,063 MW as on 31.10.2007.

(d): The Government has been providing several concessions in the form of fiscal and financial incentives to encourage the use of renewable energy sources. These include capital/interest subsidy, accelerated depreciation, nil/concessional excise and customs duties. Further, as applicable to all new infrastructure projects, profits earned from sale of renewable power are exempt from Income Tax for any 10 years out of the first 15 years of project’s operation. This apart, preferential tariff for grid interactive renewable power is being given in most potential States. Publicity and awareness on the use of renewable energy systems / devices is also created through print, postal and electronic media and special events like the Rajiv Gandhi Akshay Urja Diwas are being organised. District-level Advisory Committees have been constituted in the states to facilitate effective coordination of renewable energy schemes / programmes.

records.qtitle: IMPROVING OF MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut

(a) whether it is a fact that there are 5-6 million people who are chronically disabled due to acute mental illness and about one lakh people die every year of suicide;

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto; and

(c) the details of corrective steps taken or proposed to be taken for improving mental health services in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE

(DR. ANBUMANI RAMADOSS)

(a): Epidemiological studies have revealed that 1 to 2% of the population has major mental disorders and 5 to 10% suffer from minor mental disorders. As per the records of National Crime Records Bureau, the number of suicides reported in the country during the period 2004-2006 is as under: 
Year                Total no. of
suicides.
2004                1,13,697
2005                 1,13,914
2006                  1,18,112 (provisional)


(b) & (c) : Under National Mental Health Programme, efforts are made to
 provide mental health services as a part of general health system. In this 
regard, Central Government supplements the State Governments’ efforts through 
District Mental Health Programme, Strengthening of Psychiatric Wings of Medical
 Colleges/General Hospitals and Modernisation/Upgradation of Mental Hospitals to
 make them as therapeutic units. The Govt. proposes to re-strategise the Nation 
Mental Health Programme during 11th Plan to expand District Mental Health 
Programme to cover the areas of suicide prevention, stress management, School 
Mental Health etc. and also to create infrastructure for production of quality 
manpower/training of personnel etc. for effective delivery of mental health 
services.

records.qtitle: INDIA TO CROSS CHINA AS MOST POPULOUS COUNTRY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether at the current rate India is expected to cross China as the most populous country by 2045;

(b) if so, whether any comprehensive action plan has been worked out to achieve the target of zero growth;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) the time by when the zero growth target is likely to be achieved thereunder?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE

(DR. ANBUMANI RAMADOSS)

(a)to(c) As per Technical Group on Population Projection Report, May, 2006, at the current rate, India’s population is expected to exceed that of China before 2030 to become the most populous country in the world. However, United Nation’s population projection has estimated that India’s population is likely to cross China in the year 2025.

Population stabilization is one of the objectives of National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) as well as Reproductive and Child Health Programme (RCH-II). The approach of Government is to provide quality health services in remote rural areas along with a wide range of contraceptive choices to meet the unmet demands for reproductive health services which include delivery, safe abortions, treatment of reproductive tract infections and family planning services. The RCH-II intends to improve the performance of family welfare services by reducing total fertility rate, maternal and infant morbidity and mortality, and unwanted pregnancies. Under NRHM & RCH-II, the Programme Implementation Plans of States interalia include the action plan for family planning activities.

(d) As estimated by Technical Group on Population Projection, the total fertility rate would reach replacement level fertility of 2.1 only by the year 2021. The population stabilization i.e. zero growth of population, would be achieved only after 35 to 40 years of reaching replacement level fertility. It implies that India’s population is likely to stabilize by 2060.

records.qtitle: PRICING OF GAS IMPORTED FROM IRAN .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the present status of Iran-Pakistan-India Gas Pipeline;

(b) whether it is a fact that there are some differences with Iran or pricing method of Gas as well as conflicts with Pakistan on gas transport tariff;

(c) if so, the details thereof and Government’s response thereto; and

(d) what strategy Government would like to take for getting enough natural gas for the future need?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS

(SHRI DINSHA PATEL)

(a) to (c): India has been pursuing the import of natural gas from Iran through the Iran-Pakistan-India (IPI) transnational gas pipeline. Various important issues are under discussion amongst the participating countries.
Such multilateral projects involve protracted discussions, as all the aspects have to be carefully examined and deliberated upon to the satisfaction of the participating countries to protect each country’s interests as also to avoid any future problems in the successful operation of the project.

(d): Government of India has adopted a multi-pronged strategy to augment gas supplies and bridge the gap between supply and demand for the domestic market. These cover:-

(a) Intensification of domestic exploration and production activities;

(b) Exploitation of unconventional sources, like Coal Bed Methane (CBM);

(c) Underground Coal Gasification;

(d) Implementation of Natural Gas Hydrate Programme (NGHP) for evaluation of hydrate resources and their possible commercial exploitation;

(e) LNG Imports; and

(f) Gas sourcing through transnational gas pipelines.

records.qtitle: EXTENSION OF PIPELINES GAS CONNECTIONS IN THE COUNTRY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have set any target for extending pipelines gas connections in various parts of the country;

(b) if so, the details thereof indicating how much of financial assistance is required and how it will be fulfilled for providing piped gas connections in the country;

(c) whether any objections have been raised by the present dealers and distributers of IOC, IBP, HPCL and BPCL; and

(d) if so, what are their objections towards Government’s decision for extending piped gas-line in the country and Government’s response thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS

(SHRI DINSHA PATEL)

(a) & (b): No such target has been fixed. The extension of pipeline gas connections in various parts of the country is linked with availability of gas, commissioning of necessary infrastructure and economic viability. Government of India does not allocate funds for providing piped gas connections in the country. Entities allocate and spend funds according to the plans of their projects.

(c) & (d): No, Sir. The LPG distributors, appointed by the Public Sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), have not raised any objection. However, All India LPG Distributors Federation (AILPGDF) has submitted a representation for rehabilitation of pipe gas affected distributors which, inter alia, requested for resitement of distributorships to alternative areas where pipeline network expansion is in progress. OMCs have reported that they have noted the position about the expansion of piped gas network while planning new LPG distributorships in the country.

records.qtitle: ENQUIRY INTO MIS MANAGEMENT OF UNIT
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) What is the present status of enquiry of officials involved in Unit-64 schemes mis-management;

(b) Whether the enquiry of all concerned officials had taken place through the CBI;

(c) If so, what is the status and whether there have been any recovery from these officials

(d) If so, the details thereof; and

(e) How much total money has been paid by Government to recoup the deficit in Unit-64 scheme?
records.ans_text:
SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(a to d) Certain investment decisions concerning US 64 were examined by the internal Vigilance Cell as recommended by the Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC). CBI conducted the enquiry into purchase of some equity shares by erstwhile Unit Trust of India (UTI) and has filed charge sheet in special court for CBI cases against the concerned officials. Civil suit has been filed by the Administrator of Specified Undertaking of Unit Trust of India (SUUTI) and UTI Trustee Company Pvt. Ltd. (UTI Mutual Fund) against concerned ex-officials for claiming damages/compensation for the loss suffered by erstwhile UTI in respect of investment in some shares.

(e) Rs. 2393 crore was given by Government for meeting the shortfalls between assured repurchase prices and NAV of US-64.

records.qtitle: HIGH RATE OF INTEREST CHARGED BY MONEY LENDERS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is aware that money-lenders, in rural areas are charging monthly interest rate more than 2 to 15 per cent to the poor and needy and many deprived persons commit suicide due to their inability to repay the money borrowed;

(b) if so, what is Government’s reaction thereto, indicating steps taken for providing more credit facilities to the poor against nominal interest rate;

(c) the measures taken or proposed to be taken against such money-lenders with the help of various State Governments;

(d) whether Government is considering to bring any legislation for regulating the unorganized money lending sector; and

(e) if so, the details thereof ?
records.ans_text:
(THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE)

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a)&(b) : Yes, Sir. However, there are many reasons behind the suicides by the farmers. Excessive borrowing from formal and non-formal sources, social tension, continuous drought affecting the yield and their income, emerging changes in social milieu and alienation of the individuals from family and society are some of the major reasons reported for the distress situation of the farmers leading to suicide.

Keeping in view the extreme conditions of the farmers and to address the issue of farmer`s distress, the Government. of India has announced a rehabilitation package in the identified 31 debt stressed districts of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala and Maharashtra.

To ensure that the farmer receives Short-Term Production Credit at 7% upto Rs.3 lacs on the principal amount, from Kharif 2006 the Government is providing interest subvention of 2% per annum to Public Sector Banks, Regional Rural Banks(RRBs) and Cooperative Banks on their lending from their own resources and concessional refinance by NABARD to cooperative banks and RRBs.

(c) to (e) : Reserve Bank of India set up a Technical Group to review the efficacy of the existing legislative framework that governs money lending as also the enforcement machinery in different States and make recommendations for its improvement.

The report of the Group has been submitted and is placed on the website of RBI for comments of the stakeholders. The process of consultation is to take some time as the report has been sent to all the State Government also for their comments. In the circumstances no time frame for its implementation can be specified.

The model legislation proposed by the Technical Group, inter-alia, provides for the following: 
·	a simple and hassle free procedure for compulsory registration and 
periodical renewal of their registration by money lenders;
·	a simplified dispute resolution mechanism to ensure better enforcement ;
·	adoption of the rule of ‘Damdupat’ restricting the maximum amount of 
interest chargeable by the money lender.

records.qtitle: DIVERSION OF PROFITS OF NATIONALISED BANKS TO NPAS

The Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance

(Shri Pawan Kumar Bansal)

records.qtitle: BLIND POPULATION IN THE COUNTRY
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that India has become home to the world`s largest number of blind people;

(b) if so, how many eye donation banks are available in the country, particularly in Maharashtra State and how many of them donate eyes every year;

(c) how many optometrists pass out every year and considering our population, whether they are sufficient to fulfil patients requirements; and

(d) whether Government has set any target to eliminate blindness or control of blindness and if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE

(DR. ANBUMANI RAMADOSS)

(a)to(d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

(b) As per the Eye Bank Association of India, Hyderabad, there are 500 Eye Banks/ Eye Donation Centres in the country including 148 in Maharashtra. Around 30,000 donated eyes are collected annually in the country.

(c) There are about 6000 Optometrists in India and about 1200 pass out every year. More Optometrists are needed to fulfill patients` requirements for eye care in the country as the Ophthalmologists - para medical personnel ratio should be 1:4 .

(d) As per the survey conducted during 2006-07, the prevalence of Blindness in the country has come down to 1% as compared to 1.1% during the year 2001-02.

The National Programme for Control of Blindness (NPCB) is committed to reduce the burden of avoidable blindness to 0.3% by the year 2020.

The following steps have been taken under NPCB to achieve the targets and for effective implementation of the programme:-

records.qtitle: DEDICATED FREIGHT CORRIDOR PROJECT .
records.name: Sanjay Raut

records.qtitle: INCREASE IN MSP FOR COTTON .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that higher production cost of cotton, Minimum Support Price (MSP) of Cotton and import of cotton has exaggerated the situation of the farmers in Maharashtra;

(b) whether it is also a fact that there is a big gap between minimum support price and production cost of the cotton;

(c) if so, whether Government has any proposal to increase M.S.P. and also increase of import duty on cotton;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES

(SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN)

(a): No Sir.

(b): No Sir. The MSP is fixed by the Government of India every year on the recommendation of Commission on Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP) which takes into account the cost of cultivation per hectare, cost of production per quintal in various regions of the country, changes in input prices like seeds, pesticides, fertilizers etc., demand and supply situation, effect of industrial cost structure, parity between prices paid and prices received by the cotton farmers etc., plus a reasonable profit margin to the cotton farmers. This mechanism of fixing MSP on year to year basis helps in guaranteeing an assured price to the cotton farmers and sustain their continued interest in cotton cultivation. The import of cotton is under Open General Licence (OGL) since 19.4.1994 without any qualitative or quantitative restrictions and the said policy is still being continued. The existing basic custom duty on import of raw cotton is 10%. Import of cotton in the last year was 1.78% of the total production.

(c): MSP is fixed every year taking into account the cost of various inputs and a reasonable margin of profit. There is no proposal for increase of import duty on cotton.

(d) & (e): Question does not arise in view of above.

records.qtitle: . CORRUPT PRACTICE FOR SIPHONING OFF MONEY FROM NREGA FUNDS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received some cases/complaints of corrupt practices like making fake muster roll, work contract process etc. for the purpose of siphoning off money from National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) funds;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for strict and transparent implementation of NREGA programme in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI CHANDRA SEKHAR SAHU)

(a) & (b): Yes, Sir. A total of 80 cases/complaints from 13 States have been received regarding misuse of NREGA funds. Details of these cases are being collected.

(c): To ensure transparency in the implementation of NREGA, the programme is reviewed and monitored on regular basis. Vigilance and Monitoring Committees have been set up at State as well as district levels. Village level Vigilance and Monitoring Committees have also been set up for local monitoring. Section 17(2) of the Act provides for regular Social Audit of all projects by Gram Sabhas. National level Monitors (NLMs) and Area Officers visit various districts to oversee the progress of the Act. Members of the Central Employment Guarantee Council also undertake field visits to various districts.

records.qtitle: INCREASE IN UNEMPLOYMENT .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether with economy registering a regular growth of 7 to 9 percent every year, unemployment has out-stripped all economic growth;

(b) if so, the comparative figures of economic growth, growth in employment and unemployment over the last three years, indicating the number of the unemployment generated both in rural and urban sector during these years; and

(c) the main reasons for increase in unemployment and the concrete steps proposed to be taken to deal with this menace?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT

(SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES)

(a & b) Reliable estimates of employment and unemployment are obtained through quinquennial labour force survey conducted by National Sample Survey Organisation and estimates of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) are obtained through National Accounts Statistics compiled by Central Statistical Organisation. As per these reports, the Indian Economy registered an average annual growth rate of 6.7% during 1993-94 to 1999-2000 and 5.98% during 1999-2000 to 2004-2005, whereas the annual rates of growth of employment as on usual status basis during these periods were 0.98% and 2.95% as against unemployment growth rate of 3.23% and 3.7%. Number of unemployed persons was estimated to have increased from 9.04 million in 1999-2000 to 10.84 million in 2004-05, resulting into an increase of 1.80 million (1.15 million in rural and 0.65 million in urban areas).

(c) Increase in unemployment is mainly attributed to higher rate of growth of working age population than total population, increase in labour force participation rates, particularly among women and higher unemployment among educated youth. Approach paper to 11th Five Year Plan envisages creation of 70 million job opportunities during the Plan period and in order to achieve this target, rate of growth of non-agricultural employment is to be accelerated to 5.8% per annum from 4.7% in 1999-2005.

records.qtitle: ACTIVE PRESENCE OF ISI AND TERRORIST GROUPS IN U.P. .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether Union Government are aware of the information that provided by the Uttar Pradesh Government about more than 34 districts of Uttar Pradesh State that have become sensitive due to active presence and anti-national activities by I.S.I and terrorist groups; and

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto and the details of adequate steps taken or proposed to be taken to help the State Government to control the unlawful activities of terrorist and I.S.I agents?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a): As per available information, during the period 2004 to 2007 (till date), a total of 10 Pak ISI backed espionage modules have been neutralized in Agra, Meerut, Varanasi, Rampur, Lucknow, and Saharanpur Districts of Uttar Pradesh resulting in the arrest of 13 espionage agents, including 05 Pak nationals.

(b): The Central Government has been sensitizing the State Governments about the activities of ISI. Periodic coordination meetings are also held with the State Governments for sharing inputs from various quarters as well as devising strategies, to counter such activities. Security and Intelligence agencies belonging to the Union and States have been working together to check the activities of ISI.

Over two lakh wells have been drilled with a success rate of over 90 percent.

records.qtitle: BIRD HIT INCIDENTS AT MUMBAI AIRPORT .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Mumbai have logged more bird - hits than any other aiport in the country;

(b) if so, how many cases have been registered in last three years;

(c) what are the financial losses Government have suffered during the last three years; and

(d) what action Government had taken/proposed to take to prevent this Bird - Hit incidents particularly at Mumbai Airport?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION

( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )

(a):- Yes, Sir.

(b):- During the last three years a total of 86 bird hit incidents have been registered at Mumbai airport.

(c):- Govenrment does not maintain record of losses suffered by airlines due to bird hit incidents.

(d):- Government has ensured many preventive measures. Airfield Environment Management Committees have been constituted at those airport where scheduled flights operate to identify the sources of bird attraction and take remedial steps for prevention of such incidents. Various steps have been taken to reduce bird hits inside and outside the airports such as proper disposal of garbage, prevention of water logging, coverage of garbage bins, establishment of modern abattoirs and scaring and shooting of birds etc. At Mumbai airport, regular joint inspection of the areas around the airport and deployment of Watch & Ward staff during the aircraft operations are also done.

records.qtitle: INCREASING THE PRODUCTION OF ETHANOL .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government propose to declare some concessions for increasing the production of ethanol keeping in view of its utility;

(b) whether those sugar mills which have their own distilleries but not having the facility of producing ethanol would be provided with concessional loans from the Sugar Development Fund and be allowed to set up plants; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR)

(a), (b) & (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE STARRED QUESTION NO. 347 DUE FOR ANSWER ON 07.09.2007 IN THE RAJYA SABHA.

(a): The Government has decided to encourage production and use of ethanol for blending with petrol as a fuel. Some of the difficulties faced by the industry in production and unrestricted movement of ethanol have been brought to the notice of the Government. The Government has not taken any final view in the matter.

(b)&(c): The Sugar Development Fund Act and Rules were modified in June, 2002 and January, 2003 respectively under which loans from Sugar Development Fund (SDF) are given to sugar mills for production of ethanol at a concessional rate of interest of 2% below the Bank Rate which effectively works out to 4% per annum at present. Loans are already being provided from SDF to sugar mills which have their own distilleries for production of anhydrous alcohol or ethanol from alcohol as follows :-

(i) In case any sugar factory, implementing a project for production of anhydrous alcohol or ethanol from alcohol, has been approved for financial assistance by a Financial Institution/Scheduled Bank and 12.5% of the cost of the project, is being met by the factory from its own resources, the SDF funding will be upto 40% of the eligible project cost or the amount as required by the Financial Institution/ Scheduled Bank whichever is less.

(ii) In case any sugar factory is implementing a project for production of anhydrous alcohol or ethanol from alcohol, which has been appraised by a Financial Institution/Scheduled Bank or any agency approved by the Central Government for this purpose and it undertakes to meet 25% of the cost of the project, from its own resources, will be eligible for SDF loan upto 75% of the eligible cost of project.

records.qtitle: HIGH SPEED TRAIN .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether his Ministry had decided to implement high speed train in various parts of the country;

(b) if so, what are the details in this regard;

(c) whether Government have asked for demonstration of high-speed corridor and technological upgradation and how many companies had come forward for this project, including International agencies;

(d) whether Government would be able to arrange the required fund for this mega project; and

(e) if so, the details thereof and if not the reasons therefore?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R. VELU)

(a) & (b): As per the Budget speech 2007-08, it was announced that Ministry of Railways will conduct pre-feasibility studies for construction of high speed passenger corridors, equipped with state of the art signalling and train control systems, for running high speed trains of 300 to 350 kms per hour; one each in the Northern, Western, Southern and Eastern regions of the country. The issue of implementation will be examined later.

(c): No, Sir.

(d) & (e): Yes, Sir. However, the high speed train corridors being highly capital intensive, Railways will find it difficult to fund the project fully. Therefore, all modes of financing such as public private partnership, funding by State Government etc. will be explored.

records.qtitle: RECOMMENDATIONS OF NCA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the National Commission for Agriculture has submitted its report to Government recently;

(b) if so, the salient recommendations of the Commission;

(c) whether it is also a fact that inspite of a number of packages announced by Government, suicides by the farmers are still continuing; and

(d) if so, the steps taken by Government to check such incidents?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a) & (b): The National Commission on Farmers submitted its final Report to the Government in October, 2006. The salient recommendations of the Commission included asset reforms in respect of land, water, livestock, fisheries and bio-resources, support services like science and technology, inputs and services, credit and insurance, assured and remunerative marketing, social security and curriculum reforms and other initiatives like special category farming, food security etc.

(c) & (d): Government approved a Rehabilitation Package involving an amount of Rs.16978.69 crore for 31 Districts in the four States of Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Kerala, reporting high number of suicides by farmers. Progress of implementation of rehabilitation package is being monitored and reviewed on a regular basis at District, State and Central level. Feed back received from some of the State Governments regarding implementation of package indicates that it has made positive impact on mitigating the distress of farmers covered by the Rehabilitation Package.

records.qtitle: SUBSIDIES AND INTEREST FREE HOUSING LOAN TO URBAN POOR
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number of people especially poor and middle class family were deprived of having their own homes due to hike in interest rates for housing loan;

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto;

(c) whether Government are considering any scheme for providing subsidies and interest free housing loan to urban poor; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING & URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION

( KUMARI SELJA )

(a)to(d): The interest rates on housing loans are decided by the managements of various Primary Lending Institutions (PLIs) after taking into account the cost of funds, transaction/ operation expenses and the general interest rate scenario in the country emerging from various monetary/ credit/fiscal policies announced from time to time. The Government, with a view of providing interest rate subsidy for housing loans availed by Urban poor categorized as Economically Weaker Section (EWS) and Low Income Group (LIG) people has made a Budget provision of Rs.30 crore for the financial year 2007-08.

records.qtitle: FUNCTIONING OF JAILS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the functioning of jails in the country has not improved despite the recommendations given by various Reforms Commissions and Committees;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

(c) the number of deaths/suicides occurred in jails during the last three years; and

(d) the number of undertrials for over ten years in jails and those without trial for over two years?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI MANIKRAO HODLYA GAVIT)

(a) to (d): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 314 FOR 5.9.2007 REGARDING FUNCTIONING OF JAILS.

(a) & (b): “Prisons” is a state subject under List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India and, therefore, functioning of jails comes under the realm of the respective State Governments. Committees set up to look into issues relating to prison reforms and correctional administration have made several recommendations to improve the functioning and condition in prisons. Most of these recommendations primarily focused on tightening of security in prisons, improving the physical conditions and providing basic amenities to prisoners. Emphasis was also laid on vocational rehabilitative programmes with a view to integrate prisoners into society once they complete their sentence. The Central Government has also taken the following measures to supplement the efforts of the State Governments in this regard:-

(1) The Government of India is implementing the Scheme for Modernization of Prisons to reduce overcrowding and improving the condition in prisons. The components of the Scheme include construction of new jails, repair and renovation of existing jails, improvement in sanitation and water supply and construction of staff quarters for prison personnel.

(2) Advisories have been issued to the State Governments for strengthening security in jails.

(3) The Government of India had prepared a Model Prison Manual which was circulated to all the State Governments/ Union Territories for their guidance. The manual aims at bringing in basic uniformity in laws, rules and regulations governing every aspect of prison administration and management.

(4) With a view to provide relief to undertrial prisoners, a new section viz 436A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 has been inserted in the

Code to provide that where an undertrial prisoner other than the one accused of an offence for which death has been prescribed as one of the punishments, has been under detention for a period extending to one-half of the maximum period of imprisonment, provided for the alleged offence, he should be released on his personal bond, with or without sureties. It also provides that in no case will an undertrial prisoner be detained beyond the maximum period of imprisonment for which he can be convicted for the alleged offence. Section 436 (1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 has also been amended to make a mandatory provision that if the arrested person is accused for a bailable offence and he is an indigent and cannot furnish surety, the Court shall release him on his execution of a bond without sureties.

(5) In 2006, the Government of India has introduced the system of plea bargaining primarily to reduce pendency of cases in trial courts and overcrowding in prisons.

(6) For disposal of long pending sessions and other cases, Government of India has also set up 1562 Fast Track Courts which have disposed off a total of 10.4 lakh cases out of 18.2 lakh cases transferred to them.

(c): As per the statistics compiled by the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) till 2005, the number of deaths/ suicides which occurred in jails during the last three years with reference to that year are at Annexure-I.

(d): As per available information compiled by NCRB, till December 2005, the number of undertrial prisoners by period of detention is enclosed at Annexure-II.

(http://mha.nic.in/fore.htm).  16 cases have been referred to CBI for detailed

records.qtitle: DECLINE IN EXPORT GROWTH .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that export growth is declining during the last two years and there is alarming situation for export growth;

(b) if so, the details thereof, indicating the reasons behind this situation and how much of impact have occurred over the current dollar rate against rupee in the market;

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for export promotion;

(d) whether Government is proposing any plan for taking active support of the States for export promotion efforts; and

(e) if so, the details of the scheme and its modus operandi?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH)

(a) & (b) There was no decline in export growth during the last two years. According to latest revised data, exports increased by around 23% in dollar terms during 2005-06 and 2006-07. However, according to provisional data available for the current year, export growth when compared with previous years has decelerated to 18 per cent in dollar terms and 6 per cent in Rupee terms during the period April-July 2007. The current deceleration in export growth is influenced by the sharp appreciation in the exchange rate which has effected certain export sectors which are less import intensive.

(c) Export promotion is an ongoing endeavour of the Government and initiatives are taken from time to time in accordance with the Foreign Trade Policy and its Annual Supplements. In addition, during the current year the Government has announced a relief package to help neutralise the adverse impact of Rupee appreciation on exporters. This package comprises enhanced Duty Entitlement Passbook (DEPB) rates, reduction in Export Credit Guarantee Corporation (ECGC) premium, release of Rs.600 crore for clearing all arrears of terminal excise duty and Central Sales tax reimbursement, enhancement of duty drawback rates and reduction in interest rates on pre and post shipment credit.

(d) & (e) The Government recognises the importance of active support of States for export promotion efforts. In view of this the Government has operationalised a scheme for assistance to States for Developing Export Infrastructure and Allied Activities (ASIDE). The Scheme consists of State Component with 80% allocation of total outlay and Central Component with the rest 20% of the outlay. The infrastructure projects for promoting exports are approved by the State level Export Promotion Committee headed by the Chief Secretary of the respective states. The projects under Central Component are approved by an Empowered Committee in the Department of Commerce. For the Eleventh Five Year Plan, an outlay of Rs.4450 crore has been proposed. An outlay of Rs.600 crore has been approved for this scheme for the current financial year, i.e., 2007-08.

records.qtitle: ELECTRICITY GENERATION FROM RENEWABLE SOURCES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have a target of 10 thousand megawatt of power from renewable sources like wind energy during the Eleventh Five Year Plan;

(b) if so, the efforts made for power generation in bio-mass, wind power and small hydro power sector; and

(c) the efforts made for strengthening the transmission and distribution system alongwith the power production?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY

(SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR)

(a): A capacity addition of 14,000 MW is envisaged during the 11th Plan period through renewable energy sources comprising 10,500 MW wind power, 2100 MW bio power and 1400 MW small hydro power.

(b): Investment in renewables is being encouraged through fiscal and financial incentives that include capital / interest subsidy, accelerated depreciation, concessional duties and relief from taxes. These apart, preferential tariff for renewable power is being given in most potential states. Around 10,465 MW grid interactive renewable power generation capacity comprising 7231 MW wind power, 1221 MW bio-power and 2013 MW small hydro power has been set up as on 30.06.2007.

(c): Efforts underway in the country for strengthening transmission and distribution systems include optimum development of transmission network based on feasibility analysis and techno-economic evaluation, inter regional transmission to enable exchanges across the country and matching development with consumer level requirements.

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): Government of Maharashtra has formulated following schemes to lessen the mortality rate of infants:

1. The Navsanjivani Scheme is being implemented in the tribal areas of Maharashtra, which includes: 


i. Matrutva Anudan Yojana
ii. Pada Volunteer Scheme
iii. Flying Squad Scheme
iv. Dai meeting scheme
v. Admitting Grade III & IV children to hospitals.



In addition, the following schemes areas being implemented all over Maharashtra



2. Rajmata Jijau Mata and Bal Health and Nutrition Mission has been 
established for decreasing the malnutrition and child deaths.  Malnutrition and 
infant mortality rate have come down. 

3. Integrated Child Development  
Scheme is being implemented under which all services are being given through 
anganwadi. 

4. Under second phase of the Reproductive and Child Health 
(RCH-II) programme and National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) following schemes 
are being implemented to decrease the deaths of infants and children.
Janani Surakasha Yojana: cash incentive for emergency medical & obstetric care 
is paid to Below Poverty Line (BPL), SC and ST pregnant mothers.  In rural 
areas, the incentive is Rs.700/-, in urban areas, the incentive is Rs.600/-.  
In all the fifteen tribal districts of the state, the quantum of the incentive 
is Rs.1400/- in the rural areas and Rs.1000/- in the urban areas.  In addition, 
the component of ASHA is implemented in the rural areas of these tribal 
districts, which at the current point in time is Rs.600/-.
 Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illnesses (IMNCI) is being 
implemented in 9 districts of the state and additional 11 districts are being 
added this year.  Of these, the tribal districts are Chandrapur, Nandurbar, 
Thane, Amravati, Nasik and Gadchirolli.
 Village level referral scheme: for referral of pediatric and maternal 
emergencies
 Sub centre strengthening project for referral of pediatric and maternal 

emergencies.



Provision of Ante Natal Care (ANC) for pregnant women by registration, 
protecting the mothers fully with 2 doses of Tetanus Toxoid (TT) and Iron Folic 
Acid (IFA) tablets is being done.  Involvement of Non Governmental 
Organizations (NGOs) and mobile medical units in provision of health care is an integral part of NRHM and RCH.



All of the above mentioned schemes are being implemented in the Vidarbha region 
of Maharashtra.


(c): The Government of India has implemented National Rural Health 
Mission programme in all the States and Union Territories of the country.


(d): Not applicable.

records.qtitle: CORPORATE FARMING .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are lots of shortcomings while promoting corporate farming in the country;

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto;

(c) whether Government are taking any initiatives for making long term transparent policies for making corporate farming successful in the country; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and the details of steps taken or proposed to set up strong systems to monitor contracts and corporate farming so as to avoid exploitation of the workers/growers and farmers in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a)&(b): The Ministry of Agriculture is promoting contract farming in the country, in which corporate agencies or others enter into agreement of purchase of agricultural produce with the producers, but, it is not promoting corporate farming in the country.

(c ): No, Sir.

(d): Question does not arise with respect to corporate farming, however, in order to put required systems in place for contract farming arrangements, suitable provisions have been included in the Model Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC) Act formulated by the Ministry of Agriculture in 2003 and circulated to the State Governments for considering suitable amendments in their concerned Act by adopting those provisions. The Model Act provided for the registration of contract farming sponsors and recording of contract farming agreements with the Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee or a prescribed authority under the Act, protection of title or rights of the farmers over the land under such contracts, dispute settlement mechanism and a model draft agreement suggesting various terms and conditions. By now, relevant provisions have been made by several State Governments in their respective APMC Acts for providing a legal framework to contract farming. In seven States/ Union Territories there are no APMC Acts, therefore, there is no regulation of contract farming in such States/UTs. The Model Act circulated by the Ministry is suggestive in nature, and, since Agriculture is a State subject, it is for the State Governments to decide on the implementation of the contract farming arrangements in their State.

records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT

(SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY)

(a)&(b) The Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) as per the Sample Registration System for 2005 is 58 per thousand live births. The State wise details in this regard during the last three years are given in Annexure-I.

The IMR in India and other countries of the world as per “The State of the World’s Children 2007”, published by UNICEF, is given in Annexure-II.

(c) The major causes of mortality amongst infants in India are acute respiratory infections, sepsis, diarrhoea and measles. (b): if so, the details thereof; and
