records.ans_text:
MINISTER FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES

(SHRI MAHABIR PRASAD)

(a), (b) & (c): Government (in the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises) continuously promotes ‘Swadeshi’ as one of the principal objectives in so far as khadi, village industry and coir products are concerned through its programmes and measures implemented by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) and Coir Board.

The steps taken in this direction by the Government (in the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises) include the implementation of the following schemes through KVIC and Coir Board, in the country: 


(i) Schemes for development of Khadi and Polyvastra activities:  For 
this purpose, Interest Subsidy Eligibility Certificate (ISEC) is issued in 
favour of implementing agencies for availing institutional finance to meet 
working capital requirement of khadi and polyvastra activities, at 4% rate of 
interest and the difference between 4% and actual  lending rate is subsidized 
by KVIC. 10% Rebate is provided on retail sales of Khadi/Polyvasta products as 
normal rebate throughout the year and another 10% special rebate for 108 days 
in the year.  



(ii) Scheme of Product Development, Design Intervention and Packaging 
(PRODIP) has been launched in order to diversify and develop products under 
Khadi & Village Industries and also to improve the packaging of the various KVI 
products.



(iii) Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries 
(SFURTI) has been launched in October, 2005 for regeneration of traditional 
industries in 122 identified clusters in khadi, village industries and coir 
sectors.



(iv) A Rural Industries Service Centre (RISC) scheme is in vogue for 
providing common facility services to KVI programmes on a cluster based manner.



(v) Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP) is being implemented 
for establishing village industries projects with margin money assistance from 
KVIC and loan from public sector scheduled commercial banks.



(vi) Mahila Coir Yojana, Development of Production Infrastructure and 
Domestic/ Export Market Development Assistance are some of the programmes under 
implementation in Coir sector through Coir Board. 



(vii) Development of Production Infrastructure Scheme for coir 
production through supply of equipment and machinery at subsidised rates.



(viii) Research and Development Schemes.



(ix) Financial assistance for participation in national and 
international exhibitions.

STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1109 FOR 22.8.2007 REGARDING WOMEN OFFICERS IN THREE DEFENCE SERVICES.

women officers during the year 2006, have revealed that factors like personal 
reasons, depression and psychological adjustment disorder etc. led to these 
incidents.



The measures adopted by the Government to prevent such incidents include:


(i)Increased formal and informal interaction between senior and junior 
officers, improved accessibility of leaders and frequent interaction of junior

Government has now constituted an Empowered Group of Ministers (EGoM) to consider issues related to gas pricing under the NELP regime.

records.qtitle: UNDER ASSESSMENT OF TAX ON COMPANIES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a): whether it is a fact that large number of companies escaped over Rs.1,000 crores in taxes due to under assessment by tax authorities;

(b): the stages at which the under assessment of the companies were detected; and

(c): whether Government propose to recover the amount under assessed as also to fix responsibility against the concerned officials/authorities?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE
SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM

(a): In some cases under assessment of income and short levy of tax was detected during assessment of different years.

(b): Under assessment of income in such cases was detected either in the course of review or inspection by supervisory officers, or in the course of audit by Revenue Audit or Internal Audit.

(c): Yes, Sir. Whenever under assessment is detected, consequential remedial action is duly taken and short levy of tax is recovered from the assessee. Responsibility against concerned officials / authorities is also fixed, if the mistake is not bonafide.

records.qtitle: SHORTFALL IN ELECTRICITY GENERATION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the total deficit of electricity generation compared to national requirement and the number of States facing a shortfall of electricity by more than 25 per cent;

(b) the estimates of generation of electricity for the Tenth Five Year Plan and the actual generation at the end thereof;

(c) whether it is a fact that even 50 per cent target of generation of electricity was not achieved during that plan;

(d) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(e) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for lessening the gap of electricity demand and supply upto 2012?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )

(a) : The energy requirement and energy availability in the country during the year 2007-08 (April – July,2007) was 240,834 Million Units (MU) and 221,865 MU respectively, resulting in energy deficit of 18,969 MU (7.9%). The gross energy generated in the country during the said period was 234,208 MU (including import from Bhutan).

Among the States, Maharashtra, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram faced peak shortage of more than 25% and Meghalaya faced peak as well as energy shortage of more than 25% during the period April – July, 2007.

(b) : The target for generation of electricity is decided on an annual basis. The year- wise actual electricity generation vis-à-vis the target for the Tenth Plan was as under: 


Year					Generation



			Targets (MU)	Actual (MU)	Actual generation as % of target


2002-03			545,552		531,607			97.4
2003-04			572,900		558,336			97.4
2004-05			586,412		587,416			100.1
2005-06			621,500		617,510			99.3
2006-07			663,000		662,523			99.9
Total			2,989,364	2,957,392		98.9



Thus, the actual energy generation in the country during the 10th Plan Period has 
been 98.9% of the target.


(c) :		No, Sir.


(d) :		Does not arise in view of answer to part(c) of the reply.


(e) :		The National Electricity Policy envisages `Power for all by 2012` and per 
capita availability of power to be increased to over 1,000 units by 2011-12.  The steps 
taken/proposed to be taken to achieve this include:


-	Augmentation of generation capacity.  Capacity addition to the tune of 78,500 MW is 
	proposed for the 11th Plan. 


-	Development of Ultra Mega Power Projects of 4000 MW capacity each under tariff 
	based competitive bidding route.


-	Strengthening of inter-state and inter-regional transmission capacity for optimum 
	utilization of available power.


-	Accelerated Power Development and Reforms Programme (APDRP) for reduction of 
	AT&C losses, etc.


-	Harnessing surplus captive power into the grid.


-	Promoting demand side management, energy efficiency and energy conservation 
measures.

records.qtitle: PUBLIC PRIVATE PARTICIPATION ROUTES IN DENSE CROWDED CITIES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether his Ministry has strategically decided to adopt public- private participation route for build, maintain and operate shorter version of train in various dense- crowded cities ;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether his Ministry has given permission to western railways for adopting PPP route in Mumbai city; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and policy made in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS
( SHRI R. VELU )

(a): No, Sir.

(b): Does not arise.

(c) & (d): No, Sir. At present there is no such proposal. However, Western Railway has been asked to conduct a comprehensive study to establish the feasibility of introducing Air Conditioned EMU Services.

records.qtitle: SHORTAGE OF BLOOD BOTTLES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is an acute shortage of supplying blood bottles at various major hospitals in the country;

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto;

(c) whether it is also a fact that the shortage of blood is an artificial one created by vested interests;

(d) if so, Government’s response thereto and the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government for averting such problems of blood supply; and

(e) whether Government are considering to make one window-data/ national helpline system for providing required blood, so that life of patients is not harmed and get it in good time?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) & (b): No, Sir. There are no reports of any acute shortage of availability of blood units in major hospitals except an occasional shortage of rare blood groups like ‘O’ –ve and ‘B’ –ve etc.

(c) & (d): There are no reports on the artificial shortage of blood, created by vested interests. The Government of India has taken following steps to check the practices which may lead to such instances and to ensure supply of blood in blood banks:

(i) Augmentation of Voluntary Blood Donation through about 45000 voluntary blood donation camps annually.

(ii) Awareness programmes to motivate the youth and thereby recruiting and retaining them as Voluntary Blood Donors.

(iii) Every year 14th June and 1st October are celebrated as World Blood Donors Day and National Voluntary Blood Donors Day to promote Voluntary Blood donation in the country.

(iv) The State Blood Transfusion Council reviews the Blood Transfusion Services in the blood banks and on receipt of any complaint of this nature, suggests action to State Drug Authority accordingly.

(e) No Sir. There is no such proposal, however, the following steps have been taken to ensure streamlining system of Blood Transfusion Services in the country:

(i) The National Blood Transfusion Council is established as a registered society to make required policy changes and put in place an action plan to ensure efficient and sustained blood transfusion service in the country.

(ii) State Blood Transfusion Councils have been established as registered societies in the States in the Medical and Health department. These societies implement the decisions taken by the National Blood Transfusion Council and oversee the implementation of various activities to ensure access of quality blood to needy patients.

(iii) The State Blood Transfusion Councils implement the voluntary blood donation programme to increase the volume of blood collection and to ensure continuous supply of blood.

(iv) Some State Blood Transfusion Councils e.g. Maharashtra had put in place an effective information system to track the availability and supply of blood in various parts of the State through State Blood Transfusion Council website to monitor the availability of blood in various blood banks in the State.

records.qtitle: PM S RKVY INITIATIVE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Prime Minister has announced a Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana of Rs. 30,000 crores initiative to provide incentives to various States for their better farm performance; and

(b) the details of the scheme and the modus-operandi of the financial arrangement?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a) & (b): The National Development Council`s resolution dated the 29th May, 2007 has identified the need for introducing a new Additional Central Assistance scheme to be administered by the Ministry of Agriculture to incentivize the States to draw up plans for their agriculture sector more comprehensively. The scheme is being formulated, and it is proposed to have an outlay of Rs.25,000 crore during the XI plan period for the scheme.

records.qtitle: CONTRACTORS ON NON PERFORMING LIST .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the number and names of Indian and foreign contractors put on the “non-performing” list by NHAI since August, 2004 debarring them from doing any project or contracts with NHAI anywhere in the country; and

(b) the parameters to judge a contractor becoming a non-performing contractor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

(SHRI K.H. MUNIYAPPA)

(a) The names and addresses of nine Indian and eight foreign contractors put on the “non-performing” list are enclosed as Annexure-I.

(b) The parameters fixed for judging a non-performing contractor are as under:- 


(i)                Slow progress.


(ii)             Delayed completion.


(iii)           Poor performance of the contractor in multiple contract packages, and


(iv)            Joint and several liability of Joint Venture partners.

records.qtitle: COMPLETION OF IRRIGATION PROJECTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that several irrigation projects have been hampered due to financial crunch and various irrigation projects are pending for approvals;

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto and the steps taken so far by the Union Government for early completion of all the ongoing irrigation projects;

(c) whether Government have explored the possibilities for increasing the irrigation capacity in the coming years keeping in view the irrigation demand in the country; and

(d) if so, the details of initiatives formulated by Government to meet the demand?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING

(SHRI M.V.RAJASEKHARAN)

(a): The responsibility of planning, funding and execution of irrigation projects primarily lies with the State Government concerned as irrigation is a State Subject. The priority for irrigation sector funding has declined from about 22.54% in first Plan to about 6.28% in Tenth Plan. Also states take up large number of irrigation projects and the resources are invariably thin spread.

Irrigation and Flood Control projects, which are located on inter-state rivers and tributaries, are being techno-economically appraised by Central Water Commission. The projects are further being considered in Advisory Committee for Irrigation, Flood Control and Multipurpose projects of Ministry of Water Resources for acceptance and according investment approval by Planning Commission.

(b) to (d): The guidelines for the Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme have been relaxed in December 2006 and assistance is provided to the states in the form of either 90 per cent grant or 25 per cent grant for completing the irrigation projects.

Under Bharat Nirman, 10 million hectare is proposed to be brought under irrigation during the four-year period 2005-2009. The Working Group on Water Resources for the Eleventh Five-Year Plan has suggested a target of creating 16 million hectare of irrigation potential. The State Governments have to provide adequate funds under the State Plan for achieving these targets.

records.qtitle: PHOTO IDENTITY CARDS FOR ENTRY AT AIRPORTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Govenment are considering to issue new and comprehensive smart photo identity cards for entry at all major international and domestic airports of the country keeping in view the increasing threat of terrorism;

(b) if so, the details thereof and by when such smart cards are likely to be issued; and

(c) if not, what are the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION

( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS)have issued technical specifications for the Smart Cards based airport access control system. While the system software and design as also the Central Database would be monitored by the BCAS, the airport operators would be procuring, installing and operating the system as per the BCAS prescribed specifications. Such an arrangement will facilitate interoperability and enabling monitoring of system security by BCAS.

(c) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: MERCHANT AIRPORTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are going to follow, built and operate policy for construction of new airports in the country now;

(b) whether it is also being considered to allow the private companies to built and operate such airports without any interference of Government under the policy named as merchant airports; and

(c) the details of the decision taken in this regard by Government?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION

( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )

(a), (b) & (c) The extant policy on Airport Infrastructure facilitates construction of new Greenfield airports in public or private sectors or to be taken up as a joint venture subject to obtaining technical clearance and licence from the competent authority and approval of the Central Government.

records.qtitle: EFFECT OF CORRUPTION IN EDUCATION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received any study report recently from UNESCO`s International Institute for Educational Planning, which reveals that various shades of corruption afflict the education system in the country;

(b) if so. the details thereof and Government`s reaction thereto; and

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken against such erring institutes in the country for securing the career of students?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI ARJUN SINGH)

(a) to (c) A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE RAJYA SABIIA STARREI)
QUESTION No.26 BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT TO BE ANSWERED ON 13.8.2007 REGARDING EFFECT
 OF CORRUPTION IN EDUCATION.




(a) The Government has seen a Report published in 2007 by 
UNESCO/International institute of Educational Planning entitled `Corrupt 
Schools, Corrupt Universities; what can be done?` This report is not India 
specific and highlights the issues related to corruption in education and the 
consequent loss to the system in terms of its adverse effect on access, equity 
and quality, in developed and developing countries around the world. The report 
includes references to teacher absenteeism and private tuitions by teachers, 
etc. and also suggests strategies to reduce corruption and improve governance in
 education.


(b)&(c) Details regarding the references made to India in the Report are
 enclosed  as Annexure-1. Central Government is continuously engaged, through 
consultations with State Governments and apex bodies such as University Grants 
Commission, the Central Board of Secondary Education and others, in eliminating 
malpractices in the educational system. Government also recognizes that 
eliminating the kinds of malpractices mentioned in the UNESCO/IIEP Report will 
require not only the continuous and committed participation of State Governments
 but also increased public awareness and greater transparency and accountability
 in the public bodies.



ANNEXURE-I



ANNEXURE-I AS REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (b) & (c) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED
 QUESTION No. 26 BY SHRI SAN JAY RAUT TO BE ANSWERED ON 13.8.2007 REGARDING 
EFFECT OF CORRUPTION IN EDUCATION.



The report presents the conclusions of the research conducted by the IIEP in the
 field Of ethics and corruption in education. It aims at sensitizing decision-
makers, educational planners and managers to the importance of combating 
corruption in education; at providing them with key tools to detect and assess 
corruption problems: and at guiding them in the formulation of adequate 
strategies to curb malpractices.



The Report is not India specific. However, references have been made to India 
through out the Report. The points with reference to India are presented below:
 -



	 In the foreword the Report mentions that ............ Fortunately , as 
this book amply demonstrates, there are vibrant parts of society - even among 
the poorest and the most vulnerable countries like Bangladesh and India - that 
will organize in support of rational democratic and progressive dismantling of 
existing corrupt practices.



	Referring to the magnitude of corruption, the Report mentions that there
 are a few estimates of the economic costs of corruption. Two national estimates
 of corruption corroborate the tact that this is major phenomenon. In India, it 
was estimated at around 20 per cent of the GNP in the 1980s.



	Decision-makers in Government. academia and advocacy groups have come to 
recognize the potential of public feedback in making the Government more 
responsive and accountable. The Public Affairs Centre (PAC) in Bangalore, India 
and Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB), in particular, designed `Report
 Cards on Public Services` in 2000, which proved to be relatively uncomplicated 
and widely replicable tools for improving transparency and public 
accountability.



	In the chapter titled `Teacher management and behaviour’ the Report 
opines that corrupt practices in teacher management and distortions in teacher 
behaviour can also have a high incidence on educational quality.



More globally, a variety of misbehaviours associated with teachers can disturb
 the implementation of planned interventions within the education sector, and 
particularly progress toward Education for All goals. Any plan to increase 
access to education, improve educational quality or reduce school inequities may
 thus prove unsuccessful if it does not properly take into consideration issues
 such as unauthorized fees for school admission, teacher-student relationship 
for private gain. and embezzlement of school finances. A study demonstrated, for
 instance, that a 10 per cent increase in teacher absence is associated with a 
1.8 per cent



decrease in student attendance. At the same time, another study conducted by the
 World Bank showed that teacher absenteeism is not a marginal phenomenon. It Can
 be as high as one third of all teachers in the state of Uttar Pradesh, India 
(World Bank, 2004).



	The chapter also contains a table showing Major sources of unethical 
behaviour among teachers in South Asia. The report deals with `Teacher absence
 rate in various countries and cost implications`. India has also be included in
 the table with 25% teacher absence rate in primary schools with consequent 
budget leakage of 22.5%.



	The analysis conducted by Chaudury et al (2005) in Bangladesh, India. 
Indonesia, Peru and Uganda, for instance, shows that there is no significant 
relationship between teachers` absenteeism and their residence with the 
catchments area of school, their average tenure in the school and how recently
 they have attended, training programme.



	In the sub-topic `Designing and enforcing teachers` codes of conduct`, 
the Report concludes that Even though codes of conduct are generally perceived
 as used instruments, they are not always effectively enforced. Various modes of
 enforcement have been experimented throughout the world, with more or less 
success. Existing social, political, cultural and institutional factors in 
Bangladesh, India and Nepal have greatly influenced the implementation of these
 codes.



	In the chapter-7 which deals with exams, credentials and accreditation, 
the Report mentions that in some places in India, cheating is now so well 
established that when Universities try to resist, students protest and demand 
their traditional right to cheat. In the Report, some examples of academic fraud
 have been mentioned. One of them is related to the findings of The Commission
 of Investigation on Abuse of Authority in Nepal. which suspects that 10% of the
 Himalayan Kingdom`s 1,40.000 school teachers are using diplomas purchased from 
India (Chronicle of Higher Education. 2003). Similarly, some press reports on 
figures on academic fraud have been included, which are as under:-


	India : fees for manipulating entrance tests scores between US$ 80 and US
$ 20:000 for the most popular programmes, such as computer sciences, medicine or
 engineering.



India : Post dated cheques totaling more than US$300,000 collected by people
 offering to sell answers for a nationwide examinations for physicians.



	In the chapter titled `Private tutoring: How to avoid the corruption of 
mainstream education?`, the Report mentions that according to a recent 
comparative study undertaken by the IIEP on teachers codes of conduct in South
 Asia, private tuition is thus regarded as a major source of unethical behaviour
 in Bangladesh, India and Nepal.




	The Report also says that in India, a 1997 survey of 7,879 primary 
schools pupils in Delhi found that 39.2 per cent were receiving tutoring.  Other
 reports have suggested that 70 percent of urban children receive private 
tutoring in one or more subjects.



	In the chapter regarding memo to policy makers, planners and managers on 
how to address the challenge of corruption in the Education Sector, there is a 
subtopic titled `How to address external factors (mainly political, legal, 
economical and educational)’.



This chapter mentions that lessons from experience and evidence suggest that 
five key elements hold a lot of promise when they can coalesce, namely, 
leadership; competition in the political and economic arena; the right to 
information; collective action; and an integrated approach.



Under sub-title `Right to Information’ the Report concludes that freedom of the 
press and access to information is key to transparency and accountability.  The 
experiences of countries  such as India that have progressively provided a legal
 basis for the right to information can prove extremely useful in this regard.

records.qtitle: POWER SHORTAGE IN MAHARASHTRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware of the electricity shortage and problems being faced by the people and industrialists, particularly in Maharashtra;

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto;

(c) the details of steps taken by Government for increasing the electricity generation and supply;

(d) whether Government are considering any exclusive proposal for increasing electricity generation in the State; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )

(a) : Yes, Sir

(b) & (c) : Electricity is a concurrent subject. Supply and distribution of electricity in a state/UT is in the purview of the respective State Government/State Power Utility concerned. The Government of India supplements the efforts of the state government by establishing power plants in central sector through CPSUs. The following steps have been taken/are being taken to improve overall availability of power in the country: 


(i)	Augmentation of generation capacity to the tune of over 78,500 MW is proposed for 
	the 11th Plan. 


(ii)	Development of Ultra Mega Power Projects of 4000 MW capacity each under tariff 
	based competitive bidding route.


(iii)	`Partnership in Excellence` Programme starting with adoption of better operation and 
	maintenance (O&M) practices to enable enhancement of Plant Load Factor (PLF) of 
	existing thermal power stations through tie-up with well performing power utilities as a 
	pre-cursor to renovation and modernization.


(iv)	Renovation, modernization and life extension of old and inefficient generation units.


(v)	Harnessing surplus captive power into grid.


(vi)	Strengthening/Augmentation of sub-transmission system in State under Accelerated 
	Power Development and Reforms Programme (APDRP) as a major step towards 
	reduction of Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) Losses.


(vii)	Coordinated operation and maintenance of hydro, thermal, nuclear and gas based 
	power stations to optimally utilize the existing generation capacity.


(viii)	Strengthening of inter-state and inter-regional transmission capacity for optimum 
	utilization of available power.


(ix)	Promoting demand side management, energy efficiency and energy conservation 
	measures.


(x)	Rigorous monitoring of production, transportation and supply of coal by an Inter-
	Ministerial Group on weekly / fortnightly basis to review and resolve the constraints.


(d) & (e) :	Besides other measures, the following measures have been taken exclusively for 
increasing of electricity generation in Maharashtra:


(i)	Capacity Addition of about 4750 MW is proposed in the State Sector in 
	Maharashtra during the 11th Plan. 


(ii)	Revival of the Dabhol Power Project under the aegis of Ratnagiri Gas & Power 
	Private Ltd. with facilitation through an Empowered Group of Ministers. 


(iii)	The establishment of Mauda Thermal Power Project (1000 MW), the first NTPC 
	Project in the state with maximum share to the Home State.

records.qtitle: RURAL ELECTRIFICATION IN MAHARASHTRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Maharashtra Government had requested for sanctioning electrification of remaining 17 districts of that State under the Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana;

(b) if so, by when, and the total estimate of these proposals;

(c) the reasons for delay in sanctioning these proposals; and

(d) the present position of these proposals and by when these would be endorsed so that the State can achieve the target of total rural electrification before December, 2008?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )

(a) to (d) : In Phase-I of Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana (RGGVY) 235 projects were taken up for implementation out of which 4 were of Maharashtra. Sanctioning / execution of balance 30 projects of Maharashtra at an estimated cost of Rs. 439.93 crore is dependent on approval of the Government for continuation of RGGVY in the 11th Plan period. RGGVY envisages electrification of all the un-electrified villages and provision of access to electricity to all rural households in the country, including Maharashtra by 2009.

records.qtitle: DEMANDS OF RAILWAY LABOUR CO OPEPRATIVES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received any representation from Railway Labour Co-operatives for considering their long standing demands;

(b) if so, what are the main demands been made by the Railway Co-operatives and Government’s response thereto; and

(c) how many labour co-operatives are in existence in the country and what kind of assistance his Ministry is providing since last three years?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R. VELU)

(a) to (c) A statement is attached.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.104 BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT TO BE ANSWERED IN RAJYA SABHA ON 10.08.07 REGARDING DEMANDS OF RAILWAY LABOUR CO-OPERATIVES

(a) & (b) Yes Sir. Main demand of the Railway Labour Co-operatives is that a fresh notification incorporating the reservation of skilled works up to Rs. 15 lakhs and un-skilled works without any limit related to Railways should be done as per the recommendation of National Advisory Council on Labour Co-operatives.
The said recommendations had been examined and it was not found feasible for acceptance.

(c) A total number of 34744 labour contract/construction and forest co-operative societies are registered in different states/union territories as on 31st March, 2006 out of which 163 labour Co-operatives are working with Railways in different zones.
Some of the assistance/concessions available to Railway Labour Co-operatives are: 
1)	Award of handling contracts both parcel and goods to the genuine 	
	Labour Cooperatives without any ceiling limit without call of 	tenders.
2)	Provision of accommodation for office, canteen at a nominal rent 	
	of Rs. 20/- per annum.
3)	90% of  payment of  bills to be  made  within a  week’s time, after 	
	submission of the bills and the balance being made within one month of the 
	receipt of the bills.    
4)    	No earnest money is obtainable if the contract is awarded 		
	through negotiations. 
5)	In case of tenders, earnest money is chargeable at 10% subject to a minimum of
	Rs. 500/- and a maximum of Rs. 1000/-.  
6)	Deduction of security deposit through bills at the rate of 5% from 	
	each bill.

records.qtitle: ILLEGAL OCCUPATION OF HVOCL LAND .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH)

(a): Yes Sir, The ex-employee while in service had been allotted a portion of the accommodation built on a corner of the land. The said person has not vacated the same.

(b): The Company has not paid retrenchment/terminal benefits to the ex-employee. Legal action to get the accommodation vacated has already been initiated, which is pending in the Tis Hazari Court.

(c): No sign of any factory running in the premises was noticed by the team of officials of HVOC who last inspected the site on 28.4.2007.

(d): A case has been filed in the Court of Law for vacation of the premises under the ex-employee`s unauthorized occupation.

records.qtitle: SPECIAL MISSION FOR WHEAT RICE AND PULSES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government propose to launch a special mission very soon in order to increase the production of wheat, rice and pulses; and

(b) if so, whether any other programme is also proposed to increase the growth rate of agriculture sector alongwith the above programme?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)


(a) & (b): The Government is contemplating a Centrally Sponsored Scheme `National Food Security Mission` in the country to enhance the production of wheat, rice and pulses during XI Five Year Plan. Besides, a proposal for introduction of Additional Central Assistance (ACA) scheme to State plans to be administered by the Ministry of Agriculture over and above its existing Centrally Sponsored Scheme is under consideration of the Government to increase growth in agriculture in the country.

records.qtitle: MASS TRANSIT SYSTEMS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for the successful implementation of Mass Transit Systems (rapid bus and rail based) in various parts of the country while seeking rapid growth of urban population and its deterioration impact on urban transports;

(b) whether Government have received any proposal from various parts of the country;

(c) if so, the details thereof and Government`s response thereto;

(d) whether Government have made any comprehensive project with regard to Mass Transit Systems; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT



( SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY )


(a)to(e): A statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha.
STATEMENT

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.602 FOR ANSWER ON 17.5.2007 REGARDING MASS TRANSIT SYSTEMS

(a): The details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by the Government for successful implementation of Mass Transit Systems

(rapid bus and rail based) in various parts of the country are as under:- 




(i)   National  Urban Transport Policy (NUTP) was formulated  by
the  Govt.  in consultation with the State Governments and
circulated  to  all  stake  holders  in  May,  2006.   The
objective  of  this policy is to ensure safe,  affordable,
quick,  comfortable,  reliable and sustainable access  for
the  growing number of city residents to jobs,  education,
recreation  and such other needs within the cities.   This
is  sought  to be achieved by various  measures  including
greater use of public transport and non-motorised modes by
offering  Central  financial assistance for this  purpose,
enabling  the establishment of quality focused multi-modal
public  transport  systems that are well integrated,  etc.
This  policy  lays  down   broad  guidelines  for  guiding
investments in urban transport.


(ii)  Govt.  of India has launched the Jawaharlal Nehru National
Urban   Renewal  Mission  (JNNURM)   on   3.12.2005   that
inter-alia seeks to bring about comprehensive improvements
in   urban  infrastructure,   including  urban  transport,


committing   substantial  funds  for   this  purpose   and
requiring  a  series  of  reforms   that  would  make  the
investments  sustainable.  All State Governments have been
advised  to ensure that projects proposed under JNNURM  in
the urban transport sector are NUTP compliant.


(iii) Guidelines  for preparation of Detailed Project Report for
Integrated Mass Transit System development plans (both bus
and  rail  based)  have  been   circulated  to  all  State
Governments  for  their guidance and implementation.   The
adherence  to these guidelines in their project  proposals
is being insisted upon.


(iv)  Central  financial assistance in the form of Viability Gap
funding  is  also available for urban  transport  projects
under  the scheme for financial support to  Public-Private
Partnerships  in  Infrastructure of Ministry  of  Finance.
Detailed   guidelines  for   availing  Central   Financial
Assistance  under  this scheme has been circulated to  all
States.


(v)   Capacity  building efforts in urban transport sector  have
been  undertaken  through  organization  of  a  number  of
workshops across the country with the help of National and
international  experts  to provide necessary hand  holding
and facilitate peer learning.  Exercise for development of


tool  kits/guidelines  for   sustainable  urban  transport
programme, planning, strategy, technology neutral bidding,
model  concession agreement for metro projects, etc.   has
also been taken up.  This, however, is an ongoing process.


(b)&(c):   Details  of proposals received from various parts  of
the  country and Government`s response thereto are given in  the
Annexure enclosed.


(d)&(e):   Urban Transport is a State subject.  The projects are
normally  city based.  Therefore, these have to be formulated by
the  concerned  city/State.   Central Govt.  has  not  made  any
comprehensive project with regard to Mass Transit Systems.

records.qtitle: NAXALITE MENACE IN MINERAL RICH STATES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Naxals` involvement in disrupting various private infrastructure plants in Orissa, Bihar, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh have come to the notice of Government;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether it is a fact that Naxalites have become a biggest challenge for the internal security in mineral-rich States of the country; and

(d) what steps Government have taken proposed to take to control the Naxalism?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a) to (d): Naxalites groups, particularly CPI(Maoist), have occasionally attempted to disrupt private infrastructure plants in Orissa, Bihar, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh. Such attacks are carried out mainly due to non-payment of levy to the outfit. Besides, the naxalites ideologically oppose the establishment of SEZs, mining projects and proposed steel plants by private agencies as well as government on the ground that they cause displacement of tribals from their homelands and result in loss of agricultural land of poor farmers. The CPI(Maoist) and its front organizations have been propagating to build up a sustained movement of the people at an all India level to oppose development agenda of the Central and State Governments.
Government views naxal menance as an area of serious concern; therefore, this issue is being addressed both on security, development fronts and public perception management fronts. The measures include deployment of 33 Battalions of CPMFs; sanction of 29 India Reserve Battalions; Modernization of State Police Forces, Strengthening of intelligence mechanism etc on security front. On the development front financial assistance of about Rs. 1680 crores has been provided to the naxal affected States under the Backward District Initiative (BDI) component of the Rashtriya Sam Vikas Yojana(RSVY). Similar development assistance is also available to naxal affected States under the Scheme of Backward Regions Grant Fund (BRGF).

records.qtitle: INFILTRATION OF LET MEN THROUGH KARACHI MUMBAI SEA ROUTE .

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

records.qtitle: REPORT ON LESS WATER MORE CROP .

(c)&(d) Artificial Recharge of Ground Water Advisory Council while constituting the above Sub-Committee stated that the report of the Sub-Committee will be placed considered at the next meeting of the Council. records.qtitle: EMERGENCY LANDINGS AT IGIA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that three emergency/ precautionary landings were made by Al/Indian at IGI Airport, Delhi in April, 2007, the cause of which has been mainly attributed to hydraulic leakage;

(b) whether it is also a fact that Government have already taken up the issue of the hydraulic leakage in flexible hoses with Airbus which has suggested design changes, although some changes have been carried out and the rest are still in progress; and

(c) whether Government propose to consider changing the old fleet on a war footing to avoid such recurrence?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )

(a): Two Air India aircraft operating flight AI-349 and AI-737 made emergency landings at Delhi during April, 2007. However, these were not due to hydraulic leakage.

As regards Indian Airlines, there were 2 precautionary landings related to Hydraulic System made by A320 aircraft in April, 2007.

(b): Yes, Sir. Infact, Air India has implemented all applicable solutions in its fleet resulting in considerable reduction of hydraulic leaks on A310 aircraft.

(c): As the aircraft get older, some snags develop on the components and structural members of the aircraft due to wear and tear and the cyclic load subjected on them. From time to time, the manufacturers prescribe maintenance requirements for each type of aircraft. DGCA ensures that the operators strictly follow the manufacturers instructions for maintenance of their aircraft. Thus, every aircraft of Air India and Indian Airlines is maintained as per manufacturers instructions and is considered airworthy and safe for operations.

However, for modernization of its fleet and for expansion of routes, both the airlines are in the process of inducting new aircraft in their fleet. While, Air India has signed a purchase agreement with M/s Boeing for purchase of 68 aircraft, Indian Airlines Limited has signed an agreement with M/s Airbus Industries for procurement of 43 Airbus aircraft. The above fleet expansion programme envisages induction of aircraft in a phased manner and also phasing out of some of their older aircraft in the present fleet.

records.qtitle: PENDING HYDRO ELECTRIC POWER PROJECTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY

(SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR)

(a): This Ministry has been giving central financial assistance (CFA) for setting up hydro power projects upto 25 MW station capacity. Proposals for the grant of CFA are received on a regular basis. At times, these proposals are found to be incomplete or not in line with the provisions of the schemes. Complete proposals are considered and approved subject to budget provisions. During the last two years, i.e., 2005-06 and 2006-07, the Ministry has given CFA for
(i) detailed project report preparation for 93 potential small hydro power (SHP) projects
(ii) 38 new SHP projects
(iii) 57 ongoing SHP projects, including 2 in Maharashtra, and
(iv) 875 watermills.

(b): Details of the support currently provided by this Ministry for the development of SHP sector are given in Annexure.

(c): No, Sir. However, no major obstacle is envisaged at this juncture for the attainment of proposed target of 1400 MW for SHP during the 11th Plan.

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M.A.A. FATMI)

(a) and (b): As per information furnished by Government of Maharashtra, after the Class-X mathematics paper-I (Algebra) and paper-II (Geometry) examination ,of Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education held on 20th and 21st March, 2007 respectively, representations were received about the difficulty levels of the question papers. After examining the representations it was decided to accord 15 marks each to all students for the D level questions in all sets in paper-I and paper-II.

(c): No, Sir.

(d): In view of (c) above, does not arise.

(e): According to information received from the State Govt. of Maharashtra, new syllabi have bee, n introduced for classes IX and XI from 2006-07 and are scheduled for introduction for classes X and XII from 2007-08 based on National Curriculum Framework. Importance has been given to application of knowledge with inclusion of commercial mathematics.
Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has introduced mathematics. laboratories in CBSE affiliated schools to make students understand mathematical concepts through activities and project work

records.qtitle: SUBSIDY UNDER NHB .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) what are the salient features of the scheme wherein subsidy is provided to horticulture through National Horticulture Board;

(b) whether it is compulsory to opt for loan from the banks to make farmers eligible for this subsidy;

(c) why they are deprived of this incentive when they manage to raise crops without falling in the trap of bank finances and whether it is an offence; and

(d) whether Government are ready to change this policy with retrospective effect?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a): The salient features of the scheme of National Horticulture Board (NHB) for providing subsidy is given in Annexure.

(b): Credit linked backended subsidy is provided under two Schemes, viz. `Development of Commercial Horticulture through Production and Post Harvest Management` and `Capital Investment Subsidy for Construction/Expansion/Modernization of Cold Storages for Horticulture Produce` and released through bank after successful completion of the project. However, under the scheme, `Capital Investment Subsidy for Construction/Expansion/Modernization of Cold Storages for Horticulture Produce`, bank loan is not required for the projects falling under self-financing category. The subsidy is restricted to 3000 MT capacity for such self financing projects.

(c ): The advantage of a credit linked subsidy is that the loaning agency appraises the project for its estimates and viability, otherwise, it is possible for a promoter to inflate cost estimations and effectively get higher levels of subsidization than intended. Therefore, bank finance is insisted upon by NHB for release of subsidy.

(d): No such proposal exists at present.

records.qtitle: PROCUREMENT OF MUSTARD SEEDS AT MSP .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Central Government have made any arrangement for procurement of mustard seeds at support price through NAFED, as about more than 25 lakh tonnes of mustard seed produce are expected this year;

(b) if so, the criteria fixed by the Central Government, so far, for the procurement of mustard seeds by cooperating the farmers in distress; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)


(a) to (c): Yes, Sir. The Central Government has fixed Minimum Support Price (MSP) of Fair Average Quality of mustard seed for Rabi crop season of 2007 at Rs.1715/- per quintal. The Government, through NAFED as the Central Agency, like in Rabi 2005 and Rabi 2006, has made adequate arrangements for procurement of Fair Average Quality mustard seed under Price Support Scheme (PSS) during Rabi 2007 at the MSP. It has been reported by NAFED that during the current Rabi crop season, the prices of mustard seed are generally ruling at or above the MSP. However, NAFED has procured 20,600 MT mustard seed under PSS during Rabi 2007 season in the States of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhatisgarh and Punjab from the farmers through State Cooperative Marketing Federations/Oilseeds Growers Cooperative Federations where ever the prices ruled below the MSP. In case the prices rule above the MSP, the farmers are at liberty to sell their produce at the prices higher than the MSP.
