records.qtitle: MANUAL SCAVENGING
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that manual scavenging still persists in the country despite earlier target fixed by the Central Government upto 31st March, 2007 as scavengers free country;

(b) if so, Government`s view and reaction thereto;

(c) the main problems for non-implementation of Integrated Low Cost Sanitation Scheme (ILCS) by the State Governments;

(d) whether it is also a fact that fund allocated by his Ministry to the State Governments were unspent;

(e) if so, the details thereof; and

(f) whether Government are considering to revive ILCS scheme for successful implementation in various parts of the country by making it more transparent?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING & URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION

( KUMARI SELJA )


(a)&(b): Water flush toilets are not available to the entire population of the country. Dry toilets and manual scavenging still exists in some parts of the country.
To eradicate manual scavenging from the country, this Ministry is administering the `Employment of Manual Scavengers and Construction of Dry Latrines (Prohibition) Act 1993` which prohibits construction of dry latrines and employment of manual scavengers.

It is also implementing Integrated Low Cost Sanitation Scheme which envisages conversion of dry latrines into water flush latrines in the urban areas of the country.

(c): The ILCS Scheme has been implemented in all the urban areas of the States. While implementing the scheme, the state governments faced some constraints as under: 


(i)   No subsidy for superstructure


(ii)  In  the  congested  areas,   due  to  non-availability  of
sufficient  space,  the  individual   latrines  cannot  be
constructed with twin pits.


(iii) Poor  loan  recovery from individuals.  State  Governments
are reluctant to provide guarantee for securing loan.


(iv)  Subsidy  being  provided to the EWS families is  only  45%
which  is  much on the lower side and hence the scheme  is
less demanding.


(d)&(e):  Major portion of the subsidy released by this Ministry
to the states has been utilized by the state governments.


(f):   Yes  Sir,  based  on the suggestions  received  from  the
Planning    Commission,   State     Governments   and    various
stake-holders, revision of guidelines of the scheme is under the
consideration of the Government.

records.qtitle: NATIONAL CITIZEN SMART CARD .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering seriously the introduction of multipurpose unique identification National Citizen/Smart Card, which would help the citizens, receive a number of benefits and services like making payments, electronic voting, obtaining ration card, passport, driving license etc. in the country;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) what are the new cost effective technology in use in other parts of the country in respect of comprehensive National Citizen/Smart Card; and

(d) the Government`s observations for adopting such new innovative and cost effective technology in the country, with the active support of IITs, private sector, for introducing the multi-purpose National Citizen/Smart Card in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI MANIKRAO H. GAVIT)

(a) & (b): The Government propose to issue Multipurpose National Identity Cards (MNICs) to the citizens of he country. The main purpose of MNICs is to provide a credible individual identification system for improving the security conditions and to help the e-governance by improving the citizen-Government interface.

(c) & (d): The proposed identity card is a smart card having a microprocessor chip. This is a secure card for which recommendation was made by the Technical Committee constituted by Government of India having representatives from National Informatics Centre (NIC), IIT Kanpur, Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), Indian Telephone Industries Limited (ITI) and Electronics Corporation India Limited (ECIL), Intelligence Bureau (IB) etc.

records.qtitle: EVASION OF STAMP DUTY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a): whether Government are aware about the large scale evasion of stamp duty for the registration of the properties and payment of property tax because of high percentage;

(b): if so, whether Government have evolved any mechanism to check the evasion of above duty/taxes as large number of buyers and sellers prefer to pay black money or unaccounted money to seal the deal rather than pay the high taxes; and

(c): if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a) to (c): Under the Constitution of India, Stamp Duties (but not including rates of stamp duty) fall under Entry 44 of the Concurrent List. Regarding rates of stamp duty, the Central Government has powers to fix the rates in respect of 10 instruments listed in Entry 91 of the Union List, whereas States have the powers in respect of the remaining instruments by virtue of Entry 63 of the State List. The fixing of rates of stamp duty on properties is in the domain of the States. The revenue from stamp duties leviable within any State is assigned to that State by virtue of provisions of Article 268 of the Constitution. Thus, the stamp duty is collected and appropriated entirely by the States concerned. The administration of stamp duty laws (Central as well as the State) is entirely with the States. Therefore, it is for the States to take necessary measures to prevent tax evasion in respect of stamp duties. In fact, most of the States have taken legal and administrative measures to deal with the issue of under-valuation of properties for evading payment of stamp duty. During recent years, there is also a trend of States lowering the rates of stamp duty to more moderate levels. Since this is a matter concerning the States, it is for the States to take necessary steps in this regard.

records.qtitle: INTEGRATE INCOME RISK MANAGEMENT FOR FARMERS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government .are seriously considering any proposal of integrated income risk management mechanism for farmers on the eventuality of losing their expected income by various reasons, i.e. flood, drought etc. as this mechanism is successfully going on in the western world;

(b) if so, what are the details thereof and by when it will be implemented in the country; and

(c) if not, what are tie reasons for not implementing this? AMSWER
records.ans_text:
(MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE) (SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) to (c) : Yes, Sir. Agricultural Insurance Company of India Ltd. (AICIL) introduced Rainfall Insurance Scheme known as `Varsha Bima` during 2004 south-west monsoon period. Varsha Bima provided for five different options suiting varied requirements of farming community:
(i) seasonal rainfall insurance based on aggregated rainfall from June to September,
(ii) sowing failure insurance based on rainfall between June 15 and August 15,
(iii) rainfall distribution insurance with the weight assigned to different weeks between June and September-,
(iv) agronomic: index constructed on the basis of water requirements of crops,
(v) a catastrophe option covering extremely adverse deviation of 50 per cent and above in rainfall during the season. Varsha Bima was piloted in 20.rain-gauge areas spread over Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, .Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh in 2004-05. Based on the experience of the pilot project, the scheme was fine tuned and implemented as Varsha Bima 2005` in 130 districts across ten states during Kharif 2005 and as Varsha Bima-2006 in 150 districts/rain gauge station areas of 16 states during kharif 2006. AICIL is also piloting another weather related insurance product, for mango and coffee.

records.qtitle: DEBT BURDEN OF DABHOL POWER PROJECT .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) what is the Dabhol Power Project`s current debt burden;

(b) what kind of support have been provided so far by the Central Government in view of the Dabhol Power Project`s debt burden so that power generation may be increased by reducing its cost of power generation; and

(c) how much power is likely to be generated in the next three months to one year, and at what cost from the Dabhol Power Plant?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )

(a) : Ratnagiri Gas & Power Private Ltd. (RGPPL) have informed that Dabhol Power Project`s debt burden, as on 31.03.2007 is Rs.7537 Crores as per their books of accounts.

(b) : Government of India (GOI) has provided several fiscal incentives to RGPPL to improve the project viability which includes Mega project status to the integrated project

(including the LNG facility) which has reduced the overall project cost. Besides, Government has granted CD/CVD exemption on import of fuel (Naphtha/gas) for the plant for 5 years to soften the impact of the cost of generation and increase project viability. The benefits under Section 80-IA of Income Tax Act have also been made available to RGPPL.

(c) : The Commercial operation of the power blocks shall commence on availability of R-LNG. In case 1.5 MMTPA R-LNG, currently tied up by Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, is made available by 2nd week of June 2007, two power blocks (1480 MW) can be operated commercially from July 07 and August `07 respectively. The third power block (670 MW) is expected to be ready for Commercial operation by January, 2008 subject to availability of additional 0.6 MMTPA of R-LNG.
The Power tariff based on current price of R-LNG (Rs.263/MMBTU at burner tip) based on a USD rate of Rs. 42 is expected to be about Rs. 3.00 per kwh.

records.qtitle: ONLINE EDUCATION AT IITS AND IIMS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Institutes like IITs and IIMs are preparing to offer online education for Indian students;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) the details of co-operation provided by Government for providing online education in the country so far; and

(d) how much benefit of online education will be accrued by the students in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SMT. D. PURANDESWARI)

(a) to (d) :- The information is being collected and will be laid on the Table of the House.

records.qtitle: . REFUND RULES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the National Consumer Commission has advised his Ministry for making refund rules user-friendly and simple;

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto;

(c) how much of refund amount is not paid to the rail passengers since last three years;

(d) what are the reasons behind this refund amount unclaimed; and

(e) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken to simplify the present rules for getting refund amount to rail passengers?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS
(SHRI R. VELU)

(a): No, Sir.

(b): Does not arise.

(c): No separate data is maintained.

(d): Does not arise.

(e): Rules for refund are already quite simple and passenger friendly. The passenger, who has paid the fare in cash, is granted due refund at the station itself on surrendering the ticket within the prescribed time limits. Thereafter, a Ticket Deposit Receipt is issued to him and this case for refund is examined in the concerned Refund Office.

records.qtitle: STATUTORY POWER TO A COMMISSION LOOKING THE WELFARE OF SMALL AND MARGINAL FARMERS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) what are the details of policy initiative measures that have been taken or proposed to be taken to alleviate the sufferings of the farmers, particularly the small and marginal ones;

(b) whether his Ministry has issued statutory powers, to any commission so that they take decisions for arranging funds and providing the funds to the needy and poor farmers against nominal interest rates; and

(c) if not, what are the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)


(a): The Government has taken a number of initiatives to alleviate the sufferings of the farmers including small and marginal farmers. These, inter-alia, include the announcement of a credit policy in the year 2004 to double the flow of credit to the agriculture sector in three years. From Kharif 2006-07, farmers are being provided crop loan up to Rs. 3 lakh at 7% rate of interest. Keeping in view the importance of flow of credit to agriculture, in particular to the smaller borrowers who may not have the necessary assets as collateral, the banks have been advised to waive margin/security requirements for agricultural loans up to Rs. 50000/-. The Government also announced a package for revival of cooperative credit structure. A major effort has been initiated for diversification of agriculture. National Horticulture Mission has been launched since the year 2005 for ensuring end-to- end approach with backward and forward linkages covering research, post harvest management, processing and marketing. Other initiatives taken by Government include expanding the area under irrigation, improved water management with watershed development and rain harvesting and establishment of National Rain-fed Area Authority. National Agricultural Insurance Scheme is being implemented with the objective of protecting the farmers against the crop losses occurring on account of natural calamities.

(b): No Sir.

(c): Government has taken adequate steps to provide funds to the needy and poor farmers at comparatively lower interest rates.

records.qtitle: PENDING IRRIGATION PROJECTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that several irrigation projects have been hampered due to financial crunch and various irrigation projects are pending for approvals;

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto and the steps being taken by the Union Government for earlier completion of all the ongoing irrigation projects within next two years;

(c) whether more than hundred irrigation projects of Maharashtra Government are pending with Union Government.;

(d) the reasons for the projects lying pending; and

(e) the steps taken or proposed to be taken for the clearance of pending irrigation projects of Maharashtra ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING

(SHRI M.V.RAJASEKHARAN)

(a) to (e): The responsibility of planning, funding and execution of irrigation projects primarily lies with the State Government concerned as irrigation is a State Subject. During IX Plan the expenditure in the irrigation sector was Rs 63,049 crore as against this the anticipated expenditure in the X Plan is Rs 1,04,524.39 crore which is 66 per cent higher than IX Plan expenditure.
During 2006-07 the Planning Commission accorded investment approval to 7 Major and Medium Irrigation projects of Maharashtra with an estimated cost of Rs 2914.20 crore and 1.78 lakh ha of cultural command area. No irrigation project of Maharashtra is pending in the Planning Commission for investment approval.

records.qtitle: JOINT OPERATION AGAINST LET .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether United States of America has offered any proposal for joint operations against Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT);

(b) if so, the details of proposal;

(c) whether it is a fact that Indian Government have rejected US offer of joint operations against LeT; and

(d) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for improving intelligence agencies while terrorists are using various innovative methods like internet terror, electronic money transfer for increasing terrorist activities in the country?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)


(a) No.

(b) & (c) Do not arise.

(d) The Government pursue a multi-dimensional approach to deal with terrorist activities. The Government have taken measures to enhance the capacity of the intelligence machinery to counter new methods being used by terrorists.

records.qtitle: SASAN ULTRA MEGA POWER PROJECT .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any evaluation committee, headed by HDFC`s Shri Deepak Parekh has recommended to remove Lanco Infratech from the Rs.16000 Crore Sasan Ultra Mega Power Project which has offered to supply power at rate of Rs.1.196 per unit;

(b) if so, the details of recommendations made by the said committee;

(c) Government`s response and reaction thereto;

(d) whether it is a fact that there were also some questions raised about the financial strength of Globeleq Singapore, which was the entity partnering Lanco Infratech; and

(e) if so, the details thereof and Government`s response thereto?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )


(a) : No, Sir. There is no such recommendation by evaluation committee.

(b) & (c) : Do not arise in view of (a) above.

(d) & (e) : Yes, Sir. However, the matter is under examination at this stage.

records.qtitle: OUT OF SCHOOL CHILDREN .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that more than 40 per cent of children in the age group of 6-14 are out of schools despite utilization of 86 percent fired of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan in the country;

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto and the reasons therefor;

(c) whether it is also a fact that there has been diversion of SSA funds as well as financial irregularities in many States;

(d) if so, Government`s reaction thereto and whether Government have taken any steps for effective supervision and monitoring of the SSA `scheme at both national and State levels; and

(e) how much funds have been utilized for children`s health from SSA scheme during the last three years and the details thereof ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M.A.A.FATMI)

(a) & (b) As per the reports from the States/UTs, the number of out of school children has come down to 70 lakhs as of April, 2006 which is less than 5% of the total children in the 6-14 years age group.

(c) In the light of the report on the Performance Audit of the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), submitted by the Comptroller & Auditor General of India in August 2006, for the period 2001-.02 to 2004-05, and the examination of the points raised therein by the Government of` India and State/UT SSA programmes, an amount of about Rs.53 crores can be classified as expenditure not covered under the SSA guidelines.

(d) The States/UTs have already been strictly instructed to avoid recurrence of such instances in future. Government of India is monitoring the use of SSA funds through annual State/UT audits, independent concurrent financial reviews and field monitoring through 41 social science institutions. In cases of diversion of funds for other educational purposes the Government of India has directed the concerned States to recoup the inadmissible expenditure to the State SSA programmes.
e) The SSA guidelines do not provide for a school health programme which is in the domain of the National Rural Health Mission.

records.qtitle: BLIND POPULATION IN THE COUNTRY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) what are the total number of blind population in the country and what are the numbers of the blind persons who would be cured in the country;

(b) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for elimination of blindness in the country;

(c) whether it is a fact that around 80 per cent of blind population lives in the rural areas;

(d) whether Government have fixed any target for elimination of blindness in the country upto 2015 with the help of W.H.O. and NGO’s in the country; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) & b) It is estimated that there are nearly 12 million blind persons in India and nearly 80% of blindness could either be prevented or cured. National Programme for Control of Blindness (NPCB) was launched in the year 1976 as a 100% centrally sponsored programme with the goal of reducing the prevalence of blindness. The following steps have been undertaken under the NPCB are 


 Setting up of State Blindness Control Societies in States / UTs
 Providing Eye Care facilities to the needy people at primary, secondary and 
Tertiary level through Primary Health Centers, District Hospitals, Institutes of 
ophthalmology.
 Strengthening of Eye Banks in govt / voluntary sectors.
 Financial support to NGOs for strengthening of their Infrastructure for Eye 
Care.
 Organizing Eye Donation Fortnight every year from 25 August to 8 September.
 Screening of School Children for detection of Refractive Error and providing 
Free Glasses to poor.
 Strengthening of Regional Institutes of Ophthalmology by providing assistance 
for development of pediatric eye units / low vision units / retina units and 
training infrastructure.
 Strengthening of Medical Colleges by providing assistance for development for 
Pediatric Eye Units / Low Vision Units / Retina units Imparting training to 
Ophthalmic Surgeons from Government Hospitals / Medical Colleges in various 
Specialities of ophthalmology for quality eye care
 Intensification of IEC activities to create awareness about eye care 
activities.




(c) 	Yes.


(d) & (e) 	The target fixed under National Programme for Control of 
Blindness is to reduce prevalence of Blindness from 1.1% (2001-04) to 0.3% by 
2020.

records.qtitle: SUGAR PACKAGE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether sugar industries as well as sugarcane-growers are facing severe problems since the last six months due to fall in prices of sugar;

(b) if so, the details thereof and Government`s response thereto;

(c) whether Government have announced any package of Rs. 850 crores for overcoming the problems of sugar industries and sugarcane-growers; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and how much of this package would be given to the sugarcane-growers?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH)


(a),(b),(c)&(d): The prices of sugar have declined mainly due to excess production of sugar in the current sugar season 2006-07 and expectations of higher sugar production in the next sugar season 2007-08 in the country, coupled with expected higher global surpluses. The ex-mill prices of sugar in the month of March, 2007 were lower by Rs.200-410 per quintal as compared to prices at the start of the sugar season i.e. in the month of October, 2006. The decline in sugar prices have constrained the capacities of sugar mills to pay cane price to sugarcane farmers. In order to ensure that over production of sugar does not lead to a situation of mounting cane price arrears, Government have decided:-

(i) to create a buffer stock of 20 lac tons for a period of one year (01.05.2007 to 30.04.2008) under which interest charges, insurance and warehousing charges for the quantity taken as buffer will be reimbursed to sugar factories. The cost of this subsidy is estimated to be Rs. 378 crores for one year. Further, banks would provide additional credit of Rs. 420 crores on creation of 20 lac tons of buffer. Thus, Rs.798 crores would be available with sugar factories to pay cane price to sugarcane farmers, for the sugar season 2006-07 including the cane price arrears of previous sugar seasons. The buffer subsidy and the additional credit are to be used exclusively for the payment of cane prices.


(ii) to provide export assistance to defray the internal transport and freight charges, marketing and handling charges at the flat rate of Rs.1350 per ton on export of domestically manufactured sugar from sugar factories situated in the coastal States and at the flat rate of Rs.1450 per ton from sugar factories situated in other than coastal States. Exports made under Open General License (OGL) only (and not under `advance license`) on or after 19th April 2007 and up to 18th April 2008 or till further orders, whichever is earlier, would be eligible for this assistance. Further, the amount so received is also to be used for cane price payment. The cost of export assistance is estimated to be Rs.205 crores.

(iii) to allow sugar exports under OGL without any quantitative ceiling.

records.qtitle: MISLEADING ADVERTISEMENTS BY BUILDERS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have come across large scale misleading advertisements promising the prospective buyers houses/flats with attractive facilities even without owning land;

(b) whether Government propose to issue any guidelines to regulate the builders and developers to refrain themselves from this practice so that the prospective buyers do not suffer losses;

(c) whether Government propose to deal firmly with the developers/builders who indulge themselves in such activities; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )

(a): No such information is available with this Ministry.

(b): The Government is considering formulation of draft Real Estate Management (Regulatory and Control) Bill.

(c)&(d): Construction activity is regulated by the Urban Local Bodies and Development Authorities etc. Therefore, the matter comes within the purview of the State Governments. Government is not considering to establish any statutory authority to deal with developers/builders etc.

records.qtitle: E OF PARTICIPATORY NOTES BY TERRORISTS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the inflow of Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) investment in the country are rising through Participatory Notes (PN) routes;

(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor;

(c) whether it is also a fact that some terrorist mafia organizations are using the Participatory Notes route in the country and misusing such investments in the Indian markets; and

(d) if so, the details of steps taken/proposed to be taken against erring financial institutes?
records.ans_text:
FINANCE MINISTER

( SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM )

(a) to (d): A Statement is placed on the Table of the House.

Position No. 6

Statement referred to in the reply to Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 306 by Shri Sanjay Raut, Member of Parliament, for 20th March 2007 regarding Misuse of Participatory Notes by terrorists

(a) & (b): As per information available with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the notional value of Participatory Notes (PNs) has increased from Rs. 1,17,325 crore in January 2006 to Rs. 2,02,487 crore in January 2007. The assets under management of Foreign Institutional Investors (Fils) increased from Rs. 3,84,491 crore to Rs. 5,81,087 crore during this period. The notional value of PNs as a percentage of assets under management of FIIs has increased from 30.5% to 34.8% during this period.

(c) The Securities and Exchange Board of India have informed that there is no evidence with them to support such a conclusion.

(d): There are systems and mechanisms in place to deal with different aspects of illegal flow of money. The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 as amended in September, 2004 has provisions to combat financing of terrorism. The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 1976 (FCRA), also regulates and monitors receipt and use of foreign funds by the recipients. The Foreign Exchange Management Act, (FEMA) has provisions to deal with cases of unauthorized transfer of foreign exchange including through hawala. The Prevention of Money Laundering Act and the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU-1ND) have also come into effect. The security and law enforcement and revenue agencies are sensitized from time to time to pursue an inter-agency approach to detect channels and use of funds received by terrorist groups.

At the international level, India is a member of Asia Pacific Group (APG) on Anti-Money Laundering and Combating of Financing of Terrorism and has Observer status in the Financial Action Task Force (FATF).

records.qtitle: SHORTAGE OF STAFF IN MEDICAL COLLEGES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a shortage of teaching staff in medical colleges of Maharashtra State;

(b) if so, the details thereof and the number of teaching staff seats which are vacant since the last two years; and

(c) what are the main reasons behind this and the action Government have taken to fill the vacant seats in medical colleges of Maharashtra State?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE

(DR. ANBUMANI RAMADOSS)

(a) As per inspections carried out by Medical Council of India (MCI) during 2006-07, there is shortage of teaching staff in the following medical colleges in Maharashtra.

1. Rajiv Gandhi Medical College, Thane

2. Dr. Panjabrao Allied Bhausaheb Deshmukh Memorial Medical College, Amravati.

3. Seth G.S. Medical College, Mumbai.

4. Maharashtra Institute of Medical Sciences & Research, Latur.

5. LTM Medical College, Mumbai. 6. K.J. Somaiya Medical College, Mumbai.

(b) & (c) This information is not centrally maintained Action to fill up vacancies of teaching staff is taken by the State Government. However, the Central Government informs the State Governments from time to time to filling up the vacancies.

records.qtitle: HINDUS IN PAKISTAN AND BANGLADESH .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government’s attention has been drawn towards press reports about the miserable plight of minority community of Hindus in Pakistan and Bangladesh; and

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto and the official number of Hindus residing in Pakistan and Bangladesh?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)

(a)-(b) Government are aware of media and other reports in Pakistan and Bangladesh on the condition of the Hindu minority in these countries. As per the census conducted by Government of Pakistan in 1998, there were 24,43,614 Hindus in Pakistan out of a total population of 13,23,52,279. According to National Report (Provisional) on the Population Census 2001, the number of Hindus in Bangladesh was 1,13,79,000, about 9.2% of the total population.

records.qtitle: MERGER OF D.A. WITH BASIC PAY FOR NTC EMPLOYEES
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the employees of National Textile Corporation have been allowed merger of 50 per cent of D.A with their basic pay, w.e.f. October, 2006, while Government had allowed such merger w.e.f. January, 2004;

(b) whether this belated decision of Board of N.T.C. has affected the interests of the employees of NTC badly; and

(c) if so, whether Government would consider grant of the merger of 50 per cent D.A. with the basic pay of the employees w.e.f. January, 2004, as has been done for all Central Government/PSUs employees, so as to cover the financial interests of the existing/retired employees?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES

(SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN)


(a) to (c): Government had allowed merger of 50 per cent DA with basic pay from 1.4.2004 to the CDA employees in Public Sector Undertakings(CPSUs). However, as per Deptt. of Public Enterprises orders dated 24.5.2005, such merger shall be allowed to employees of those Public Sector Undertakings that are not loss making and are in a position to absorb the additional expenditure on account of merger of DA with basic pay from their own resources without any budgetary support from the Government. Accordingly, the Board of Directors decided to implement these orders w.e.f. 1.10.2006 only, after reviewing the performance of the Company for the year 2005-2006.

records.qtitle: ACTIVITIES OF TERRORISTS IN NORTH EASTERN STATES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that terrorist groups of North-Eastern States are preparing to form a new country like Bangladesh;

(b) whether ULFA, Maoist and other terrorist groups have full control in North Eastern States of India;

(c) how many of them are active terrorist groups in the North-Eastern States; and

(d) what strict action Government had taken or propose to take against such terrorist organizations?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI S. REGUPATHY)

(a) to (d): A Statement is annexed.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1712 FOR 14.3.2007 RAISED BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT REGARDING ACTIVITIES OF TERRORISTS IN NORTH-EASTERN STATES.

a) There is no report to suggest that terrorist groups of North Eastern States are preparing to form a new country like Bangladesh.

b) According to reports, Maoists are not active in North Eastern States. Some terrorist outfits are operating in the North States.

c) Details of major militant outfits operating in North Eastern Region (State-wise) are as under:

Assam: United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA), National Democratic Front of Boroland (NDFB), Dima Halam Daogah (DHD) and its faction, and United People’s Democratic Solidarity (UPDS).

Manipur: There are approx. 23 militant groups divided on ethnic lines viz. Meiteis, Kukis, Nagas and Pangals.

Nagaland: National Socialist Council of Nagaland (NSCN) which is having two factions NSCN (IM) and NSCN (K) and Naga National Council.

Tripura: National Liberation Front of Twipra (NLFT) and All Tripura Tiger Force (ATTF).

Arunachal Pradesh: NSCN (IM) and NSCN (K) are active in two districts of Tirap and Changlang in Eastern Arunachal Pradesh adjoining Nagaland and Assam.

Meghalaya: Hynniewtrep National Liberation Council (HNLC) and Achik National Volunteer Council (ANVC).

d) The Government has taken various steps to control the separatist and terrorist activities in North Eastern States. These include, inter alia, deployment of Para-military Forces and Army in the State, coordinated action by Army, Para Military Forces and State Police for counter insurgency operations, declaration of insurgent groups as unlawful association under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, declaration of “disturbed area” under the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958, reimbursement of security related expenditure to the state Government and modernization/up-gradation of State Police Force. Regular review of the situation both at state and Central Government level is being made. A number of outfits in the North East have entered into Suspension of Operations (SoO) Agreement. Currently ceasefire/Suspension of Operations (SoO) is on with: National Socialist Council of Nagaland (NSCN), which is having two faction NSCN (IM) and NSCN (K), National Democratic Front of Boroland (NDFB), Dima Halam Daogah (DHD), and United People’s Democratic Solidarity (UPDS) and Achik National Volunteer Council (ANVC).

records.qtitle: IMPROPER BANKING POLICIES TOWARDS MICRO RURAL FINANCE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government`s attention has been drawn to the statement made by Noble Prize winner, Professor Mohammed Yunus, in which he criticized about our banking system and according to him suicidal, cases of poor farmers are growing only due to improper banking policies towards micro rural finance in our country;

(b) if so, what is Government`s reaction thereto; and

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government for improving banking system particularly for poor and needy persons in the country?:
records.ans_text:
(MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE) (SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) & (b) : The suicidal cases of poor farmers are happening due to many reasons, credit may be one of them.

(c) : An Institutional Credit delivery mechanism is already in place in India to extend credit to large number of borrowers including the poor. The reach of these institutions is being further increased through various policy measures by the Government/ RBI such as the Business Correspondent and Business Facilitator models and SHG-Bank Linkage Programme. It has been announced in the budget for 2007-08 that a Financial Inclusion Fund with NABARD will be formed for meeting the cost of developmental and promotional interventions for Financial Inclusion. Further, it has been announced to establish a Financial Inclusion Technology Fund to meet the cost of Technology adoption. Each fund will have an overall corpus of Rs.500 crore, with initial funding to be contributed by Central Government, RBI and NABARD.

records.qtitle: UNEMPLOYMENT OF ENGINEERS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of engineers unemployed from various branches of engineering like electronic, mechanical, civil, communications etc.;

(b) the reasons for such unemployment problems of such qualified engineers in the country and the details of the areas where our engineers are lagging behind the rest of the world ;

(c) whether Government are considering to evolve any programme to start finishing courses to improve skills for unemployed engineers through Internet;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SMT. D. PURANDESWARI)

(a) & (b): No central database is maintained regarding number of engineers unemployed from various branches of engineering. Unemployment of engineers may be due to various reasons including the demand pattern within and outside the country, which ‘inter alia’ depends upon performance of economy, particularly the manufacturing sector etc. Non-availability of qualified faculty and lack of adequate infrastructural facilities are some other factors, which have impact on the quality of education imparted in the Engineering Institutes.

(c) to (e): In order to impart communication and IT skills to engineering graduates as well as to brush-up their knowledge of core subjects so as to make them more employable in industry, it has been decided to start Finishing Schools, initially in seven National Institutes of Technology (NITs) at Jaipur, Kurukshetra, Durgapur, Warangal, Trichy, Calicut and Surathkal as well as at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Roorkee. The Finishing School courses will be organised during summer vacations for a period of 8 to 10 weeks. The Institutes would utilize their existing infrastructure for conducting these courses.

records.qtitle: INADEQUATE PROCESSING AND COLD STORAGE FACILITIES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the country wastes roughly $ 13 billion worth of farm products, including dairy items annually because of inadequate processing and cold storages facilities;

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto;

(c) whether some major players in the retail sector have made any requests like abolition of Agricultural Produce Marketing Commission Act to speed up growth in food processing industry;

(d) if so, the details thereof and Government’s reaction thereto; and

(e) the steps taken or proposed to be taken for reducing the distance between production and processing of food in the country?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES

(SHRI SUBODH KANT SAHAI)

(a) to (e): According to the report of M/s Rabo India Finance Pvt. Ltd., wastage of agricultural food items is estimated to be about Rs.58,000 crores occurring at various stages of handling after harvesting due to fragmented farming, provisions in Agricultural Produce Marketing (Development & Regulation) Act, lack of adequate post-harvest infrastructure such as lack of cold chain facilities, transportation, proper storage facilities, etc. The loss due to wastages could be reduced by a developed food processing industry, strengthening of the post-harvest infrastructure and filling the gaps in the supply chain.
A Vision 2015 on Food Processing Industries has been finalized by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries, which envisages, inter- alia, cluster based and demand driven farming, achieving integration of food processing infrastructure from farm to market, promoting a dynamic food processing industry which could result in trebling the size of the processed food sector by increasing the level of processing of perishables from 6% to 20%, value addition from 20% to 35% and share in global food trade from 1.5% to 3% by 2015. Under the Vision 2015, the thrust areas identified for strategic intervention are establishing Mega Food Parks, Modernization of abattoirs, Cold- chain/value addition and preservation infrastructure, capacity building by setting up of National Institute of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship & Management (NIFTEM), enacting Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, upgrading safety and quality of street food and establishment/upgradation of Quality Control Laboratories. Government has identified strategies along with a detailed action plan in this regard to realize the Vision 2015. An estimated investment of Rs.100,000 crores is required to achieve the Vision 2015.
Government has formulated and implemented several Plan Schemes to provide financial assistance for the establishment and modernization of food processing units, creation of infrastructure, support for R&D, human resource development besides other promotional measures to encourage development of food processing industries. In order to give boost to growth of FPI sector the Government has allowed in 2004-05, under Income Tax Act, a deduction of 100% of profit for five years and 25% of profits for the next five years in case of new agro processing industries set up to process, preserve and package fruits and vegetables. Excise duty of 16% on dairy machinery has been fully waived for promotion of dairy processing industries. Excise duty on meat, poultry and fish products has been reduced from 16% to 8%. Excise duty on food grade hexane used in edible oil industry has been reduced from 32% to 16%. In the Budget of 2005-06 excise duty of Rs.

1.00 per kg on refined edible oil and Rs. 1.25 per kg on vanaspati was abolished. Customs duty on refrigerated vans was reduced from 20% to 10%. In the Budget of 2006- 07, custom duty on packaging machines has been reduced from 15 per cent to 5 per cent, excise duty on condensed milk, ice cream, preparations of meat, fish and poultry, pectins, pasta and yeast has been fully exempted, excise duty on ready-to-eat packaged foods and instant food mixes, like dosa and idli mixes has been reduced from 16 per cent to 8 per cent, excise duty on aerated drinks has been reduced from 24 per cent to 16 per cent and excise duty on packaging paper has been reduced from 16 per cent to 12 per cent. Taxation has been lowered with a view to encourage the growth of Food Processing Industries. In Union Budget 2007-08, it has been proposed to reduce Excise Duty on Biscuits (with retail price not exceeding Rs.50/kg) and all types of food mixes including instant mixes to 0% from 8%. Customs Duty on Food Processing Machinery has been reduced from 7.5% to 5%. These measures are designed inter alia to promote and link processing with production.
According to a World Bank report, the existing Agricultural Produce Marketing (Development & Regulation) Act, restricts the farmers’ choice in selling their produce at the regulated markets limiting other marketing channels that could offer better returns to farmers. In some cases, ban on direct sale to processors and other bulk buyers leads to higher transaction cost. The Act also hinders greater private sector involvement in the construction and operation of wholesale markets in many States. On the basis of the suggested Model Act, various State Governments have initiated reforms in the agricultural marketing sector by suitably amending the respective State level Acts. The major reforms sought to be introduced include, inter-alia,

(i) enabling legal persons, growers and local authorities to establish new markets in any area,

(ii) removing the restriction on the growers to sell their produce only through existing regulated markets,

(iii) establishment of Direct Purchase Centres and Consumers’/ Farmers’ Markets for direct sale,

(iv) providing a separate provision for establishment of special markets for commodities like onions, fruits, vegetables, flowers etc., and

(v) introducing an institutional support mechanism to contract farming arrangements. The reforms would encourage a marketing regime, where there is fair competition, so that the farmers can gain from the options available and take their produce to the centres that offer the best prices and services. The contract farming arrangements will provide an effective method of linking small farm sector to agro-processing industry and to sources for extension advice, seeds, credit card to assured and profitable markets.

records.qtitle: RELIEF TO FARMERS UPON FAILURE OR DESTRUCTION OF CROPS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have made any provision at the ground level to provide immediate financial assistance or relief to the farmers in the event of failure or destruction of their crops so that the farmers are not compelled to commit suicide;

(b) if so, the comprehensive details thereof;

(c) whether it is a fact that in view of suicides being committed by the farmers, Government have decided to constitute any Agriculture Commission, so as, to provide immediate assistance to the farmers in the time of crisis; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR)

(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 161 FOR 09/03/2007 REGARDING RELIEF TO FARMERS UPON FAILURE OR DESTRUCTION OF CROPS.

(a) & (b): Agriculture being State subject, the State Governments are responsible for providing various services to farmers at the ground level including provision of relief in the events of failure or destruction of the crops. The Government of India supplements the efforts of the State Governments through various schemes, programmes and policies with financial and other support for the development of agriculture. Further, fund is readily available with the State Governments under the Calamity Relief Fund to enable them to take necessary relief measures in the wake of natural calamities resulting in destruction of crops. Government of India and State Governments concerned contribute to this Fund in the ratio of 3:1. Additional assistance over and above the Calamity Relief Fund is considered by Government of India from the National Calamity Contingency Fund for natural calamities of severe nature in accordance with the established procedure. Under the existing norms, assistance towards agricultural inputs subsidy is admissible to small and marginal farmers where crop loss on account of natural calamities is 50% and above at the rate of Rs.1000 per hectare for rainfed areas, Rs.2000 per hectare for irrigated areas and Rs.4000 per hectare for perennial crops. Input subsidy is also admissible to farmers, other than small and marginal farmers, in case of severe calamity occurring for a second consecutive year (or subsequent year) at the above rates and subject to certain conditions.

Government of India has also put a comprehensive credit policy in place for providing timely and adequate credit support to farmers to enable them to adopt modern technology and improved agricultural practices. The policy includes the following provisions to assist farmers. 

-	Debt restructuring in respect of farmers in distress and farmers in arrears 
providing for rescheduling of outstanding loans over a period of five years 
including moratorium of two years, thereby making all farmers eligible for fresh 
credit.


-	Banks are allowed to advance loans for redeeming the loans taken by farmers 
from private money lenders.
-	Simplified credit delivery mechanism through refinement of Kisan Credit Card 
scheme.



The rate of interest on crop loans up to a principal amount of Rs.3 lakhs has been 
reduced to 7% per annum with effect from kharif 2006-07.



	The National Agricultural Insurance Scheme is also under implementation with 
the objective to protect the farmers against the crop losses suffered on account of natural 
calamities.  Comprehensive risk insurance is provided to cover yield loss due to non-
preventable risks such as natural fire and lightening; Storm, Hailstorm, Cyclone, 
Typhoon, Tempest, Hurricane, Tornado, Flood Inundation and Landslide; Drought, Dry 
Spells; Pests/Diseases etc.



	In addition to the above, the Government of India has announced a rehabilitation 
package amounting to Rs.16,978.69 crore for 31 districts worst affected by farmers` 
suicides.


(c):	No, Sir.


(d):	Does not arise.

records.qtitle: GANGMEN DIED ON DUTY
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of gangmen died on duty due to train accidents, while actually repairing the railway tracks in the year 2005-06 and how many died in the current year;

(b) what precautions his Ministry proposes to save the precious life of gangmen while repairing railway track;

(c) how much compensation is paid to each gangman who dies, while working on railway track; and

(d) whether his Ministry give employment to one member of family of gangman who dies in the accident?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

( SHRI R. VELU )

(a): 183 Nos. Gangmen died on duty to train accidents in the year 2005-06 and 198 Nos. died in the current year while actually repairing the railway tracks.

(b): The following precautions are taken to contain accidents at work spots to save the precious lives of gangmen while repairing Railway track:- 
 

(i)   Introduction of visibility reflective safety jackets for the gangmen working on the 
track during the night.  

(ii)  Provision of remote operated hooters to give warning to working gangmen at all work sites. 

(iii) Mobile phone or Walkie-Talkie sets wherever necessary are being provided at work sites. 

(iv)  Posting of look-out men at all work sites where visibility is poor. 

(v)   At locations where night working is unavoidable, proper lighting arrangements 
are being made. 

(vi)  Provision of torches to all night Patrolmen/ Watchmen. 

(vii) Welding works and other important tracks works that require line block 
are being carried out under traffic line block. 

(viii)  Posting of competent Supervisors at all works sites to ensure safety. 

(ix)   In case of line, block works such as renewal of points and crossing etc., 
Caution orders are being issued for the trains passing on adjoining track to give 
whistle freely to alert the working gangmen. 
 


(c):   As per sections 124 and 124-A of the Railways Act, Compensation is payable to 
the dependents of passengers including Railway men on duty who are killed as 
a result of passenger train accidents or other untoward incidents.  The amount of 
compensation payable in case of death is Rs.4 lakhs.  Gangmen being Railway employees 
are entitled to compensation under the Workman’s Compensation Act.  However, 
they can claim compensation only under one of the above mentioned two Acts.



(d):   Yes, Sir. Railways give employment to one member of family of gangman who dies 
in the accident.

records.qtitle: PROBLEMS OF SUGARCANE GROWERS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering to make any short-term and long-term measures to address the problems faced by sugarcane growers and sugar industry;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government are also planning to make any long-term policy for production of ethanol and power through co-generation plants to facilitate Indian sugar industry to become a major player in global markets; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and by when it would be implemented?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH)

(a)&(b): The Government takes appropriate measures, as and when needed, to address the problems of sugarcane growers and sugar industry.

(c)&(d): The Government has drafted a National Policy on Bio-fuels, which includes bio-ethanol and bio-diesel, for promotion and use of bio-fuels on short, medium and long term basis in the country. As regards co-generation, the Government is implementing a programme for promotion of grid interactive power generation project based on Renewable Energy sources including surplus power generation from bagasse in the sugar mills.

records.qtitle: ALTERNATIVE ROUTE FOR KAILASH MANSAROVAR YATRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of pilgrims who visited Kailash-Mansarovar since last two years;

(b) whether Government have made any request to the Chinese Government for opening an alternative route for the Yatra through Ladakh, which would be shorter and more convenient to the Indian pilgrims; and

(c) if so, the details of response received from Chinese counterpart so far and the details of the steps taken by Government for opening of an alternative route for Kailash-Masarovar Yatra?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)


(a) 529 pilgrims performed the Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra in 2005, while 592 pilgrims undertook the Yatra in 2006.

(b)-(c) Government have proposed to the Chinese side, the opening of an alternative route to Kailash-Mansarovar through Demchok in Jammu and Kashmir. During the visit of the Chinese President Hu Jintao to India in November last year, the two sides agreed to explore the possibility of opening an additional route for the Yatra.

records.qtitle: DELAY IN ISSUING STUDENT VISAS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received many complaints about the inordinate delays in issuing student and research visas to the foreign students;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor and the number of requests of visas received at various Indian embassies during the last two years and the number of foreign students who got visa permissions so far; and

(c) the details of corrective steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government for issuing more student visas to the foreigners by implementing it in a transparent and simplified method?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI E. AHAMED)

(a) There have been a few instances of delay in issuing student and research visas by Indian Missions/Posts abroad.

(b) The delay in grant of student visas has mainly been due to foreign students not fulfilling the prescribed conditions concerning grant of student and research visa. The information on number of requests for student and research visas received at various Indian Missions during the last two years and the number of student and research visas granted is being collected from Indian Missions/Posts abroad and will be laid on the table of the House as early as possible.

(c) Government have recently liberalized grant of student visas. The liberalized provisions are given below:
i. Visa to be granted for admission in recognized/reputed educational institutions in India. ii. Visa co-terminus with the duration of the course or 5 years whichever is less. iii. No restriction on number of courses that can be pursued. iv. No restriction with respect to change of the course or institute or both. v. Student visa for industrial training/summer project/internship. vi. Waiver of the requirement of No Objection Certificate from Ministry of Human Resource Development. vii. Extendibility on the ground of clearing supplementaries.

records.qtitle: SLUGGISH DEVELOPMENT OF PMGSY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware of the sluggish development of Pradhan Mantri Gramin Sadak Yojana in various States;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor and the details of problems being faced by Government for such slow process of road development in the country; and

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for enhancing rural road connectivity within the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI CHANDRA SEKHAR SAHU)

(a) to (c) Under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY), projects valued at Rs. 42582.19 crore to connect 60556 habitations having 2,16,950.58 km road length have been approved and Rs. 21210.91 crore released. 33041 habitations have been provided connectivity, 111461.04 km of road length has been constructed. Expenditure incurred is Rs. 19040.95 crore. In some of the States the pace of implementation of Programme is slow because of the following reasons: 


?	Constraint of qualified and trained manpower.
?	Administrative delays including late award of projects.
?	Inadequate capacity of the Programme Implementing Units due to the smaller 
work load being handled by them earlier. 
?	A long rainy reason.
?	Non availability of construction materials such as cement, steel, bitumen, 
machinery, locally.
?	Long travel distances from one part to another within the State and also lack 
of excess discourages resources to reach these areas.
?	Non availability of land or the land falling under forest area.


Steps have been taken to improve the pace of implementation of the Programme 
through enhanced allocation of funds, training of field staff including contractor`s staff,  
providing interest free advance for procurement of required plants and machinery, 
continuous and regular monitoring of the programme.

records.qtitle: INCREASE IN UNEMPLOYMENT RATE
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Planning Commission has estimated that the unemployment rate for the economy as a whole shot up significantly during the last two years;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether employments even in the organised sector, declined between 2004 to 2006, in both the public and the private sector, particularly in Maharashtra;

(d) whether any concrete progamme of action has been considered by Government to provide more jobs in the country; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT

(SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES)

(a&b) As per two most recent quinquennial round of National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO) Reports on employment and unemployment, unemployment rate on Current Daily Status basis was estimated at 7.32% in 1999-2000 (55th round) which has gone up to 8.30% in 2004-05 (61st round).

(c) In the state of Maharashtra employment in organised sector has increased in the Private Sector whereas the employment in the Public Sector has shown declining trend between 2004 to 2005 as per latest available data. Detailed information for All India & Maharashtra is Annexed.

(d&e) Approach paper to the Eleventh Five Year Plan envisages creation of 70 million new work opportunities. Additional employment opportunities in the future will be generated mainly in services and manufacturing sectors and policy initiatives need to support this. Measures would need to be taken in the 11th Plan to boost, in particular, labour intensive manufacturing sectors such as food processing, leather products, footwear and textiles, and service sector such as tourism and construction.

records.qtitle: BANGLADESHI INTRUDERS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that more than two crore Bangladeshi intruders are living in our country and are enjoying every rights;

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto and the corrective steps taken or proposed to be taken against Bangladeshi intruders entering our country through Malda, Siliguri, Murshidabad, Dinazpur and North-East Region; and

(c) the details of steps taken by Government, so far with the help of concerned State Governments, to identify the Bangladeshi intruders in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a): According to available reports, Bangladeshi nationals have been using porous Indo-Bangladesh border to enter into India illegally. It is difficult to make a realistic estimate about the number of such illegal Bangladeshi immigrants because they enter surreptitiously and are able to mingle easily with the local population due to ethnic and linguistic similarities. However, there are reports that some of the illegal Bangladeshi migrants have managed to obtain ration cards, passports and voter identity cards, etc. The State Governments / UT Administrations are competent to deal with such cases, as and when detected, in accordance with the provisions of law.

(b) & (c): The State Governments/UT Administrations have been empowered under section 3 (2) (c) of the Foreigners Act, 1946 to detect and deport foreign nationals illegally staying in India. Administrative instructions are issued from time to time requesting the State Governments/UT Administrations to detect and deport illegal Bangladeshi migrants staying in the country.
Further, for the purpose of detection, prosecution and deportation of illegal migrants, the Government has implemented the Prevention of Infiltration of Foreigners (PIF) and Mobile Task Force (MTF) Schemes. In addition, the Government has taken various measures to check illegal infiltration. These measures, inter-alia, include round the clock surveillance of the borders by carrying out patrolling; upgradation of intelligence network and co-ordination with other intelligence agencies; erection of border fencing; riverine patrolling; and introduction of modern surveillance equipments including night vision devices.

records.qtitle: BILATERAL DEFENCE COOPERATION BETWEEN INDIA AND RUSSIA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether talks between India and Russia were held recently for strengthening bilateral defence cooperation;

(b) if so, the details thereof, alongwith the details of agreements signed between the two countries;

(c) whether Government have decided to access the Russian Global Navigation Satellite System (GLONASS); and

(d) if so, the details thereof and the salient features thereof? ANSWER (SHRI A.K. ANTONY)
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(a) Yes, Sir. The Sixth India-Russia Inter Governmental Commission on Military Technical Cooperation took place on 24.1.2007 in New Delhi.

(b) During the meeting both sides reviewed progress of the on-going bilateral defence cooperation and discussed various issues of mutual interest in the areas of defence and security. The following Agreement/Protocols were signed on conclusion of the meeting:-

(i)Inter Governmental Agreement on license production of RD-33 aero engines in India.

(ii)Protocol of Intent for co-development and co-production of Multi Role Transport Aircraft.

(iii)Protocol on the Sixth meeting of India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Military Technical Cooperation.

(c) & (d): During the recent visit of the President of the Russian Federation to India, the Governments of India and the Russian Federation signed two agreements with regard to access to the Russian Global Navigation Satellite System (GLONASS) data.

records.qtitle: RISE IN PERSONAL DEBT .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there has been a substantial rise in the personal debt, which is in the form of credit card outstanding balances, personal loans, vehicle loans, home loans etc. by our countrymen since last three years;

(b) if so, the details thereof and how much of :foreign amount has been borrowed by our countrymen as personal debt;

(c) whether Government in this regard sees any alarming and perilous situation in the future economy; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and Government`s response thereto?
records.ans_text:
FINANCE MINISTER

(SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM)

(a) to (d) : A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT FOR RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.114 FOR 6TH MARCH, 2007 REGARDING RISE IN PERSONAL DEBT TABLED BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT.

(a) & (b). Yes, Sir. The outstanding loans in the retail portfolio - comprising housing loans, loans for consumer durables, credit card receivables, auto loans and other personal loans - of all banks as on 31st March 2004, 2005 and 2006 are as under:- 
 

(Amount in Rs. crore)



Particulars		March-2004	March-2005	March-2006
Housing Loan		89,449		1,34,276	1,79,116
Loans for Consumer	6,256		3,810		4,469
Durables
Credit Card		6,167		8,405		12,434
Receivables
Auto Loans		NA		35,043		61,369
Other Personal Loans	87,170		85,077		1,18,351
	TOTAL		1,89,042	2,66,611	3,75,739

In terms of extant regulations, general permission is available to an 
individual resident in India to borrow from his / her close relatives outside 
India in such a manner that the amount outstanding at any given point of time 
does not exceed US$ 2,50,000/- or its equivalent, subject to the conditions 
that 
(i) the minimum maturity period of the loan is one year 
(ii) the 
loan is free of interest; and 
(iii) the amount of loan is received by 
inward remittance in free foreign exchange through normal banking channels or 
by debit to the Non-Resident External (NRE) / Foreign Currency Non-Resident 
(FCNR) account of the non-resident lender. Reserve Bank of India (RBI) does not 
collect data about such borrowings.



(c) & (d)  In its Third Quarter Review on Annual Statement on Monetary 
Policy for the year 2006-07, RBI has expressed concern over the continued high 
credit growth in the real estate sector, outstanding credit card receivables, 
loans and advances qualifying as capital market exposure and personal loans. 
Accordingly, RBI has taken prudential and regulatory measures including 
increasing the provisioning requirement and risk weights in respect of the 
aforesaid categories of loans and advances.

records.qtitle: VOCATIONAL TRAINING .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that our vocational training lags far behind the rest of the world and only 153 courses are recognised out of 2945 vocational courses offered round the globe;

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto; and

(c) whether Government are seriously considering to introduce career oriented new specialized vocational courses for getting more employment opportunities to the youth in various parts of the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI ARJUN SINGH)

(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 86 FOR ANSWER ON

5.03.07 ASKED BY SH. SANJAY RAUT REGARDING VOCATIONAL TRAINING

(a) & (b) Vocational training is dealt with by Ministry of Labour and Employment whereas vocational education at the higher secondary stage is dealt with by Ministry of Human Resource Development (HRD). Vocational training is being imparted in 153 designated trades in public and private sector establishments in our country under the Apprenticeship Training Scheme of the Ministry of Labour and Employment. Director General of Employment and Training of the Ministry of Labour deals with the Craftsmen Training Scheme in 107 trades implemented through a network of Industrial Training Institutes/Centres (ITIs)/(ITCs) in the country. ITIs also imparts multi-skill courses in 20 industrial sectors.

At the Higher Secondary stage ( 11th and 12th classes), vocational streams are offered by several schools. Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Vocationalisation of Secondary Education, competency-based curricula have been developed for 82 vocational courses. Under the Skill Development Initiative of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, 156 short-term modular employable courses have been developed through public-private partnership. As per NSSO Report of 2004-05 only 2% persons of 15-29 age group in India are reported to have received vocational training, and another 8% are reported to have received non-formal vocational training. According to a report “Evaluation of the Scheme of Vocationalisation of Secondary Education” prepared by Operation Research Group

(ORG) in September, 1996 the share of students of vocational schools at the higher secondary stage in India was 4.8%. According to the findings of a joint World Bank – ILO Study Report on ‘”Skills and change: A synthesis of findings of a Multi Country Study of vocational Education and Training Reforms”, the Vocational-Technical Secondary Education track share for some of the countries are given –

Tanzania                    65
