Egypt                       68


(c)     Ministry of Labour and Employment has informed that
new  career oriented courses are introduced by the Director
General  of Employment and Training from time to  time   to
make  the youth in the country more employable.  Similarly,
new  vocational  courses are added at the Higher  Secondary
level from time to time based on the need.

records.qtitle: AIR CONDITIONED BOGIES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering to facilitate all mail and express trains bogies with air-conditioned facility;

(b) if so, by when Railways could provide such A/C facilities to all the passengers of mail/express trains in the country;

(c) whether it is a fact that minimum 10 to 15 years time would be required for providing such facilities to the commuters; and

(d) if so, the reason therefor ?
records.ans_text:
(MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS)


(SHRI R VELU)


(a) No, Sir.


(b) to (d) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: PENDING RAIL PROJECTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that rail projects worth thousand of crore rupees have been pending with his Ministry for years together;

(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that his Ministry has constituted a high-power Committee to review these projects; (

(c) if so, the names of the projects lying pending over past several years; and

(d) by when these projects would be implemented?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R. VELU)

(a) : Railways have a huge throwforward of projects requiring over Rs.54,000 crore for completion. The funds are limited and projects are being progressed as per the availability of resources keeping in view the operational requirements and other considerations.

(b): Yes, Sir. An Empowered Committee has been constituted to review progress of works costing more than Rs.100 crore.

(c): The names of the ongoing projects is given in the Budget Documents.

(d): It is not feasible to give definite time schedule for completion of ongoing projects. However, a number of initiatives have been taken to generate non-budgetary resources through cost sharing with States, Public-Private Partnership, Defence Funds and National projects to expedite completion of these projects.

records.qtitle: PROGRAMMES TO CONTROL POPULATION GROWTH .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any specific time-bound programmes have been identified by Government recently with the help of experts to deal with the population growth in our country;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government have given any response recently towards notice issued by the Hon’ble High Court/Supreme Court regarding implementation of two child norm for containing population growth in the country; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE

(DR. AMBUMANI RAMADOSS)

(a) and (b): The Government has launched the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) on 12th April, 2005 throughout the country with special emphasis on 18 States with week demographic and health indications. More attention is being paid to these States to provide accessible, affordable, accountable, effective, reliable, and quality primary health care, through creation of a cadre of Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHA), improved hospital care measured through Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS), decentralization of programme to district level to improve intra and inter-sectoral convergence and effective utilization of resources. The NRHM provides for a thrust on population stabilization as well. Special efforts to deal with population growth, in line with the National Population Policy is being attended under NRHM in the following manner: Improvement in functioning of Public health facilities at all levels to meet unmet demands for Family Planning. Quality family welfare services under the RCH-II component of NRHM. Intensive campaign for creating awareness, especially with the help of ASHAs Provision for additional manpower and service guarantees at all levels of health facilities. Training of Medical Officers/ANMs/Nurses in still upgradatiion for providing salary planning services.

(c) and (d): Yes, Sir. The notice of Writ Petition NO. 23/2004 filed by the Azadi Bachao Andolan and another versus UOI and other in the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India has been received. The Writ Petition is regarding Population growth and implementation of National Population Policy, 2000.

records.qtitle: RECOMMENDATION FROM INVESTMENT COMMISSION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received any recommendations from the Investment Commission for organizing and hosting large sporting events in the country;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government are considering to accept their suggestions and recommendations for all-round development of infrastructure facilities through sporting events in the country; and

(d) if so, the details of the steps taken or proposed to be taken in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ, YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS AND DEVELOPMENT OF NORTH EASTERN REGION

(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) The Investment Commission, while making suggestions for enhancing growth, has recommended hosting of mega sporting events in India which will focus the country`s attention on infrastructure development while also building national pride.

(c) & (d): No specific decision has been taken on this as a matter of policy. However, it has already been decided to hold the Commonwealth Games in Delhi in 2010, for which necessary sports and other infrastructure facilities are being developed. As a part of this the Commonwealth Youth Games will also be held in 2008 in Pune. India has also bid for hosting the Asian Games, 2014 in Delhi, on which a decision will be taken by the Olympic Council of Asia later in the year.

records.qtitle: DEVELOPMENT OF SHIPPING INDUSTRY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of programmes made by Government for development and modernization of ports, shipping, shipyards, and inland navigation since the last two years by harnessing the long coastline of our country;

(b) whether Government have decided for public-private partnership projects in the port sector; and

(c) if so, the details thereof and the steps proposed for the development of shipping industry in view of the increasing growth rate of exports?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

(SHRI T.R. BAALU)

(a) to (c): The Department of Shipping has formulated the National Maritime Development Programme (NMDP) with the objective of upgrading and modernizing India’s maritime infrastructure, keeping in view India’s fast growing economy and increasing share in the international trade. Under the Programme, to be taken up for implementation in phases over a defined period, a total of 387 specific projects have been identified. Total investment involved under the Programme is Rs.1,00,339 crores. Out of this, Rs. 55,804 crores is for the Major Ports and the balance is for the Shipping and Inland Water Transport Sectors. In the Major Ports, 276 projects covering entire gamut of activities, namely construction/upgradation of berths, deepening of channels, rail/road connectivity projects, equipment upgradation/modernization schemes and other related schemes for creation of backup facilities have been identified to be taken up for implementation over the period upto 2011-12 under the said Programme. Out of Rs.55,804 crores envisaged for the Major Ports, Rs.34,505 crores is expected from private sector mainly in commercially viable projects like development and operation of berths, terminals, etc. Thus, public private partnership will be a significant mode for implementing the Programme in the Major Ports. In the Shipping Sector, a total of 111 projects involving total investment of Rs.44,535 crores over a period of 20 years have been identified for inclusion in the Programme. The activities covered under the Programme include tonnage acquisition, maritime training, coastal shipping, aids to navigation, shipbuilding and building up of Inland Water Transport (IWT) infrastructure.

records.qtitle: DELAY IN GOLDEN QUADRILATERAL PROJECTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that many projects like Golden Quadrilateral highway projects run through National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) were delayed and running very late;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

(c) the details of corrective steps taken or proposed to be taken by his ministry for improving the situation;

(d) whether Government are considering to run highway projects through involving public private partnership on the country; and

(e) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

(SHRI K.H. MUNIYAPPA)

(a) & (b) There has been some delays in the completion of a few contracts pertaining to Golden Quadrilateral, due to problem associated with acquisition of land, shifting of utilities, difficulty in environment and forest clearances, poor performance of some contractors and termination of some contracts etc.

(c) The steps taken to expedite the projects is at Annexure-I

(d) & (e) Yes, Sir. It has been decided to award National Highways Development Project contracts on BOT basis (either based on Toll or Annuity) as far as possible.

ANNEXURE-I

ANNEXURE REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (c) OF RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 363 FOR ANSWER ON 1ST MARCH, 2007 ASKED BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT REGARDING DELAY IN GOLDEN QUADRILATERAL PROJECTS.

The following steps have been taken to ensure early completion of the project:-

(a) The Contracts are regularly monitored at various levels such as by Supervision Consultants/Project Directors, Senior Officers of National Highways Authority of India. Progress reviews are also held at the level of Chairman, National Highways Authority of India, Secretary, Department of Road Transport & Highways and the Minister, Shipping, Road Transport & Highways.

(b) State Governments have appointed senior officers as nodal officers for resolving problems associated with implementation of the National Highways Development Project such as land acquisition, removal of utilities, forest/pollution/environment clearances etc. These nodal officers hold periodic meetings to review the projects and take action to resolve the problems.

(c) A Committee of Secretaries has been constituted under Cabinet Secretary to address inter-ministerial and Centre-State issues such as land acquisition, utility shifting, environment approvals, clearance of Road Over Bridges etc.

(d) The procedure of issue of Land Acquisition notifications has now been simplified.

(e) To expedite the construction of Road Over Bridges, an officer of the Railways has been posted to National Highways Authority of India to coordinate with Ministry of Railways. Memorandum of Understanding has been signed with M/s IRCON for construction of some of the Road Over Bridges.

(f) Action has been taken against non-performing contractors and they are not allowed to bid for future projects unless they improve the performance in existing contracts.

(g) Steps have been taken to improve cash flow problems of contractors by granting interest bearing discretionary advance at the request of contractor, release of retention money against bank guarantee of equal amount, deferment of recovery of advances (on interest basis) and relaxation in minimum Interim Payment Certificate (IPC) amount.

records.qtitle: INVESTMENT IN RURAL INFRASTRUCTURE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have taken any initiatives for the development of rural infrastructure by bringing huge investments in rural areas by 2010; and

(b) if so, the details thereof by indicating various schemes and policy made by the Planning Commission so far for the infrastructure development in rural areas by making it transparent and accountable in the country, particularly in Maharashtra State?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING

(SHRI M.V.RAJASEKHARAN)

(a): Yes, sir.

(b): The Government has launched Bharat Nirman programme as a four-year plan to build infrastructure in rural areas with identified physical targets for completion by 2009. The estimate of total expenditure for the Bharat Nirman has been assessed as about Rs 1,76,000 crore. Bharat Nirman has six components, namely, irrigation, roads, water supply, housing, rural electrification and rural telecom connectivity. In each of these areas targets to be achieved by 2009 are as below.

(i) To bring additional one crore hectares under assured irrigation.

(ii) To connect all villages that have a population of 1000(or 500 in hilly/tribal areas) with road.

(iii) To construct 60 lakhs additional houses for the poor.

(iv) To provide drinking water to the remaining 74000 habitations that are uncovered.

(v) To reach electricity to the remaining 1,25,000 villages and offer electricity connection to 2.3 crore households.

(vi) To give telephone connectivity to the remaining 66,822 villages.

The details of names of schemes under which the respective Ministries assist the states are as below. The schemes are formulated and got implemented through the states by the respective Ministries.

				Ministry concerned

				Water Resources 


2.Roads				Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana- Ministry of Rural 
				Development 


3.Housing			Indira Awaas Yojana- Ministry of Rural Development


4.Drinking Water  
including water quality		Accelerated Rural Water Supply Programme- 
				Department of Drinking Water Supply , Ministry of 
				Rural Development

  

5.Electrification		Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidhyutikaran Yojana- Ministry 
				of Power


6.Telephone connectivity	Universal Service Obligation fund –Ministry of 
				Telecommunication



The entire Bharat Nirman Programme has been web enabled with details of the 
individual schemes, statewise, including Maharashtra, with the physical and 
financial status being updated in the web site of Bharat Nirman. The Committee on 
Rural Infrastructure chaired by the Prime Minister (in which the Deputy Chairman 
Planning Commission is the Member –Convener) is monitoring Bharat Nirman 
programme.

records.qtitle: DEMANDS FROM CO OPERATIVE BANKS IN MAHARASHTRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether his Ministry has received any demands from Co-operative Banks, particularly from Maharashtra; and

(b) if so, the detail of their demands and response thereto?
records.ans_text:
(MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE)

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) & (b) : Government has been receiving references from individuals, Hon’ble Members of Parliament and Cooperative Banks etc. on an on going basis from different parts of the country including Maharashtra on different aspects of Banking. The appropriate action is taken as per norms in consultation with NABARD, Reserve Bank of India and other banks involved within the permissible policies of the respective banks.

Further, concerned with the need to strengthen the rural cooperative credit institutions, the Government of India constituted a task force under the chairmanship of Prof. A Vaidyanathan, Based on the discussions held with the State Governments on the recommendations of the Vaidyanathan Committee report and also such other feedback: received, Government had approved a revival package for revival of short term cooperative credit structure subject to certain legal and institutional reforms to be initiated by State Govts. The States willing to implement the package are required to sign an MoU with Central Government and NABARD. State of Maharashtra is among the nine states which had already signed the MoU.

records.qtitle: TRAINING FOR LANDING IN POOR VISIBILITY CONDITIONS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of flights of all the airlines operating in the country which were forced to land at another airport due to bad visibility because of dense fog during the last two years;

(b) whether it is a fact that many pilots of private airlines do not have proper and adequate training facility to land the aircrafts in bad visibility due to fog in winter season;

(c) the details of number of pilots in each airline who have not had this training; and

(d) the action Government propose to take in this regard against the airlines?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )

(a) The number of flights of private scheduled airlines diverted to land at another airport due to fog etc. in the year 2005 and 2006 are 145 and 263 respectively.

(b) & (c) Private Airlines have been training their pilots regularly for Low Visibility Operations. The number of pilots who have not had ILS CAT- II/ III Training are as under:

In Jet Airways-512, Sahara Airlines Limited-200, Kingfisher Airlines Limited-162, Air Deccan-314, Spicejet Airlines-60, Indigo Airlines-43 and Go Airways-34.

(d) Airlines have been directed not to roster their CAT-III trained pilots on internatinal routes during the fog season.

Only such pilots who are CAT II/ III qualified, are approved as Instructor/ Examiner so as to ensure that more trained pilots are available for CAT-II/ III operations during low visibility conditions.

The Airlines are encouraged to upgrade their aeroplanes and train their pilots for operations in low visibility conditions. Their flight schedules are approved on the basis of number of pilots trained by the operators for low visibility operations and the suitability of the planes for such operations. If the operator can not provide data for their capability to fly under low visibility, they are not allowed to schedule their flights during normal fog hours.

records.qtitle: NEW COMPANY AGENCY FOR POWER PLANT EQUIPMENT .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering to establish one more power company/agency for producing power plant equipments or achieving Ministry`s ambitious Mission 2012 – Power for all;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor and the details of the steps taken or proposed to be taken for getting required power plant equipments at affordable cost and environment friendly?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )

(a) to (c) : NTPC is exploring the possibility of entering into a strategic partnership with Transformers and Electricals Kerala Ltd. (TELK), a Government of Kerala owned Public Sector Undertaking engaged in manufacturing of Transformer and allied electric equipment and services related thereto. In this regard, an Expression of Interest has been signed with TELK on 18th August, 2006. A joint working group, comprising representative from NTPC Ltd., TELK and Government of Kerala has been constituted to carryout the due-diligence.

records.qtitle: DEVELOPMENT OF GARBAGE BASED POWER PLANT BY APTDC .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Andhra Pradesh Technology Development and Promotion Centre (APTDC) has developed a big power plant based on use of garbage and Municipal Solid Waste in Andhra Pradesh since last more than three years;

(b) if so, the details thereof and how many such solid waste based projects are running in the country;

(c) whether Government are considering to promote such innovative power generation projects in various towns and cities with the help of APTDC; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and if not the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY

(SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR)

(a)&(b): Andhra Pradesh Technology Development and Promotion Centre (APTDC) has extended technical support to industries for setting up of two power projects of 6.6 MW and 6 MW at Hyderabad and Vijayawda. These projects are based on power generation from Refuse Derived Fuel (RDF) produced from Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) at processing plants of 700 tonnes per day capacity at Hyderabad and 500 tonnes per day capacity each at Guntur and Vijayawada.

(c)&(d): Government is implementing an Accelerated Programme on Energy Recovery from Urban Wastes which provides for financial and promotional incentives for setting up of projects on Energy Recovery from Municipal Solid Wastes. Under this Programme, power projects based on production of RDF from MSW are eligible for capital subsidy of upto Rs.1.5 crore per MW. APTDC can extend technical support to such projects for processing of MSW for power generation. However, no further projects could be supported on account of a stay by Hon’ble Supreme Court of India on further subsidies by Government for projects on energy recovery from MSW.

records.qtitle: DAMS BUILT FOR IRRIGATION OF VIDHARBHA REGION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any special scheme has been made to utilize more water of the dams built for the irrigation of Vidharbha region in Maharashtra;

(b) if so, the names of such schemes; and

(c) what steps have been taken to provide maximum benefits of these schemes to the farmers of Vidharbha?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

(SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV)

(a) The Government of Maharashtra has informed that any specific scheme to utilize more water of the dams for irrigation of Vidharbha region in Maharashtra has not been prepared. However, as per the information provided by the Government of Maharashtra 15 major, 37 medium, 13 ERM and 156 minor irrigation projects / schemes are under implementation. 8 major, 9 medium and 65 minor irrigation schemes of Vidharbha region are included in the Rehabilitation Package for the Farmers in agrarian distressed districts.

(b) & (c) Do not arise.

records.qtitle: PURCHASE OF BIO DIESEL .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that PSU Oil Companies could not purchase bio-diesel product since last one year;

(b) if so, what are the reasons behind non-procuring of bio-diesel;

(c) whether Government are considering to provide direct financial help to the bio-diesel producer-farmers;

(d) if so, the details in this regard; and

(e) if not, what are the main reasons in this regard?
records.ans_text:
Minister of State in the MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS

(SHRI DINSHA PATEL)

(a) & (b): Yes, Sir. Public Sector Undertaking, Oil Marketing Companies have not been able to purchase bio-diesel at the idientified purchase centres so far, as the parties who have expressed interest are not willing to supply at the declared price. Facilities are not yet ready with other parties who have expressed their interest.

(c) to (e): The Ministry of Rural Development has proposed to launch a National Mission on Bio-diesel, which is to be implemented in two phases i.e. Phase-I as Demonstration Project and Phase-II, a self-sustaining expansion of Bio-diesel Programme. Under the Demonstration phase of the Mission, plantations of Tree Borne Oilseeds (TBOs) like jatropha and pongamia would be taken up essentially on degraded forest lands and wastelands belonging to the village communitics/panchayats/government. It is not contemplated to involve private land owners/farmers in the mission activities at this stage. Since there is no reliable and tested database on various aspects of jatropha cultivation and costs and returns involved, Research & Development (applicable to both planting and processing), would also be an important and significant component of the Demonstration Phase.

records.qtitle: ACCOMMODATION FOR WOMEN IN URBAN AREAS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether many working women are facing problems in getting accommodations in urban cities;

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto; and

(c) the details of measures taken by Government to setup more hostels for working women in the country so that they can feel a secured atmosphere?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY)

(a) Yes, Sir. Many working women are in need of hostel accommodation in urban cities.

(b)&(c) Ministry of Women and Child Development has been implementing a scheme of Assistance for Construction/Expansion of Hostel Accommodation for Working Women since 1972-73. 873 hostels have been sanctioned so far under the Scheme all over the country with a capacity of 63281 women. The Scheme is proposed to be revamped and expanded in the 11th Five Year Plan (2007-2012).

records.qtitle: REGULATORY AUTHORITY FOR BIO TECHNOLOGY SECTOR .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government. are considering to set up an independent regulatory authority to bolster biotechnology sector for increasing more investment in the country;

(b) if so, by when it will be set up; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY AND MINISTER OF OCEAN DEVELOPMENT


(KAPIL SIBAL)


(a), (b)& (c) Yes, Sir. The Ministry of Agriculture & Cooperation had submitted a Note for Cabinet for setting up of National Bio-technology Regulatory Authority (NBRA) and resubmitted a revised Note for Cabinet after the proposal was considered by the Committee of Secretaries (COS). The Ministry of Agriculture & Cooperation is taking necessary follow up as per the recommendations of COS. Therefore no specific time frame can be committed at this moment.

records.qtitle: AVAILABILITY OF STEEL AND COKING COAL .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of special efforts taken or proposed to be taken by Government for increasing availability of steel and coking coal in the country;

(b) whether it is a fact that any high power committee has submitted any report for boosting the availability of coking coal for the steel companies;

(c) if so, the details of recommendations made by the committee; and

(d) Government`s response thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE

(DR. AKHILESH DAS) IN THE MINISTRY OF STEEL

(a) As per the National Steel Policy entrepreneurs in the country are free to set up steel plants and downstream units of the capacities of their choice based on their commercial judgments. In a free market economy, Government acts only as a facilitator. The Government has taken several steps to increase the production of steel such as modernization and expansion of public sector steel plants and adoption of various policy measures to encourage creation of additional steel production capacity in the private sector. Various companies are on the look out for strategic alliances for ensuring raw material

(coking coal, iron ore) supplies, according to their corporate strategies.

(b)to(d) Yes, Sir. A Committee under the chairmanship of Director (Fin.), RINL has submitted a Report for securing coking coal supplies for SAIL & RINL. The Boards of these companies are yet to take a view on the proposals contained in the Report, and if Government approvals are required, these would be formally processed after the companies take a view on the recommendation of the Committee.

records.qtitle: MEDICINE FROM AFEEM .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that two pharma companies have been given licenses to make medicines from Afeem;

(b) if so, the reasons for giving such licenses to private companies;

(c) whether in view of the increasing demand of medicines made from opium there is any plan to expand the opium and alkaloid factories situated in Neemuch in Madhya Pradesh and Ghazipur in Uttar Pradesh; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE (SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) to (d) Afeem is a synonym of the term Opium which is Narcotic Drug and used in the production of Alkaloids such as Morphine, Codeine etc.
The production of Opium is under the control of Government of India and there are two Government Opium and Alkaloid factories in the country, one is located at Ghazipur in Uttar Pradesh and the other one is at Neemuch in Madhya Pradesh.
The Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance is examining the feasibility of permitting pharma companies to produce Alkaloids/APIs from Opium after obtaining the Opium from Government Opium and Alkaloids works.

records.qtitle: FINANCIAL CRISIS IN STATES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that various State Governments are unable to spend much on social and infrastructure development of their respective State as they are facing acute financial crisis;

(b) if so, Government`s reaction thereto; (

(c) whether Government are considering any structured and transparent approach to lessen the burden to debt on various States so they can increase their expenditure and investments on infrastructure and social sectors like power, irrigation, roads, tourism, rural development etc;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING

(SHRI M.V. RAJASEKHARAN)

(a) & b): No, Sir. Does not arise

(c) to e): Yes Sir, In order to lessen the debt burden of the States, they have been provided with incentives to enact Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act with specific annual targets with a view to eliminating the revenue deficit by 2008-09 and reducing fiscal deficits based on a path for reduction of borrowings and guarantees. Enacting of FRBM Act on stipulated lines makes a State eligible for debt relief. The Central loans to States contracted till 31.3.2004 and outstanding on 31.3.2005 are to be consolidated and rescheduled for a fresh term of 20 years resulting in repayment in 20 equal installments at a lower interest rate of 7.5%.
A debt write-off scheme linked to the revenue deficit of States has also been envisioned. Under the scheme repayments due from 2005-06 to 2009-10 on Central loans contracted up to 31.3.2004 and recommended to be consolidated, will be eligible for write-off.

records.qtitle: LACK OF DRINKING WATER AND SANITATION FACILITIES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that more than 50 per cent of our country does not have toilets and 80 per cent of all the diseases and ailments are occurring owing to lack of safe drinking water and sanitation;

(b) if so, Government`s response and reaction thereto; and

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for improving this ill and unwanted situation in the country by 2010 ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRIMATI SURYAKANTA PATIL)

(a) & (b) Yes, Sir. As per 2001 Census, 63.6% households in the country do not have toilets. In the rural area, 78.1% of the families do not have toilets. Lack of access to safe drinking water and sanitation facility is cause of several diseases but its exact share in overall diseases in the country is not available. To improve the sanitation coverage, Total Sanitation Campaign (TSC) has been launched in 1999 and it is planned to achieve 100% coverage of rural households by the end of Eleventh Plan. TSC aims to ensure full sanitation coverage in all villages in the country with the help of State Governments and local Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). TSC projects are sanctioned district-wise, and entire rural areas of a TSC project district are covered under the programme. At present, this programme has been taken up in 569 districts in the country.

(c) Government has taken various initiatives to increase rural sanitation coverage, which include scaling up TSC projects in all districts of the country, increased budgetary allocation for TSC, launching of incentive-cum-reward scheme, Nirmal Gram Puraskar for Panchayati Raj Institutions, awareness generation activities and capacity development of different stakeholders etc. As per revised TSC guidelines issued in March 2006, by the Government of India, Solid and Liquid Waste Management has been included as a component of TSC and up to 10% of the total project cost can be utilized for this purpose. Provision has been made for APL families who need assistance by providing soft loan through `Revolving Fund` mechanism for construction of toilets. To increase the speed of providing sanitation facilities in schools and Anganwadi centres, requirement of community contribution for construction of toilets in the schools and Anganwadi centres have been removed. Efforts are being made to develop convergence with NRHM and SSA authorities for awareness creation and hygiene education among the people and children in the rural areas.

records.qtitle: HELP OF PRIVATE SECURITY AGENCIES FOR GATHERING INFORMATION ABOUT TERRORIST ACTIVITIES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Ministry has taken decision to take the help of Private Security agencies, working in the country, to collect secret information regarding the terrorist activities in the country;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether it is also a fact that all Government intelligence agencies are grossly inadequate to collect such vital information about terrorist activities; and

(d) how many ex-servicemen are working in the private security agencies in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a): No, Sir.

(b): Does not arise in view of (a) above.

(c): The Government intelligence agencies are capable of detecting information on terrorists.

(d): Government does not compile such data.

records.qtitle: SEARCHING OF SARASWATI RIVER BY ONGC .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that ONGC has taken the responsibility for searching the Saraswati river and its pure water resources, lost deep into the ground thousands of years ago in water crisis ridden western Rajasthan area;

(b) if so, the detailed information of the same with Government, so far;

(c) whether Government want to take the help of ONGC for searching the water resources of various rivers of the country which become extinct in the past; and

(d) if so, by when?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

(SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV)

(a)&(b) Yes, Sir. ONGC has undertaken a project titled “ONGC Project Saraswati”. It is an initiative to contribute to the welfare of the people in drought prone areas of Western Rajasthan, by providing safe drinking water. Based on satellite imagery by ONGC, it was found that a few thousand years ago the river flowed from Northeastern side to Southwestern direction before disappearing into the desert. The Project is focused on identification of deeper aquifers, otherwise not tapped by agencies such as State groundwater departments and Central ground water bodies. It is planned to drill deep tubewells down to 1000 metres below ground level at several places in Jaisalmer, Barmer and Bikaner districts. The operational activities in the project have been entrusted by ONGC to WAPCOS.

(c)&(d) So far there is no proposal in MOWR/Central Ground Water Board to take the help of ONGC for searching the water resources of various rivers of the country which became extinct in the past.

records.qtitle: RESEARCH INNOVATIONS IN THE COUNTRY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that thousands of new innovations and research technology invented by our scientists could not reach at the grass root level, particularly rural areas;

(b) if so, the reasons therefore; and

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government for adopting people friendly approach for developing rural areas by carrying such research innovations in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY AND MINISTER OF EARTH SCIENCES

(KAPIL SIBAL)

(a) No Sir.

(b) Does not arise.

(c) The government has been proactively engaged in developing, adopting and disseminating people friendly technologies for rural areas with the involvement of NGOs, academic institutions, local bodies and community. Various government departments and agencies such as Department of Science & Technology, Department of Biotechnology, Indian Council of Agricultural Research, Council of Scientific & Industrial Research, Council for Advancement of People`s Action and Rural Technology, have taken many initiatives, including support for innovations. Women Technology Parks (WTP), Rural Technology Parks (RTP), Rural Technology Centres (RTC) and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVK) have been set up in rural areas for developing and disseminating location specific science and technology based solutions to local problems. Innovative projects involving development of field level technological interventions, which are capable of making a difference to rural life, are supported on regular basis by the government. Some examples of such interventions are: (1) development of rural technologies like solar drier for fish, portable cookers using briquette made of biomass, modified multipurpose water mills, small biogas plants, etc. (2) during the last one year, the KVKs (in 540 rural districts) have conducted 1318 on-farm trials to identify the location specificity of technology under various farming systems, organized 33,942 frontline demonstrations to establish its production potential on farmers’ fields, and 37,963 training programmes with participation of 8.4 lakh farmers and 84,925 extension personnel. The KVKs produced 5322.5 tonnes of seeds and 52.2 lakh planting material, besides 233.2 lakh livestock strain/fingerlings for its availability to the farmers, and (3) 670 units of ultra-filtration membrane based water filters, based on the technology developed by a Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR) laboratory, have been installed in different rural areas for providing virus-free clean drinking water.

records.qtitle: DISTRIBUTION OF ANSWER SHEET COPIES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering to instruct all higher education bodies to provide photocopies of answer-sheets to the graduate students in the country, by charging them a nominal charge;

(b) if so, the details thereof and by when it will be started by fulfilling the long standing demand of students and their parents; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor ? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SMT. D. PURANDESWARI )

(a)to (c): According to the information furnished by the University Grants Commission(UGC), there is no such proposal under its consideration.

records.qtitle: NEW TECHNOLOGY TO TEACHERS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have taken any new initiatives for making teachers aware of new technology by providing them all latest technical support and guidance; and

(b) if so, the details thereof and the steps taken or proposed to be taken for making available quality and fruitful education to the students in the next five years?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

( SMT. D. PURANDESWARI )

(a) & (b): National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE), a statutory body of Ministry of Human Resource Development, has taken steps for integration of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) as a component in the pre-service curriculum, to be made effective by each examining body.
Teachers are also being trained in using ICT in their teaching to bring more efficacy and also in preparing software for e-learning and EDUSAT programmes A few teacher educators have already been sensitized in teaching through the use of EDUSAT.

records.qtitle: HIGH SPEED TRAINS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering to run high speed train service between the long distance busy routes as well as considering to reduce the journey time by increasing the speeds of various long distance trains in the country;

(b) if so, details thereof; and

(c) how many trains would be benefited, particularly from Maharashtra bound trains?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R. VELU)

(a) to (c): At present, high speed trains (speed above 200 kilometre per hour) are not run over Indian Railways. The fastest train running over Indian Railways, at present, is 2001/2002 New Delhi- Bhopal Shatabdi Express which attains a maximum speed of 150 kmph between Tughlakabad and Agra only. However, speeding up of passenger trains is an ongoing process over Indian Railways subject to availability of resources, requisite infrastructure and operational feasibility, irrespective of geographical boundaries. During the current financial year 2006-07, 657 trains have been speeded up and other 192 trains have been made superfast so far.

records.qtitle: POLIO IN MAHARASHTRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that some polio infected patients were found in Maharashtra State in the current year;

(b) if so, the details of polio infected children, State-wise during the year 2005-06;

(c) whether it is a fact that the present advertisement campaign of polio eradication is grossly inadequate and ineffective;

(d) if so, what new steps his Ministry proposes to take in this regard; and

(e) what immediate action Government had taken or propose to take to eradicate polio virus?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) Four Virological positive polio cases have been detected in Maharashtra State in the current year.

(b) Details of polio cases reported during 2005 and 2006 are at Annexure.

(c) to (e) No Sir.Following actions are being taken to eradicate polio virus.
ú Conducted consistent high quality supplementary immunization rounds in January, February, April and May, June, July, September and November 06 and planned National immunization rounds in the month of January and February 2007.
ú Monovalent oral polio vaccine 1 (mOPV1) are being used in the high risk districts and States to enhance immunity so that the presently circulating P1 virus can be interrupted.
ú Since polio virus type 3 circulation is limited to few districts of Moradabad region, an immunization round using Monovalent Oral Polio Vaccine 3 (mOPV3) is being taken up in 9 districts of Western Uttar Pradesh from 10 December 2006.

ú To enhance the immunity of newborn, a special drive to vaccinate newborn with mOPV1 within 72 hours of birth have been initiated in selected high-risk blocks of Moradabad district.
ú Social Mobilization activities are being intensified by involving the local influencers, community and religious leaders to improve community participation and acceptance of polio vaccine.
ú State Political Leadership and Administration are continuously being updated on the identified gaps in the implementation of the Program, they in-turn are constantly monitoring the progress with the District Administration. The District Magistrates are taking corrective action through the District Task Force formed to accelerator the program implementation.
ú The ASHA workers are also now being fully involved in Pulse Polio Immunization especially in tracking of newborn and missed children and vaccinating them during the monthly Health day.
ú IEC activities have been intensified in the affected States.

records.qtitle: NON ALLOTMENT OF SERVICES TO DISABLED CANDIDATES
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that UPSC has not allotted any service to three disabled candidates despite their successful qualifying the Civil Services Examination;

(b) if so, the details in this regard and the reasons for not allotting any service to these successful candidates;

(c) whether it is also a fact that disability certificates are repeatedly challenged while giving benefits under disabled quota; and

(d) if so, the cases that have come up in this context and the policy of Government in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS.(SHRI SURESH PACHOURI)

(a): The Union Public Service Commission recommends candidates on the basis of Civil Services examination. Service allocation is done by the Department of Personnel and Training on the basis of rank, preference, medical status, eligibility of the candidate and vacancy position in the relevant category. All the 12 disabled candidates recommended by the UPSC for Civil Services Examination, 2005 are being allocated one service or the other.


(b): Does not arise.

(c): No, Sir.

(d): Does not arise.

records.qtitle: . INVESTMENT IN TEXTILE INDUSTRY
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) what is the need-based investment required to be made in the textile industry by 2010 and what is the investment made so far;

(b) whether the investment made so far is lagging behind the need-based requirement, if so, what steps are being taken to promote investment in the industry; and

(c) what would be the impact on the textile industry, if the investment does not place as required?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES

(SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN)


(a) As per the “Vision Statement for the Textile Sector” made by the Indian Cotton Mills’ Federation in August 2004, an investment of Rs.140,000 crore for the textile sector is required by 2010 towards machinery. Against this requirement, the investment made by the textile industry, based on the indigenous demand of the textile machinery is estimated to be Rs.74640 crore up to 31.8.2006.

(b) No, sir. Domestic companies have accelerated the pace of investment in the textile sector in the recent years in tandem with favorable schemes and policy measures introduced by Government. A list of such measures is at Annexure. The pace of investment is also increasing subsequent to quota phase out and industry is, therefore, expected to easily reach the targeted investment of Rs. 1,40,000 crore by 2010.

(c) Does not arise.

ANNEXURE
Important measures taken by the Government in the recent past to help the textile sector 


(i) To improve productivity and quality of cotton for manufacture and 
export of competitive downstream textile products, Government has launched the 
Technology Mission on Cotton (TMC).  The Mission has achieved success in 
increasing the productivity and reducing the contamination through upgradation 
of cotton market yards and modernisation of Ginning & Pressing factories.  


(ii) The Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS) was launched to 
facilitate the modernisation and upgradation of the textile industry both in 
the organised and unorganized sector.  The Scheme has been further fine tuned 
to increase the rapid investments in the targeted sub-sectors of the textile 
industry.  The cost of machinery has been further brought down by reducing the 
customs duty on imports.  

(iii) For speedy modernisation of the textile 
processing sector, Government has introduced w.e.f. 20.04.05, a credit linked 
capital subsidy scheme @10% under TUFS, in addition to the existing 5% interest 
reimbursement. 

(iv) To provide the textile industry with world-class 
infrastructure facilities for setting up their textile units meeting 
international environmental and social standards, a Public-Private Partnership 
(PPP) based Scheme known as the “Scheme for Integrated Textile Park (SITP)” has 
been introduced in August 2005. 

(v) In 2004-05 Budget, the entire 
textile sector, except for man-made fibre and filament yarn was provided 
optional exemption from excise duty.  In 2005-06 Budget, Central Value-aided 
Tax (CENVAT) on Polyester Filament Yarn has been reduced from 24% to 16%.  
These modifications in fiscal levies aim at attracting more investments for 
modernization of textile sector. 

(vi) To facilitate import of state of 
the art machinery to make our products internationally competitive in post 
quota regime, in 2005-06 Budget, the customs duty on textile machinery has been 
brought down to 10% except 23 machinery appearing in List 49 which attracts 
Basic Customs Duty (BCD) of 15%.  The concessional duty of 5% continues to be 
at 5% on most of the machinery items.  

(vii) In 2005-06 Budget, 30 
items of knitting and knitwear have been de-reserved.  This would facilitate 
setting up of large sized modernized units for meeting the international 
competition. 

(viii) In the Budget 2006-07 the following important 
announcements for the textile sector have been made:-

 Reduction in the excise duty on all man-made fibre yarn and filament yarn from 
16 per cent to 8 per cent.

 Reduction in the import duty on all man-made fibres and yarns from 15 per cent 
to 10 per cent. 

 Reduction in the import duty on raw materials such as DMT, PTA and MEG be from 
15 per cent to 10 per cent. 

 Provision of Rs.189 crore during 2006-07 for the Scheme for Integrated 
Textiles Parks (SITP) 



(ix) Government has launched the Debt Restructuring Scheme w.e.f. 
Sept., 2003 with the principal objective to permit banks to lend to the textile 
sector at 8-9% rate of interest.  

(x) In order to cater to the growing 
skilled manpower requirements at shop floor level, Government is providing 
assistance for strengthening existing and opening new Apparel Training and 
Design Centres (ATDCs).  

(xi) Government has allowed 100% Foreign 
Direct Investment in the textile sector under automatic route. 

(xii) 
Government has de-reserved the readymade garments, hosiery and knitwear from 
SSI sector so that large scale investments may be encouraged in these sectors. 


(xiii) National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) has been set up 
to provide the leadership role in sensitizing the Industry to the concept of 
value addition by inducting trained professionals to manage the industry. This 
has resulted in an increased demand for trained professionals in various 
sectors servicing the industry.  

(xiv) To take a serious look at 
Fashion Education in the changing business context of the opening up of World 
Economies, Government is taking steps for:-

 Establishing an institution of National Excellence for imparting Fashion 
Business Education with International Benchmarking.

 appointing a nodal agency for standardizing and benchmarking Fashion Business 
Education in the country.

 Setting up an Apex Body to train the teachers / trainers imparting Fashion 
Business Education in the country.

records.qtitle: NON PAYMENT OF PROMISED WAGES TO WORKERS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received large number of complaints that workers were receiving their wages around Rs. 15, instead of promised Rs. 60, per day under the National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREGS), in most parts of the country;

(b) if so, Government`s response and reaction thereto; and (

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for providing workers the promised wages directly under the NREG scheme?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI CHANDRA SEKHAR SAHU)

(a) No, Sir.

(b) Question does not arise.

(c) In accordance with Section 6(1) of National Rural Employment Guarantee Act 2005, Central Government may, by notification, specify the wage rate for the purposes of the Act provided that the wage rate by such notification shall not be at a rate less than Rs. 60/- per day. The Central Government has, however, not fixed any wage rate under the Act so far. Section 6(2) of the Act, further provides that until such time a wage rate is fixed by the Central Government in respect of any area in a State, the minimum wages fixed by the State Government under Section 3 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 for agricultural labour shall be considered as the wage rate applicable to that area. All State Governments are paying wages to the workers under the Act in accordance with the wages fixed by them in accordance with the provisions of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948. State Governments have, however, been asked to undertake comprehensive work, time and motion studies for evolving norms for measurement of work and schedule of rates for the purposes of the Act.

records.qtitle: CLONING OF CREDIT CARDS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware of complaints of credit cards issued by several banks and international credit cards being cloned and unauthorisedly used by unscrupulous elements;

(b) the details of instances of cloning of credit cards brought to light indicating the nature of probe conducted, if any, by the concerned bank and / or police;

(c) the details of outcome of the completed probe; if any; and

(d) the steps taken by banks to eliminate cloning and to provide their customers clone-proof credit cards and / or ensure appropriate security cover to credit card holders against unauthorised use of the facility by means of such unscrupulous technological innovations?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) to (c): Yes, Sir. A few instances of frauds by skimming of credit cards have been reported to RBI, whereby the miscreants copied the data from the magnetic stripe of customers` genuine card and misused the same through a duplicate card.

(d) : RBI has issued a circular to all commercial banks on 26`` June, 2006 listing out various measures that could be initiated by the banks including measures to educate customers through hand-outs, e- mails, display at ATM terminals, websites, etc. and operational / security measures to be taken by the banks to prevent fraudulent withdrawal from ATMs and misuse of credit / debit cards. These measures, inter-alia, include:- 



	Customers should protect their ATM Personal Identification Number (PIN), 
periodically verify the transaction history to ensure its correctness, 
immediate inform to the bank if the ATM / Credit card is lost or stolen, etc.
Banks should conduct regular inspection of ATM machines and ensure that cash is 
loaded in the machines in the presence of bank officials, conduct random checks 
for identifying any signs of tampering of fixtures attached to ATMs, 
investigate customer complaints quickly to determine if ATM was misused, 
evaluate the latest security features like anti-skimming features offered by 
ATM vendors and implement the important features based on the perceived risks, 
etc.

records.qtitle: IMPROVEMENT IN QUALITY OF PILOTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that flying institutes in our country are disappointing in keeping airline industry`s demand for pilots;

(b) if so, whether airline companies also have to compromise on quality of pilots?

(c) the number of pilots appeared for Pilot`s Licences Exams in 2005; and

(d) what steps Government have taken/proposed to be taken to improve the quality and quantity of pilots?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )
(a):- The training efforts of flying institutes in the country are constrained mainly by the non - availability of Flying Instructors due to comparatively higher renumeration available to them in the industry.
(b):- No, Sir.

(c):- 14,939 candidates appeared in the year 2005.
(d):- Strict quality and standards in training of pilots are maintained and monitored by Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) officers. However to ensure availability of adequate number of trained pilots, Government in the Annual Plan 2006-07, has made a provision of Rs. 12.79 crores for releasing as Grants - in - Aid to Aero Club of India for procurement of aircraft to be alloted to identified needy flying clubs, approved by DGCA for conducting flying training for Commercial Pilot Licence. Government have decided to upgrade and modernise the training infrastructure at the premier flying training institute namely Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Uran Akademi (IGRUA) to enhance its training capacity from 40 to 100 pilot cadets per annum. A world class flying training institute is planned as a Joint Venture Enterprise under the aegis of Airports Authority of India, at Gondia, Maharashtra.

records.qtitle: REFRIGERATOR RUNNING ON SOLAR ENERGY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government’s attention have been drawn to the recent report about the newly invented refrigerator which runs on solar energy and successfully demonstrated by Dr Rajendra Shende at Rashtrapati Bhawan;

(b) if so, Government’s views and response thereto; and

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for providing necessary help to the Dr Shende for utilizing this invention in our country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY

(SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR)

(a), (b), (c): Yes Sir. An improved vaccine refrigerator, called Solarchill, has been demonstrated by Dr. Rajendra Shende, Unit Head of United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP). The unit has been installed at the President’s Estate Clinic on experimental basis. Solarchill has been developed, through partnership programme of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), the United Nations Children`s Fund (UNICEF), the World Health Organization (WHO), the Danish Technological Institute (DTI), Greenpeace International, GTZ Proklima, and Programs for Appropriate Technologies in Health (PATH). The refrigeration companies Vestfrost and Danfoss participated in SolarChill`s development phase. The SolarChill technology does not use any ozone depleting or potent global warming substances. It stores energy in ice packs and eliminates the use of storage batteries. The benefits of the unit with respect to presently available solar powered vaccine refrigerators will be known after the reports on the field trials of the unit are available.

records.qtitle: SPENDING ON AIDS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that AIDS situation in our country found to be alarming;

(b) the number of persons infected with HIV/AIDS virus, age group-wise;

(c) which are the worst affected States and what is the percentage in our country as compared to other countries;

(d) how many anti-retroviral therapy centres are open or proposed to be opened all over country and the details thereof, State-wise; and

(e) what is the budget allocation by the Government for AIDS control and treatment for the year 2005-06?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a): As per annual sentinel surveillance, an estimated HIV infected persons in the country in 2005 were 5.2 million. The overall adult prevalence for the last three years has remained below 1%.

(b): The age group wise distribution of total reported AIDS cases in the country is as below: 




Age group   No.       %
0-14        7869      4.9
15-24       49840     31.2
30-49       91435     57.1
>50         10968     6.8
Total       160112    100%




(c ):     The worst affected states are six high prevalence
states namely Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal,
Maharashtra, Karnataka, Nagaland. The comparative information
on HIV/AIDS  situation from some of the countries as  per  UNAIDS
global report 2006 is as below:


Country       Adult prevalence
percentage
China         0.1 (< 0.2)
Brazil        0.5 (0.3-1.6)
Thailand      1.4 (0.7 - 2.1)
South         18.8 (16.8-20.7)
Africa
India         0.9 (0.5-1.5)




(d)   At  present  there are 101 ART centers in  the  country.
Another  44  centers are planned to be opened in  2007  and  a
total of 250 centers will be operationalised by 2011.  A state
wise list of existing centers is at Annexure.


(e):   The total budget allocation  was  Rs. 533.50 crores for
the year 2005-06.

records.qtitle: DECLINING FEMALE POPULATION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that population of females has reached at alarming position in Maharashtra State;

(b) if so, the report for the last five years, State-wise;

(c) whether it is also a fact that ultra sound test of uterus is also increased in the country though it was banned by Government; and

(d) what precautionary steps Government have taken or proposed to be taken against this situation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) & (b) The Sex Ratio in Maharashtra declined form 934 in 1991 to 922 in 2001. The Child Sex Ratio (0-6 years) declined from 946 to 913. State/UT wise Sex Ratio and Child Sex Ratio is during 1991& 2001 is Annexed.

(c ) The number of units registered in the country are 29831 as on 31.10.06. The number of court/police cases filed in the country under the Act are 417 as on 31.10.06.

(d) Government has been issuing directions from time to time to the States and Union Territories to strictly implement PC&PNDT Act and the Supreme Court Directions in this regard. The State/UTs have been requested to set up State Inspection and Monitoring Committees.
National Inspection and Monitoring Committee, which includes representatives from National Commission for Women, Department of Women and Child Development and NGOs, regularly takes stock of the ground realities by undertaking inspection and monitoring of the clinics in all the States.
A National Support and Monitoring Cell has been set up for strengthening the implementation of PC&PNDT Act.
Various activities have also been undertaken to create awareness against the practices of pre-natal determination of sex and female foeticide through Radio, Television and print media units. Workshops and seminars have also been organized through Voluntary Organisations at state/region/district/block levels to create awareness against this social evil. Cooperation has been sought from religious leaders, as well as medical fraternity to curb this practice. Funds are provided for organizing Padyatras By Swami Agnivesh. Indian Radiological and Imaging Association (IRIA) has been provided financial support to organize workshops for creating awareness among the radiologists on this issue in the country At the same time, sensitization of the medical community and training of judiciary has been done for better implementation of the Act.

records.qtitle: TRAUMA CARE CENTRE FOR VICTIMS OF HIGHWAY ACCIDENT PEOPLE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that yearly an estimated 1.27 lakh people are seriously injured on the roads of which 80,000 people die due to accidents on the Highways in various parts of the country;

(b) if so, Government’s response towards the increasing number of accidents on Highways;

(c) whether Government are seriously considering to set up Integrated Highway Trauma Care Centre for providing instant trauma care to accident victims in various districts particularly in Maharashtra State; and

(d) if so, by when and in what manner it would be incorporated in the country?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

(SHRI K.H. MUNIYAPPA)

(a) &(b): As reported by the States/UTs, during the year 2004, the number of persons injured were 143140 and persons killed were 34723 in road accidents on National Highways. Data regarding persons injured and persons killed doesn’t overlap. The number of road accidents on National Highways during 2002 were 131738 whereas the number of road accidents during 2003 & 2004 were 127834 & 130265 respectively. Some of the important steps taken by the Government besides highway design to check the road accidents are as under: 


i)	Various steps to enhance road safety such as road furniture, road 
markings/road signs, introduction of Highway Traffic Management System using 
Intelligent Transport System, enhancement of discipline among contractors 
during construction, road safety audit on selected stretches, have been 
undertaken by National Highways Authority of India.
ii)	Refresher training 
to Heavy Motor Vehicle drivers in the unorganized sector.
iii)	Involvement 
of NGOs for road safety activities by Department of Road Transport and Highways 
and National Highways Authority of India. 
iv)	Setting up of Driving 
Training School in the country.  
v)	Publicity campaign on road safety 
awareness through audio-visual-print media.  
vi)	Institution of National 
Award for voluntary organizations/individual for outstanding work in the field 
of road safety. 
vii)	Tightening of safety standards of vehicles.  

viii)	Provision of cranes and ambulances to various State Governments/NGOs 
under National Highway Accident Relief Service Scheme. National Highways 
Authority of India also provides ambulances at a distance of 50 Km. on each of 
its completed highways under its Operation & Maintenance contracts.
ix)	Widening and improvements of National Highways from 2 lanes to 4 lanes 
and 4 lanes to 6 lanes etc.


(c)&(d) : Provision of assistance in case of road accident is basically 
the responsibility of the State Government. This Ministry has been providing 
ambulances to States/UTs/NGOs to evacuate accident victims to the nearest 
medical center under National Highways Accident Relief Service Scheme.   During 
the period from 2000-01 to 2004-05, 266 ambulances had been given to various 
States under this scheme.  In addition, National Highways Authority of India 
provides an ambulance at an average interval of 50 kms under their Operation 
and Maintenance Contracts/Build operate Transfer agreements on the completed 
stretches of National Highways entrusted to them.  81 ambulances have been 
deployed on National Highways by National Highways Authority of India.
Apart from the above, the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare provides 
assistance to the States/UTs under the scheme of ‘Assistance for Capacity 
Building’ for upgradation of emergency services/trauma care facilities in 
hospitals including those located near the National Highways for the purpose of
treatment of victims of accidents.

records.qtitle: TELECASTING QUALITY AND POPULAR PROGRAMMES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the revenue collected by Doordarshan from various serials is extremely low as compared to serials telecast on private channels; and

(b) if so, what are the observations of Government thereof and the steps taken or proposed to be taken for telecasting quality and popular programmes through Doordarshan?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING & PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS

(SHRI P.R. DASMUNSI)


(a): Doordarshan is a public service broadcaster and is not motivated by purely commercial considerations. The details of revenue earned by private channels are not maintained by the Government. However, the overall revenue of Doordarshan including that from serials has increased during the last three years.

(b): Prasar Bharati has informed that in order to obtain quality software for its channels, the Self-Finance Commissioning scheme and Indian Classics programming have been introduced by Doordarshan. Further improvement is a constant and continuous exercise and Doordarshan continues to meet competition through appropriate initiatives.

records.qtitle: CONSUMER PRICE INDEX .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether consumer price index number for different centres including Mumbai with 2001 as the base year has been released by the Labour Bureau;

(b) if so, the principles on which the linking factor for conversion of the new index series into 1982 series has been worked out; and

(c) whether the charge made by employers about the inflated linking factor has been critically examined by the Labour Bureau?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT

(SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES)

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): The linking factors have been worked out as per the methodology approved by the Technical Advisory Committee on Statistics of Prices and Cost of Living (TAC on SPCL) by using arithmetic conversion method, which are the ratios of the average monthly Consumer Price Indices for Industrial Workers with base 1982 = 100 to that of base 2001= 100 for the latest 12 months (January 2005 to December 2005), preceding January 2006; the month of introduction of new series.

(c): The Linking Factors worked out and released alongwith the index for conversion of new series indices on base 2001=100 and were thoroughly examined to ensure that these calculations were in accordance with the methodology approved by the TAC on SPCL.

records.qtitle: TERRORIST ATTACKS ON FAMILY MEMBERS OF DEFENCE POLICE PERSONNEL IN J K .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) how many members of the families of the personnel of Jammu and Kashmir Police, CRPF, BSF and Army have been attacked by the terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir during the last two years;

(b) whether there have been a large number of complaints of the villagers from Kashmir Valley, that they are forced to shelter the terrorists and give them food at the gun point; and

(c) whether the Ministry is preparing any separate plan to protect the families of CRPF, BSF, Army and other security personnel in Jammu and Kashmir from terrorist attacks?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a): As reported by the State Government of Jammu and Kashmir, during 1.1.2005 to 25.11.2006, 19 incidents of terrorist attacks on the families of the security personnel, mostly residing in far-flung areas, took place in the State.

(b): This has been the tactics of terrorists especially in the rural areas to make forced entry into residential houses during the night and demand food and shelter. Security Forces after getting information about presence of terrorist groups promptly cordon off the area and take action.

(c): No, Sir. However, advisories have been issued on the basis of threat assessment received from, intelligence agencies.

records.qtitle: SALT PANS IN MUMBAI .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) what is the total area of salt pans in Mumbai and who are their owners;

(b) how many persons are employed in cultivating salt in these salt pans;

(c) whether the Ministry proposes to allot the land of these salt pans for low cost housing, for the resettlement of slum dwellers; and

(d) if so, the details in these regard and what are plans of the Ministry to resettle the workers working on these salt pans?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY

(SHRI ASHWANI KUMAR)


(a): The area of salt pan lands in district Mumbai and district Mumbai Suburban is 5378 acres. These lands are owned by the Government. However, in many cases where the Government had granted lease/license for manufacture of salt, licensees/lessees or their successors have claimed ownership rights over salt lands and there are several cases of ongoing litigations.

(b): Presently 437 labourers are engaged in the salt industry in the Bhandup, Trombay and Wadala salt factories in Mumbai.

(c)&(d): Though presently no proposal is under consideration for low cost housing, the Government had taken an ‘in-principle’ decision to use the salt pan lands to meet the bonafide needs of Government departments, to implement urban infrastructure projects and for other public purposes.

records.qtitle: PROTECTION OF ASI MONUMENTS AND MUSEUMS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that the Ajanta, which is among the first examples of early Buddhists architecture pertaining to 2nd century BC, is now facing problem of seepage;

(b) if so, what is the number of caves which are under threat of water seepage;

(c) the details of the steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government to protect this world heritage site;

(d) whether there is requirement of more security personnels for curbing the illegal trafficking and the protection of various ASI’s monuments and museums in the country; and

(e) if so, what is Government’s response thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER FOR TOURISM & CULTURE

(SMT. AMBIKA SONI)

(a) to (e) The Statement is laid on the table of the House.


STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (a) TO (e) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 88 FOR 28.11.2006


(a)to (c) Yes, Sir. Seepage of water is observed particularly in the verandas, in cave Nos. 1, 2, 12, 16, 17, 21, 23 and 26. The conservation of the Ajanta caves is a continuous and multidisciplinary process. Archaeological Survey of India has undertaken detailed geo-technical studies on the caves and the surrounding hill slopes through the Geological Survey of India and the Central Water and Power Research Station, Pune. Contour drains are presently provided on the hill slopes for draining the surface water. Based on the recent recommendations of the Geological Survey of India an additional drain is being designed by the Central Water and Power Research Station.The conservation of the caves is also monitored by an International committee of Consultants which has been constituted under the ongoing Japan Bank & International Co-operation (JBIC) project.

(d) & (e) There is requirement of additional security personnel for protection of monuments and museums under the Archaeological Survey of India in the country. In addition to the available strength of 3463 Monument Attendants, the Archaeological Survey of India deploys private security guards (789 personnel) and also engages CISF (459 personnel) for the security of Taj Mahal, Agra and Red Fort, Delhi. The state police and home guards are deployed in some of the site museums. Archaeological Survey of India proposes to install modern security gadgets like CCTV, metal detectors and burglars alarms to augment the physical security system.

records.qtitle: TASK FORCE TO IMPROVE SKILL BASE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are setting up a task force on vocational education to improve the skill base of the countrymen as the country would be faced with shortage of ,employees with essential skills with the rapid growth in the industry, particularly in Information Technology and electronics sector;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) whether Government are serious to introduce Careeroriented new vocational courses at secondary and Higher Secondary levels for getting more employment opportunities to the students in the country; and

(d) if so, the details in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M. A. A. FATMI)

(a) There is no proposal with the Ministry of HRD at present to set up a task force on Vocational Education.

(b) Does not arise.

(c) and (d): There is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Vocationalisation of Secondary Education at Higher Secondary level. This was introduced during 1987-88.

records.qtitle: ILLEGAL TRADE OF ANIMALS AND BIRDS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that large number of animals and birds are illegally being transported by trains to various destinations in the country;

(b) if so, how many such cases had been brought to book during the last one year; and

(c) the strict action Government had taken or propose to take against this illegal trade?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER FOR ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI A. RAJA)

(a),(b) & (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House
STATEMENT REFERRRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 56 DUE FOR REPLY ON 24.11.06 REGARDING `ILLEGAL TRADE OF ANIMALS AND BIRDS`.

(a) & (b) There are no reports of illegal transportation of animals and birds by train for the last two years.

(c) Necessary instructions have been given to all concerned, including the Railway Board, regarding the strict enforcement of Transport of Animals (Amendment) Rules, 2001.

records.qtitle: HIV INFECTED RAILWAY EMPLOYEES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that large percentage of both the Western and Central Railway employees of Mumbai Division have been afflicted by the HIV-virus.

(b) if so, what is the percentage thereof ;

(c) which specific section/ class of employees in Railways, is infected by this dreaded disease; and

(d) if so, what steps his Ministry has taken in this regard, so far?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R. VELU)



(a) to (d) A statement is attached.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 385 BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT TO BE ANSWERED IN RAJYA SABHA ON 24.11.06 REGARDING HIV INFECTED RAILWAY EMPLOYEES.

(a) : No, Sir.

(b) : Does not arise.

(c) : In Central Railway, Mumbai Division :- Out of 268 employees found infected with HIV virus following is the distribution amongst various categories of Railway employees viz 


Group ‘D’	126
Group ‘C’	141
Group ‘B’	1
Group ‘A’	0


In Western Railway, Mumbai Division :- Amongst the employees found 
infected with HIV infection highest number is amongst Group ‘D’ 
employees.


(d) : Following steps have been taken to prevent and control HIV/AIDS 
in Mumbai Division of Central and Western Railway.


1.  Collection of correct information about number of persons infected
with HIV Virus. 

1.1	Testing facilities : HIV testing facilities is available in Mumbai 
Division both in Central and Western Railway.  HIV testing is done in 
accordance with National Aids Control Organisation guidelines for pre 
and post test counseling. 

1.2 	Voluntary Counseling and Testing Centres :  Voluntary Counseling 
and Testing Centres are operated at Jagjivan Ram Hospital, Western 
Railway, Dr. Babasahib Ambedker Memorial Hospital, Byculla/ Central 
Railway. 

1.3	Uro-Genital Clinic :  Uro-Genital Clinic manned with a 
Dermatologist, Gynecologist have been developed at Mumbai. 

1.4 	All steps are being taken to ensure that the number of screening 
tests with proper counseling is increased.


2.  Prevent spread of HIV virus. 

2.1 Education and training :
a)	Doctors and Staff :  All doctors of Mumbai division of Western
and Central Railway have been trained and training of most of the 
paramedical staff has also been completed.
b)	Information Education Communication activities :
Various Information, Education and Communication activities such as 
Exhibitions Street Plays, Lectures, Quiz Competitions, Rallies. 
Distribution of Educational Material and Condoms are being performed
in co-ordination with respective State AIDS Control Societies and 
Mumbai District AIDS Control Society. 

2.2  Universal work precaution at work place : Guidelines are being
followed, Staff trained in the same and periodic re-training is 
conducted. 

2.3  Blood transfusion : Guidelines are being followed. 

2.4 Condom availability : All Health Units and Hospitals of Mumbai
Divisions of Central and Western Railway are distributing condoms. 

2.5 Post exposure treatment : Free Anti Retroviral Treatment medicines
are made available within 24 hrs. of needle – stick injury. 

2.6 Workplace Intervention Programme :  Workplace intervention 
programmes have been initiated. 

2.6.1 The sensitization workshops are organized for Administrators, 
Community Leaders and Trade Union Representative and Medical Officers. 

2.6.2 A group of Peer educators have been trained to carry out 
workplace intervention. This group include volunteers, both female 
and male, who are serving railway employees.
