2.6.3 Focus group discussion with employees on HIV/AIDS and Sexually 
Transmitted Diseases are being carried out based on assessment of 
knowledge levels of the employees.


3.   Management of HIV positive persons. 

3.1 All registered HIV persons are being followed up in Mumbai 
Divisions of Central and Western Railway. 

3.2 Medical Officers have been identified to interact and follow 
up the HIV positive persons.


4.  Treatment of AIDS cases. 

4.1 All eligible AIDS persons in Mumbai Divisions of Central and 
Western Railway are being provided free Anti Retroviral Treatment. 
Patients are being followed up. After necessary investigations 
including free CD 4 count, free Anti Retroviral Treatment is rendered
to needy persons. 

4.2 All cases are being managed as per latest recommendations. 
Medicines are being supplied to patients. 

4.3 Continuing Medical Education programme have been conducted to 
train Medical Officers in Anti Retroviral Treatment management and 
post exposure prophylaxis.

records.qtitle: SPREADING OF AIDS THROUGH SYRINGES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government’s attention have been drawn to the news reports that India dangerously underestimated the number of its estimated 5.7 million HIV-infected people who caught the virus through reused needles in hospitals and similar hygiene lapses;

(b) if so, Government’s reaction thereto;

(c) whether it is a fact that faulty blood-testing kits for HIV and Hepatitis may have been fraudulently sold to Government clinics across the country, possibly resulting in people receiving transfusions of infected blood; and

(d) if so, the details of action taken or proposed to be taken in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) & (b): India had an estimated 5.2 million HIV infected people by the end of 2005. The probable mode of transmission among the reported number of AIDS cases has been observed to be sexual mode of transmission in 85.7%, transmission from mother to child - 4.3%, blood and blood products as 1.9% and Injecting drug users as 1.9%. In 6% of the cases the mode of transmission could not be determined. There is no compelling evidence that unsafe injections are a predominant mode of HIV transmission, except in injection drug users. Clinical history and epidemiological evidence indicate that sexual transmission is the major mode of transmission.

(c) & (d): Yes, Sir. Reports were received regarding supply of substandard testing kits for Hepatitis – B and C, which were supplied to blood banks in the State of West Bengal, by a Hyderabad based company called M/S Monozyme India Ltd.. However, there are no reported cases of possibly resulting in people receiving transfusions of infected blood.
In view of the complaint received from West Bengal State AIDS Control Society, all State AIDS Control Societies have been directed to suspend proposals if any, to procure from Monozyme India Ltd. and to strictly follow guidelines and procedures laid down. Further, the Drugs Controller General (India) has been asked to investigate into the matter and take appropriate action under rules.

records.qtitle: OBESITY AND OVERWEIGHT AMONG SCHOOL CHILDREN .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the incidence of obesity and overweight are rising and affecting even the urban poor and school children in the country; and

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto and the steps taken or proposed to be taken for safeguarding such problems of obesity and overweight in the country?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)



(a): According to Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), the overall cross sectional study suggests an increase in the prevalence of obesity and overweight over the period. A cross sectional study undertaken in Delhi schools show that the prevalence rate of overweight and obese children is 29%. This is an increase from previous studies which showed it as 16% (2002-2004, adolescents). According to ICMR, the 2nd report of National Nutrition Monitoring Bureau showed that the prevalence of obesity was 2.3% and 3.4% in males and females respectively during 1975-79 which increased to 3.8% and 6.0% respectively in 1996-97.

(b) The main reasons attributed to the rising prevalence of over-weight and obesity include reduced level of physical activity/increase in sedentary life style as also increased consumption of calorie dense and nutrient deficient food items. Since creating awareness through information, education and communication is the main strategy to tackle this issue, this component has been incorporated in the proposed National Programme for Control of Diabetes and Cardiovascular Diseases (CVD).

records.qtitle: FINALIZATION OF MIRAJ PANDHARPUR RAIL LINE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the finalization of Miraj-Pandharpur line (137 Kms) including the construction of minor bridge works is pending since long time;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

(c) whether this delay is due to re-tendering; and

(d) if so, how many tenders were re-tendered for minor bridges on Pandharpur (137 Kms) section and how may times and the reasons therefor ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS


(SHRI R. VELU)


(a) to (d): Pandarpur-Miraj Gauge Conversion (137 Kms) is planned for execution as last phase of Miraj-Latur Gauge Conversion (374 kms) project. On this section, one contract of minor bridge had been terminated as contractor abandoned the work asking for enhancement in rates due to increase in prices of steel. Risk and cost tenders were invited twice but could not be finalized first time due to quoted higher rates and second time none of the tenderer fulfilled the eligibility criteria.

records.qtitle: PROPER UTILIZATION OF MANPOWER .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are more staff in Doordarshan comparing to other private channels in the modern satellite age;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor and steps taken or proposed to be taken for the proper utilization of manpower;

(c) whether it is a fact that there are huge numbers of causal labour working in Doordarshan since more than 10 years to 30 years and they are waiting for their permanent appointment in Doordarshan; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and Government’s view thereon?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS

(SHRI P.R.DASMUNSI)

(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFFERED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO 416 FOR REPLY ON 24.08.2006


(a): No, Sir. The staff requirements of Doordarshan are not comparable with those of private channels as Doordarshan is also running a large terrestrial network all over India apart from the satellite channels.

(b): Does not arise

(c) & (d): At present 253 casual labourer and 278 Casual Artists are working in various field offices of Doordarshan. The Casual Artist in the categories of Floor Assistants, Production Assistant, Carpenter, Painter, Tailor, Graphic Artists, Make up Assistant etc are considered for regularisation in accordance with the provisions of regularisation scheme of Prasar Bharati as and when the regular vacancies come up in the respective grades. The casual labourers are considered for regularisation in accordance with the Casual Labourers (Grant of Temporary Status and Regularization) Scheme of Government of India, 1993.

records.qtitle: MUMBAI URBAN TRANSPORT PROJECT
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government of Maharashtra had initiated a Mumbai Urban transport Project for improvement of traffic and transportation conditions in Mumbai, with the help of World Bank aid;

(b) if so, the details of infrastructure including the rail component to be created and improved, the cost thereof and the manner in which the cost is to be shared and the nature and extent of World Bank and Central assistance proposed or secured for the purpose; and

(c) the stages of approval/clearance the matter has been through and the schedule for implementation thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): The project includes the following components: 


(A)  RAIL COMPONENTS:


(i)   NEW LINES:


(a)  5th & 6th line between Kurla and Thane.


(b)  2  additional  lines between  Borivali  and
Virar.


(c)  One  additional line between Santacruz  and
Mahim.


(ii)  Optimization:


(a)  Central Railway.


(b)  Harbour Line.


(c)  Western Railway.


(iii) Procurement of EMU Rakes.


(iv)  D.C.  to A.C.  conversion.


(B)  ROAD COMPONENT:


(i)   Construction of Jogeshwari-Vikroli Link Road.


(ii)  Santacruz-Chembur Link Road.


(iii) Rail Over Bridge at Jogeshwari South and North.


(iv)  Station Area Traffic Improvement Scheme.


(v)   Pedestrian  Grade  Separation Scheme  at  Phadke
Chowk,  Siddhivinayak  Chowk, Shivaji  Park  and
Karariya Marg and Mahim Church.


(vi)  Area  Traffic  Control Study of 53 Junctions  in
South Mumbai under Phase-I.


(vii) Procurement of 644 buses by BEST.


The  total  project cost is estimated at Rs.  4526  crore,
out  of which World Bank has provided a loan of Rs.  2602 crore.
The  balance cost of Rs.  1924 crore is to be contributed by the
Implementing   Agencies  namely  viz.    Mumbai  Railway   Vikas
Corporation  (Indian  Railways)  Rs.  865 crore,  Government  of
Maharashtra,  Rs.   988  crore (Rs.  745  by  MMRDA),  Municipal
Corporation  of  Greater  Mumbai Rs.  64 crore and BEST  Rs.   7
crore.


(c):   Mumbai  Metropolitan  Region  Development  Authority  and
Ministry  of  Railways have reported that the project  has  been
approved  by Government of Maharashtra, Government of India  and
the  World  Bank.   It is being implemented since  2002  and  is
targeted for completion by 2008.

records.qtitle: GRANTS TO PRASAR BHARATI .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the grants Government are providing to the Prasar Bharati, Doordarshan annually since last three years, and whether Prasar Bharati is incapable to generate its own revenue;

(b) if so, the problems thereof and reasons therefor; and

(c) the steps Government are going to take for making Prasar Bharati independent and Competitive Prasar Bharati?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING AND PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS (SHRI. P.R. DASMUNSI)


(a) & (b): Government is providing grants to Prasar Bharati as a whole and not to Doordarshan separately. During the last 3 years, details of grants provided to Prasar Bharati are given below: 


Year	Amount in crores
2003-04		1001.47
2004-05		1010.78
2005-06		1078.02


Prasar Bharati is not running purely on commercial basis.  The earning of 
commercial revenue is not the only objective of the organization but is only 
incidental to its activities.  During the last three years, the revenue 
generation by Prasar Bharati is given below:


Year		  	Amount in crores
2003-04		  	569.79
2004-05		  	718.10
2005-06			1064.83


(c): A Committee was constituted on 30/3/2005 by the Government under 
the Chairmanship of Secretary, Information and Broadcasting for suggesting a 
viable capital and financial structure for Prasar Bharati to strengthen its 
functioning. The Committee has dealt and deliberated on the restructuring 
options available and submitted its Report to the Government.  Its 
Recommendations are currently before the Group of Ministers (GoM) constituted 
by the Government to examine various issues pertaining to the functioning of 
Prasar Bharati.

records.qtitle: BPL SURVEY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Maharasthra Government had requested for re-consideration the change of methodology of Below Poverty Line (BPL) Survey, 2002;

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto; and

(c) what are the details of methodology of Below Poverty Line Survey and whether Government are considering to revive this, after consideration of various State Governments` request, particularly Maharashtra ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRIMATI SURYAKANTA PATIL)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) & (c): The Ministry of Rural Development provides financial and technical assistance to the States to conduct the BPL Census in the beginning of every Five Year Plan to identify the poor households in the rural areas who could be targeted for assistance under the various programmes of the Ministry. For the 10th Five Year Plan, BPL Census 2002 was conducted based on the methodology recommended by the Expert Group which was finalized after a wide range of discussions with the various stakeholders and the State Governments. The methodology for the BPL Census 2002 was a `Score Based Ranking` of the BPL households and for this purpose 13 socio-economic parameters were prescribed which included size of operational holding of land, type of house, availability of clothes, food security, sanitation, ownership of consumer durables, literacy, status of labour force of the household, means of livelihood, status of children`s education, indebtedness and reasons for migration etc. The main objective of this methodology was to prepare the BPL list based on comparative deprivation and transparency. The State Governments have been provided adequate flexibility to determine the number of BPL households to account for local factors and situation. The guidelines also provide a two- stage appeal mechanism to redress the grievances of the people relating to their rank in the BPL list. The Government of Maharashtra has been accordingly requested to finalise the list so that poorest of the poor get the priority under the programmes.

records.qtitle: VIOLATION OF FCRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Home Ministry and the European Union`s Anti Fraud Office, OLAF are inquiring into a human rights NGO in Delhi that has allegedly been receiving funding from the European Commission, the Ford Foundation and the Foreign and Commonwealth Office of the British Government, without foreign Contributions Regulations Act clearance;

(b) if so, the details of steps taken so far against such violations of FCRA by South Asia Human Rights Documentation Centre, an NGO based in New Delhi; and

(c) what are the specific complaints of misappropriation of money received so far and details of corrective measures taken against such illegal activity?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a) to (c): On receipt of complaints alleging receipt of foreign contribution without prior permission/registration under Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 1976, by a Delhi based human rights NGO, the Ministry has since referred the matter to the concerned Government agencies for investigation. The NGO has, however, denied having received any foreign contribution. Further action can be taken only when allegations are substantiated after investigation.

records.qtitle: . SETTLEMENT OF SALT PAN LANDS IN MUMBAI .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether government had mooted any proposal to open up salt pan lands for settlement in Mumbai;

(b) if so, whether Government studied the adverse effect of reclamation of coastal land and encroachment of mangroves in this area;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) whether the Ministry is aware of the approximate number of workers working in Salt production industry; if so, the details in this regard ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (SHRI ASHWANI KUMAR)

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b) & (c): There is no proposal to reclaim any coastal land or allow any development in tracks with mangroves. The question, therefore, does not arise.

(d): About 1.20 lakh workers are employed in the country in the salt industry and the average number of workers in Mumbai in this industry is 437.

records.qtitle: CONTROL OVER MISUSE OF PARTICIPATORY NOTES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) what steps Government are taking to control misuse of participatory notes as an instrument of investment in Indian Capital Market;

(b) whether participatory notes holders disclose their identity by submitting constitutional documents, address proof, photo ID etc.; and

(c) how it is ensured that investment through participatory notes is made in compliance with provision of Anti Money Laundering Act?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) and (b): in 2004. the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Foreign Institutional Investors) Regulations 1995 were amended to bring FIIs issuing Participatory Notes (PNs) within the ambit of the FII regulations, The amendment to the regulations is intended to ensure that FIIs issuing PNs would do so only to regulated entities. Also further downstream issuance, if any, would be done to regulated entities only. An appropriate reporting format has been put in place wherein FIIs issuing PNs are required to report the same on a monthly basis. As per the format of this report, the following information is furnished it the end of every month: 


	the name of the entity to whom it has been issued,
	the jurisdiction where the subscribing entity has been incorporated,
	the regulator for the jurisdiction,
	the date of issue
	the date of maturity
	outstanding investments at the end of each month.


The reporting FII also provides an undertaking which essentially states that PNs have not been
issued to NRIs/OCBs.


(c): The Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002 and the Rules made thereunder, put an
obligation on the Banking Companies, Financial Institutions and intermediaries to submit Cash 
Transaction Reports and Suspicious Transaction Reports to curb crimes of money laundering and 
related crimes.
SEBI has issued circulars dated 18.01.06 and 20.03.06, to all the intermediaries registered 
with SEBI, including foreign institutional investors, advising them to ensure that a proper 
policy framework on anti-money laundering measures is put into place within one month from the 
date of the circular. The intermediaries have also been advised to designate an officer as 
`principal officer` and intimate their details to the Financial Intelligence Unit, India on 
an immediate basis.

records.qtitle: PERMANENT HOUSING SHELTER FOR POOR AND NEEDY
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Institute of Human Development and Centre for Development Alternatives of Ahmedabad has recently recommended for providing permanent housing shelter to the poor and needy people;

(b) if so, the details thereof and Government`s response thereto;

(c) whether Government have also received any suggestions from experts for providing low-cost housing shelter to the poor people in definite time; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and Government`s response thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING & URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION

( KUMARI SELJA )

(a): The Ministry is not aware of any such suggestion made by these agencies.

(b): Does not arise.

(c): No, Sir.

(d): Does not arise.

records.qtitle: CONSTRUCTION OF COURT BUILDINGS AND RESIDENTIAL QUARTERS IN MAHARASHTRA
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government of Maharashtra has submitted the proposal for getting` financial assistance under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for the development of infrastructural facilities like construction of Court buildings and residential quarters for Judges;

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto and reasons for the delay; and

(c) by when the financial assistance will be provided to the Mahrashtra Government for the development of infrastructural facilities ? `

records.qtitle: MUMBAI SEWAGE DISPOSAL PROJECT
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government of Maharashtra have submitted a proposal for World Bank loan for Mumbai Sewage Disposal Project-Stage-II and Slum Sanitation Programme-Stage-II (SSP-II)in Mumbai, if so, the details of the project, and the World Bank loan sought;

(b) when the proposal was sent, the terms of the loan;

(c) whether the proposal has since been sponsored by Government, if not, the reasons for the delay; and

(d) the process to be adopted for disposal of sewage and the products and by products to be obtained thereby?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )

(a)to(c): Yes Sir, Government of Maharashtra have submitted a proposal for World Bank loan for Mumbai Sewage Disposal Project Stage - II and Slum Sanitation Programme Stage - II (SSP-II) in Mumbai.

The State Government proposal consists of two parts, namely, Mumbai Sewage Disposal Project Stage-II for US$ 432 million and Slum Sanitation Programme of US $ 110 million. Components under the Mumbai Sewage Disposal Project Stage-II are rehabilitation of sewers and manholes, diversion of all illegal connections (house connections discharging to storm water drains or nallahs) to the foul sewer system, provision of new and up-sized sewers to carry predicted flows, remedy of problems at the pumping stations, replacement of old pumps and equipments, modification of the treatment works, etc. The areas to be covered under Sewerage Works include Colaba, Worli, Bandra, Versova, Malad, Bhandup & Ghatkopar.

Mumbai Sewage Disposal Project Stage-II was recommended to Deptt. of Economic Affairs for financial assistance through World Bank in the year 2004. The State was, however, categorized as `debt stressed` State from debt sustainability point of view. Accordingly, the Deptt. of Economic Affairs informed that since Maharashtra is a debt stressed State, these proposals could not be forwarded to the World Bank.

In addition to above, Deptt. of Economic Affairs also informed that in November, 2004, Chief Minister of Maharashtra requested for engaging the World Bank to prepare a five year business plan for transforming Mumbai into a world class city and to include Mumbai Sewage Disposal Project Stage-II in the comprehensive plan for the city. Subsequently, Deptt. of Economic Affairs requested the World Bank in February, 2005 to field a dedicated multi-sectoral team to draft a comprehensive strategy for the city.

The World Bank teams visited Mumbai twice last year and held extensive discussion with officials of Government of Maharashtra and with Task Force, appointed by the Chief Minister for preparing an Action Plan to develop Mumbai into a world class city. The World Bank team, which visited Mumbai from 8th to 21st November, 2005, has proposed a time schedule for Action Plan preparation relating to the Mumbai Development Action Plan. The proposed Action Plan involves action by State Government on a comprehensive package of key reforms, investing and financing. As per time schedule, prepared by World Bank, the Action Plan is expected to be launched in December, 2006. The State Government has been requested to adhere to the time schedule. The likely estimated expenditure to be spent on the project will be available on finalisation of `Action Plan`.

(d): The process to be adopted for treatment and disposal of sewage are as follows:- 

     For  Colaba  Zone,  Worli  &  Bandra  Zone,  the  proposal
envisages removal of grit and screening followed by marine
outfall.



     For  Versova zone, the proposal envisages, removal of grit
and  screening  with three stages of aerated  lagoons  and
effluent discharge directly into Malad Creek;



     For  Malad  Zone, proposal envisages, removal of grit  and
screening and discharge directly into Malad Creek;



     For  Ghatkopar  and Bhandup zone, the  proposal  envisages
removal of grit and screening with single stage of aerated
lagoons effluent discharge directly into Thane Creek;



No  by-product  is  envisaged  to  be  obtained  from  the
proposed Sewage Treatment Plant.

records.qtitle: DIESEL PETROL SEIZED BY CUSTOMS DRI.
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a whether it is a fact that custom officials seized a tanker on 24th May,2006 in Mumbai trying to smuggle over a huge quantity of highly inflammable material into the country;

(b) the total quantity of diesel and petrol seized in the financial year 2005-06 by Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) in India;

(c) whether it is a fact that large quantity of the imported fuel like kerosene finds is used to adulterate petrol and diesel in India;

(d) if so, what is the total quantity of kerosene seized in year 2005-06 by the Ministry; and

(e) what preventive actions Government have taken to stop the adulteration of kerosene?
records.ans_text:
FINANCE MINISTER (SHRI P.CHIDAMBARAM)


(a) to (e): A statement is placed on the Table of the House.






Statement in reply to Rajya Sabha Starred Question No.232 for Answer on 08-08-2006.

(a) Yes, Sir. One Supply Vessel ` Sea Bulk Toota` and one barge `M.L.Anchor` were seized by Customs Officers on 23/24-05-06 while the Vessel was transferring diesel to the barge. The total quantity of diesel seized in this operation was

1.75 MTs i.e. 2,20,000 ltrs with CIF value Rs.46.20 lakhs (apprx) and market value of Rs. 78.00 lakhs (apprx).

(b) The total quantity of diesel and petrol seized during 2005-06 by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence is 8.950 Mts.

(c)&(d) On account of the price difference between petrol/diesel and various adulterants available in the market as well as the easy miscibility of these products with petrol/diesel, the possibility of adulteration of petrol/diesel cannot be ruled out. Generally, diesel is adulterated with kerosene. During 2005-2006, the Customs Department has not effected any seizure of kerosene for reason of its being used/intended to be used as an adulterant.

(e) In order to eventually eliminate the diversion of PDS kerosene for adulteration, the Government has taken the following steps:-

(i) The Government has approved a pilot project for radically revamping the PDS kerosene network. One of the salient features of the scheme is that supplies to the sub-wholesale points will be made under the direct supervision and responsibility of the Oil Marketing Companies [OMC]s.

(
(ii) In order to monitor the movement of Tank Trucks transporting PDS Kerosene, the Government has advised the OMCs to install Global Positioning Systems that enable tracking of the vehicles on real time basis.

(iii) The import of Kerosene has been canalized since 25-11-2003 through State Trading Enterprises such as Indian Oil Company, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd etc for all purposes and also through the State Trading Corporation by Advance License Holders. Since November 2003, there has been no import of kerosene by private agencies who were earlier allowed to import and market kerosene under the Parallel Marketing System.

records.qtitle: INFRASTRUCTURE STATUS TO MICRO IRRIGATION SECTOR .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a)whether there is long standing demand from Micro irrigation sector to approve infrastructure status for enabling the industry to avail institutional financing in the country;

(b) if so, Government response thereto;

(c) whether there is also a proposal to reduce taxes, duties, octroi and local taxes on micro-irrigation systems in the country so that cost of micro irrigation systems reduced further; and

(d) if so, Government`s views and reaction thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a & b): No representation has been received by the Government in this regard.

(c & d) The Task Force on Micro Irrigation headed by Shri Chandrababu Naidu, Ex-Chief Minister, Andhra Pradesh has recommended that no taxes of the nature of sales tax, trade tax, purchase tax, local taxes like Octroi, entry tax should be levied on the micro-irrigation system. The Task Force also recommended that the Import Duties on plastic raw materials required for the micro-irrigation industry should be abolished. It has also recommended the abolition of VAT, Excise Duty on micro-irrigation system including its components namely lateral tubing, main pipeline, filtration equipment and its automation etc. The Government has extended the benefits of Section 80 IA of the Income Tax Act to the Micro-Irrigation Sector.

records.qtitle: DEVELOPMENT OF INFRASTRUCTURE FACILITIES
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received any recommendations from Investment Commission for the development of infrastructure facilities in the country;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government are considering to accept their suggestions and recommendations to all round development of infrastructure facilities in the country; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?.
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a & b) Yes Sir, The Investment Commission (IC) in its report `Investment Strategy for India` of February, 2006 has made in set of broad recommendations to facilitate and improve the investment climate The main recommendations are

(i) Remove/reduce restriction on sector caps and entry route on sectors other other than those considered `Strategic`
(ii) Provide labour flexibility
(iii) Promote SEZs for key sectors
(iv) Provide a level playing field in sectors with PSU dominance
(v) Eliminate scope for discretionary interpretation to stem corruption
(vi) Establish effective mechanisms to resolve centre-state issues, and
(vii) Create National Thrust Areas which include Tourism, Power, Textiles and Agro- processing. Sector specific recommendations in respect of infrastructure sectors are as Annexure.

(c & d) The IC observed that as a result of their extensive investor interactions, many representations on policy/procedures or other impediments were resolved through reference to Government. The recommendations of the Commission, which are more broad in nature, have been forwarded to the concerned administrative Ministries/Departments. In February 2006, Government have also undertaken a major rationalization of the FDI policy and associated procedures to further improve the investment climate.

Annexure
Recommendations
The recommended strategy to enhance investment requires policy interventions at a sectoral level, especially for those sectors significant impediments. In addition, certain changes in policy and procedures that impact multiple sectors also need to be undertaker~ to improve the investment environment.
Sector specific recommendations
Based on the detailed sectoral analysis carried out by the Investment Commission the investment goal, impediments and recommendations for select sectors are presented in this section.
Infrastructure Sectors

1. Energy
Power
Investment Goal - $140 billion by 2010
Sustained growth in power generation is fundamental to enabling economic growth. About 90,000 MW of new generation capacity is required by 2012, along with associated increase in transmission capacity and upgradation and expansion of distribution assets. An estimated investment of # 140 billion is required over a 5 year period. Based on current investment plans, only about $ 54 billion worth of investment appears likely at present leaving a gap of about $ 85 billion. Current and projected capacity addition plans of CPSUs, SEBs and private sector will still leave an expected shortfall in generation of 35,000 MW by 2012. It is strongly recommended that India`s strategy for growth in power generation should be coal based.
Impediments
> Poor financial health of the SEBs, resulting from power theft, high technical losses and free/subsidised power, is deterring investment in generation.
> Uncertainty of fuel availability
> India`s large thermal coal reserves are not being leveraged - CIL operations result in supply shortages

Recommendations
> Establish 25-30 sites for mega projects with land acquired and with all approvals in place for a total of 35,000 MW with an estimated investment of over $ 30 billion.
> Combination of pithead coal based (of 2000, MW), coastal plants based on coal and gas (-1,000 MW each) and hydel of average 250 MW capacity,
> Coal to be the fuel of choice for setting up generation capacity
> Ten year PPAs on competitive bidding on tariffs.
> In energy rich States, discourage policies that impose additional charges on generation and export of power.
> Improve output of existing assets - Reduce theft, Imporve PLF, Operate idle plants, Increase hydel peaking capacities - could increase power availability by 11,000 MW.
> Expedite the implementation of large Hydel projects, by review of environmental norms/clearances; if necessary.
> Joint development of Nepal`s estimated potential of 80,000 MW.
> Projects in the North East (e.g. Slang Hydro project in AP) and in the North (HP, Uttaranchal, J&K).
> Enhance transmission capacity of facilitate flexibility of energy transfer -especially on the East - North and East -West Corridors.
> The Tala Project could be used as a PPP modal.
> Reform distribution to energize investment in generation by:
> Dividing state distcoms into manageable sized business units; operate on commercial lines with transitional support for pre-determined period.
> Encouraging PPPs in distcoms based on the Delhi model.
> Ensure Regulator autonomy

(it is suggested that Power be considered by the Government as a National Thrust Area - outlined in the Looking Ahead section on page 45)

Coal
> Investment Goal - $15 billion by 2010
Given India`s large reserves of 240 billion tonnes, it is assumed that coal would be the major source of energy, especially for power generation. Despite its vast reserves, India produces only 360 Mtpa of coal. An investment of about $ 30-40 billion is required over the next 10 years ($15 billion by 2010) for India to double its annual coal production apart from modernizing existing mines and developing related infrastructure. Current visibility on investments in this sector is less than $ 2.5 billion.
Impediments
> Monopoly of CIL is the largest impediment to investment in this sector. The dominant incumbent is not only perceived to be inefficient, but also carries a poor record of quality, quantity and on-time delivery of coal.
> Restrictions on private and foreign investment (except for captive consumption)
Recommendations
> Carve out specified viable mining blocks from Coal India Ltd. (CIL) for captive exploitation. Alternatively, encourage the subsidiaries of CIL to induct strategic partners from leading mining companies - partners could develop existing blocks on a production share basis.
> Offer all mines that have been closed by CIL to the private sector - in case there are viable recoverable reserves.
> Adapt the NELP model for private sector participation in Coal mining by offering good quality coal blocks for bids:
> As in NELP award to be based on a quantitative evaluation of financial package/bid, technical capability, financial capability and work programme.
Fixed Royalty payments per tonne extracted, extracted, as currently notified, to be offset against upfront bid amount.
> Institute a use or loose policy for all blocks, to prevent hoarding and ensure best competitive use.
> Permit 50% FDI under the automatic route

> Permit merchant sale of coal by coal mines. Oil & Gas Investment Goal - $ 30-35 billion by 2010
India imports over 65% of its crude oil and almost 45% of its gas- with demand growing at 6-7% p.a. An equitable and sustainable policy regime with an independent regulator needs to be put in place to enhance private investment and especially FDI. While the refinery segment is expected to see large investment, areas such as gas pipelines and city gas distribution need greater investment. An estimated $ 30 billion across all elements of the value chain (E&P: $7-8 billion, Refining: $ 10-12 billion, Retail $ 2-3 billion and Gas Distribution: $ 5 billion) is required to meet the expected demand in this sector over the next 5 years. Current commitments and plans account for only $13.3 billion.
Impediments
> Administered pricing mechanism resulting in distortions in pricing and unpredictable returns.
> Dominance of PSUs at all points in the value chain - perceived lack of a level playing field as policies appear to favour PSU incumbents.
> Restriction on FDI/minimum investments clauses especially in marketing. Recommendations > Permit 100% FDI under automatic route in all segments of the value chain from Petroleum and Natural Gas exploration to retailing without subsequent divestment of 26% or any upstream investment criteria.
> Tender and award City Gas Distribution (CGD) licences for Local Distribution Companies to invest in retail gas grid/distribution networks.
> Offer CGD in cities through competitive bidding; use the Phased Competition model.
> Enact Petroleum and Natural Gas Board Bill and the Natural Gas Pipelines Policy
> Set up Regulator speedily, thereafter

> Phase out APM - subsidy for LPG and Kerosene should be funded by a surcharge on all refining output, both in the Public as well as private sector units.
Roads
> Investment Goal - $ 25-30 billion by 2010
Execution of the NHDP needs to be speeded up. Greater efforts need to be made to attract large international investors and contractors - by better outreach, offering tender blocks that are larger, and with specifications that ensure long term quality of the assets created. Excluding development of rural roads and the North East Road Development Project, this sector requires investment of about $ 30 billion, spanning completion of NHDP project ($15-18 billion), expansion of express - ways ($ 4-5 billion) and development of urban roads ($ 4-5 billion) over the next5 years. Based on existing plans, an investment of $ 20 billion seems likely.
Impediments
> The projects for road development and maintenance are too small ( = 100 km) to attract major international bidders and strategic investors.
Recommendations
> Award BOT, for NHDP-III, IV and parts of II, in larger blocks of at least 300-500 km stretches rather than sub 100 km stretches so as to attract strategic investors and enable better/faster implementation.
> Initiate an outreach programme, as for NELP, to attract international bidders/investors
> Privatize maintenance of highways.
Ports
> Investment Goal - $ 8-10 billion by 2010
With significant success in attracting domestic and foreign private investment, this sector should be subject to minimal regulation/restrictions with the focus on creating opportunities for greater investment and competition. The National Martime Development Project (NMDP) is an ambitious plan for upgradation of Major and Minor Ports, based on which the sector will require investment of over $15 - 17 billion over the next 10 years and over $ 8 billion in the next 5 years to grow cargo handled at 8% p.a. Based on current plans, an investment of only about $ 5 billion seems likely.

Impediments
> Price controls by Tariff Authority of Major Ports (TAMP)
> Poor connectivity of road and rail; monopoly of railways/CONCOR on movement of container traffic.
Recommendations
> Complete transition of all Major Ports to landlord ports by outsourcing port activities to private operators.
> Put Minor Ports up for re-bid if no development after 3 years from award.
> Convert Tariff Authority of Major Ports (TAMP) into a Regulator.
> Free up tariff setting - interventions restricted to abuse of pricing power.
> Regulator to smoothen relationship between operators and landlord ports e.g in disputes arising out of calculation of revenue in revenue sharing model.
> Implement proposed of monopoly of railways/CONCOR on movement of container traffic.
Civil Aviation & Airports
> Investment Goal. $15-17 billion by 2010
Rapid growth in passenger and cargo traffic can be sustained only if there is significant improvement in aviation infrastructure. Delays in execution of green-field airports and leasing of existing airports are unaffordable. Apart from green-field airports at Hyderabad, Bangalore, Navi Mumbai, Ludhiana, Pune and Goa, the sector also requires investments in up-gradation and modernization of about 30 major airports which account for over 95% of the country`s aviation traffic. The .visibility of investments currently is only about 20% of the total requirement of about $15 billion over the next 5 years. : Impediments
> Lack of transparency and consistency in tender conditions and project execution.
> Inordinate delay between decision to set up a green-field airport and its financial closure.

Recommendations of Permit 100% FDI in green-field airports. Invite bids for green-field airports in select cities based on demand forecasts. > E.g. Navi Mumbai, NODIA, Nagpur, Goa, Ludhiana
> Implement privatization of Chennai and Kolkata expeditiously.
> Incorporate learnings from Delhi/Mumbai tenders.
> From SPVs for the next 10 large airports (mix of city and resort destinations), and privatize - provide viability gap funding where required.
Ensure developers have adequate experience and develop world-class facilities for all airports (green-field as well as up-gradation and modernization of existing).
> Modernize Air Traffic Control (ATC) systems and enhance capabilities of personnel.
> Ensure airport facilities and ATC are comparable to best in class airports like Singapore, Dubai, Hong Kong etc.
> Remove restrictions on foreign ownership in domestic airlines.
> Complete `open skies` at the earliest (as done with the US) with all other key markets e.g. UK, Singapore - no seasonal `window`, no restrictions.
> Reduce cost of ATF to international levels. Telecom > Investment Goal - $ 22 billion by 2010 The telecom sector is the back-bone for sustaining India`s growth momentum in service including IT and IteS. This sector needs to cater to the needs to over 150 million new subscribers in addition to the existing 100 million subscribers over the next 5 years. This would require an investment of over $ 20 billion. Achieving the investment goal (with a large FDI component anticipated) is contingent on a fair and transparent long term policy regime.
Impediments

> Lack of an equitable and sustainable policy environment.
> Lack of regulator independence leading to a perceived absence of a level playing field.
> FDI regulations and other conditionalities seen to be detrimental to increased investment.
Recommendations
> Allow 74% FDI under the automatic route without additional conditionalities.
> Encourage new service (e.g. Mobile Virtual Network Operators (MVNOs), and more efficient utilisation of existing infrastructure (e.g. through local loop unbundling), while ensuring a level playing field and `non worse off` situation for existing telecom service licencees.
> Establish an equitable and sustainable spectrum policy.
> Establish an equitable policy covering incumbent and private service providers` operations and growth.
> Align levies and fees on telecom with international benchmarks, especially in the Asian region.
> Ensure Regulator autonomy.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) THEFT AT PRIME MINISTER S SPECIAL AIRCRAFT .
records.name: Ramdas Agarwal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that theft occurred in Prime Minister`s Special Aircraft, while his way back from a State visit to Berlin and Tashkent during 21st to 26th April, 2006;

(b) whether it is also a fact that Air-India has refused to furnish the contact details of the escorting officer to the investigation SPG team;

(c) whether it is a fact that, the civil Aviation Secretary has observed that the behavior of Air-India officers was cavalier and irresponsible in this matter and if so, what action the Ministry proposes to take against those officers; and

(d) what concrete action the Ministry propose to take against such security lapse for VVIP dignitaries?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )

(a): When the VVIP flight carrying Hon`ble Prime Minister was about to take-off from Hanover for Berlin on the 24th of April, the Air India Flight Purser in charge of a bar cart on the upper deck of the plane, noticed that a plastic bar seal had been broken off and 6 bottles of liquor were missing.

(b): No, Sir. The escorting officer, who was on the VVIP flight, was constantly in touch with the SPG officials on flight itself.

(c) and (d): On coming to know of the incident, Secretary Civil Aviation took a serious view and has directed Air India to investigate the matter thoroughly. The matter is, accordingly, under investigation. However, as per a preliminary report the matter has not been found to be in the nature of a security lapse. Individual responsibility is being fixed and concerned staff and crew have been taken off from VVIP flight duties till further orders. Further, the process of selection of staff and crew for VVIP flights has been made more stringent.

records.qtitle: PILOT POWER PROJECT IN DHANGAON .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government’s attention has been drawn to the pilot project of micro energy in Dhangaon, District Nandurbar, which has set an excellent example of starting power project with active public participation;

(b) if so, the salient features thereof;

(c) whether it is a fact that the cost and production ratio of this said power project is also very good as compared to the other Government power projects;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) whether Government will come out with a good package to promote such low budget experiment in various parts of the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NON-CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES (SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR)

(a), (b), (c), (d) and (e): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
Statement
Statement referred to in reply to parts (a), (b), (c), (d), and (e) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 206 for 07/08/2006 regarding Pilot Power Project in Dhangaon


(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): A 15 kW small hydro project has been set up in January,2003 in Bilgaon village, Dhangaon block, Nandurbar district, which is reported to provide electricity to about 200 households of 12 hamlets of the village.

(c)&(d): Costs of small hydro projects are location and site specific. However, the reported cost of the project is Rs. 7.5 lakhs @ Rs. 50,000/kW which is comparable to 828 similar projects in Uttaranchal, Jammu & Kashmir and elsewhere supported by this Ministry, as per the existing scheme. In addition, another 1108 such off-grid projects are under various stages of implementation.

(e): This Ministry is already implementing a scheme for promotion of small hydro power projects up to 25 MW capacity. Under the scheme, small hydro power projects upto 100 kW capacity are given a higher level of support. In addition, there is also a scheme for promotion of water-mills for mechanical, and electricity generation purposes for which subsidy upto 75 per cent of system cost or Rs. 1 lakh, whichever is lower, is being provided.

records.qtitle: SUPPLY OF NAPHTHA FOR POWR PROJECTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the details and number of power projects affected due to poor reserve of naphtha fuel;

(b) Government`s reaction thereto;

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for assured and regular supply or naphtha fuel to various power projects in the country;

(d) whether Government have made any agreement with any foreign country for regular supply of naphtha fuel; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )

(a) to (c) : No power project is affected due to poor reserve of Naphtha fuel as there is no shortage of Naphtha for power projects in the country.

(d) : No, Sir. There has been a reduction in demand of Naphtha for power plants mainly because of increase in the cost of Naphtha by about 150% over the last 5 years. As a result of the reduced off-take by the power plants, there is a surplus situation in Naphtha and the same is being exported by Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs).

(e) : Does not arise.

records.qtitle: CLOSURE OF POWER PROJECTS FOR UPGRADATION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that some thermal and hydro power projects in the country particularly in Maharashtra are closed down in order to upgrade their capacity of power generation, which affects power generation heavily; and

(b) if so, the details of the steps taken or proposed to be taken for providing necessary assistance to re-start these power projects with more capacity?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )

(a) : Thermal & Hydro Power Projects in the country are shut down when Renovation & Modernisation (R&M)/Life Extension (LE) and Upgrading (U) of the generating units are taken up and that effects the generation. At present no thermal unit is under shut down due to R&M/LE works in Maharashtra. Shut down of Nasik Thermal Power Station Unit 1&2 identified for LE works would be taken up in phased manner to ensure minimum disruption of generation from the power station.

(b) : To expedite the implementation of R&M works, the Government is providing benefits under the Accelerated Generation and Supply Programme (AG&SP) for funding the identified R&M/LE schemes through Power Finance Corporation and Rural Electrification Corporation.

records.qtitle: PROPOSALS OF MAHARASHTRA FOR ENVIRONMENTAL CLEARANCE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) The details and number of proposals submitted by Maharashtra Government related to environment issues to Central Government including necessary assistance and clearance to the environmental projects of Maharashtra since last two years; and

(b) The details of pending proposals submitted by Maharashtra Government with his Ministry by indicating the reasons behind the delay?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a)&(b) The details of the projects received from the Government of Maharashtra during last two years along with the reasons for delay in the clearance in the case of pending proposals are given in Annexure.

records.qtitle: MOBILE STORAGE FOR CONTAINING WASTAGE OF FOODSTUFFS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that more than Rs.50,000 crore of agricultural foodstuffs are lost annually in the country;

(b) if so, the strategy Government would like to take in this respect;

(c) whether Government would like to make available mobile storage at every village;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a): In a study conducted by the Directorate of Marketing & Inspection post harvest losses at producers` level have been estimated to be varying from 1.79 to 7.14 per cent for foodgrains and pulses and from 16.35 to 30.00 per cent in the case of fruits and vegetables. The wastage depends on nature of produce, its shelf life, mode of transportation, packaging, processing, distance from the market, availability of infrastructure facilities like rural godowns and cold storage etc.

(b): The Government has taken the following step to reduce post-harvest losses in the country:-
Indian Council of Agricultural Research has been developing new techniques/ systems to minimize the losses in agricultural produce in the country through the Central Institute of Post Harvest Engineering & Technology, Ludhiana and the All India Coordinated Research Project on Post Harvest Technology. The All India Coordinated Research Project on Post Harvest Technology has 33 co-operative centres located throughout the country to develop regionally differentiated post harvest technology packages for crop, livestock product and fisheries produce in terms of reducing post harvest losses, aiding value to the main produce and by-products.
National Horticulture Board, an autonomous body under this Ministry is implementing programmes to reduce post harvest losses by providing investment subsidy on the capital cost of infrastructure projects for post-harvest handling, processing and marketing of horticulture produce. The rate of subsidy is 20 percent of the project cost with a maximum limit of Rs. 25 lakh per project.
The Department is also implementing schemes for construction/ modernization of Rural godowns in the country with a view to provide scientific storage facilities to farmers. Under the scheme, subsidy is provided @ 25% of capital cost of the storage project in general and @ 33.33 percent in case of North Eastern States, hilly areas and Scheduled Castes/ Scheduled Tribes entrepreneurs. The scheme of Construction of Rural Godown has recently been revised to restrict subsidy on the storage projects for individuals, companies and corporations @ 15 percent of the project cost,

(c) to (e): No, Sir. The Central Sector Scheme of Construction of Rural Godowns being implemented by this Department has no provision to make available mobile storage at every village.

records.qtitle: IMPROVING THE STANDARD OF SPORTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is constant decline in the standard of sports in the country;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

(c) whether Union Government are formulating any new sports policy for improving the standard of our country`s sports facilities at various level; and

(d) if so, by when it would be incorporated?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ AND YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS

(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR)

(a) & (b): No, Sir. While it is a fact that there is considerable room for improvement in the standards of sports in the country, the performance of Indian sportspersons since the Commonwealth Games, 2002 indicates that the standard of sports & games has improved in the last few years due to the combined efforts made by National Sports Federations, State Governments, the Sports Authority of India and the Government of India. India won a record haul of 69 medals (as against 25 in the last games) in the 2002 Commonwealth Games and secured fourth position. The tempo was sustained in the Bussan Asian Games in which India secured 36 medals. In the Melbourne Commonwealth Games 2006, India performed well by winning 50 medals consisting of 22 gold, 17 silver and 11 bronze and retained its fourth position despite limitation of events/disciplines of India`s strength. Indian sportspersons have performed creditably in a number of international competitions including the First Afro-Asian Games in Hyderabad and SAF Games in Islamabad in 2004. In Athens Olympics 2004, India won a first ever silver medal in an individual event since independence while some of the sportspersons gave their best performances. In Paralympic Games 2004 at Athens, India won 1 gold medal in athletics and 1 bronze medal in power-lifting.

(c) & (d): The existing National Sports policy was formulated in 2001. This is being reviewed in the context of the 11th Plan, and the evolving needs and priorities in the sports sector.

records.qtitle: CORRUPT GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that many Government officials have been found guilty and crores of rupees unearthed by the C.B.I. from their houses in the last two years;

(b) if so, the details in this regard; and

(c) the details of concrete steps that have been taken or proposed to be taken for making Government’s administrative machinery free from inefficiency, corruption and lethargy?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS.(SHRI SURESH PACHOURI)

(a)&(b): CBI conducts searches including at the houses as part of investigation depending on the facts and circumstances of cases. Details of searches form part of records of individual cases including those registered for amassing of disproportionate assets and no separate record is maintained about the amount recovered during searches.

(c): The Government has taken several steps to make the administrative machinery free from inefficiency, corruption and lethargy. These steps include formulation, monitoring and effective implementation of anti-corruption policies and practices, constitution of preventive anti-corruption bodies (CVC/CBI); establishing a system based on transparency in public procurement and management of public finances, and enactment of Right to Information Act, 2005.
Government organizations are constantly engaged in improving their functioning through e-Governance, issue of Citizen Charters and simplification of procedures and systems, which are aimed at eradicating corruption, by improving transparency and accountability.

records.qtitle: ASSISTANCE TO WEAVERS IN MAHARASHTRA. .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) what are the details and the number of proposals submitted by Maharashtra Government related to textile issues to the Union Government, including necessary assistance to weavers of Maharashtra, during the last two years; and

(b) Government’s response thereto, so far?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES

(a) & (b) : The Schemes being implemented in the Textile Sector are neither state nor community specific and the funds under the Schemes are released to various implementing agencies after evaluating the viability of the proposals received. lakhs respectively were released to various implementing agencies in the State
of Maharashtra.

records.qtitle: PERMISSION TO RELIANCE FOR RATE OF GAS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Reliance Industries are seeking the permission to sell 28 million cubic meters of gas from its Krishna-Godavari field to Reliance Natural Resources Limited at a delivered price of $ 3.18 mBtu as against current international market rates of $ 9-10 mBtu; and

(b) if so, what is Government`s response thereto and what formula is considering to be adopted by Government in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS.

(SHRI IDINSHA PATEL)

(a) & (b): The Government has not agreed to the proposal of Reliance Industries Ltd., (RIL) to approve the gas price formula for sale of natural gas from the KG-DWN-98/3 block to RNRL (Reliance Natural Resources Ltd.,) as the same was not in accordance with the provisions of Production Sharing Contract (PSC) signed between the Government and the consortium of RIL - Niko Resources Ltd.
