records.qtitle: PROTECTION AND PRESERVATION OF HISTORICAL AND RELIGIOUS PLACES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware of newspaper reports of sale of historical fort Underi in District Raigad, Maharashtra built by Shivaji Maharaj to a private builder;

(b) if so, what is Government’s response thereto and what steps the Archaeology Department propose to protect and preserve all the historical and religious places in the country so that, these places are not sold to any private party; and

(c) whether the Central Government propose to ask the State Government of Maharashtra, to take strict action against all the concerned revenue officers responsible therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER FOR TOURISM AND CULTURE

(SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI)


(a) to (c) Underi Fort is not protected either by the Central Government or State Government of Maharashtra. The land at Survey No.302, area 1-21-0 of Underi Fort belonging to a group of six individuals was sold to one Shri Ramesh Hiralal Kundalmal, a promoter of Dolphin Stone Crest Estate Pvt. Ltd. for an amount of Rs.2 crores and a sale agreement was entered into on 26th January, 2006. This was registered vide No.1451/2006 on 16.5.2006. The State Government under Section 155 of the Maharashtra State Revenue Act has initiated action against the sale and the land is now recorded in the name of State Government. Two officials of the Revenue Department of Government of Maharasthra have been suspended for their involvement in the registration, and action has been initiated by the Government of Maharashtra to protect the Underi Fort under the State legislation.

records.qtitle: RESEARCH PROJECTS IN THE FIELD OF RENEWABLE ENERGY SOURCES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the number and details of research projects submitted in Government’s Patent Office particularly in the field of renewable energy sources in the country;

(b) the salient features thereof; and

(c) the steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government for the encouragement to the research projects in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NON-CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES (SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR)

(a) & (b): Research projects are not required to be submitted to the Patent Office as only applications for obtaining patents for innovations are required to be filed. Patent applications have been filed in the areas of solar photovoltaics, solar thermal, biomass production, biomass gasification, sensor-less torque control device of an induction generator of a wind turbine, hydrogen storage and fuel cells.

(c): The Ministry of Non-conventional Energy Sources has been supporting R&D in new and renewable energy technologies in the country. In this regard, more than 550 projects in the aforesaid technologies have been financially supported, with a support level of around 50 percent.

records.qtitle: ELECTRICITY FROM SEA WAVES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering to generate electricity from sea-waves in different regions of the country;

(b) if so, the schemes formulated in this regard and the estimated expenditure likely to be incurred on the same; and

(c) the quantum of electricity likely to be generated from this scheme in next 3-4 years?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY AND MINISTER OF EARTH SCIENCES

(KAPIL SIBAL)

(a) and (b) National Institute of Ocean technology, an organization under Ministry of Earth Sciences has set up a wave energy demonstration power plant at Vizhinjam, Kerala, which is working on experimental basis. However, this type of land-based plant is not cost effective and the research in this regard is continuing. Presently, there is no scheme to set up more such plants.

(c) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: INCREASING CASES OF BREAST CANCER
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware that breast cancer cases are alarmingly increasing in the country since last three years;

(b) if so, Government`s views and reactions thereto;

(c) whether Government have any proposal for making available breast cancer screening test at free of cost to ordinary people of our country;

(d) if so, by when it will be implemented; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE

(DR. ANBUMANI RAMADOSS)

(a)to(e): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 84 FOR 28TH JULY, 2006

There is no alarming increase in Breast Cancer in the country. However, the data from the population-based Cancer Registries (PBCR) indicates a gradual increase in the incidence rate of Breast Cancer over the past 20 years in the cities of Mumbai, Chennai , Bangalore, Delhi and Bhopal. There is no such increase in the Rural areas in and around Barshi in Maharashtra. These statements are based on the data collected from 1982-2000. Data regarding the incidence of breast cancer over the past three years is being compiled and analysed. There are two ways of early detection of Breast Cancer - one, by Mammorgraphy and two, Clinical Breast Examination (CBE). Experts are of the view that Mammography is not practicable and an affordable method for Breast Cancer screening in India. It has been suggested that Breast Cancer would be best tackled through an early detection programme using Clinical Breast Examination performed by trained Para Medical Personnel such as Female Health Workers. As such, there is no proposal for breast cancer screening in the country.
However, as per the revised schemes of National Cancer Control Programme (NCCP), special emphasis is now being laid on early detection of Cancer by promoting health education, creating awareness etc. Under this Programme, Breast Self Examination is being advocated. Mammography is used by experts in tertiary care centres to diagnose high risk cases, or suspected cases and also for follow up of patients. The Central Government is also supplementing the efforts of the State Governments by providing financial assistance for procurement of diagnostic and therapeutic equipment in cancer care in Government Medical Colleges/ Hospitals. In addition, the comprehensive cancer detection and management facilities including cancer testing facilities in respective regions/States are provided by 25 Regional Cancer Centres developed over the years under NCCP. The public awareness about cancer is also being carried out through the telecast of the Programme `Kalyani` on Doordarshan.

records.qtitle: ADVERTISEMENT TO COMPLAIN AGAINST RAILWAY TICKET CHECKING STAFF .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that his ministry has issued an advertisement, to complain against railway ticket checking staff who demand money illegally from the railway passengers.

(b) if so, whether this advertisement declares no trust on their own employees.

(c) whether it is also a fact that the office bearers and workers of Central Railway Mazdoor Sangh, Mumbai, have openly protested against this advertisement

(d) whether the said union has threatened to start an agitation against the advertisement; and

(e) if so, what steps his ministry propose to take about this advertisement?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

( SHRI R. VELU )

(a) & (b) Advertisements were taken out to assist on-board train passengers in registering their grievances, in case they faced any harassment / extortion from the railway staff on duty. The advertisements were in no way intended to target any category of railway employee, but were designed to act as a deterrent to corrupt employees.

(c) to (e) In May 2006, some sections of ticket checking staff had expressed their resentment through their affiliated federations / unions at the singling out of this category as corrupt. Central Railway Mazdoor Sangh was also one such union which registered its protest. In deference to their sensitivities the word `TTE` has been replaced by `Railway Official` in the subsequent advertisements brought out by zonal railways .

records.qtitle: SPORTS INFRASTRUCTURE IN RURAL AREAS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is acute shortage of sports infrastructure facilities in rural areas;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor and the steps taken to start an effective programme for youth of rural areas; and

(c) the details of the schemes under which financial assistance is provided for the promotion of sports in the country through NGOs and performance review of such schemes, particularly in Maharashtra State?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ AND YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS

(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR)

(a)to(c) : A statement is laid on the table of the House.


STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 62 FOR 27.7.2006 BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT REGARDING SPORTS INFRASTRUCTURE IN RURAL AREAS

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) As `Sports` is a State subject in the constitution , the primary responsibility for the creation of sports infrastructure facilities throughout the country, including the rural areas, falls on State Governments . Till 31.3.2005, the Ministry was supplementing the efforts of the State Governments for the creation of sports facilities in various states by providing assistance under the Centrally sponsored Sports Infrastructure Schemes in accordance with the approved pattern subject to the receipt of viable proposals. With effect from 1.4.2005 however, the Sports Infrastructure Schemes were transferred to the State sector. Thus, fresh cases of Sports Infrastructure projects will have to be funded by State Governments out of their own resources. All State Governments were informed accordingly in February, 2005. However, the Planning Commission has indicated that funds to the extent of committed liabilities will be provided for ongoing approved Sports Infrastructure projec ts during the remaining period of the X Plan only. In recognition of the continuing acute , shortage of sports facilities in rural areas, thus denying the vast majority of children, adolescents and youth access to organised sports & games, consideration is being given to the promotion of a Panchayat Yuva Khel Abhiyan in collaboration with schools and other educational institutions, on the one hand, and with Panchayati Raj Institutions, on the other .

(c )The Ministry is implementing the scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations. Under the scheme, Central assistance is provided to the recognised National Sports Federations, which are autonomous registered bodies, for purposes such as for participation in tournaments & Training abroad, organizing National/International Championships in India and purchase of Sports Equipments. These recognised Federations are National level bodies which are responsible for promotion of Sports in the country as a whole in consultation with their affiliated State Units. Government of India does not deal with State Level Sports Federations/Associations and as such state-wise data are not maintained . The performances of the recognised NSFs are reviewed from time to time.
However, details of financial assistance provided to different States during the last three years under the erstwhile Scheme of `Grants for Creation of Sports Infrastructure`(including Maharashtra) is annexed. The figures indicated include grants released to NGOs in respective States.

records.qtitle: MANPOWER SHORTAGE IN BSF .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Border Security Force (BSF) is facing a shortage of manpower and requires more security men;

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto; and

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government for covering more border areas for security, in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a) (b)& (c): The strength of BSF has been augmented by adding 157 Coys Additional battalions of CRPF have been sanctioned leading to release of 38 Bns of BSF deployed on IS duties to provide the latter with adequate manpower to perform its role of guarding India-Pakistan and India-Bangladesh borders.

records.qtitle: STANDARD OF TREATMENT IN ESI HOSPITALS . .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received any reports about problem being faced in E.S.I. Hospital`s about standard of medical facilities and treatment in the country;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for improving the medical treatment facilities to its beneficiaries?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT

(SHRI CHANDRA SEKHAR SAHU)

(a): No, Sir.

(b): Does not arise in view of (a) above.

(c): Several steps have been taken by the ESI Corporation for re-organizing & up-grading the facilities in hospitals/dispensaries as per norms of ESI Corporation. i) The State Governments have been asked to re-organize the dispensaries/hospitals in the States to ensure optimum utilization of the facilities and re-deploy the staff as per requirement and work load in hospitals and dispensaries. ii) Action plans have been drawn up from time to time to augment the availability of equipment and for upgrading and modernizing the diagnostic and clinical facilities. iii) To provide comprehensive Medical services to Insured Persons and their families, tie-up arrangements with specialized hospitals have been made by various State Governments. iv) One hospital per State has been/is being taken over, with the consent of State Government concerned by ESI Corporation to be run directly as Model Hospital. These hospitals are better equipped and their scope of services is being widened to pr ovide comprehensive secondary care medical services. v) The ceiling for reimbursement of expenditure on provisions of medical care by State Governments has been enhanced from Rs. 750/- to Rs. 900/- per Insured Person family unit w.e.f. 1.4.2005. vi) To expedite the process of sanction of equipment powers have been delegated to Senior State Medical Commissioners/State Medical Commissioners of the States to sanction equipment upto Rs. 15.00 lacs per unit cost at state level itself. vii) The ESI Corporation has decided to set up four super specialty hospitals at Hyderabad, Mumbai, Kolkata & Delhi to provide quality medical car to the Insured Persons at State level itself.

records.qtitle: PETROLEUM SMUGGLING
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government`s attention has been drawn to the recent reports regarding growing number of petroleum smuggling business operations in the country, particularly in western coastal line;

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto; and

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken against such illicit petroleum smuggling in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS (SHRI MURLI DEORA)

(a) to (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 32 TO BE ANSWERED ON 25.7.2006 REGARDING PETROLEUM SMUGGLING.

(a) to (c): Yes, Sir. All Customs field formations including Directorate of Revenue Intelligence are alert and vigilant to prevent and thwart attempts of petroleum smuggling into the country particularly on Western Coast line. Based on specific intelligence regarding smuggling of HSD into the country, the DRI conducted searches and seized 8.950 MT of HSD at Kakinada Port in March, 2006. In April and May 2006, the Commissionerate of Customs conducted two operations in Indian waters around Mumbai port in which approximately 3 lakh litres of smuggled HSD have been seized.

records.qtitle: OUTSOURCING FOR RATIONALISING OPERATIONAL COSTS BY BANKS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that several Nationalised Banks are increasingly using outsourcing for rationalizing operational costs by avoiding wasteful expenditure;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government have issued any guidelines or direction to all Nationalised Banks for managing risks arising from such outsourcing activities in the country effectively; and ~

(d) if so, what are the details thereof?.
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) to (d) : Banks are increasingly using outsourcing for rationalizing operational costs by avoiding wasteful expenditure. In this regard, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued draft guidelines on outsourcing financial services by banks on 6.12.2005 for feedback. The guidelines on Outsourcing are intended to provide direction and guidance to banks to adopt sound and responsive risk management practices for effective oversight, due diligence and management of risks arising from such outsourcing activities. In terms of the said draft guidelines banks cannot outsource core management functions like, corporate planning, organization, management and control, and decision making functions like determining compliance with KYC norms for opining deposit account, according sanction for loan and management of investment portfolio.

records.qtitle: NON PAYMENT OF DUES BY BCCI
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
te:

(a) whether it is a fact that the huge earning sports board in the country, BCCI had not paid any outstanding dues of taxes of Rs.361 crore since the last three years;

(b) if so, what is Government`s reaction thereto; and

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for recovering the tax money from the BCCI;

(d) whether Government are observing BCCI`s financial decisions as there has been lot of criticisms going on about the financial misappropriation; and

(e) if so, what are Government`s views and response thereto ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM

(a) All taxes raised against BCCI have been paid. There are no outstanding dues of taxes of Rs.361 crore. A demand of Rs.35.36 lakhs has been recently raised in the month of March, 2006 for A.Y. 2003-04 and the same will be recovered at the earliest.

(b) does not arise.

(c) does not arise.

(d) Returns of income are regularly filed. Details as required, are filed at the time of assessment. No evidence of misappropriation or irregularity has been noticed. No complaint of such nature has also been received by the Directorate of Exemption, Mumbai or has been filed before the Assessing Officer.

(e) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: TRAINING OF BANK EMPLOYEES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have any training facilities for the Public Sector Bank employees for increasing awareness of upcoming New Age Computing Banking Technology and most importantly Security of Information Assets, Cyber Laws etc, and

(b) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) & (b) : All the; major public sector banks have got their own training establishments complete with all necessary infrastructure to cater to the training needs of their employees. Besides this, training establishments like College of Agricultural Banking, Pune, Bankers` Training College, Mumbai, National Institute of Bank Management, Pune etc. conduct round-the-year ~training programmes on contemporary topics, for the employees/officers of the banks, where subjects like, core banking solutions, e-Banking/lnternet Banking, Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti Money Laundering (AML), Risk Management, system related frauds, etc. now form an integral part of the training, curricula.

records.qtitle: . INCREASE IN RETIREMENT AGE OF JUDGES IN HIGH COURTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any representation has been received from organization for increasing retirement age of Chief Judges of High Courts to 65 from 62 years as in the case of Judges of the Supreme Court;

(b) if so, whether any action has been taken thereon ;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) whether Government are proposing any legislation in this regard*?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LAW & JUSTICE (SHRI K. VENKATAPATHY)

(a) to (d): The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC) recommended that the retirement age of the Judges of the High Court should be increased to 65 years and that of the Judges of the Supreme Court should be increased to 68 years. In the Chief Justices1 Conference held from 13th to 15th September, 2002 in New Delhi, a resolution was passed on raising the age of retirement of High Court Judges. The resolution reads as follows: Resolved that the age of retirement of the High Court Judges be increased. Resolved further, that the age of retirement of the High Court and the Supreme Court Judges be the same. A common cadre of the Chief Justices of the High Courts and the Judges of the Supreme Court be formed leaving allocation to the Hon`ble the Chief Justice of India.
This resolution has been examined by the Government. The increase in the age of retirement of Judges would be effected by amending Article 217 of the Constitution of India in accordance with the procedure laid down in its Article 368(2). Since this Article is covered under Chapter V of Part VI of the Constitution, amendment in the aforesaid Article will require ratification by the Legislatures of at-least one-half of the States, as per the provision of Article 368(2). So far, no decision has been taken by the Government in this regard.

records.qtitle: VACANCIES IN VARIOUS VIDYAPEETHS . .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are more than 50,000 teachers and allied posts lying vacant in various Vidyapeeths of the country;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor and by when these posts would be filled up;

(c) whether Government have issued any` instructions for filling up these teachers posts in Vidyapeeths of the country; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF` HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M.A.A. FATMI)

(a) No, Sir.

(b) to (d) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: YOGA EDUCATION CENTRE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that University Grants Commission has recently decided to set up Yoga Education Centre for benefiting the students health and social activities at various Universities in the country; and

(b) if so, the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government for promoting Yoga education ac various school level? ANSW~.R
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI M.A.A. FATMI)

(a) According to the information furnished by the University Grants Commission (UGC), the UGC has been providing grants to Universities under the scheme of Promotion of Yoga Education and practice & positive health in universities for the over all development of students, teachers and non teaching staff of universities. An amount of Rs.43.35 lakhs and Rs.41.31 lakhs has been spent during the years 2004-05 and 2005-06 respectively under the scheme.

(b) The National Curriculum Framework for School Education - 2005 prepared by the National Council of Educational Research and Training provides for Health and Physical Education as a compulsory subject from primary to secondary stage and as an optional subject at higher secondary stage. Yoga is one of the core components of Health and Physical Education.
A Centrally Sponsored Scheme titled `Introduction of Yoga in Schools` provides for central assistance to State Governments, Union Territory Administrations and reputed NGOs for expenditure on yoga training to teachers and upgrading library facilities. More than 3700 teachers have since been trained. The scheme is now a component of the recently formulated composite scheme of `Quality improvement in schools`

records.qtitle: PAMPHLETS AGAINST PULSE POLIO PROGRAMME .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that certain Muslim organizations in the country, particularly in Maharashtra State have distributed pamphlets in Urdu against the Pulse-polio vaccination campaign, Stating that polio drops contain dangerous germs of AIDS, Cancer, etc.;

(b) what action his Ministry proposes to take action against certain elements that mislead and give wrong information about the health campaign sponsored by Government; and

(c) how many incidents of polio were detected in the country, particularly in Maharashtra State during the last two years?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)


(a) : Yes Sir, It is true that certain organization has published an article in Urdu Times, published in Mumbai and circulated in minority dominated areas. It was published in April & May 2005, and also in April, 2006 in local news paper in Malegaon and Bhiwandi towns. Zerox copies of this article were deliberately circulated in Malegaon and Bhiwandi towns.

(b) : Editor of the News Paper was requested not to publish such type of articles. Meeting of Mullahs & Maulvies in Malegaon and Bhiwandi towns were organized to convince the opinion leaders of the communitry. Meeting of Madarsa Teachers were also organized both in Malegaon and Bhiwandi towns. Meetings of Muslim doctors were organized both in Malegaon and Bhiwandi towns. Messages of Mullahs & Maulvies were published through cable network in both the places. Press Conference/workshops of Medical Personnel were organized with the help of Nagpur, Aurangabad, Nashik and Bhiwandi corporation during April 2006. Commissioner, Malegaon organized specific rallies before each round, where in prominent muslim leaders actively participated. Joint efforts were made by WHO/UNICEF and corporation authorities to persuade to accept OPV vaccine.

(c) : During the year 2004, there was 3 virological positive polio cases in Maharashtra i.e one in Bhiwandi, Thane district, one in Malegaon of Nashik district and one in P North Ward of Mumbai Municipal Corporation. No polio cases has been detected during the year 2005 as well as during the year 2006 till date.

records.qtitle: PAEDIATRIC SUPER SPECIALITY HOSPITALS IN MAHARASHTRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) how much of cost has been borne by the Central Government and Delhi Government for setting up an exclusive Chacha Nehru Bal Chikitsalaya, Children’s Super Speciality Hospital, Geeta Colony, Delhi and details of such children’s hospitals running in the country;

(b) whether Government are considering to set up such hospitals in other parts of the country, particularly in Maharashtra;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) Chacha Nehru Bal Chikitsalaya, Children’s Super Speciality Hospital, Geeta Colony, Delhi has been set up by GNCT of Delhi. The Central Government has not provided any financial assistance for setting up this hospital.

(b) to (d) Health being a State subject, it is for the State Government concerned to consider setting up of such hospitals in their States.

records.qtitle: INDUSTRIES IN MAHARASHTRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the States doing well on the industrial/manufacturing front;

(b) whether it is a fact that the industrial sector in Maharashtra is on the decline;

(c) if so, the reasons therefor and whether Government are devising any package for the benefit of Maharashtra where industries are suffering due to several problems; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY

(SHRI KAMAL NATH)

(a) : As per the CSO data for the year 2004-05, Jharkhand, Chandigarh, Maharashtra, Kerala, Karanataka, Orissa, Andhra Pradesh, Assam and Delhi were among the States/UTs, which registered an industrial growth rate higher than the national average.


(b) : Maharashtra registered industrial growth rates of 8.6 per cent in 2002-03, 11.6 per cent in 2003-04 and 9.8 per cent during 2004-05 compared to all-India averages of 6.8 per cent, 6.6 per cent and 7.7 per cent respectively during these three years.


(c)& (d): Do not arise in view of reply to (b) above.

records.qtitle: LAUNCHING OF WEBSITE BY NAXALITES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the naxalites have now become `hi-tech` by launching their own website and have issued serious threats from website to the State and Central Government;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) how his Ministry propose to effectively face this situation?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a) & (b): Certain websites with pro-maoist/naxalite contents are found to be hosted on Internet. These websites are largely hosted outside India.

(c): Besides intercepting any information transmitted through any computer resource in relation to interests of the sovereignty or integrity of India, security of the State, Public order etc., the Central Government can also issue instructions to Internet Service Providers for blocking of such websites in India.

records.qtitle: LOSSES DUE TO FIRE
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of fire incidents took place in ONGC project in Bombay High in the last three years and the approximate amount of loss due to such fire accidents.

(b) what precautionary measures are taken by ONGC for preventing such fire accidents in the future; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS

(SHRI DINSHA PATEL)


(a) Oil & Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) has informed that there was one fire incident in Mumbai High at BHN platform during the last 3 years. The loss estimated by the surveyors/ average adjustors in the accident is about US$ 375.10 Million.

(b)& (c) ONGC has taken the following precautionary measure to prevent fire accidents:-

(i) Review and Upgradation of Marine Operating Procedures.

(ii) The review of engineering design through an internationally reputed consultant M/s. Mustang. Based on the report, an action plan has been drawn to provide further safeguard the Offshore structures.

records.qtitle: FIXING OF UNIFORM CUSTOMS AND EXCISE DUTY STRUCTURE
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is immense instability in industrial sector in the country due to diverse schemes and subsidies of State Goernments as well as different Central and customs duty structure in various parts of the country?

(b) if so, what is the Government`s response thereto;

(c) whether Government are seriously considering to fix uniform customs and excise duty structure in the country for reducing instabilityamong industrial segment in the country; and

(d) if so, what are the details in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S.PALANIMANICKAM)

(a) Customs duty is applicable uniformly to the entire industrial sector in the country. As regards excise duty, the Government has given exemptions from excise duty in order to encourage industrial development of special category states. Government is not aware of any immense instability in the industrial sector because of such area based exemption.

(b) Does not arise in view of (a) above.

(c) At present, there is no proposal under consideration of the Government for withdrawing prematurely the excise duty concessions currently available for the special category States.

(d) Does not arise in view of (c) above.

records.qtitle: CORE BANKING SYSTEM FOR PUBLIC SECTOR BANKS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) what are the customer-centric initiatives taken by the Public Sector banks to compete effectively with private sector and foreign banks in terms of the existing product portfolio on offer and introduction of new products and services to match those of its competitors;

(b) whether Government have issued any directions for adopting Core Banking/Any Branch banking system to all Nationalised Public Sector Banks in the country; and

(c) if so, the details thereof and by when, it will be operational in the country ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a), (b) & (c) :- Reserve Bank of India (RBI) have reported that Public Sector Banks have put in place several measures which would lead to better facilities to customers such as computerisation of branches, installation of ATMs, single window concept, time norms for important services, any branch banking, delivery channels like Electronic Clearing Service, Electronic Fund Transfer, Telebanking, Internet Banking Services etc.
RBI has issued instructions to all scheduled commercial banks on implementation of core banking solutions and has advised that the pace of internal computerization of branches of banks and their inter-connectivity, providing for core banking solutions or centralized database access/clustered solutions needs to be expedited.
So far, seven Public Sector Banks have reported that they have fully implemented the Core Banking Solution.

records.qtitle: REHABILITATION OF SLUM AROUND MUMBAI AIRPORT .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether his Ministry has prepared a blueprint to rehabilitate the elegible slum dwellers on the periphery of Mumbai airport;

(b) if so, the details thereof including the total number of slum dwellers to be rehabilitated and the total cost involved; and

(c) whether Government have fixed time-schedule for the rehabilitation work, if so, by when it will be completed?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )
(a):- No, Sir.
(b):- Does not arise
(c):- Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport has been handed over to the Joint Venture Company (JVC) Mumbai International Airport Pvt. Limited. As per the State Support Agreement betweeen the JVC and Government of Maharashtra the JVC will deal with the issue of encroachment and Airports Authority of India and the State Government will make endeavour to help the Company in this regard. The cost for relocation shall be borne by the JVC.

records.qtitle: MALNUTRITION IN CHILDREN .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is growing percentage of malnutrition problems among children in the country, particularly in the Maharashtra State for the last two years;

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto; and

(c) the details of steps taken so far by Government for tackling this issue in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY)


(a) According to studies, the underweight prevalence among children declined from 53.4% [National Family Health Survey- 1:1992-93] to 47% [National Family Health Survey-2: 1998-99] in the country. In the State of Maharashtra, the prevalence of underweight in children declined from 54.2% to 49.6% during this period.

(b)&(c) The problem of malnutrition is multi-dimensional and inter-generational in nature which needs to be tackled through holistic coordinated interventions in areas of food security, sanitation and safe drinking water, nutrition, family welfare and poverty alleviation.
To tackle the problem of malnutrition, the Government of India has introduced several programmes being implemented by various Ministries/Departments which include: 


(i)  Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) Scheme; 

(ii)  National Nutritional Anaemia Control Programme, (Ministry of
Health & Family Welfare); 

(iii) National Prophylaxis Programme against Blindness due to
Vitamin-A, (Ministry of Health & Family Welfare); 

(iv)  National Iodine Deficiency Control Programme, (Ministry of
Health & Family Welfare); 

(v)   Reproductive & Child Health Programme, (Ministry of Health &
Family Welfare); 

(vi)  Poverty Alleviation Programme, (Ministry of Rural
Development); 

(vii) National Programme for Nutritional support to Primary
Education (Mid-day Meal Scheme), (Department of Elementary
Education & Literacy); 

(viii)Targeted Public Distribution System, (Department of
Food & Consumer Affairs); 

(ix)  A Pilot project in 51 districts to provide free foodgrains
to undernourished adolescent girls and pregnant & nursing
mothers, (Planning Commission); 

(x)   National Rural Health Mission (Ministry of Health & Family
Welfare).


In  so  far  as  Ministry  of  Women  &  Child  Development  is
concerned it is administering ICDS Scheme which aims at  holistic
development of children below the age of 6 years and  pregnant  &
lactating  mothers.   The  steps taken  in  the  recent  past  to
increase the effectiveness of the delivery of services under  the
Scheme include:


Ø   Expansion of the Scheme from existing 5652 Projects and 7.54
lakh Anganwadi centres to 6118 Projects and 9.46 lakh Anganwadi
Centres which includes 416 Projects and 78551 Anganwadi Centres
in Maharashtra.
Ø    Doubling of financial norms for supplementary nutrition.
Ø    Sharing of 50% cost of supplementary nutrition with the
States.
Ø    Constant emphasis on States to:
Ø
·  Ensure regular supply of supplementary nutrition as per
schematic norms;
	·   Ensure effective convergence of health, nutrition, education
	    and safe drinking water services under various programmes.

records.qtitle: WIND ENERGY POTENTIAL .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that our country has enormous potential for wind energy;

(b) if so, details thereof and what are the project costs and capacity of wind energy;

(c) whether Government find any difficulties in installing these projects in country`s every taluka; and ¦i

(d) if so, Government`s response thereto and the steps taken for installing more wind power generation projects in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NON-CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES (INDEPENDENT CHARGE)

(SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR)

(a)&(b): A gross wind power potential of over 45,000 MW has been estimated in the country. The State-wise details are given in Annexure. Capital cost of wind power projects varies from Rs.4.5 crore to Rs.5.0 crore per MW depending upon the location. Wind Power Projects with an aggregate installed capacity of 5340 MW have been set up in the country till 31st March, 2006.

(c) ; Setting up of Wind power projects is feasible only at locations which have the requisite wind speed, availability of electricity grid and power evacuation facilities. Therefore, it may not be possible to install such projects in every taluka of the country.

(d): The steps taken by the Government to promote setting up of wind power projects include concessional import duty for wind electricity generator sub-systems, excise duty exemption, ten years tax holiday on power projects, benefit of accelerated depreciation and loan from Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (IREDA) and other financial institutions. Wind resource assessment studies are supported in various states for identifying new areas for deployment of wind power projects. Resource assessment, Testing & Certification and R&D support are being provided by the Centre for Wind Energy Technology (C-WET), Chennai, which is an autonomous institution under the administrative control of this Ministry.

records.qtitle: BANNING OF DRUGS TO SAVE VULTURES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the number of three common vultures species has dropped by 95 per cent in last 10 years;

(b) if so, what are the reasons and what provisions are done to protect these species;

(c) whether it is also a fact that Hon’ble Prime Minister has asked to withdraw the use of certain drugs for protecting these species; and

(d) if so, details thereof and what are the reasons for non withdrawal of these drugs even after one year? A N S WE R
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a) As per the reports available, the population of three vulture species namely Slender billed, White backed and Long billed vultures has declined by about 97% in the Indian sub-continent in the last ten years.

(b) Studies carried out in the Indian sub-continent have revealed that the veterinary formulation of the drug diclofenac is the major cause for this sharp decline. These three species of vultures have been included in Schedule-1 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, affording highest degree of protection. They have also been listed by IUCN, the World Conservation Union as ‘critically endangered’ in the year 2000. An action plan has been prepared by Ministry of Environment and Forests for saving the vultures.

(c) & (d) Yes Sir. The National Board of Wildlife, in its meeting held on 17th March, 2005 under the chairmanship of Hon’ble Prime Minister, recommended a ban on the drug diclofenac. Subsequently, consultations with concerned Ministries and pharmaceutical companies to phase out the drug have been held. Since diclofenac is an effective and economical veterinary drug, various issues like availability of a viable substitute, its production and availability in the market, use in humans, etc., involving number of stakeholders, have to be ascertained before a ban is imposed.

records.qtitle: SOCIAL SECURITY COVER FOR FISHERMEN .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have schemes and programmes for the social security cover for the fishermen against accidents caused by cyclone, super-cyclone, etc.;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and

(d) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for the socio-economic protection of small fishermen in the country?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI TASLIMUDDIN)

(a)to (d): The assistance is extended to the people including fishermen affected by the natural calamities such as cyclone, super-cyclone etc. from the Calamity Relief Fund (CRF) and the National Calamity Contingency Fund (NCCF). This includes repair/replacement of boats, nets damaged or lost, input subsidy etc. Besides, Centrally Sponsored National Scheme of Welfare of Fishermen comprising of Group Accident Insurance for Active Fishermen, Development of Model Fishermen Villages through construction of houses, community hall and drinking water facilities and Saving-cum-Relief components is in operation during the Tenth Plan. Under the Group Accident Insurance component, assistance of Rs.50,000 in case of accidental death/ permanent total disability and Rs.25000 for permanent partial disability is provided to the families of the affected fishermen covered under the scheme. Further, safety of fishermen at sea is one of the main components of the macro scheme on Develop ment of Marine Fisheries, Infrastructure and Post Harvest Operations. Under this component, financial assistance to the extent of 20% cost or subject to maximum of Rs.30,000 per unit is extended through National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) for installation of Global Positioning System (GPS) and wireless set on the small mechanized fishing vessels of below 20 meter length.

records.qtitle: NON RECEIPT OF PAYMENTS FOR MILITARY EQUIPMENTS SUPPLIED TO NEPAL
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a payment of about 2.64 crore dollars for providing military equipments to the Nepalese Army has not been made to more than 20 Indian companies even after a lapse of 18 months; and

(b) If so, the action proposed to be taken by Government to recover the money from the Government of Nepal ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI E. AHAMED)

(a) There are certain outstanding dues payable by the Government of Nepal on account of purchase of defence supplies from India for use by the Royal Nepalese Army.

(b) The Government is fully seized of this matter. It has urged the Government of Nepal to settle outstanding dues at the earliest.

records.qtitle: AGREEMENTS IN THE ENERGY SECTOR .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have made agreements with various countries, particularly U.S.A., Russia & France for the further cooperation and development in the energy sector during the last six months; and

(b) if so, the details thereof and the countries with whom agreements were entered into along with the details of each agreement in the field of Energy sector?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI ANAND SHARMA)

(a) - (b) . Government is engaged in a dialogue with a broad range of countries including the US, Russia and France on civilian nuclear energy cooperation with India. During the visit of Prime Minister to the US, the two sides issued a Joint Statement on July 18, 2005 in which the US inter alia stated that it will work with its partners to adjust the international regime to enable full international civil nuclear cooperation with India. Further discussions were held on this issue during the visit of President Bush to India in March 2006. During the visit of Prime Minister to Russian Federation in December 2005 both sides agreed to actively explore opportunities to further expand cooperation in the sphere of peaceful uses of atomic energy. India and France signed a Declaration on the Development of Nuclear Energy for Peaceful Purposes during the visit of President Jacques Chirac to India on February 20, 2006, which underlines the need to develop international cooperation in promoting the use of nuclear energy for peaceful purposes. These discussions are ongoing.

records.qtitle: COMPLAINTS ABOUT IRREGULARITIES IN PMGSY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received complaints about some irregularity and loopholes in Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana in various parts of the country;

(b) if so, details thereof and the steps taken or proposed to be taken against erring agencies;

(c) whether Government have fixed accountability and responsibility for the proper implementation of this scheme in the country; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRIMATISURYAKANTA PATIL)

(a) to (d) `Rural Roads` being a State subject, the State Governments are primarily responsible for ensuring
(i) proper implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) and
(ii) the quality of the road works being taken up under the programme. The complaints relating to irregularities in the implementation of PMGSY are normally referred to the State Governments concerned for appropriate remedial action. The quality of every road work is required to be examined by the Programme Implementation Units and State Quality Monitors appointed by the State Governments. However, as the third tier of Quality Control Mechanism, the National Quality Monitors (NQMs) are engaged for inspection, at random, of the road works under the programme.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) NAXAL ATTACKS .

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a): The number of attacks by naxal outfits during the period from March, 2005 to April 30, 2006 on police stations, jails, trains and railway properties are as under: 


Police Stations/ Pickets/ camps	44


Jail				3


Trains/ Railway properties	27



(b): Naxalites have been able to carry out successful attacks mainly 
due to detailed planning, military type operations and striking at soft 
targets.  The States have been asked to intensify policing and collection and

records.qtitle: GROWTH RATE OF MANUFACTURING SECTOR IN EXPORTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the growth rate of imports has increased more than exports during the financial year 2005-06;

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto and whether it is a fact that the manufacturing sector is slowly losing while the service sector is gaining ground in India;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) the details of steps taken by Government for improving growth rate of manufacturing sector in the country ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH )

(a) As per the provisional data of the Directorate General of Commercial Intelligence & Statistics (DGCI&S), for 2005-06 exports registered a growth rate of 25% while imports increased by 32% over the previous year.

(b)&(c) In the case of India, the higher growth of imports vis-à-vis exports, inter alia, indicates the growing demand for capital goods, raw materials and intermediates in the manufacturing sector and is therefore not a matter of concern for the Government at the moment. According to the advance estimates of the Central Statistics Organisation

(CSO) for 2005-06 manufacturing sector growth is expected to be 9.4% whereas service sector growth is expected to be 9.8% against the overall growth of 8.1% for the economy. This reflects the growing share of both these sectors in GDP.

(d) Government has put in place various policies to improve the growth rate of manufacturing sector. These measures include delicensing of industrial capacity, liberalisation of the foreign trade regime to provide better access to inputs at competitive prices, rationalisation and reduction of taxes, etc. In addition, Industrial Infrastructural Upgradation Scheme (IIUS) has been launched to provide quality infrastructure in functional clusters to enhance international competitiveness of the manufacturing sector.

records.qtitle: SUPREME COURT DIRECTIONS ON TWO CHILD NORM .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have recently received any notice from the Hon’ble Supreme Court regarding implementation of two child norm for containing population growth in the country;

(b) if so, what are Government’s views and the reaction thereto;

(c) whether any specific time-bound programme has been identified by Government, with the help of experts, to dealt with the population growth in our country; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) Yes, Sir. The notice of Writ Petition No. 23/2004 filed by the Azadi Bachao Andolan and another versus UOI and others in the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India has been received. The Writ Petition is regarding Population growth and implementation of National Population Policy, 2000.

(b) Government considers Population stabilization is a vital and priority issue for the nation. The National Population Policy, 2000 (NPP) seeks to promote Family Welfare through responsible and planned parenthood, through voluntary and informed choice of Family Planning method best suited to informed acceptors.

(c) & (d) The Government has launched the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) on 12th April, 2005 throughout the country with special emphasis on 18 demographically and infrastructrally weaker States. More attention is being paid to these States to provide accessible, affordable, accountable, effective, reliable, and quality primary health care, through creation of a cadre of Accredited Social Health Activities (ASHA), improved hospital care measured through Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS), decentralization of programme to district level to improve intra and inter-sectoral convergence and effective utilization of resources. United funds at the rate of Rs.10,000/- per sub centre for all the sub centres for making ASHA and sub centres functional to optimal level and funds for up-gradation of Community Health Centres (CHC) to the level of Indian Public Health Standard @ Rs. 20 lakh per CHC for two CHCs per district have been released to all States/Uts. The Reproductive and Child Health (RCH-II) taken up under the NRHM envisages providing quality services for meeting unmet demands such as free distribution of condoms. IUD, Insertions, Non-Scalpel Vasectomy (NSV), sterilisation etc. with the objective of stabilising population growth in the country, especially in these high focus States.

records.qtitle: UNIFORM SALES TAX ON PETROLEUM PRODUCTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is different percentage of sales tax charged by various State Governments on petroleum products and whether Central Government have received any representations from the State Governments for fixing uniform sales tax like VAT on petroleum products in the country;

(b) whether Government are seriously considering to fix uniform sales tax on petroleum products in the near future; if so, by when; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a) to (c): Under Entry 54 of the State List of the Constitution, `tax on purchase or sale of goods within a State` is a State subject. Thus, the State Sales Tax as well as State VAT (which has replaced the State Sales Tax) is a State subject. An Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers (EC) has been constituted to decide all matters concerning Sales Tax/VAT, including the structure of rates of tax on various commodities. The EC has decided different rates for various petroleum products. Motor Spirits (including Petrol, Diesel and Aviation Turbine Fuel) are non-vatable and are subject to 20% floor rate of tax (except that the floor rate for diesel is 12.5% in case of North-Eastern States, Sikkim and J&K). States may levy taxes at rates higher than the floor rates for these items. Therefore, the rates of tax on these items vary from State to State. The rate of tax for Cooking Gas (LPG), Natural Gas, Naphtha, Lubricants, Low Sulphur Heavy Stock (LSHS) and Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) is 12.5% under VAT. PDS Kerosene is taxable @ 4%.
Since Sales Tax/VAT is a State subject, it is entirely for the EC and the State Governments to take a decision regarding rates on tax on various petroleum products. There is no question of the State Governments making representation to the Central Government or the Central Government deciding to fix uniform sales tax on petroleum products.

records.qtitle: VIOLATIONS BY OVERSEAS INSURANCE COMPANIES .

(d) if so, the details thereof and Government`s reaction thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) As per Insurance Act, 1938, no overseas insurance company can transact insurance business in the country. However, overseas companies are permitted to conduct insurance business in India as joint venture with Indian insurance companies with maximum foreign equity of 26%. List of Indian insurance companies in joint venture with overseas . insurance companies is given at Annexure.

(b) Indian insurance companies are regulated under Insurance Act, 1938, Insurance Regulatory and Development. Authority (IRDA) Act, 1999 and IRDA Regulations which also stipulate protection of policyholders` interests, thereby safeguarding the investors` money.

(c) No, Sir.

(d) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: INCREASING FOREST COVER .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have made any comprehensive strategic plan for increasing the forest cover by maintaining greenery in the country for the next twenty years;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) what steps have been taken or proposed to be taken for increasing forest cover in the country;

(d) the estimated amount to be spent on this plan and whether Government have chalked out any plan for the increasing participation of local people in these plans; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)


(a), (b), (c), (d), and (e) A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
Statement referred to in reply to parts (a), (b), (c), (d), and (e) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No.285 to be replied on 10.03.2006

(a) and (b) The National Forestry Action Programme (NFAP) of India 1999 is a 20 year perspective plan for the forestry sector of the country. The programe document envisaged expansion of forest and tree cover by 21.80 million hectares besides regeneration of 26.43 million hectares of existing forest area with a proposed total investment of Rs.133902.78 crores in 20 years.


(c) Following steps have been taken to increase the forest and tree cover in the country:- 


(i)	Ministry of Environment and Forests is implementing National 
Afforestation Programme (NAP) Scheme for regeneration of degraded forests and 
adjoining forest lands during the Tenth Five Year Plan. The Scheme is being 
implemented through two-tier decentralized mechanism of Forest Development 
Agency (FDA) at forest division level and Joint Forest Management Committees 
(JFMCs) at village level.  As on 06.02.2006, 680 FDA projects have been 
approved in all 28 States at a total cost of Rs.1489.42 crores to cover  
project area of 9.04 lakh hectares through 22,878 JFMCs. 

(ii)

	Consultations with State Governments and Union Territory (UT) 
Administrations, including conferences of Forest Ministers of States and Union 
Territories on 5-6 August 2004 and 15 February 2006, have been held to 
sensitize State/UT authorities about the increased tree planting targets.  


(iii)	State Government and Union Territory Administrations have been 
requested to constitute Chief Secretary-level Committee of all land owning and 
other concerned Departments to involve them in tree planting activities. 


(iv)	Guidelines for rationalization of felling and transit regulations 
for tree species grown on non-forest private lands have been issued by the 
Ministry of Environment and Forests to the State Governments and Union 
Territory Administrations to encourage private tree plantation. 

(v)
	State Government and Union Territory Administrations have been requested 
to formulate and implement a comprehensive Media Plan to create mass awareness 
about tree planting. 

(vi)	Multi-Stakeholder Partnership (MSP), 
involving State Forest Department, the local village community and the private 
sector, has been mooted for forestation of degraded lands.



(d) and (e) The NFAP 1999 envisaged a total investment of Rs.133902.78 
crore in 20 years.  People’s participation is considered as an important 
element of forestry sector in the country.  The Ministry has issued guidelines 
dated 1.6.1990 for involving village communities and voluntary agencies for 
regeneration of degraded forest lands within conceptual framework of Joint 
Forest Management (JFM).  The Ministry is implementing National Afforestation 
Programme (NAP) during the Tenth Five Year Plan to institutionalize and expand 
JFM.  As per information received from States, 99,868 JFMCs are functioning in 
all 28 States covering 21.4 million hectares of forest area. An allocation of 
Rs.1205 crores have been provided for NAP during the Tenth Five Year Plan

records.qtitle: SUBSTANDARD GOLD ARTICLES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that people in our country are purchasing around 15 percent of substandard gold articles and losing their hard earned money annually, according to the Bureau of Indian Standards;

(b) if so, Government’s reaction thereto; and

(c) the steps taken or proposed to be taken against such unethical business?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(SHRI TASLIMUDDIN)

(a) : During the year 2001-2002, Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) had conducted surveys in Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Bangalore, Ahmedabad and Kolkata, associating consumer activists to find out the actual purity of gold jewellery available in the market as against the claims made by jewellers. About 11% of the samples tested were found conforming to the purity claimed. The survey revealed the average shortage of purity of 11%. India consumes around 880 tonnes of gold every year, of which 80% goes into jewellery manufacturing. Based on average 11% shortage in purity, as revealed in the survey, loss to consumers could be estimated at around Rs. 6000 crores annually.

(b) & (c): In order to protect the interests of the common consumers in the purchase of gold jewellery, BIS have launched the Hallmarking Scheme for Gold Jewellery.

records.qtitle: GRANT OF PATENTS TO INVENTIONS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of inventions, which have been granted Patents by Government in the field of energy and automobile sectors since last two years; and

(b) the steps taken or proposed to be taken for using such inventions for the all-round development in energy and automobile sectors in the country?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI ASHWANI KUMAR)

(a): Details of patents granted in the years 2004 and 2005 in the fields of energy and automobile sectors are as in Annexure.

(b): Patents are private property rights granted for new inventions. Patent discloses the invention to the public, including possible investors. In the new liberalized economy, investment decisions are taken, inter-alia, on techno-economic considerations. Technologies which contribute to the competitiveness of the enterprise are naturally preferred by investors. This preference leads to utilisation of patented technologies by the patent holder or licencees of the patent in a manner that permits the optimal and beneficial use of patents. There is also a provision for compulsory licensing of patents under the Patents Act, 1970 as amended by the Patents (Amendment) Act, 2005.
Under Section 84 of the Patents Act,1970, at any time after the expiration of three years from the date of the grant of a patent, any person interested may make an application to the Controller of Patents for grant of compulsory licence on patent on any of the following grounds, namely:-

(a) that the reasonable requirements of the public with respect to the patented invention have not been satisfied, or

(b) that the patented invention is not available to the public at a reasonably affordable price, or

(c) that the patented invention is not worked in the territory of India.

records.qtitle: REPORT ON IMPROVEMENT OF BANKING SYSTEM .

FINANCE MINISTER (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM)

(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT FORRAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.221 FOR 7TH MARCH, 2006 REGARDING REPORT ON IMPROVEMENT OF BANKING SYSTEM TABLED BY SHRISANJAY RAUT

(a) to (d): No, Sir. No Committee/Working Group has been set-up by the Government in the recent past specifically for suggesting measures to improve the nationalised banking system in the country. However, to improve the health of the banking sector in India in general and that of Public Sector Banks in particular and also to bring it at par with the international standards, the Reserve Bank of India has prescribed measures for strengthening of prudential supervision coupled with wide ranging steps undertaken by the Government. After initiation of reforms in early 1990s, financial performance of the banking sector in general and public sector banks in particular, has improved significantly. Balance sheet and profitability indicators viz. Return on Assets, Net Interest Margin, NPA Ratios, Provisioning and Classification norms for NPAs, Capital Adequacy Ratio etc. suggest that the Indian banking sector now compares well with global benchmarks. To facilitate quick and efficient decision-making and to provide Bank Boards sufficient managerial autonomy to be able to compete internationally, Govt, has announced an Autonomy Package on 22.02.2005 for the public sector banks.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M.A.A. FATMI)


(a) to (c) : A statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha.
THE STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION No. 220 ASKED BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT, REGARDING SMART SCHOOLS FOR QUALITY EDUCATION, DUE FOR REPLY ON 6.3.2006.


(a): Yes, Sir.

records.qtitle: REDUCTION IN ECONOMIC COST OF FCI .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have sought suggestions from some organizations during the last two years to reduce the economic cost of the Food Corporation of India;

(b) if so, the names of those organizations alongwith the suggestions given by them; and

(c) the steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government to implement those suggestions?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH)

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b) & (c): M/s McKinsey & Co. was engaged by the FCI to conduct a study to bring about substantial and sustainable efficiency improvements in the FCI’s functioning, including, inter-alia, recommendations on new business models and structural changes, to reduce the subsidy burden while improving its effectiveness in meeting the Government of India’s social objectives. M/s McKinsey & Co have submitted their report on 28th July, 2005.
The important recommendations made in the report are at Annex-I. The recommendations are at various stages of examination/implementation. To implement the recommendations contained in the report, a Programme Implementation Office (PIO) has been set up in FCI.

ANNEXURE-I
ANNEXURE REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (b) & (c) OF THE UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1221 DUE FOR ANSWER ON 3RD MARCH, 2006 IN THE RAJYA SABHA
The important recommendations made in the report of M/s McKinsey & Co. relate to: 


I)  	Financing Cost Reduction:-



a) 	Advance subsidy release linked to stock holding to reduce interest cost.

b)	Refinancing of buffer stock through issue of bonds. 

c)	Refinancing of receivables through issue of bonds and/or term loan. 


II)    	Optimization of rail movement costs by using Linear Programming to 
generate least cost linkages for movement of food grain rakes between the 
source and destination stations.

III)    	Consolidation of handling and transport contracts to reap the 
benefit of	economies of scale. 

IV)     	Renting out/De-hiring of excess storage capacity.

V)	    	Reduction of gunny costs by using once used gunny for procurement 
              of paddy and by making purchase through open tender.

VI)     	Reduction of procurement cost by Direct Procurement.

VII)   	Reduction in Arthiya commission, Purchase tax & other statutory 
              charges.

VIII)   	Reduction of Establishment cost by rationalised deployment of 
              manpower & outsourcing of non-critical activities such as 
              security, housekeeping etc..

IX)    	Improving efficiency by implementing a management Information 
              System that tracks key performance indicators and provides 
              accurate operational data necessary for effective decision 
              making.

X)     	Reduction of Labour cost by Increasing handling norms,  
              Redistribution labour across depots for better match of handling 
              load and labour availability, identifying surplus labour and 
              developing targeted VRS & preventing departmentalization of DPS 
              and Contract Labour.

XI)    	Advance payment to state agencies against Central pool procurement 
              to reduce interest cost.

records.qtitle: LACK OF SAFE DRINKING WATER
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that around 80 percent of all diseases and ailments occurred due to lack of safe drinking water and sanitation facilities in metropolitan cities and urban cities of our country and there is great disgrace and dissatisfaction among the people;

(b) if so, Government`s reaction thereto; and

(c) the details of the steps taken or proposed to be taken against such gloomy situation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )

(a)to(c): Tenth Five Year Plan document indicates that water borne diseases to the extent of 70-80% are related to water contamination and poor sanitation. `Water`, that is to say, `Water supplies` falls within the jurisdiction of the legislative powers of the State Governments vide item 17 of the List II-State List under Seventh Schedule referred to in the Article 246(3) of the Constitution. However, Ministry of Urban Development has been providing assistance to the State Governments under Centrally sponsored Accelerated Urban Water Supply Programme (AUWSP) for water supply projects in small towns with a population upto 20,000 as per 1991/2001 Census. The Centrally sponsored AUWSP has been subsumed in the newly launched scheme of Urban Infrastructure Development Scheme for Small & Medium Towns (UIDSSMT). In order to provide safe drinking water supply and other infrastructure facilities/basic amenities for all cities/towns in the country, Government has launched Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission

(JNNURM) on 3.12.2005 along with two omnibus schemes namely
(i) UIDSSMT and
(ii) Integrated Housing and Slum Development Programme. 63 cities have been selected on the basis of population criteria as per 2001 census and religious/historic and touristic importance for coverage under the Mission. The cities/towns not covered under JNNURM are eligible for assistance under UIDSSMT. Water supply and sanitation are eligible components for assistance under JNNURM and UIDSSMT.

records.qtitle: SUBSIDY TO PRIVATE POWER COMPANIES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )


(a) & (b) : Yes, Sir. The following suggestions have been made by the industry leaders: 


(i)	A suitable framework to be evolved for granting Mega Power Project status and 
	corresponding fiscal benefits to Ultra Mega Projects.


(ii)	Debt equity ratio considered for Ultra Mega Power Projects could be higher than 
	70:30 as this would have a positive impact on the tariff.


(iii)	Matter regarding sectoral cap on exposure for each sector in term of funding to be 
	taken up with RBI so as to facilitate funding of Ultra Mega Power Projects.


(iv)	Some States were charging a tax on auxiliary consumption which needs to be 
	exempted for Ultra Mega Power Projects in addition to sales tax exemption.


(v)	Section 80 IA and Section 10(23)(G) of Income Tax Act 1963 must be applicable 
	for Ultra Mega Power Projects.




The suggestions of  IPPs have been noted for consideration.

records.qtitle: GROWTH RATE OF INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the annual growth rate of industrial production is expected to increase in the current year as compared to the last three years;

(b) if so, the actual growth-rate during the last three years and the estimated growth rate for the year 2005-06;

(c) whether Government have also identified those industries in which growth rate is either increasing or decreasing, as compared to the last three years; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY

(SHRI KAMAL NATH)

(a) & (b): The annual growth of industrial production, in terms of GDP (at constant 1999-2000 prices) originating from mining & quarrying, manufacturing, electricity, gas & water supply, and construction for the current year 2005-06 stands at 9% as per the Advance Estimate of the Central Statistical Organisation, compared to 8.6% in 2004-05, 7.6% in 2003-04 and 7% in 2002-03.

(c) & (d) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (c) AND (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 146 FOR ANSWER ON 1.3.06 REGARDING GROWTH RATE OF INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTION

(c) & (d): The industries whose growth rates increased during the period 2002-03 to 2004-05 are Beverages & Tobacco products, Cotton textiles, Jute products, Textile Products, Machinery & equipment, other Manufacturing industries, Chemicals, Leather & its products, and Metal Products & parts. Also, electricity showed a marginal increase.
The industries currently showing a decreasing growth rate are Food products, Wool, Silk & man-made fibres, Wood & its products, Paper & its products, Rubber, Plastic, Petroleum & coal products, Non-metallic mineral products, Basic metals & alloy and Transport equipment & parts. Mining also registered a decline.

records.qtitle: CORRUPTION IN EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government`s attention has been drawn to the recent raid by income tax department in various educational institutes particularly in Maharashtra in which they found large number of unaccounted fixed deposit receipts, cash deposits and other incriminating documents after mounting complaints by people about blatant corruption during the admission process;

(b) if so, Government`s reaction thereto and the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken against erring educational institutes;

(c) whether Government are bringing any stringent laws for free and fair admission in the engineering and teclinical institutes; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and by when it will be implemented?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M.A.A. FATMI)

(a) to (d): According to the information furnished by the office of Director General of Income Tax (Investigation), Pune, surveys were conducted on certain educational institutions at Pune, Kolhapur, Thane, Mumbai, Nagpur, Latur, Jaisinghpur and Nepani including search actions on officers and some trustees of the institutions. According to the said office, cash seizure of about Rs. 6.00 crores was effected and certain documents showing receipts of donations / capitation fee were found and the assessment proceedings are underway. Details of institutions proceeded against are awaited from the Income Tax authorities.
In order to ensure free and fair admissions in Engineering and Technical Institutes, States are empowered to make appropriate laws under the provisions of Article 15 (5) of the Constitution.

records.qtitle: AIR CONDITION FACILITIES TO SLEEPER CLASS PASSENGERS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:

(b) if so, the details thereof and by when it would be started; and

(c) how much of approximate difference cost would be borne by the Railways between sleeper class coach and 3rd AC coach ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R.VELU)

(a) to (c): With a view to optimise the utilisation of available accommodation in train, a scheme to upgrade full fare paying passengers to the next higher class against the available vacant accommodation has since been extended to all Mail/Express trains having sleeping accommodation w.e.f. 24-02-2006. The salient features of the scheme are given below: -

(i) The scheme is applicable to only full fare paying passengers, free of charge.

(ii) It is applicable only in those trains having sleeping accommodation.

(iii) The passengers for upgradation will be selected on random basis by the System at the time of preparation of reservation charts.

(iv) Upgradation of passengers will be done as under:- 


> Sleeper to 3AC or First Class
> 3 AC to 2AC
> 2AC to 1 AC


(v) Upgradation will not be done for block booking transactions.



(vi) Upgradation will be done only to the extent of clearance of the 
combined waiting list of all classes. If there is no waiting list, no 
upgradation will take place. 



(vii) If a passenger, who has been upgraded, cancels his ticket, 
cancellation charges of the original class only will be payable.

records.qtitle: BOGUS DOCTORS .

(d) whether Government are aware that Literary Conferences are giving such degrees; and

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)


(a) to (e): As per the provisions of Indian Medical Council Act, 1956, Indian Medicine Central Council Act, 1970 and Homeopathy Central Council Act, 1973, only medical practitioners registered under the provisions of the respective Acts are eligible to practice in the concerned system of medicine. Provisions exist in these Acts to take action against unregistered practitioners of medicine. Any person who acts in contravention of the provisions can be punished with imprisonment and fine under respective Acts. The Government do not maintain list of unregistered doctors.
-

records.qtitle: SUGAR PRICES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that sugar prices were growing up since last one year due to shortage of sugar production;

(b) if so, Government’s reaction thereto and the steps taken or proposed to be taken for stabilizing the sugar prices;

(c) whether Government have exported sugar to other countries, particularly Pakistan despite its shortage; and

(d) if so, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH)

(a): The production of cane sugar in the sugar year (October - September) 2004-05 was 130 lakh M.Ts as against the estimated production of 182 lakh M.Ts in the current sugar year 2005-06. The average retail price of sugar in the four principal markets of the country during the calendar year 2004 was in the range of Rs.13.25 – 19.00 per Kg. whereas in the year 2005 it has been in the range of Rs.17.50 – 20.50 per Kg.

(b): To pre-empt unreasonable hike in sugar prices on account unhealthy speculative tendency, if any, and creation of artificial shortage by holding back the released mandatory free sale sugar quota by unscrupulous sugar mills, the Government have, inter-alia, decided to take the following steps to stabilize the prices: 



(i)	Mandatory sale of free sale quota released for a particular month
 within the stipulated period, 



(ii)	Convert the unsold/undespatched quantity of free sale sugar into
 levy sugar,



(iii)	Activate the enforcement/checks of the sugar mills on random
 basis, 


(iv)	Assess the possibility of facilitating imports through Tariff 
Rate Quota mechanism of sugar in long term, notwithstanding the extant 
operational scheme of raw sugar imports under Advance License Scheme. 



(v)	Resort to adequate additional release of free sale quota into
 the open market to tame prices. 



(vi)	Closely and constantly monitor the price of sugar in the country
 for taking necessary fiscal/non-fiscal measures as warranted.



(c):	No, Sir.



(d):	Question does not arise.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) SEWRI NHAVA SEA LINK .

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINSITRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA) 


(a)	Yes, Sir.


(b)	The Mumbai Trans Harbour Sea Link Project will be 22 km long, six lane road bridge (in
	Phase-I) connecting Sewri in Mumbai to Nhava on mainland. The application for
	environmental clearance as per prescribed procedure was received in May, 2001.


(c)	The Central Government has accorded environmental clearance to the project on 11th March
