(d)	As reported by Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) Limited, a State
	Government of Maharashtra Undertaking, the estimated cost escalation is 6% per annum and

(e)	MSRDC has informed that the pre-qualification bids have been 
invited from the prospective 	entrepreneur to implement this project. The 
estimated period for completion of the 	project is around five years from the 
date of award of work.


(f)	Yes, Sir. MSRDC has stated that the minimum concession period 
offer received from the
	bidders would determine the terms. The interested parties who have 
applied for pre-
	qualification are (1) China Harbour Engineering Co., (2) Dywidag-SPCL-
Afcons J/V, (3)
	IIMC Consortium, SKANSKA, (4) Infrastructure Leasing and Financial 
Services Limited,
	SKIL Infrastructure, (5) Larsen & Toubro Limited and (6) Reliance Energy, 
Hyundai
	Engineering Construction Company.

records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether a meeting of Chief Ministers and State Ministers of Co-operatives was held in New Delhi on 9th September 2005, regarding constitution of a Task Force for Co-operative Credit Structure Reforms;

(b) if so, the terms of reference of the Task Force;

(c) whether the Chief Minister and representatives of the Government of Maharashtra has made certain suggestions to revitalize the rural credit system, if so, the details thereof; and

(d) the decisions taken thereon?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)


(a): Government of India held an interactive session with the Chief Ministers/Lt. Governer of all States/UTs on 9th September, 2005 in New Delhi to discuss the recommendations of the Task Force on revival of Rural Cooperative Credit Institutions.

(b): The Terms of Reference of the Task Force constituted by the Government of India in August, 2004 under the Chairmanship of Prof. A. Vaidyanathan to suggest an implementable action plan for reviving the Cooperative Credit Structure (CCS) were as under:- 



i)	To recommend an implementable action plan for reviving the Rural Cooperative 
Banking Institutions, taking into consideration, inter alia, main 
recommendations made by various committees in this regard.


ii)	To suggest an appropriate regulatory framework and the amendments which 
may be necessary for the purpose in the relevant laws.


iii)	To make an assessment of the financial assistance that the Cooperative Banking 
Institutions will require for revival, the mode of such assistance, its sharing 
pattern and phasing.


iv)	To suggest any other measures required for improving the efficiency and 
viability of Rural Cooperative Credit Institutions.


(c):	Suggestions made by the Government of Maharashtra on major items of the revised 
package for revival of Cooperative Credit Structure are as under:


i)	      Audit should be done by the existing audit system.


ii)	Instead of 10% annual increase in recovery level for PACS for release of financial 
assistance, 4% have been suggested.


iii)	Government of India should bear 80% of total financial package.


(d):	After several rounds of consultation with the State Governments, major 
recommendations of the Task Force under Prof. A Vaidyanathan with regard to short term 
cooperative credit structure have been finalized by the Government.  The Government of 
India`s share of the total financial package has been increased from 53% as recommended in 
the report of the Task Force to 68% on an aggregate basis.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) SOIL EROSION .
records.name: R.S. GAVAI
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the rate of soil erosion is growing at an unacceptable rate in various parts of the country;

(b) if so, the country`s average soil erosion rate per hectare per annum and the present rate of soil erosion;

(c) Government`s response thereto; and

(d) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for solving the problem by implementing various programmes in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a)&(b): The soil formation and erosion is a natural process occurring simultaneously to maintain the equilibrium in eco-system. Due to over exploitation, unscientific use of natural resources etc. the land denudation is more than natural formation.
As per available estimate, the average rate of soil erosion in the country is 16.4 tonnes per hectare per year and over 5.3 billion tonnes of soil is lost every year through soil erosion. Soil loss varies from less than 1 tonnes/ha./year in dense forest area to more than 80 tonnes/ha./year in the denuded Shivalik hills. Study conducted by National Bureau of Soil Survey and Land Use Planning (NBSS &LUP), envisages out of 328.60 million ha., about 146.82 million ha. area (45%) is suffering from various kinds of land degradation as given below: 


S.No.	Type of Land Degradation	Extent of Area in million ha. 

1.	Water erosion		93.66 

2.	Wind erosion		9.48 

3.	Water logging		14.30 

4.	Salinity/alkalinity	5.95  

5.	Soil acidity		16.03
6.	Complex problem		7.38
	Total Degraded area	146.82




(c)&(d):    With a view to control soil erosion and land degradation,
Government of India is implementing following Schemes/Programmes:-


(i)	National Watershed Development Project for Rainfed Areas (NWDPRA)	 

(ii)	Soil Conservation for Enhancing the Productivity of Degraded Lands in the Catchment of 
River Valley Projects and Flood Prone Rivers (RVP & FPR) 

(iii)	Reclamations of Alkali Soil (RAS). 

(iv)	Watershed Development Project in Shifting Cultivation Areas (WDPSCA).	 

(v)	Drought Prone Areas Programme (DPAP). 

(vi)	Desert Development Programme (DDP). 

(vii)	Integrated Wasteland Development Programme (IWDP).


Under above programmes upto March, 2005, about 28.5 million ha. has been developed with 
expenditure of Rs.14577.00 crore.

MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND CULTURE ( SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY )

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): A Statement is enclosed.

(c): Funds under the Mission are not earmarked state-wise/city wise. For accessing funds, cities are required to prepare `City Development Plans` (CDPs) and `Detailed Project Reports` (DPRs) and submit them for appraisal to the competent authorities prescribed under the scheme. Projects shall be funded after due appraisal and signing of tripartite agreement among the Central Government, State Government and the Urban Local Bodies/Parastatals. 


	STATEMNT     REFERRED     TO IN REPLY TO PART (b) OF RAJYA     SABMA     USO
	NO.2858 FOR 19.12.2005.


	DETAILS	OF JNNURM AND ITS	OBJECTIVES


	The	Mission comprises	two sub-missions, viz., Sub-Mission-I
	for Urban Infrastructure	and Governance and Sub-Mission-II for
	Basic Services for the Urban Poor.
The Mission provides focussed attention to 63 select cities in different 
States.


For cities/towns not covered under the Mission, the Ministry of Urban 
Development has launched a scheme Known as Urban Infrastructure Development 
Scheme for Small and Medium Towns (UIDSSMT) while the Ministry of Urban 
Employment & Poverty Alleviation has formulated a scheme known as Integrated 
Housing and Slum Development Programme (IHSDP).


The following on-going schemes of the Ministries of Urban Development and Urban 
Employment & Poverty Alleviation have been subsumed in JNNURM :-


	i)	Infrastructure Development in Mega cities,
	ii)	Integrated Development of Small & Medium Towns.
	iii)	Accelerated Urban Water Supply Programme.
	iv)	Urban Reform Incentive Fund


	  Provision of Central assistance is linked to implementation of
	certain mandatory as well as optional~reforms at the State and
	ULB/Parastatal levels.


	  Implementation of all mandatory and optional reforms has to be
	completed during the Mission period of 7 years beginning from
	2005-06.



	Central assistance is in the form of 100% grant to be funded
as	Additional Central Assistance (ACA).
Cities have to prepare City Development Plans (CDPs) and Detailed Project Reports (DPRs).


5% of the Central grant or actual requirement, whichever is less, is provided 
for preparation of City Development Plans, Detailed Project Reports, Capacity 
Building, Information, Education and Communication (IEC) activities etc.
Signing of Tripartite Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) by the
State Governments and Urban Local Bodies/Parastatals with Central Government is 
a necessary condition to access Central
funds. MoA should indicate commitments and milestones to be achieved in the 
implementation of reforms at the State & ULB/Parastatal levels.




FINANCING PATTERN



Depending upon population, geographical location of the cities and category to 
which a city belongs, fund is provided as indicated below:-


(i) 35%/50%/80%/90% of the cost of projects would be funded by Govt. of India through 100% ACA and


(ii) 65%/50%/20%/10% would be funded by State/ULBs/Financial 
Institutions.



 Funds to be released in four installments.



= First installment shall be released on signing of MoA and approval of City 
Development Plans (CDPs)/Detailed Project Reports (DPRs).



Release of subseauent installment to be linked to achievement of 
reform/milestones and progress of projects.



OBJECTIVES OF JNNURM ARE :


1. To provide focused attention to integrated development of 
infrastructural services in the cities.


2. To secure effective linkages between asset creation and asset 
management so that the infrastructural services created in the cities are not 
only maintained efficiently but also become self-sustaining over time.



3,    To ensure adequate investment of funds to fulfill deficiencies in the 
urban sector.


4. To have planned development of identified cities including peri-
urban areas, out growths, urban corridors.


  

5. To scale up delivery of civic amenities and provision of 
utilities with emphasis on universal access to urban poor.



5. To take up urban renewal programme, i.e., re-development of inner (old) 
cities area to reduce congestion.

records.qtitle: DAMAGE TO ONION CROP IN MAHARASHTRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether heavy rains and floods in Maharashtra have caused extensive damage to onion crop in Maharashtra, if so, the extent of loss and damage to the crop;

(b) what percentage of demand for onion in the country is met by Maharashtra, and how far the recent onion crisis in the country was attributable to this damage; and

(c) what Central aid, if any, was sought and given to the Government of Maharashtra to help the farmers out of the crisis caused by such damage to onion crop?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR)

(a) to (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 343 FOR 16/12/2005 REGARDING DAMAGE TO ONION CROP IN MAHARASHTRA.


(a) to (c): Heavy rains and floods in Maharashtra have caused extensive damage to onion crops during this year (2005). During April-May, 2005, unseasonal rain and high temperature during harvesting time of rabi crop resulted in poor quality which was responsible for reduced shelf-life because of which quantity of onion stored, decreased by 25% in comparison to last year. Against 7 lakh tonnes stored in 2004, only 5.25 lakh tonnes could be stored in 2005. During July 2005, owing to continuous rains in Maharashtra, there was damage to the seed sown during early kharif, forcing the farmers to re- sow, causing production loss and delayed kharif crop in Maharashtra by about a month. Loss of nursery and delayed monsoon resulted in reduction of onion cropped area by about 15%. Again, during October 2005, heavy rains damaged the kharif crop in some of the districts of Maharashtra. The overall loss in kharif production in Maharashtra is estimated to be about 43%. Against the production of 2.70 lakh tonnes in kharif 2004, the production in Maharashtra during kharif, 2005 is 1.55 lakh tonnes.
The State of Maharashtra meets 28% of the total demand of onion in the country. As mentioned above, the unseasonal and excess rainfall is responsible for shortage in availability of onion and consequent price hike. This situation prevailed for a short period during the month of October 2005, which soon stabilized due to sufficient arrival of onion from Rajasthan and other Southern States.
Government of Maharashtra submitted a memorandum to the Central Government for the floods that occurred in July – August 2005 indicating the total agricultural loss at Rs.1239.57 crore. Memorandum of the State Government did not indicate crop-wise breakup of the losses. Government have approved release of an amount of Rs.697.45 crore.

records.qtitle: FARMERS LEAVING AGRICULTURE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that more than 40 per cent farmers would like to quit agriculture business due to unsafe and low margin to agro-produce, water dependent production as well as unavailability of agriculture loan on lower percentage of interest rate in the country;

(b) if so, Government`s views and reaction thereto; and

(c) the details of measures taken or proposed to be taken for improving the current unfavourable atmosphere in the agriculture by keeping in view the poor farmers of the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a): As per the 59th Round Survey Report of National Sample Survey Organisation submitted in July 2005, 40 per cent of the farmer households do not like farming as a profession as they consider it unprofitable, risky, lacking social status etc. While 27 per cent of the farmer households consider agriculture being not profitable, 8 per cent consider it as a risky venture. Remaining 5 per cent dislike it for some other reasons, which also include lack of social status.

(b) & (c): The Government is seized of the problems being faced by the farmers. A number of measures have been taken by the Government to increase production and productivity in agriculture sector as also to raise the farm income by ensuring remunerative prices and thereby reasonable return to them. The measures, inter-alia, include easy and timely availability of institutional credit in a hassle free manner to the farmer at low rate of interest, better risk management through implementation of crop insurance scheme, strengthening of marketing and storage facilities, promotion of agricultural diversification towards income enhancing crops and activities suitable to small holdings, sustainable dry-land farming, subsidy and price support measures like announcement of Minimum Support Prices and organizing of purchase operations to prevent distress sales by the farmers.
A number of specific Schemes are being implemented for the benefit of farmers including small and marginal farmers. Prominent among these are National Horticulture Mission, Macro Management of Agricultural Scheme, Integrated Scheme of Oilseeds, Pulses, Oil Palm & Maize

(ISOPOM), Technology Mission on Cotton, Technology Mission on Coconut; Technology Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture in North Eastern States including Sikkim, Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttaranchal, Seed Village Scheme, Strengthening of Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure. Under these Schemes financial assistance is provided to the farmers. Besides, efforts are also on to cover larger areas under irrigation to reduce dependence on rain

records.qtitle: HYDRO POWER PLANTS IN THE WESTERN PART OF THE COUNTRY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the number with capacity of hydro plants that are running in the western parts of the country particularly in Maharashtra State;

(b) whether Government are considering any proposal to tap resource for hydro projects in the western part of the country, particularly in Maharashtra State;

(c) if so, the details thereof by indicating how much of power will be generated from this region; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND MINISTER OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS

( SHRI PRIYA RANJAN DASMUNSI )


(a) : In the Western Region, 45 hydro-electric plants (of capacity above 3 MW each) with aggregate installed capacity of 6388.50 MW are in operation. Of these, 29 hydro-electric plants with installed capacity of 2825.30 MW are in operation in the State of Maharashtra. In addition, Maharashtra has 27% share of power in the Sardar Sarovar hydro-electric project with installed capacity of 1450 MW of which 1050 MW capacity has been commissioned and 400 MW is under construction. The State of Maharashtra also has 33.3% share of power from Pench hydro-electric station (160 MW).

(b) to (d) : Five hydro-electric projects with installed capacity of 1230 MW are under construction in the Western Region of which one hydro-electric project namely, Ghatghar Pump Storage Scheme (250 MW) is under construction in the State of Maharashtra. Besides, commercial viability of the Bav hydro-electric project Stage-II (20 MW) in Maharashtra has been assessed and the project is to be executed by National Hydroelectric Power Corporation.
The Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) of 16 hydro-electric schemes with estimated installed capacity of 4355 MW in the Western Region have been returned to the project authorities by the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) for re-submission after compliance of the observations of the CEA/Central Water Commission and Geological Survey of India. Of these, 4 schemes with installed capacity of 1430 MW are in the State of Maharashtra.
Under the 50,000 MW Hydro-electric Initiative of the Government of India, the pre-feasibility reports of 17 schemes with installed capacity of 1464 MW have been prepared for the Western Region. Of these, 9 schemes with total installed capacity of 411 MW are in the State of Maharashtra. As the first year indicative tariffs of these schemes are high, these are not being considered for preparation of Detailed Project Report in the first instance.

records.qtitle: INTERNATIONAL BIDDING FOR LOWER TRAFFIS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is considering to allow power generation and distribution only through competitive global bidding to ensure lower tariffs;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for providing `Electricity to all` in the next five years?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND MINISTER OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS

( SHRI PRIYA RANJAN DASMUNSI )

(a) & (b): Under the provisions of the Electricity Act, while generation of electricity is delicensed, distribution is a licensed activity and the license is granted by the respective Electricity Regulatory Commission.
The National Electricity Policy recognizes that competition will bring significant benefits to consumers, in which case, it is competition which will determine the price rather than any cost plus exercise on the basis of operating norms and parameters. The policy states that all efforts would need to be made to bring the power industry to this situation as early as possible, in the overall interest of consumers.
Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003 provides that the Regulatory Commissions shall adopt the tariff if it is determined through transparent process of bidding in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Central Government. The guidelines in this regard have already been issued.

(c) : The Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojna has been launched in April, 2005 towards realizing the goal of providing access to electricity to all households in five years through creation of :- 


i)	Rural Electricity Distribution Backbone (REDB) with at least one
 33/11 KV 	(or 66/11 KV) sub-station in each block.


ii)	Village Electrification Infrastructure (VEI) with at least one
 distribution 	transformer in each village/habitation.


iii)	Decentralised Distributed Generation (DDG) Systems where grid
 supply is not feasible or cost-effective.


		There is a provision of 90% capital subsidy from the Central
 Government for projects sanctioned under the scheme.

records.qtitle: PROGRAMME OF VILLAGE ENERGY SECURITY BASED ON BIO MASS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have made announcement that programme of village energy security based on bio-mass will be implemented in 600 villages from 600 districts in the country in the last year;

(b) if so, the details of progress made by Government in this regard;

(c) whether this programme is being implemented successfully and if not, what are the difficulties Government is facing therefor; and

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NON-CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) (SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR)

(a) : An Outline Plan was prepared by the Ministry of Non-Conventional Energy Sources for creating energy security in villages through biomass. In the National Conference on Renewable Energy for Rural Areas organized by the Ministry in July, 2004, it was stated that the Ministry would consider one village energy project in every district and a beginning would be made by setting up pilot projects in a few selected villages.

(b) & (c) : 24 test projects were taken up last year in three States, viz., 11 in Madhya Pradesh, six in Rajasthan and seven in West Bengal. In these projects the total energy requirements including cooking, lighting and motive power will be met through the energy production systems using locally available biomass resources, with participation of the local community. The first test project in an adivasi village in Betul district of Madhya Pradesh has been implemented successfully. A total of 100 test projects are planned upto the end of March, 2006.

(d) : During 2006-07, it is envisaged to take up another 100 test projects on village energy security in different States.

records.qtitle: PROBLEMS IN GETTING EDUCATIONAL LOANS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that many students flora poor and middle class families are facing problems in getting educational loan is for their further studies;

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto and the, details of` step taken :for making available the education loans to every student belonging 11:o poor and middle class family who desires to seek higher studies;

(c) whether Government are seriously considering to raise Corpus Fund which will offer students loans at zero or minimum rate of interest; and

(d) if so, the details thereof mad if riot, the :reasons therefor? A NSWER
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM

(a)&(b): No specific complaint has come to the notice of the Government that students from poor and middle class families are facing problems :in getting educational loans. Government in consultation with RBI & IBA has framed a comprehensive educational loan scheme to ensure that no deserving student in the country is deprived of higher education for want of finances. Under the revised model educational loan scheme (August. 31, 2004) the simplified procedure/criteria are under:
Security:
Education Loan up to Rs.4 lakh: No Security. Above Rs.4 lakh and up to Rs.7.5 lakh: collateral in the form of a suitable third party guarantee. The bank may, at its discretion, waive third party gurantee if satisfied with the net-worth/means of parents who would be executing the document as “Joint borrower”. Above Rs.7.5 lakh: collateral security of suitable value or suitable third party guarantee alongwith the assignment of future income of the student for payment of installments. Margin: No collateral or margin requird for loans up to Rs. 4 lakh. Interest: Interest not to exceed PLR for loans up to Rs.4 lakh.and PLR +1% for loans above Rs.4 lakh.

(e): No, Sir.

(d): Does not arise.

records.qtitle: MASS RAPID TRANSIT SYSTEM IN MUMBAI
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Government of Maharashtra has taken a decision to implement Mass Rapid Transit System along Andheri-Ghatkopar Corridor in Mumbai with public private participation with the estimated cost of Rs.1500 crores;

(b) whether the Government of Maharashtra has forwarded the proposal to the Union Government to provide 15 per cent of equity and 50 per cent of viability gap funding and extend all necessary concessions for customs and excise duty on lines of Delhi Metro;

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND CULTURE

( SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY )

(a): Yes, Sir. The Government of Maharashtra proposes to construct Mass Rapid Transit System on the Versova-Andheri-Ghatkopar Corridor (15.0 km) on Build, Operate & Transfer (BOT) basis at an estimated cost of Rs.1500 crore

(April` 03 prices).

(b)&(c): The Government of Maharashtra has undertaken a bidding process to identify a private promoter. No firm proposal of the extent of funds required has been received by the Central Government, as this would depend on the outcome of the bidding process.

(d)&(e): Do not arise.

records.qtitle: WELFARE SCHEMES FOR WIDOWS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government propose to implement any welfare scheme by involving State Governments for helpless poor widows so that, they can survive;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI KANTI SINGH)

(a)&(b) The Government has launched a scheme called Swadhar in 2001-2002 which seeks to Rehabilitate the women in difficult circumstances like widows, destitute and deserted women, women ex-prisoners, victims of several abuse and crimes, including those trafficked and rescued from brothels, migrant or refugee women who have been rendered homeless due to natural calamities like flood, cyclone, mentally challenged women, women victims of terrorist violence etc. The components covered include shelter, food, counseling, medical and legal support, training for the economic rehabilitation of women and helpline facilities. The implementing agencies can be Social Welfare/Women and Child Welfare Department of State Government, Women’s Development Corporations, Urban Local Bodies, reputed Public/Private Trust in Voluntary Organizations who are willing to take up the responsibility of rehabilitating such cases duly recommended by the State Governments are placed before the Project Sanctioning Committee which decides the case on meetings.

(c) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: PRIVATIZATION OF RAIL BASED CONTAINER TRANSPORTATION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have finalised any plan or policy for privatization of rail-based container transportation in the country; and

(b) if so, the details thereof, indicating advantage therefrom?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R.VELU)

(a) : No, Sir.

(b) : Does not arise.

records.qtitle: PANTRY CAR IN MAIL AND EXPRESS TRAINS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) how many long distance mail and express trains do not have a separate pantry car for serving hot and fresh refreshments to railway passengers and how many mail and express trains have pantry car facilities ;

(b) whether it is a fact that Railways has incurred heavy loss for providing refreshments to railway passengers since last so many years as Railways does not offer any subsidy thereon ;

(c) if so, the details of reasons therefor ; and

(d) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for providing quality and fresh refreshments to railway passengers at ostensible price by avoiding losses thereon ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

( SHRI R. VELU )

(a) There are about 468 long distance Mail/ Express trains which presently do not have pantry car and approximately 250 Mail/Express, trains including Rajdhani/Shatabdi trains, are running with Pantry Cars.

(b) & (c) : Based on costing methodology, losses have been incurred by Indian Railways on catering services as a whole. This is mainly due to the reason that total cost of catering services, which inter-alia includes running cost of pantry car and terminal cost of both pantry cars and stationary units, is more than earnings from theses services.




(d) In order to provide quality and fresh refreshments at reasonable price with a view to avoid losses, Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) has been set up to upgrade, professionalise and manage the catering service and upgrade the quality of food and earnings. Refreshment rooms, Automatic Vending Machines, Food Plazas and Stall have been established through reputed and experienced caterers. Regular and surprise checks are conducted by officials of Railways/ IRCTC to monitor quality/quantity/tariff of catering services. Licences are being awarded through two packet open tender system on competitive bidding basis in which a minimum of 12% of sales turnover is fixed as floor price and licence is awarded to the highest bidder. Sales of units are assessed realistically to avoid losses to Railways.

records.qtitle: DEVELOPMENT OF PORTS IN MAHARASHTRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the State Government of Maharashtra had submitted proposals for the development of ports in the Maharashtra;

(b) if so, the details of these proposals which are still pending and the progress made so far in respect thereof; and

(c) when were these proposals mooted and the reasons for the delay?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

(SHRI T.R. BAALU)

(a) to (c): The Maharashtra Maritime Board had proposed four projects of development of minor ports at Jaigad, Dharamtar, Redi and Vijaydurg under the proposed National Maritime Development Programme (NMDP). Government has for the time being decided to prepare the National Maritime Development Programme, comprising schemes/projects for development of Major Ports, Shipping and Inland Water Transport Systems.

records.qtitle: POOR SERVICES BY MTNL TO MOBILE USERS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that MTNL`s more than five lakhs mobile phones were standstill throughout day during the last week of October, 2005;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(c) the details of precautionary measures taken or proposed to be taken for providing best and uninterrupted services of MTNL mobile users?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

(a) & (b) Sir, on 24-10-2005, there was an interruption in Cellular Mobile network for incoming calls only for a period of two hours on in Main Switching Centre at Tis Hazari, Delhi.
The services of Dolphin Mobile in Mumbai were affected for five hours on 26.10.2005 due to technical problems.

(c) All efforts are made to provide uninterrupted services by closely monitoring and taking prompt corrective measures.

records.qtitle: DEVELOPMENT OF WASTE AND DROUGHT AFFECTED LAND . SHILL SAN JAY RAUT
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering to formulate a comprehensive action plan for development of waste land, drought affected land by producing agro-crop in the country with the help of National Employment Guarantee Scheme; and

(b) . if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI SURYAKANTA PATIL)

(a) & (b) : The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 has been notified on 7.9.2005. Under the Act, rural employment Guarantee Schemes are to be formulated by the State Governments. The State Governments have been instructed to formulate rural employment Guarantee Schemes under the Act. Land development, irrigation canals including micro and minor irrigation works and provision of irrigation facilities to land owned by households belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes or to land of beneficiaries of land reforms or that of the beneficiaries under the Indira Awaas Yojana are some of the permissible works under National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA).

records.qtitle: SHORTAGE OF COAL IN THERMAL POWER PLANTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are grave shortage of coal and many thermal power plants are facing acute shortage of coal in the country since last three months;

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto; and

(c) the details of measures taken or proposed to be taken for providing required coal to the power plants?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI P.M. SAYEED )

(a) & (b) : There was no grave shortage of coal during the last three months and no generation loss has been reported by any thermal power station in the country due to shortage of coal.

(c) : Following steps have been taken by the Government for augmenting supply of coal to the power plants in the county: 


	-	The coal supply position of thermal power stations is vigorously
 monitored in the Central Electricity Authority and Ministry of Power on daily
 basis.


	-	The Infrastructure coordination Committee, reviews the coal
 production and supply to thermal power stations in the country every month.


	-	A Sub-group headed by the Joint Secretary in the Department of
 Coal, every week reviews and resolves the problems of coal supply to thermal
power stations.


	-	Coal is being imported to supplement the augment supplies from
indigenous sources.


	-	New Coal blocks are being allocated by the Ministry of Coal to
 power producers / utilities for captive mining.


	-	Streamlined procedure by Ministry of Environment & Forests to
 expedite the 	environmental/forest clearances to pending coal mining
 projects.


		Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has been requested for
 augmentation of production of natural gas from the gas fields/wells,
 increasing availability of gas from domestic sources, encouraging import of
gas.

records.qtitle: PROBLEMS FACED BY FIREWORKS INDUSTRY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government’s attention have been drawn to the problem facing fireworks industrialists due to complexities in the present rules for exporting fireworks production to other countries; and

(b) if so, Government’s views and reaction thereto?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN)


(a) & (b) This Ministry has not received any representation relating to the rules regulating the export of fireworks. Under the simplified Explosives Rules, 1983, a licence, in form 28 is obligatory for export of fireworks. The applicant is required to submit an application in form 11 alongwith fee of Rs. 150/- to the Chief Controller of Explosives. For export by sea, the licensee is also required to comply with the requirements of International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code/Rules administered by Director General of Shipping. For export by land, Central Government’s clearance under Rule 30 of Explosives Rule, 1983 is also required. For export by air, clearance is also required from Director General of Civil Aviation and in case of export of firework item which is not included in Schedule VI of Explosives Rules, exemption of Rule 31(2) is required from Central Government under Section 14(2) of Explosives Act, 1884.

records.qtitle: STATES DEBT BURDEN .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that various State Governments are facing acute financial problems and they are trapped in debt;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether there is any possibility that interest rate against States borrowings can be slumped upto 5 to 6 percent; and

(d) if so, Government`s approach thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE SHRI S. S. PALANIMANICKAM

(a & b) States have been facing financial problems due to increase in the debt liabilities which have gone up from 24.9% of GDP in 1999-2000 to about 31.7% of GDP in 2004-05.

(c & d) Not in the short terrn. However, with respect to the Central loans disbursed to states up to 31.312004 and as outstanding on 31.3.2005, Government of India has accepted the recommendation of the Twelfth Finance Commission, to consolidate such loans at a reduced interest rate of 7.5%, with repayment in 20 equal annual installments subject to States enacting their FRBM Act.

records.qtitle: INVESTMENT OF BLACK MONEY IN URBAN SEMI URBAN PROPERTY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware that after recent anti-corruption drive at high places there are large chunks of unaccounted black money invested in urban or semi-urban property, share market as well as gold;

(b) if so, Government`s reaction thereto;

(c) whether Government are considering any proposal to unearth black money and assets in various parts of the country;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefore?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a)&(b): The Central Bureau of Investigation had conducted a special drive on 30.9.2005 wherein 59 cases have been registered against 76 public servants for various allegations, including possession of disproportionate assets. Due process of law is being followed to take action against these officers/officials.

(c)&(d): The Income Tax Department undertakes several measures to unearth black money. These include, among others, undertaking search & seizure and survey actions, and scrutiny of returns in appropriate cases. Further, the Government has recently introduced to additional anti-tax evasion measures. From June, 2005 onwards, a `banking cash transaction tax` @ 0.1% is being levied in respect of cash withdrawals from banks above a specified amount, other than from savings accounts. The tax is also levied on encashment of bank deposits above a specified amount. Further, it has become obligatory for all banks to report to the Income Tax Department all deposits which are exempt from Tax Deduction at Source (TDS) on interest.

(e): Not applicable, in view of reply to part (e) and (d) above.

records.qtitle: PRODUCTIVITY OF EDUCATION SYSTEM .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government`s attention has been drawn to the statement made by the Head of National Knowledge Commission that only 6 per cent students garner gains from the current education system aNd around 80 per cent higher education curriculum went on unproductive for .students;

(b) if so, Government`s reaction thereto; and

(c) the details of the steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government for making education system more competitive and productive by taking co-operation of the scientists and research experts in the various fields?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI ARJUN SINGH)

(a) to (c): A Statement is !i aid on the table of the House.
STATEMENT REFER?RED TO IN REPLY TO PART (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.176 FOR REPLY ON 05.12.2005 ASKED BY SHRI SANJAY? RAUT REGARDING PRODUCTIVITY OF EDUCATION SYSTEM.

(a) Chairperson:, National Knowledge Commission, has, on certain occasions, only commented that Gross Enrolment Ratio in higher education is around 6%, thus implying that a large majority of our young people do not have access to higher education. He has also commented that our education system needs to be adapted to meet the challenges of the 2lst century, and that tile Commission will, in due course, recommend strategies for dealing with these, challenges.

(b)Gross Enrolment Ratio for age group 18-.24 years in the year 2002-03 was around 9%. Government agrees that this needs to be substantially increased and that higher education needs to be made more relevant with respect to the current and emerging context.

(c) Scientists and experts are invariably associated in various statutory, advisory and other bodies engaged in designing educational reforms.

records.qtitle: USE OF GIS FOR CITY DEVELOPMENT
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering any plan to computerize all the information data of various civic, infrastructure and properties in the country like Kolkata`s Geographical Information System (GIS) for the benefit of city development;

(b) if so, by when it would be facilitated in the country; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND CULTURE

( SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY )


(a)&(b): A new scheme viz. National Urban Information System

(NUIS) has been formulated by this Ministry of Urban Development. The objective of the scheme is to establish a town level Geographic Information System (GIS) database. During the first phase 137 towns shall be covered with an estimated cost of Rs.66.28 crore. The scheme has been approved by the Government and is being operationalised during the current financial year 2005-2006.

(c): Does not arise.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) EARTHQUAKE RESISTANT BUILDINGS
records.name: M.A.M. Ramaswamy
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether Government have asked the State Governments to enforce safer building codes more vigorously in view of the frequent disasters due to earthquakes;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) the State Governments who have not yet enacted any building laws/code; and

(d) the steps taken by Government in this regard keeping in view the frequent earthquakes and other natural disasters taking place in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND CULTURE

( SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY )

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): Construction of buildings is governed and regulated by Building Bye-laws / Regulations framed by respective States / Urban Local Bodies. The National Building Code, 2005 published by Bureau of Indian Standards under Ministry of Consumer Affairs contains, inter-alia, a chapter on Structural Design (Part 6), which gives all the provisions for structural safety. Further, Model Building Bye-Laws brought out by Town & Country Planning Organisation (TCPO) under this Ministry also contains a section on Structural Design, which mentions that design of foundation, masonry, timber, plain concrete, reinforced concrete, pre-stressed concrete and structural steel shall be carried out in accordance with Part 6 of National Buildings Code. Both National Building Code, 2005 and Model Building Bye Laws are advisory in nature and have been circulated to all the State Governments for their adoption.
Ministry of Urban Development has been impressing upon the States from time to time by way of letters, workshops and conferences to suitably amend their existing bye-laws and regulations to ensure earthquake resistant houses and buildings.
A model Town & Country Planning Legislation, Zoning Regulation, Development Control and Building Regulation / Bye-laws for safety against Natural Hazards, including earthquakes, have also been prepared by an Expert Committee constituted by Ministry of Home Affairs. All the States have been advised to amend their respective Acts / Bye-laws / Regulations so that construction activities are regulated with respect to safety against earthquake hazards.
Buildings Materials & Technology Promotion Council under the Ministry of Urban Employment & Poverty Alleviation has been holding workshops to help the State Governments in amending there Acts / Bye-laws / Regulation for safety against natural hazards, including earthquake, and to disseminate recommendations of the Expert Committee at the instance of Ministry of Home Affairs.

(c): This information is being collected from the States.

(d): As already stated in reply to part (b), the subject of building construction, framing of building bye-laws / codes and its enforcement are the responsibilities of State Governments and Urban Local Bodies. The Central Government has been pursuing and sensitizing the State Governments on this matter so that safety norms for building construction are brought into practice and enforcement mechanisms established at the earliest.

records.qtitle: DETERIORATING SITUATION OF CHILDREN .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware of the fact that children’s education, health, nutrition and death rate are deteriorating in comparison to the other developing countries;

(b) if so, Government’s views thereon and those who are responsible therefor;

(c) whether Government would like to control various children oriented Central Government’s Schemes and programmes by making it responsible and accountable; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRIMATI KANTI SINGH)

(a) The child indicators in India are not very encouraging in comparison to other developing countries as per the State of the World’s Children Report of UNICEF for 2005. However, India has made steady progress in certain areas during last ten years. As per national Family Health Survey of 1992-93 and 1998-99 the position is in Annexure.

(b) Larger child population and other social and economic factors influence the condition of children in our country. Efforts are being made by the Government to overcome the difficulties and improve the overall status of the children through its schemes and programmes for children.

(c)&(d) Various schemes and programmes are being implemented by Government to address different issues relating to children, such as, health, education, nutrition, immunization, early childhood development, protection from exploitation, etc. The schemes and programmes include Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan, Integrated Child Development Services, Reproductive and Child Health, Accelerated Rural Drinking Water Supply Programme, Central Rural Sanitation Programme, Pulse Polio, Integrated Programme for Street Children, Integrated Programme for Juvenile Justice, Scheme for elimination of child labour, and others.
The Government has prepared a National Plan of Action for Children 2005 which contain the goals, objectives and strategies pertaining to children. The concerned Ministries and Departments and all States/UTs have been asked to implement the provisions of the Plan in order to achieve its targets with special focus on monitoring and outcomes.

records.qtitle: UNDP REPORT ON INFANT MORTALITY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government`s attention has been drawn to the recent UNDP`s human development report on increasing high infant and maternal mortality rates in the country, particularly in Maharashtra State;

(b) whether Bangladesh has fared much better in tackling infant mortality and malnutrition problems than India ; and

(c) if so, the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for reducing the growth rates of infant and maternal mortality and banish malnutrition among children in the country?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

( SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) & (b)The UNDP`s Human Development Report-2005 mentions that the annual rate of decline in child mortality in India has decreased from 2.9% in 1980 to 2.3% since 1990. The report also mentions that the rate of decline in child mortality has been higher in Bangladesh than in India during this period. The UNDP report, however, does not examine the infant mortality rate. According to data on infant and child mortality rates in India available from the Sample Registration System of Registrar General of India, both infant mortality rate and child mortality rate have shown a consistent declining trend over the years. The same is also true for the State of Maharashtra where the infant mortality rate has shown a decline from 45 per thousand live births in 2001 to 42 per thousand live births in 2003.


( c) Government of India have recently launched the National Rural Health Mission which aims at providing effective health care including child health and safe motherhood services to rural population throughout the country with special focus on those states which have weak public health indicators. The mission seeks to improve access of services especially to poor women and children for equitable, affordable, accountable and effective primary health care. The Reproductive and Child Health Programme which aims at accelerating decline in infant, child and maternal mortality rates is an integral part of this mission.
Under the Reproductive & Child Health Programme interventions for improving maternal and child health are being implemented in all districts of the country. The interventions for children include Immunization against six vaccine preventable diseases, control of deaths due to diarrhoea and Acute Respiratory Infections, Prophylaxis for Vitamin A deficiency, Iron deficiency anemia and Essential Newborn Care. For the mothers the interventions include essential obstetric care; emergency obstetric care; provision of referral transport through panchayats and provision of drugs and equipment at first referral units.

records.qtitle: WHEAT STOCKS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that wheat prices will be raised further in the next five months as there will be no stock of wheat with Food Corporation of India (FCI) upto March, 2006 around the time the new crop of wheat is expected to arrive in the market;

(b) if so, Government`s views and response thereto by indicating the total stock of wheat with Food Corporation of India as on 30th October, 2005; and

(c) the total quantity of wheat sold by FCI under Open Market Supply Scheme in the last nine months indicating its selling price ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION ( DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH )


(a) & (b): As on 1st November, 2005 there was a stock of 90.52 lakh tonnes of wheat in the Central Pool. This stock is sufficient to meet the requirements of the Targetted Public Distribution System (TPDS) and the other Welfare Schemes till the arrival of the next Rabi Crop in 2006. The prices of wheat under the Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) have been fixed upto the end of December, 2005 and there is no proposal under the consideration of Government for revising the wheat prices under OMSS (D) before the expiry of this period.

(c): A total quantity of 3.19 lakh tonnes of wheat has been sold under the Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) during the period January to October, 2005. The wheat has been sold in the price range of Rs. 610 to Rs. 938 per quintal, as applicable for the stocks pertaining to the various crop years/categories, in the States/UTs during the said period.

records.qtitle: PROMOTION OF S T .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have taken any new measures for the promotion of research in science and technology by bringing huge investment in this arena;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and;

(c) the details of research which have been found useful and cost effective in various sectors?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY AND MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF OCEAN DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI KAPIL SIBAL)

(a) to (c): A substantial increase, more than double the 9th plan outlay, in the tenth plan outlay for S & T Departments is a clear indication of the commitment of the Government to the overall development of science and technology in the country. Government has taken a number of initiatives for the promotion of research in science and technology in the country. During the 10th Five Year Plan the Government has focused on generating relevant innovative technologies; preserving, protecting and adding value to indigenous resources; adopting an appropriate mix of traditional, conventional and modern technologies; developing and nurturing human resource; strengthening basic research in the areas of frontline science & engineering and; promoting S&T interventions in major socio-economic ministries and states so as to make them real stake holders of S&T. The support to research is enhanced through S&T mission mode programmes, establishment of new research centres of excellence, international collaborative projects, strengthening of R&D infrastructure in academic institutions and research labs, institution of prestigious fellowships like Swarnajayanti Fellowship for outstanding Young Scientists, Ramanna Fellowship for performing scientists, Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Fellowship for Young Scientists, Ramanujan Fellowships to attract outstanding scientists and engineers from all over the world to take up scientific research in our country, J.C Bose Fellowships to recognize and support active, performing Indian scientists & engineers. Major new initiatives are: National Biotechnology Strategy; Nano Science & Technology Mission; National Mission on Bamboo Applications; Seismology Mission; Drug & Pharmaceuticals R&D; New Millennium Indian Technology Leadership Initiative; Tsunami Warning System etc. Research in sectors like Drug & Pharmaceuticals, Health & Medical; focusing research in peptide based anti cancer drug, AIDS, tuberculosis etc., Nano Science & Technology; carbon nanotube based fluid energy sensors, surface coatings etc., Information Technology, Agriculture & Waste Utilization etc. are some examples which have been found to be useful and cost effective.

records.qtitle: CONSTRUCTION OF SPORT COMPLEXES IN MAHARASHTRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have any policy to develop or construct sports complexes in the country according to the census ;

(b) if so, the details thereof ; and

(c) whether Government are considering to construct modern sports complexes as well as sports infrastructure in various districts of Maharashtra for the promotion of various sports activities ; and

(d) if so, the details thereof ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) STATISTICS & PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION, YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS AND OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS

(SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES )

(a) to (d) `Sports` is a `State` subject under the Constitution. It is, primarily, the responsibility of the State Government to create basic sports infrastructure including sports complexes. Till 31.3.2005, the Ministry was supplementing the efforts of the State Governments including Maharashtra for creation of various sports facilities in this direction by providing Central assistance for creation of various sports facilities under the Centrally Sponsored Sports Infrastructure Schemes in accordance with the approved pattern subject to the receipt of viable proposals from the State Government. The Sports Infrastructure schemes have been transferred to the State sector w.e.f. 1.4.2005 and all State Governments were informed accordingly in February, 2005. No funds have been allocated in the budget for 2005-06 for sports infrastructure schemes. Thus, fresh proposals for the Sports Infrastructure projects have to be funded by the State Governments out of their own resources.

records.qtitle: REDUCTION OF GRANTS FOR VARIOUS VIDYAPEETH UNIVERSITIES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware that around 34 sport competition games placed at the Vidyapeeth/University level have put off cancelled due to Government`s decision to reduce the grants for various Vidyapeeth /University in the country;

(b) if so, Government`s reaction thereto; and

(c) the measures taken or proposed to be taken for the development of Sports infrastructure and competition at par with International standard ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) STATISTICS & PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION, YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS AND OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS

(SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES )

(a) & (b) : Till 31-3-2005, the Ministry was providing grants to Association of Indian Universities (AIU) for organizing Inter Universities Tournaments/Coaching Camps/Participating in World Universities Games etc. which formed part of the Scheme of `Grants for Promotion of Sports in Universities and Colleges` in accordance with the approved pattern. All the Sports Infrastructure Schemes have been transferred to the State Sector w.e.f. 1.4.2005, and accordingly no funds have been allocated in the Annual Plan of the Ministry for 2005-2006 under the Sports Infrastructure Schemes. All the State Governments and AIU were suitably informed. Subsequently, AIU has informed that tournaments will be conducted out of registration fee to be collected from the participants.

( c) In view of ( a) above, `Sports` being a State subject under the constitution, State Governments have to create Sports Infrastructure out of their own resources. For conducting National/International tournaments and participating in International competitions abroad, the Ministry is presently providing central assistance in accordance with the approved pattern to the recognized National Sports Federations under the Scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations. Sports Authority of India is also implementing schemes for promotion of sports namely 


(i) National Sports Talent Contest;  

(ii) Army Boys Sports Company;

records.qtitle: SHARE OF INDIAN TEXTILE INDUSTRY IN INTERNATIONAL MARKET .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have taken any new initiatives for expanding share of Indian Textile Industry in international markets;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) what are the main reasons and obstacles for enhancing textile exports in the country;and

(d) how Government are going to tackle these problems for the benefit of textile industry?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF TEXTILES

(SHRI SHANKERSINH VAGHELA)

(a) & (b): The Government has been taking a number of steps from time to time for the benefit of the Indian Textile Industry including increasing share in international markets. Some of the important initiatives taken are given as under:- 


i) 100% Foreign Direct Investment is allowed in the textile sector 
under the automatic route.  


ii) The Government has de-reserved the readymade garments, hosiery and
 knitwear from the SSI sector. 


iii) The Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS) has been made
 operational from 1-4-1999 to facilitate the modernisation and upgradation of
 the sector.   


iv) To improve the productivity and quality of cotton, Government has
 launched the Technology Mission on Cotton (TMC). Incentives are provided for
 better farm practices, quality seeds, improvement in market infrastructure and
 modernisation of ginning & pressing sector. 

 
v) To provide the industry with world class infrastructure facilities
 for setting up their textile units, a new scheme namely, ‘Scheme for 
Integrated Textile Parks’ has been launched by merging existing two schemes 
i.e. Textile Centres Infrastructure Development Scheme (TCIDS) and Apparel Park
 for Exports Scheme (APES). Govt. of India support under the scheme by way of 
grant or equity shall be limited to 40% of the project cost subject to a 
ceiling of Rs. 40 crores.

 
vi) ‘Apparel Park for Exports Scheme (APES)’ was launched with the 
objective of imparting a focused thrust for setting up apparel units of 
international standards at potential growth centres, and to give a fillip to 
exports. Under APES, 12 projects have been sanctioned with an estimated support
 from Government of India of Rs. 191.70 crores. 

 
vii) For upgrading infrastructure facilities at important textile 
centres, the ‘Textile Centre Infrastructure Development Scheme (TCIDS)’ was
 launched. Under TCIDS, 18 projects have been sanctioned with an estimated 
support from Government of India of Rs.270.80 crores. 

 
viii) The fiscal duty structure has been generally rationalised to
 achieve growth and maximum value addition within the country. Except for 
mandatory excise duty on man-made filament yarns and man-made staple fibres,
 the whole value addition chain has been given an option of excise exemption.
 


ix) The import of specified textiles and garment machinery items has been 
allowed at a concessional rate of customs duty to encourage investments and 
to make our textile products competitive in the global market. The cost of 
machinery has also been reduced through fiscal policy measures.


x) For the speedy modernisation of the textile processing sector, Government 
has introduced, w.e.f 20.4.2005, a credit linked capital subsidy scheme @10%
 under TUFS, in addition to the existing 5% interest reimbursement.  

 
xi) The National Institute for Fashion Technology (NIFT), its seven 
branches, and the Apparel Training & Design Centres (ATDCs) are running various
 courses/programmes to meet the skilled manpower requirements of the textile 
industry, especially apparel, in the field of design, merchandising and 
marketing.


xii) Facilities like eco-testing laboratories have been created to enable 
exporters to get garments/textiles pre-tested so that they conform to the 
requirements of the importing countries.


(c):          Main obstacles for enhancing textile exports, inter alia,
 include the following:- 
 United States (US), European Union (EU) and Canada account for major share of
 world trade in textiles, and due to the quota restrictions imposed by these 
countries till 31st December, 2004 under the erstwhile Multi-Fibre Arrangement,
 India’s export growth to these markets was restrained. 
 Lack of investments towards modernisation and technological up-gradation,
 particularly in weaving and processing segments, are the weak areas that have
 been inhibiting the growth of textile exports in real terms. 
 Duty free access to some of our competitors in major markets through 
Preferential Trading Agreement and Generalised Scheme of Preferences. 
 High tariff on finished products imposed by some major importing countries.


(d):      The steps taken by the Government to tackle the problems have
 been enumerated above in reply to parts (a) & (b) of the question. Further, 
after removal of the quota restrictions, Indian textiles exports to US, EU etc.
 have shown increasing trend.

records.qtitle: MODERNISATION OF POLICE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have decided to modernize the police system by coordinating with State Governments for making it transparent and effective as well as people friendly;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Union Government are also considering a proposal to enable police stations to get FIRs through E-mail from the citizens by bringing transparency in the Citizen-Police interface in the country;

(d) if so, the details thereof and by when it will be implemented in the country; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL )

(a) & (b): `Police` is a State subject as per the Constitution of India. As such, it is primarily the responsibility of the State Governments to make it transparent, effective as well as people friendly. Government of India has been pursuing with the States to bring about the needed reforms in the Police functioning. Modernization of Police Forces Scheme is one of the means by which Central Government provides assistance to the States. Ministry of Home Affairs has recently set up an Expert Committee to draft a new Police Act which should aim at making police functionary more transparent and accountable.


(c) & (d): A multidimensional scheme named `CIPA` (Common Integrated Police Application) is presently under implementation by the Government for automation of police stations, under which FIRs will be registered and printed on Computers. The said scheme is aimed at computerizing all the important forms, records and crime data maintained by the police stations. The scheme is being initially launched at 10% police stations in all States in 2005-06 as per selection made by the respective State Governments. Remaining police stations will be covered in the next three years.

(e): Does not arise, in view of (c) and (d) above.

records.qtitle: RECRUITMENT TO DEFENCE SERVICES ON CASTE BASIS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether there have been several demands from some quarters that the recruitment to Defence services should be done on the basis of caste with SC, ST and Other Backward Classes;

(b) whether the demand has also been made for raising an entire regiment based exclusively on castes, religion or State; and

(c) if so, the details thereof and Government’s reaction thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)


(a) & (b): Yes, Sir.

(c) Recruitment in the Armed Forces is based on merit and is open to every citizen of the country including Scheduled Tribes, Scheduled Castes and Other Backward Class candidates without any discrimination on the basis of their caste, creed, religion or region. The policy of the Government is also not to raise any new Regiment based on any particular class, creed, community, religion or region, but to have an Army in which all Indian have representation.

records.qtitle: DECLINING EXPENDITURE ON SOCIAL AND INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a)whether it is a fact that various State Governments are unable to spend much on social and infrastructure development of their respective state as they are facing acute financial crisis due to heavy loan amount and mismanagement of financial structures;

(b) if so, Government`s reaction thereto;

(c) whether Government are considering any structured and transparent approach to lesion the burden of debt on various states so that they can increase their expenditure and investments on infrastructure and social sector;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) if not, the reasons thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF FINANCE
SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM

(a) to (e): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN PARTS (a) to (e) OF THE RA,IYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO, 92 FOR ANSWER ON 29-11-2005 BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT.
It is a fact that various State governments have been spending less on the social sector and physical infrastructure as evidenced by low ratio of such expenditure to their gross State Domestic Product. Increasing non developmental expenditure in the total expenditure of the States has led to partial crowding out of the expenditure in social sector and infrastructure. For many States, three major committed expenditure viz., interest payments, salaries and pensions equaled almost their entire` revenue receipts, leaving very little fiscal space for sustained expenditure on social and infrastructure development.
In order to reduce the interest burden of the States, Government of India operated a debt swap scheme in recent years. Swapping of GoI loans with interest rates of 13 per cent and above has helped the States to reduce their debt servicing costs to a considerable level.
Higher resource transfers under devolution of States` share in Central taxes and duties, social sector specific grants for States whose per capita expenditure on Education and Health are below the group average and gap filling non plan revenue deficit grants recommended by the Twelfth Finance Commission (TFC) are expected to supplement the resources of States to increase the quality of expenditure and investment in priority sectors.
Government of India has also increased its support under Central sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes to the States for filling critical gaps in social sector including health, education and nutrition. Budgetary support has been enhanced to Sarva Shikska Abhiyan, Integrated Child Development Scheme, Mid-day meal scheme. National Rural Health Mission has been launched this year.
Government of India has accepted the recommendation of the TFC for a Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility that would enable the States to pay lesser amount of repayment of principal and interest.
In addition, a debt waiver scheme, also recommended by TFC, linked to reduction of revenue deficit of States, has also been put in place. This should help the States in reducing their debt burden.
Reduction and subsequent elimination of revenue deficit by 2()08-09 should provide the much needed fiscal space and unlock the resources for higher investment in social sector and physical infrastructure.

records.qtitle: FAKE CURRENCY IN INDIAN MARKET .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there has been growing rate of fake currency in the Indian market since last six months;

(b) if so, Government`s response and reaction thereto;

(c) whether Government have presented a route map of fake Indian currency notes circulation network before Bangladesh; and

(d) if so, response of Government of Bangladesh and steps taken against counterfeit currency route?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S.PALANIMANICKAM)

(a) As per the information furnished by National Crime Records Bureau, there has been increase in number of cases detected of fake currency during last six months. However, the amount involved has declined during the same period.

(b) to (d)` To curb circulation of fake currency notes in the country, the Government has taken a number of steps which include stepping up of vigilance by the Border Security Force/Custom authorities to prevent smuggling of fake currency notes into the country, training and sensitisation of law enforcement agencies, dissemination of information on security features through print and electronic media for the benefit of public, etc. Recently new/additional security features have been introduced in the banknotes to curb counterfeiting.

records.qtitle: NON COMPLIANCE OF RULES BY COMPANIES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that more than two lakh companies are not abiding proper rules and regulations of Government;

(b) if so, what steps have been taken by Government so far against the erring companies;

(c) whether it is also a fact that Government are unable to take stringent steps against the erring companies; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and whether Government are seriously considering to adopt e-governance system for ensuring transparency and efficiency?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF COMPANY AFFAIRS

(SHRI PREMCHAND GUPTA)

(a) As per available records, 303107 companies out of 641512 registered companies were found to be in default in filing statutory returns with the Registrar of Companies during the year 2003-2004.

(b) & (c) Companies defaulting in filing of statutory returns are liable for payment of additional fees for delayed filing in addition to other legal action under the Companies Act, 1956. Penal action is being taken under law against such defaulting companies.
In respect of defunct companies, two Simplified Exit Schemes (SES) in 2003 and 2005 were introduced. 26714 companies were struck off under SES in 2003, while 26483 companies have applied under SES 2005.
Under Company Law Settlement Scheme, 2000 (CLSS 2000) 1,27,083 companies have availed the scheme and filed the required statutory documents.

(d) The Government has already taken up a major e-Governance initiative known as `MCA21` e-Governance Project, which, when fully operationalised, it would provide for electronic filing and access to corporate documents through the use of information technology and computers. This would enable transparency as well as speedy monitoring of non-compliance by the companies. The project is expected to be operational by April, 2006.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT

records.qtitle: SYLLABUS OF NON GOVERNMENTAL SCHOOLS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have no control on various Non-Governmental schools and madarsas on their school syllabus, which have contents against our Constitution and National Educational Policy; and

(b) if so, the reasons therefore and the steps taken or proposed to be taken against the erring schools and madarsas?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M.A.A. FATMI )

(a) & (b) India has a wide range of schools and school systems. Schools affiliated to the CBSE prescribe NCERT textbooks, The State schools which are affiliated to the State Education Boards use textbooks prescribed by their own state bodies. There are primary schools which are run by social and religious organizations and which are not affiliated to any Board.
A CABE Sub-Committee was set up on `Regulatory Mechanism for Textbooks and Parallel Textbooks taught in school outside the Government System`. The Terms of Reference of the Committee were - 
 

(i)	to study and report on textbooks in Government schools not using the CBSE syllabus 

(ii)	to study the textbooks and curriculum of schools outside the Government
	System including those run by religious and social organizations 

(iii)	to suggest an appropriate regulatory mechanism tbr institutionalizing the issue
	of preparation of textbooks and curricular material.


The Sub-Committee examined a selected sample of textbooks in the Social
 Sciences, Hindi, regional languages and English of certain States including
 Bihar, Chattisgarh, .Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, 
Maharashtra and West Bengal. The analysis of textbooks used in schools run by
 religious and social organizations was made within the parameters spelled out
 in the National Policy on Education, 1986 and the Constitution of India. The
 Committee had made several recommendations including setting up of National 
Textbook Council to monitor textbooks.

records.qtitle: LINKING OF SCHOOLS THROUGH EDUSAT
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that as per the pilot project of his Ministry, 1,000 schools in Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Uttar Pradesh will be linked through EDUSAT, the exclusive education satellite: and

(b) if so, the details of the project and the estimated cost thereon?
records.ans_text:
MNISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M.A.A. FATMI)

(a)& (b): Yes. Sir. A pilot project for strengthening the quality of education and teacher`s training through Edusat Supported Nettwork is in the process of implementation. 80 schools in the States of Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Chattisgrh and Uttar Pradesh are proposed to be connected under the pilot project through the Edusat Supported Network
The project will cover four districts one each in Bihar. Chhatisgarh. Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh with a Hub and Studio for the network at Jabalpur. The estimated initial cost to be met by the ISRO is nearly Rs.11.91 crore, whereas the cost of studio equipment and other peripherals will be nearly Rs.83.00 lakhs which will be met by the Ministry of Human Resource Development. The operational cost will be met by the Distance Education Council (DEC)/IGNOU which is estimated to be Rs.l.44 crore per year.

(SHRI KAPIL SIBAL)

records.qtitle: (clubbed) UN CONVENTION ON LAW OF THE SEAS .
records.name: PREMA CARIAPPA
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that the UN Convention on Law of the Seas (UNCLOS) set a 2009 deadline for countries to submit their claims about the outer limit of their continental shelf beyond 200 nautical mile Exclusive Economic Zone;

(b) Whether it is also a fact that the UNCLOS requires that, if dispute is not settled, the disputed water would be declared international Water; and

(c) If so, the details of various claims made by India and their status with regard to claims of neighbouring countries?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(RAO INDERJIT SINGH)

(a) to (c) The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea 1982 (UNCLOS) is the universally recognized regime, which has established a comprehensive framework for the regulation of all ocean space. The Convention entered into force on 16 November 1994. India is a State Party to the Convention.
According to the Convention, a state has Territorial Waters of 12 Nautical Miles and an Exclusive Economic Zone of 200 Nautical Miles determined in accordance with the provisions of the Convention. As far as India is concerned, this is also the position reflected in the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976.
Claims for a Continental Shelf beyond 200 Nautical Miles are to be submitted to the United Nations Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf by 12 May 2009.
Collection and examination of necessary data are underway for the purpose of preparing and submitting India`s claim for an extended Continental Shelf to the Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf, within the prescribed timeframe. In case of any overlapping claim between neighbouring countries, the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea 1982, provides that the issue should be resolved by these countries bilaterally through negotiations.

records.qtitle: PRIVATE INVESTMENT IN POWER SECTOR .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is considering to encourage private investment in power sector by announcing further relaxation to the mega and tiny power projects;

(b) if so, the details thereof and whether Government of Maharashtra had made some suggestion for power projects in Maharashtra; and

(c) if so, Government`s response and reaction thereto?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI P.M. SAYEED )


(a) to (c) : The mega power policy announced in 1995 has been reviewed and revised from time to time after inter-ministerial consultations considering the experience gained in its implementation and the needs of the power sector. To encourage private investment for the small hydro (upto 25 MW) and renewable energy power projects, financial and fiscal incentives which include accelerated depreciation, relief from taxes and duties are being provided. In addition, preferential tariff is given to grid interactive renewable power in most potential states. A higher level of central financial assistance, on par with special category states, is being provided for setting up renewable energy projects.
Ministry of Power had mooted a proposal for lowering the threshold qualifying capacity for the mega power projects. Government of Maharashtra have also supported the proposal of the Ministry of Power for lowering the threshold qualifying capacity to 250 MW both for thermal as well as hydro power projects. However, based on the inter-ministerial consultations and the subsequent review meetings held, presently, no changes have been effected in the provisions of the current mega policy.

(a) The total fund available for disposal with India Brand Equity Foundation is around Rs.80 crores.

(b) IBEF promotes Brand India on an overall basis. It has discontinued giving loans to Corporates to build individual product brands since the year 2003.

(c) to (e) Do not arise in view of the discontinuation of loaning activities.

(a) to (c): The policy of the Central Government is to encourage and facilitate the Zones being set up in the private sector or joint sector in association with the State Government or by the State Governments themselves. On the basis of the proposals received, approvals have so far been granted for setting up of the following SEZs in Maharashtra in the private/joint/State sector:- 


Location		Name of the Developer
