records.qtitle: INCREASE IN COVERAGE OF PENSION SCHEME .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that only about 11 per cent of the total population of our country is covered by a proper pension scheme and a large number of people are still not covered by pensions so far;

(b)if so, Government`s response thereto; and

(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for increasing coverage of pension scheme in various fields?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S. S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a) Retirement Benefits in one form or the other are available to only about 13% of the working population of the country.

(b) & (c): Government has already implemented a new restructured defined contribution pension scheme, namely, New Pension System (NPS) for all Central Government recruits (excluding Armed Forces, in the first stage) with effect from 01.01.2004. The NPS will also be available on a voluntary basis to all persons including self-employed professionals and others in the unorganised sector. State Governments may also opt to join the new system as and when they desire.
As regard to Employees` Pension Scheme, 1995, benefits of pension are available to all the eligible employees of an establishment to which the Employees` Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 applies.
As on 31.3.2004 there were 280.90 lakh members under the Employees` Pension Scheme, 1995.

records.qtitle: OBSERVATION OF UNESCO ON WORLD HERITAGE SITES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that any delegation of UNESCO has recently visited to examine the three World Heritage Sites in Agra - Taj, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri; Hampi in Karnataka and Bodhgaya in Bihar;

(b) if so, their observations on these World Heritage Sites and Government`s reaction thereto;

(c) whether Government have requested to add more sites/places in the list of World Heritage Sites; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER FOR INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND CULTURE

(SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY)

(a) & (b): The UNESCO/ICOMOS Missions recently visited the Mahabodhi Temple, Bodhgaya (Bihar) in April,2005 and Hampi (Karnataka) in August, 2005 in connection with finalization of Site Management Plans.
In case of Bodhgaya, the Mission has recommended that the work on Site Management Plan may be suspended until such time all necessary conditions for implementation of the same are in place; namely appropriate legal framework, controls in the buffer zone, management mechanism, etc. The Mission also recommended to explore the possibility of a long term extension of the Mahabodhi Temple Complex inscription to include the cultural landscape identified with Lord Buddha and other properties associated with the life of Buddha in India like, for example, Sarnath. Mahabodhi Temple at Bodhgaya is not a centrally protected monument. It is managed and maintained by the Government of Bihar through the Bodhgaya Temple Management Committee constituted under Bodhgaya Temple Act, 1949.
In case of Hampi, discussions were held with officials of Government of Karnataka, ASI and other stakeholders and it was decided to formulate an operational management plan to strengthen the functioning of the Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority at Hampi. The suggestion of UNESCO mission to establish a technical unit is receiving the attention of the Government of Karnataka.

(c) & (d): Yes, Sir. The Government of India has nominated Majuli Island in Assam for consideration of inclusion in the World Heritage List in the year 2006. Besides, the Government would also be resubmitting the nomination dossiers of Red Fort.

records.qtitle: ATM SERVICES IN POST OFFICES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for improving the current postal services in the coming years in the field of money deposits and transactions;

(b) whether Government has decided to open ATM-Banks like services in post offices ; and

(c) if so, the details thereof and the salient features thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

records.qtitle: GUIDELINES FOR PURCHASING TRANSFORMERS BY SEBS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI P.M. SAYEED )

(c) & (d) : The Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited has informed that recently in the month of March-April, 2005 a lot of transformers was found defective in the testing by Testing Engineers at Kolhapur. The whole lot of faulty transformers was straightway rejected and action was initiated against defaulters.

records.qtitle: CHECK ON FOREIGN FUNDING OF ANTI NATIONAL ORGANISATIONS .

records.qtitle: NPA OF CORPORATE HOUSES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of the corporate houses from whom NPA worth about Rs.96,000 crores are due as disclosed by All India Bank Employees Associations (AIBEA);

(b) the reasons for not recovering money from these corporate houses and measures adopted for speedy recovery of money from them;

(c) the details of the defaulter companies who were again sanctioned loan;

(d) whether it is a fact that All India Bank Employees Federation has demanded enactment of a stringent law to recover outstanding loans of Nationalised Banks by big business houses and other big borrowers; and

(e) if so, Government`s reaction thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a) The Government has not received any communication from the All India Bank Employees Association (AIBEA) with regard to the names of defaulters of banks being made public by them. However, Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited is maintaining a database on suit-filed accounts of Rs. 1 Crore and above and non suit- filed accounts (wilful defaulters) of Rs. 25 Lacs and above. The information can be accessed at CIBIL website www.cibil.com .

(b), (d) & (e) Government of India and Reserve Bank of India have stipulated certain steps for recovery of loans, which, inter-alia, include evolving and implementing a recovery policy by banks, filing of suits in civil courts/DRTs, issue of notices under SARFAESI Act, 2002, compromise settlement and monitoring and follow up of NPAs at various levels. The Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act 2005 has been enacted to provide for regulation of credit information companies and to facilitate efficient distribution of credit thereby arresting fresh accretion of NPAs. Credit Information Bureau has also been set up to disseminate information on borrowers to the banks.

(c) No such instance has been brought to the notice of the Government.

records.qtitle: TARGET FOR AGRICULTURAL GROWTH .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have set a target to increase the annual growth rate of agricultural production by more than 6.5 per cent for coming years;

(b) if so, the details of measures taken or proposed to be taken for increasing growth of agricultural products in the country; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR)

(a) to (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (e) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRE~D QUESTION NO. 285 FOR 12/08/2005 REGARDING TARGET FOR AGRICULTURAL GROWTH.

(a): No, Sir. In its Mid-Term Appraisal of the Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-2007), the Planning Commission has projected growth of GDP at 2001-2002 prices in agriculture, including allied sectors of forestry & logging, and fishing, at 4.0 per cent and 3.2 per cent during 2005-06 and 2006-07 respectively.

(b)&(c): As indicated in the Mid-Term Appraisal of the Tenth Plan, the growth rate in 2002-03 the first year of the Tenth Plan was negative (-6.8 percent) which reflected the impact of the severe drought that adversely affected agricultural production in several States/regions in the country. Favourable weather facilitated revival of agricultural growth, which improved to 9.5% in 2003-04. However, in the subsequent year, i.e. 2004-05 serious deficiency in rainfall led to deterioration in performance in the agriculture sector, and as a result, growth rate in agriculture decelerated to 1.1 per cent. The inability of Indian agriculture to withstand weather related shocks mainly reflects the fact that there has been steady decline in public investment in real terms in agriculture, including allied sectors, over successive Five Year Plans. This in turn reflects decline in investment towards irrigation and water management.
With a view to increase agricultural production, Government has adopted a multi pronged strategy for addressing specific segments of agriculture to ensure higher productivity. These initiatives are in the areas of both cereal and non-cereal crops, horticulture, livestock, fisheries and dairying. Equal emphasis is also been given to timely availability of inputs and an overall thrust towards diversification into higher value produces and plantations. Initiatives taken towards these areas include launch of the National Horticulture Mission, undertaking activities with a Mission approach for enhancing productivity and quality of cotton, oilseeds, pulses and coarse grains. The Union Budget for 2005-06 has underscored the importance of providing enhanced credit coverage to the farming community as a consequence of which Rs.1,15,242 crores was disbursed in 2004-05. Credit flow to agriculture will be stepped up by another 30% in 2005-06. Initiatives has also been taken to include micro irrigation, enhanced provisions for the accelerated irrigation technology programme, strengthening of agricultural marketing infrastructure, development of backward and forward linkages through venture capital support and facilitations to growers association for producing larger and better quality of fruits, flowers and vegetables. Determined efforts are also being made to increase fisheries production largely through inland aquaculture. Livestock and Dairying have also received greater attention through enhanced budget outlays as well as defined policies towards cross-breeding and delineation of disease free zones.

records.qtitle: DERAILMENT OF TRAINS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that some of the passenger trains and goods trains have got derailed during the last four months as well as Rajdhani Express escaped from accident thrice;

(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; and

(c) what are the details of preventive measures taken for the safety of passengers in the future ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R. VELU)



(a) to (c): A Statement is attached.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2175 BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT TO BE ANSWERED IN RAJYA SABHA ON 12.08.2005 REGARDING DERAILMENT OF TRAINS.

(a) & (b): There have been derailments of 28 passenger trains and 21 goods trains during the period from April 2005 to July 2005. The cause-wise details of these 49 derailments have been as under:- 
Cause                 Number of derailments
from April 2005 to July 2005
Failure of Railway Staff                   39
Failure of other than Railway               2
Staff
Sabotage                                    2
Incidental                                  4
Not established                             1
Under investigation                         1
Total                                      49 

( Provisional figures)
No  incidents  of  Rajdhani  Express  train  escaping
accident  during  the  above  period  have  been  reported.
However, there has been one unusual incident on 23.05.2005,
when  a gunny bag containing iron pieces was found on track

stock,  modernization of maintenance practices, replacement
of  over  aged  assets, upgradation of training  aids  like
simulators, checks on observance of safety precautions  and
provision of Anti Collision Device.

records.qtitle: CONTAINING WASTEFUL EXPENDITURE ON RAILWAY INFRASTRUCTURE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the steps taken or proposed to be taken for containing wasteful expenditure on railway infrastructure in the country since last two years; and

(b) the details of measures taken or proposed to be taken for making railway profitable?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R.VELU)


(a) and (b): A statement is attached..

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) and (b) OF UNSTARRED QUESTION NO 2174 BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT TO BE ANSWERED IN RAJYA SABHA ON 12.8.2005 REGARDING CONTAINING WASTEFUL EXPENDITURE ON RAILWAY INFRASTRUCTURE.


(a) and (b): It has been a constant endeavour on the part of the Railways to avoid wasteful expenditure and control the growth of the non-plan expenditure. The Railways have been taking a number of austerity/economy measures such as improving staff productivity by better man-power planning, asset utilization, inventory management, fuel consumption etc. to keep the expenditure under control.
Apart from above measures, efforts are also being made to make Railways financially more viable by increasing the earnings. In this regard, the initiatives under freight business segment include plans to improve throughput through increased productivity and efficiency, reduction in wagon turn around time, simplification and rationalization of preferential traffic schedule, electrification of diesel sidings, engine-on-load scheme, terminal incentive scheme, introduction of electronic payment gateway facility, simplification and rationalization of goods tariff, new premium registration scheme, wagon investment scheme, development of private sidings through cost sharing, integrated warehouse complexes, etc. Initiatives under passenger and parcel business segments include extension of PRS and UTS facilities to more and more locations, speeding up of trains, review of trains with low patronage, deployment of additional coaches in well patronized trains, additional leasing of parcel space in certain nominated trains, leasing of vacant compartment of guard in front of SLR coach, etc. These measures are likely to enhance earnings of the Railways and make it more profitable.

records.qtitle: GENERATING EMPLOYMENT IN MAHARASHTRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the problem of unemployment is increasing day by day as well as employment in the organised sector is also declining in the last two years in the country particularly in the Maharashtra State;

(b) if so, Government`s response and reaction thereto;

(c) whether Government are considering any specific programmes for generating more employment in the country specially in the Maharashtra State during the next three years; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING

(SHRI M.V. RAJASEKHARAN)



(a) to(d): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 277 REGARDING GENERATING EMPLOYMENT IN MAHARASHTRA BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT DUE FOR ANWER ON 11.8.2005.


(a): Results of the most recent quinquennial survey on employment and unemployment, which was completed in July 2005, are not available as yet. However, as per the previous two such surveys, the incidence of unemployment increased from 5.99% in 1993-94 to 7.32% in 1999-2000 at All India level, and from 5.09% to 7.16% in Maharashtra. Employment in organised sector at All India level declined from 27.96 million, as on 31.3.2000 to 26.98 million, as on 31.3.2003, and in Maharashtra State it declined from 3.76 million to 3.59 million in the same period.

(b): A higher growth of the economy especially in the labour intensive sectors is required to attain a growth in employment in excess of labour force.

(c) & (d): The Tenth Plan includes a number of programmes to increase the growth of labour intensive sectors such as Agriculture and Allied Activities, Food Processing, Rural Non-farm Sector, Small and Medium Enterprises and Services Sector including Health, Education, Information Technology & Communication. National Food for Work Programme, and the proposed Act on National Rural Employment Guarantee will generate additional demand for labour in the rural areas. These are applicable to all States including the State of Maharashtra.

records.qtitle: NOMINAL RATES FOR INCOMING TELEPHONE SERVICES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware that some mobile service providers are issuing incoming telephone services at the nominal rates of Rs. 100/- to the customers;

(b) if so, whether MTNL and BSNL are also considering to provide only incoming telephonic facility at a monthly rental of Rs. 100/- in the country;

(c) if so, by when this facility would be accorded; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

(a) Some mobile service providers are offering telephone services at the rate of Rs. 100/- per month.

(b) to (d) Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited (MTNL) is offering cellular mobile telephone service with a tariff of Rs. 100/- in its Budget plan with facility for both incoming and outgoing calls. The outgoing calls are charged as per the tariff plan subscribed by the customers and no charges are levied for the incoming calls.
Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) has no proposal to provide this facility at present. Since, the tariffs for access services are under forbearance except for rural fixed line tariffs, the service providers decide their own tariffs based on market perceptions.

records.qtitle: USE OF NUMBERS ON DOLLAR CURRENCY AS CODES BY MILITANTS IN J K .

-

records.qtitle: PROCEDURE FOR IMPORT OF AIRCRAFTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
to answer to Starred Question 541 given in the Rajya Sabha on the 3rd May, 2005 and state:

(a) what are Government rules for the import of aircraft (Private Jets)/ helicopters by private companies/individuals;

(b) what certification procedures are followed by the DGCA; and

(c) who is responsible for the maintenance of such aircraft/helicopters and whether they are approved by the DGCA?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )
(a): The aircraft/helicoper by private companies/ individuals for private use can be imported under a licence by Ministry of Commerce (Directorate General of Foreign Trade) clearance by Ministry of Civil Aviation. (b): For certification of each aircraft Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) follow a standard procedure and check list. By this process aircraft registered in India are certified airworthy before they are used in service. (c) All the aircraft/helicopters are maintained by the organizations approved by DGCA.

records.qtitle: ENTERTAINMENT TAX ON CINEMAS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware about the Uttar Pradesh Government’s recent erroneous decisions for allowing some particular cinemas to run without entertainment tax (Tax Free) in all the theatres/cinema halls of Uttar Pradesh;

(b) if so, Government’s response and reaction thereto;

(c) whether Government are considering to review the current rules and regulations for waiving of entertainment tax to some particular cinemas by advising to all the State Governments;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefore?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND CULTURE

(SHRI S.JAIPAL REDDY)

(a) No, Sir. As per entry No. 33 in the State List given in the Seventh schedule of the Constitution of India, ‘ theatres and dramatic performances; cinemas subject to the provisions of entry 60 of List I; sports, entertainments and amusements’ are subjects falling within the purview of the State Government.
Entry 60 of List I, the Union List of the Constitution of India gives subject under the Central Government states: ‘ Sanctioning of cinematograph films for exhibition’.

(b) to (e) In the recently concluded 25th State Information Minister’s Conference

(SIMCON), discussions were held, inter alia, on the issue of entertainment tax. During the Conference, there was consensus on the need to bring down entertainment tax levels to 25-30%. This meeting was also attended by a senior Minister of Government of Uttar Pradesh.

records.qtitle: COVERAGE OF SPORT EVENTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is fact that Prasar Bharati has recently offered affordable and low-cost live or deferred live coverage of the national and international level sport events; and

(b) if so, the details thereof and the response thereto?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND CULTURE

(SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY)


(a) & (b): Yes, Sir. Prasar Bharati has informed that Doordarshan will undertake live/deferred live coverage of sports events at daily charges ranging between Rs. 60,700/- to Rs. 2,11,700/- per day (excluding service tax) depending upon the travelling distance involved, availability of technical infrastructure at the concerned Kendra etc. So far two federations have signed agreements with Doordarshan on this basis.

records.qtitle: SHORTAGE OF SKILLED ENGINE DRIVERS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are acute shortages of skilled engine drivers in the Indian Railways and therefore Government have decided to give extension to retiring rail drivers for further one year;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(c) the requirement of skilled engine drivers for the Indian Railways in the next five years and how will it be met by Government?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS
(SHRI R. VELU)

(a) & (b): No, Sir. However, re-engagement (and not extension) of retired hands subject to prescribed conditions has been allowed on daily remuneration basis to tide over any exigency that may arise due to day to day shortage.

(c): Requirement of Drivers is worked out in six monthly reviews and met by normal procedure for recruitment from open market and promotion of staff from the feeder grades.

records.qtitle: DEVELOPING FPIS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that due to improper facilities and policy implementation, country loses agricultural foodstuffs worth more than Rs. 50,000 crores annually;

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto; and

(c) the details of comprehensive steps taken or proposed to be taken for developing food processing industry/sector in the country? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES

(SHRI SUBODH KANT SAHAI)

(a): As per the report of M/s Rabo India Finance Private Limited, wastage of the agricultural foodstuffs is estimated to be about Rs. 58000 crore occurring at various stages of handling after harvesting like inadequate post – harvest infrastructure, lack of cold chain facilities, transportation, proper storage facilities etc.

(b) & (c ): Government has formulated and implemented several Plan Schemes to provide financial assistance for establishment and modernization of food processing units, creation of infrastructure, support for R&D, human resource development besides other promotional measures to encourage development of food processing industries. Recently, in order to give boost to growth of FPI sector the Government has allowed under Income Tax Act, a deduction of 100% of profit for five years and 25% of profits for the next five years in case of new agro processing industries set up to process, preserve and package fruits and vegetables. Excise duty of 16% on dairy machinery has been fully waived for promotion of dairy processing industries. Excise duty on meat, poultry and fish products has been reduced from 16% to 8%. Excise duty on food grade hexane used in edible oil industry has been reduced from 32% to 16%. A National Horticulture Mission has been launched w.e.f. 1st April 2005 with an objective to boost the horticulture sector. In the Budget of 2005-06 excise duty of Rs. 1.00 per kg on refined edible oil and Rs. 1.25 per kg on vanaspati was abolished. Customs duty on refrigerated vans was reduced from 20% to 10%.

records.qtitle: SALE OF FORMER INDIAN EMBASSY BUILDING IN BONN
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether Government have decided to sell 100 years old former Indian Embassy Building in Bonn, Germany despite strong objection from the Indian Community in Germany;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

(c) whether the advertisement of selling this building appeared in the Daily Newspaper and the website in Germany; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(RAO INDERJIT SINGH)


(a) & (d) A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

Statement referred to in parts (a) to (d) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 161 to be answered on 04.08.2005 regarding `Sale of former Indian Embassy building in Bonn`.

(a) & (b) The Embassy of India shifted from Bonn to Berlin in October 1999 following a decision of the German Government to shift the capital to Berlin. A temporary office dealing with residual consular and administrative matters was maintained in Bonn up to June 2002, and was wound up with the opening of the new Consulate General of India in Munich. Consequently, the former Indian Embassy building in Bonn has been lying vacant since July 2002. The Government has received some suggestions from Indian organizations in the German State of North-Rhine Westphalia, where Bonn is located, regarding possible alternate use of the premises. However, since it was not found possible to put the building to an efficient use in a cost effective manner, the Government of India has decided to sell the property in the best interests of the Government. A number of other countries have already sold their diplomatic properties that were located in Bonn.

(c) Yes Sir.

(d) The advertisement for sale of the Bonn property appeared in the local newspapers on April 15 and 17, 2005 inviting bids by May 17, 2005. The advertisement was also put on Embassy`s website. The submission deadline was extended to June 17, 2005 following requests from prospective buyers for more time. The sale of the property had been advertised for obtaining sealed competitive bids.

records.qtitle: PENSION SCHEME IN VARIOUS SECTORS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that only about 11 per cent of the total population of our country is covered by a proper pension scheme and large number of people are not covered by pensions, so far;

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto; and

(c) the details of the steps taken or proposed to be taken for increasing coverage of pension scheme in various fields?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT

( SHRI K. CHANDRASEKHAR RAO )

(a): Retirement Benefits in one form or the other are available to only 13% of the working population of the country.

(b) & (c): Government has already implemented a new restructured defined contribution pension scheme, namely, the New Pension System (NPS) for all Central Government recruits (excluding Armed Forces, in the first stage) with effect from 01.01.2004. The NPS will also be available on a voluntary basis to all persons including self-employed professionals and other in the unorganized sector. State Governments may also opt to join the new system as and when they desire.
As regard to Employees` Pension Scheme, 1995 benefits of Pension are available to all the eligible employees of an establishment to which the Employees` Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 applies.
As on 31.03.2004 there were 280.90 lakh members under the Employees` Pension Scheme, 1995.

records.qtitle: FACILITIES TO CELLULAR USERS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that consumer can retain his cellular number by selecting any other cellular operator anywhere in the country;

(b) if so, whether Government are considering to implement this facility in the country; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor and the obstacles therein for providing this facility to cellular users
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)


(a) At present, No, Sir.

(b)&(c) The consumer can retain his cellular number by selecting any other cellular operator in case the facility of Mobile Number Portability (MNP) is introduced in the country. The Government is working towards introduction of number portability. However, the proposed measure is at initial stage. No time frame can be fixed for its introduction.

records.qtitle: RESTORATION OF PEACE IN J K .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government plan to initiate talks with separate organizations of Jammu & Kashmir to help restore peace in the militancy hit State;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government also agree that there is an urgent need to work for stopping killings by restoring peace in Jammu & Kashmir;

(d) if so, whether any measures have been chalked out to see how violence could end; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a)&(b): The Government is committed to carry forward a dialogue with all groups, which eschew the path of violence.

(c)to(e): Yes Sir. The Government have been following a multi-pronged approach in dealing with terrorist violence and bringing in peace in the State of Jammu and Kashmir. The major prongs of the strategy, inter-alia, including
(i) strengthening border management and pro-active action against terrorists within J&K
(ii) accelerating economic development and
(iii) remaining open to pursue a dialogue with all groups and different shades of opinion in the state on a sustained basis in consultation with the democratically elected State Government.

records.qtitle: PROPOSALS RECEIVED FOR SETTING UP INDUSTRIES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the details and number of proposals received by the Ministry for setting up of industries in the country particularly in Maharashtra; and

(b) Government’s response thereto?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY

(SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN)

(a) to (b) The State-wise distribution of investment proposals based on the Industrial Entrepreneur Memoranda (IEMs) filed and Letters of Intent (LOIs)/Direct Industrial Licence (DILs) issued during the last three years is Annexed. Under the liberalized Industrial Policy, decision to set up industry depends upon the commercial judgement of the entrepreneur which, in turn, is also based on the initiatives taken by the State Government by way of providing basic infrastructural facilities and other incentives. records.qtitle: DEMAND FOR PETROLEUM PRODUCTS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that demand rate of petroleum products is increasing day by day in our country as compared to other countries;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the steps taken or proposed to be taken to contain demand of petroleum products ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS AND PANCHAYATI RAJ

(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR)

(a)&(b): According to International Energy Agency (IEA), the estimated global oil demand will rise by about 1.6% per year during the period 2000-2030. Oil demand in China is expected to grow at 3% per annum and that of East Asia including Indonesia at 2.7% per annum. South Asian oil demand is projected to grow at a slightly higher rate of 4% compared to Indian projected growth of 3.3%.
The percentage increase in the consumption of petroleum products in the country during the last three years is as under : 
Year		% increase in consumption
2002-03		3.7
2003-04		3.5
2004-05 (P)	3.7 

(c): In order to promote conservation of petroleum products and improve efficiency in use of 
petroleum products in India, the Government, through the Petroleum Conservation Research 
Association (PCRA) tenders advice to the energy consuming sector, viz the industrial sector, 
the transport sector, the agriculture sector and the domestic sector about good energy 
practices. While general awareness-building for conservation measures is carried out through 
various media, including newspapers, magazines, outdoor hoardings and the electronic media, 
specific projects, including energy audit and driver training activities are undertaken in 
direct consultation with and involvement of specific energy consuming entities. The Energy 
Service Company (ESCO) concept is also being promoted.


In addition, for diversifying the energy basket, which inter alia contains the demand for
petroleum products, the Government is implementing a five per cent ethanol blended petrol
programme in notified sugar producing and adjoining areas under the provisions of GSR 705  

(E) dated 27.10.2004. Field trails are also being undertaken using bio-diesel blended diesel
in the transportation sector.

records.qtitle: PROMOTION OF LPG AT AUTO FUEL .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that many cities have been affected due to high vehicular pollution in the country;

(b) if so, what is the Government’s reaction thereto;

(c) whether Government are considering to encourage use of CNG or LPG as a fuel for controlling the vehicular pollution in the country, if so, the details thereof;

(d) whether Government are aware that a large number of vehicles are running on LPG without proper permission in the country; and

(e) if so, what are Government’s views and the reaction thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS & PANCHAYATI RAJ

(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR)

(a) to (c) Use of CNG and auto LPG is being encouraged to reduce pollution in various cities. Subject to availability of natural gas and necessary infrastructure, CNG is proposed to be introduced in various cities in a phased manner. Oil Marketing Companies

(OMCs) are also progressively introducing auto LPG at their retail outlets in different cities as per the demand.
As on July 2005, the State-wise details of CNG stations of JVs/PSUs are as under:- State City No. of CNG stations Delhi Delhi 133 Uttar Pradesh NOIDA 2 Maharashtra Mumbai 106 Gujarat Vadodara & Vaghodia 02 Andhra Pradesh Vijayawada 01 A few CNG outlets have also been set up by some private/multi-national companies in Gujarat.
As on 1.4.2005, 105 Auto LPG dispensing stations (ALDS) are also in operation in the country.

(d) & (e) Yes Sir. The following measures have been taken by the Government to forestall the misuse of domestic LPG cylinders in vehicles:-

(i) State Governments have been advised to impress upon district authorities the need to intensify their supervision of LPG driven vehicles and take action as per law in case of violations.918LPG distributors are regulated by the Oil Marketing Companies(OMCs) in line with the customer population and per capita consumption of that market, based on last year’s sales for the same month.

(iii) Publicity campaigns are launched by OMCs from time to time to make the public aware about the hazards associated with the unauthorized use of domestic LPG cylinders as auto LPG.

records.qtitle: INDIGENOUS PILOT TRAINING .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the requirement of pilots in the next five years in the country and how will it be met by the Ministry; and

(b) the reasons for getting pilot training by Boeing and Airbus abraod and not in India?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL ) 

	(a):-    The  requirement of pilots is expected to grow with
	the growth in civil aviation sector and depends on number of
	aircraft  inducted  from  time  to  time and their continued
	operations.  The  steps  taken  by  the Ministry to meet the
	future requirement of pilots include increasing the training
	capacity  of  Indira  Gandhi Rashtriya Uran Academy (IGRUA),
	setting  up  of  a new pilot training academy, relaxation of
	requirement   of   flying  hours  from  250  to  200  hours,
	relaxation  in the upper age from 60 to 61 years, subject to
	medical   fitness  and  permitting  appointment  of  foreign
	pilots.
	


(b)  :-  Since  simulators  of  Airbus  and  Boeing types of
	aircraft  are  not available with private airlines in India,
	pilots are sent for training on Boeing and Airbus abroad.

records.qtitle: PRIVATE PARTICIPATION IN RURAL EDUCATION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that private participation in running secondary schools in rural areas in virtually nil;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(c) whether Government are considering any policy for increasing private participation in secondary schools in rural ..areas so that people in rural areas can get secondary education affordably and qualitatively by fulfilling Government`s goal for education to all?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER FOR HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI ARJUN SINGH)

(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (A) TO (C) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 119 DUE FOR REPLY ON 01.08.2005 BY SHRI SAN JAY RAUT REGARDING PRIVATE PARTICIPATION IN RURAL AREAS.

(a) & (b) No Sir. As pet` available data, the percentage of private unaided schools in the secondary and senior secondary sector has risen from 6% in 1973 to 24% in 2001. Such private unaided schools are found both in rural and urban areas.

(c) Over 90% of all secondary schools, including Government, private aided and private unaided schools are affiliated to State Boards of Education. There is at present no policy aimed at promoting private participation in secondary schools. The Government of India has a scheme to establish one Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya in each district of the country to provide quality education. Seventy five per cent of the seats in every Navodaya Vidyalaya is reserved for the students belonging to the rural areas.

records.qtitle: IMPROVEMENT OF GOODS TRANSPORT FACILITATION RAIL NETWORK .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering to improve various goods transport facilitation rail network in the next five years;

(b) if so, the details thereof and the steps taken or proposed to be taken for generating additional rail capacity for carrying long and short haul bulk goods by making it industry and consumer friendly;

(c) whether it is a fact that Japan International Co- operation Agency has offered financial assistance for Mumbai- Delhi and Mumbai –Kolkata rail corridor project; and

(d) if so, the details thereof? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

( SHRI R. VELU )


(a) to (d): A Statement is attached.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (d) OF RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 624 BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT TO BE ANSWERED IN RAJYA SABHA ON 29.7.05 REGARDING IMPROVEMENT OF GOODS TRANSPORT FACILITATION RAIL NETWORK 


(a) & (b):   Improvement and expansion of the  Rail  network
is  a continuous and ongoing exercise.  Every year as
part  of  the Budget exercise works relating  to  New
Lines,    Gauge    Conversion,   Doubling,    Traffic
Facilities,  etc.  are sanctioned for improvement  of
the  goods  transport facilities as well as expansion
of  the physical rail network.  During the 10th  Plan 

(2002-07) it has been envisaged to add 1310  Kms.  of
New  Lines,  2365 Kms. of Gauge Conversion  and  1500
Kms.  of  Doubling for expansion of the Rail network.
An  Integrated Railway Modernization Plan (2005-2010)
has  been formulated for overall improvement  in  the
facilities  in  the  rail network  including  various
measures  to  improve running of  freight  trains  on
Golden  Quadrilateral  and its diagonals,  Throughput
Enhancement  Works  and  Terminal  Facilities  Works,
Computerization of the Freight Operations, etc.  This
would  also  enable making the system more  customer-
friendly.


Railways  have  also  envisaged  construction  of   a
Dedicated   Freight   Corridor   along   the   Golden
Quadrilateral & its diagonals and other high  density
routes,   keeping  in  view  the  need  for  capacity
augmentation   and  meeting  the   demands   of   the
projected growth of freight traffic.


(c) & (d):  In the Joint Declaration issued after the  visit
of  the  Hon’ble Prime Minister of Japan to India  in
April  2005, Government of Japan has confirmed  their
intention to examine the feasibility of proposal  for
Dedicated   Freight  Corridors  with  the   financial
assistance   from  the  Japanese  Government.   Japan
International  Cooperation  Agency  (JICA)  has  been
asked  to undertake a feasibility study for Dedicated
Freight  Corridors  on Delhi -  Mumbai  and  Delhi  –
Kolkata routes.

records.qtitle: CLOSURE OF HVOCL .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Hon`ble High Court, Delhi has ordered the Hindustan Vegetable Oils Corporation Limited to close its Unit by making all payments to its employees and that more than 67 per cent industrial land situated in Kirti Nagar Industrial Area, Delhi should have been given to the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) in 1996;

(b) if so, the action taken by the company so far;

(c) whether it is a fact that the employees of one of its Unit have illegally occupied 11/2 acres of land at Sabji Mandi, Ghantaghar, Delhi; and

(d) if so, Government`s initiative in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION ( DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH )

(a) & (b): No, Sir. The Supreme Court of India in its order passed in the case of M.C. Mehta vs Union of India & others, categorized the Delhi Vanaspati Unit of Hindustan Vegetable Oils Corporation Limited as a `H` category & has ordered that it should be closed down from 30.11.1996. As per the said order, the Company has to hand over part of the land to Delhi Development Authority. The exact size/measurement of the land to be handed over is subjudice in the apex Court.

(c) & (d): No Sir. One ex employee has continued to occupy the Company quarter of the Sabji Mandi Unit of the Hindustan Vegetable Oils Corporation Limited which was allotted to him during his service. As such, his final dues have not been settled. The Company has been directed to take legal action for vacation of the Company premises.

MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)


(a) No, Sir.

(b) Does not arise.

(d) & (e): The Army is tasked with the responsibility to counter all terrorist activities. The overall counter infiltration measures and counter proxy war strategy deployed by the Army include a multi-tiered arrangement on the Line of Control (LC) along with fencing and relentless operations in the hinterland so as to ensure that infiltration is minimized and violence levels in Jammu and Kashmir kept under check.

records.qtitle: PROMOTION OF BUSINESS WITH USA CHINA AND RUSSIA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have explored further possibilities to promote business with U.S.A., China and Russia during the last three months;

(b) if so, the names of items whose export and import is possible with these countries; and

(c) the other areas where business can be promoted and the facilities proposed to be provided by Government to Indian businessmen for this purpose?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN )

(a) to (c): The position in respect of Promotion of Business with USA, China and Russia is as follows:- 


USA    Expansion of Indo-US trade is a sustained and continuous effort of the 
Government. Areas that have received particular attention are gems and 
jewellery, textiles and apparel, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, marine products, 
engineering goods including auto and auto parts, processed agricultural items
 and leather and leather products.  Information Technology enabled services, 
biotechnology and other knowledge based industries are some of the other 
identified thrust areas.


	Trade facilitation is a continuous and ongoing process.  Efforts are 
regularly made to expand and diversify trade through various trade promotion 
measures such as market research, information dissemination, Buyer-Seller 
Meets, Participation in important trade fairs etc.


CHINA   Steps being taken, on an on-going basis, for promotion of business 
with China include participation in trade fairs/exhibitions, exchanges of 
delegations at both governmental and business levels, exchange of information,
 etc.   Major items of export to China are diverse and inter alia include iron
 ore, primary & semi-finished iron and steel, and value added items which 
include plastic & linoleum products, processed mineral & chemicals, drugs & 
pharmaceuticals and marine products etc.  Chinese imports into India comprise
 electronic goods, organic chemicals, pharmaceutical products, etc.  The 
 potential items of exports to China  are automobiles, auto engine & 
components, electronic components, basic drugs, chemicals and pharmaceuticals; metal 
and metal based products like alloy steel bars and rods, handicrafts, 
electrical machinery, engineering goods like diesel engines and compressors,
 textile yarns and cotton fabrics, agricultural products including grains, 
tobacco and oilseeds, IT products and services, consumer durable, processed 
and semi processed foods items, minerals and mineral products including iron
 ore, marine food, fruits, and vegetables; industrial valves, actuators, 
forgings etc., medical diagnostic equipment and laboratory equipment and 
stones and other construction material.


RUSSIA   During the 10th Session of Indo-Russian Inter-Governmental Commission
 (IRIGC) held at New Delhi on 18-19 November, 2004, both the sides decided to
 pay special attention to enhancing bilateral trade and investment cooperation
 jointly with business and banking communities and industrial organizations.



	The main items of export are Drugs, Pharmaceuticals & Fine Chemicals,
 RMG Cotton including accessories, Tea, Coffee, Tobacco unmanufactured, 
Processed Minerals, Plastic & Linoleum Products, Machinery and Instruments,
 Transport Equipments, Electronic Goods.  The main items of import are Iron &
 Steel, Fertilizers manufactured, Non-Ferrous Metals, Coal, Coke, Briquettes,
 Newsprint, Silver, Synthetic & Reclaimed Rubber, etc.


	To enhance India`s exports to Russia, Government has taken a number of
 steps which include promotion of dialogue at the highest level, constant 
review through the Joint Commission/Working Group/Sub-Group mechanism, 
promoting direct business contacts through exchange of delegations, Joint 
Business Councils, holding of exhibitions, participation in fairs, etc.  In 
addition to this, w.e.f. April 2004, Russia has also been included as a Focus
 Country in the ongoing phase of the Focus CIS programme aimed at developing 
and enhancing India`s trade with countries of the CIS Region.

(b) to what extent our country would be benefited through these agreements in the coming years;

(d) if so, what is Government`s response thereon?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS AND PANCHAYATI RAJ

(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR)

(a & b) A Sale Purchase Agreement (SPA) for import of 5 MMTPA of LNG from Iran was signed between GAIL (India) Ltd. (GAIL) / Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) / Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd. (BPCL), and National Iranian Gas Export Company Limited (NIGEC). The import of

5.0 MMTPA LNG from Iran would help to partially meet the gas requirements of the country. The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas have, on 5.3.2005 and 4.7.2005, signed an Agreement on Cooperation and a Memorandum for Cooperation, with Venezuela and Romania respectively in the hydrocarbon sector.
The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas has also entered into dialogue with a host of national Governments of countries that are rich in oil and gas resources as well as technology in the related sector. Since 1.1.2005, high level engagements have taken place at various levels between representatives of Ministry of P&NG and their counterparts of a number of countries, including Russia, Kazakhstan, Myanmar, Pakistan, Iran, Romania, Turkey, Bangladesh, Uzbekistan, United Kingdom, USA, Canada, Norway, Venezuela, Republic of Korea, Qatar, Ecuador, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, Nigeria, Angola, Gabon, Algeria, Libya, UAE, Japan, China, Australia, Malaysia, Afghanistan, Yemen, Brazil, Turkmenistan and EU. The result of these interactions have been set out in Joint Press Statements, Agreed Minutes of meetings and exchanges of letters.
This extensive international engagements has led to the identification of specific projects / proposals with Indian organizations as active partners. They have covered the following areas : -

(i) investments and joint ventures in the petroleum sector across the hydrocarbon value chain of India, host countries and third countries;

(ii) cooperation in research and development, transfer of technology and training in the upstream, downstream and natural gas sectors;

(iii) construction of trans-national oil and gas pipelines; and

(iv) achieving energy security by securing long term supplies of natural gas and petroleum products.



(c):- No, Sir.

(d) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: FINANCIAL CRISIS IN BIHAR .

(c) whether Government`s attention has been drawn to the recent report of World Bank on Bihar`s financial status;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) what are the corrective measures taken or proposed to be taken for the development of Bihar?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE
SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM

(a) & (b): No, Sir. The Central Government is not in receipt of any formal communication from the State Government indicating that the State of Bihar is facing a serious financial crunch. As a matter of fact the State has not been in a position of overdraft either in the year 2004-05 or in 2005-06. The treasury holdings of the State as on 20.7.2005 were of the order of Rs. 2970.08 crores. No request was received from the State for a Ways and Means Advance or for Medium Term Loan.

(c): Yes, Sir.

(d): The World Bank has prepared a note on Public Expenditure Management in Bihar which identified areas of strengthening in Bihar`s Public expenditure management and covers budgeting, financial management procurement and accountability related issues.

(e): In order to compensate the Bihar Government for the loss of traditional revenue sources subsequent to its partition, the Central Government announced a Special Plan for Bihar for Rs. 1000 crores as a part of RSVY for the development of the priority sectors such as power, irrigation and roads in Bihar. This is in addition to the funds provided to the backward districts in Bihar under the Backward District Initiative (BDI) under Rashtriya Sam Vikas Yojna (RSVY).

records.qtitle: MASSIVE SHORTFALL OF TEACHERS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there would be a massive shortfall of teachers against the increasing demand of teachers in various parts of the country;

(b) if so, the remedial measures Government propose to meet the situation; and

(c) the details of the steps taken or proposed to be taken to accelerate teachers training programmes both for the domestic and international purposes ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M.A.A. FATMI)

(a) Yes Sir, as per data supplied by the States/UTs there is shortage of teachers in schools in some States/UTs.

(b) & (c) Additional posts of teachers are being sanctioned under Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan based on the requirement projected by the States in their District Elementary Education Plans. Accordingly 5.46 lakh posts of teachers have been sanctioned up to 2004-05. National Council for Teacher Education has decided to take various pro-active measures to meet the requirement of trained teachers. Some of the measures taken are indicated below :- 
·    State Governments have been asked to increase the
intake in DIETs up to a maximum of 200 seats.
·    NCTE has dispensed with the requirement of ‘No
Objection Certificate’ from State/UT Governments for
establishing elementary teachers training facilities for
a period of three years for those institutions already
running B.Ed programmes recognized by NCTE.
·    NCTE is also according approval to specific
proposals of State Governments to train untrained
teachers through distance mode.

records.qtitle: FACILITIES IN GOVERNMENT SCHOOLS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have taken any steps to provide better educational facilities particularly in the Government schools where most of the students belong to the families which are unable to afford expenses of education;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI M.A.A. FATMI )

(a) to (c) : Most schools come within the purview of the State Boards of Secondary Education under the respective State Governments. Only Kendriya Vidyalayas, Navodaya Vidyalayas and schools of the Central Tibetan School Administration are within the purview of the Government of India. It is the Government’s constant endeavour to provide improved facilities in its schools.

records.qtitle: ASSISTANCE FOR LOSS ON COTTON PROCUREMENT .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Maharashtra Government has approached the Central Government seeking assistance for defraying the loss suffered and likely to be suffered this year in procurement of the cotton produce at the minimum support price fixed under the monopoly procurement system for cotton;

(b) if so, the extent of aid sought, the quantum of cotton procured and to be procured this year, the MSP fixed and the total production of cotton this year; and

(c) the Central Government`s response thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR)

(a) to (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 717 FOR 13/05/2005 REGARDING ASSISTANCE FOR LOSS ON COTTON PROCUREMENT.


(a) to (c): The Government of Maharashtra has sought subsidy for making good the loss in cotton procurement under the monopoly procurement scheme of the Government of Maharashtra and export subsidy to make cotton export competitive on the lines applicable to Cotton Corporation of India (CCI).
The estimated production of cotton in the country during 2004-05 as per the figures of the Cotton Advisory Board is 23.20 million bales of 170 Kgs each, which includes the estimated production of 5.2 million bales of 170 Kgs each in Maharashtra. Based on quality differentials, the procurement prices in Maharashtra differ, and for 2004-05 these range from Rs.2225 per quintal to Rs.2500 per quintal. The procurement prices are inclusive of additional prices over and above the guaranteed prices, which correspond to the Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) fixed by the Central Government ranging from Rs.1675 per quintal to Rs.2010 per quintal. The Government of Maharashtra has procured around 42 lakh bales of 170 kgs each during the 2004-05 season. The State Government has estimated a loss of Rs.1500 crore under the monopoly procurement scheme in 2004-05.
The Ministry of Agriculture supports the proposal for extending the benefit of cost neutralization to the Maharashtra State Cooperative Cotton Grower`s Marketing Federation

(MSCCGMF) on the same terms and conditions as are applicable to CCI.

records.qtitle: PROPOSALS FOR MAINTENANCE AND DEVELOPMENT OF DIFFERENT NATIONAL PARKS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government of Maharashtra have submitted any proposals for maintenance and development of (1) Borivali (2) Nagzira-Nawegaon (3) Peneh (4) Singh-Garh and (5) Tadoba National Parks under the Tenth Five Year Plan;

(b) if so, the Central aid sought and released therefor; and

(c) the population of different endangered species therein, in the beginning of the Tenth Five YearPlan and how far it has dwindled during the first half of the plan period and what steps are being taken to preserve, protect and promote these species?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) The details are at Annexure A.

(c) The population estimation of major endangered species is done periodically once in every four years. The population estimation of important animal species is at Annexure B. The following measures have been taken by the Government to protect the endangered animals are as follows- i. Legal protection has been provided to wild animals including tigers against hunting and commercial exploitation under the provisions of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. ii. Financial and technical help is being extended to the States under Centrally Sponsored Schemes for enhancing the capacity and infrastructure to provide effective protection to wild animals. iii. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has been empowered under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 to apprehend and prosecute wildlife offenders. iv. The Ministry of Home Affairs has addressed all State Governments to lend a helping hand to the field formations to curb poaching and illegal trade in wildlife. v. A National Wildlife Action Plan (2002-2016) has been launched with several action points and priority projects for conservation and protection of wildlife in the country. vi. Independent monitoring of tiger reserves has been done by a panel of experts drawn as per the normative guidelines of the Ministry. A standardized format for evaluation has been prescribed for monitoring and evaluation.

records.qtitle: MUMBAI URBAN INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECT .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government of Maharashtra had submitted a proposal called `Mumbai Urban Infrastructure Project` costing about Rs.2,647 crores in June, 2003;

(b) if so, the details of the proposal and Government`s response thereto;

(c) whether the State Government had requested for a special Central grant of Rs.647 crores for the project; and

(d) if so, Government`s decision in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING

(SHRI M.V. RAJASEKHARAN)

(a) to (d): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 698 REGARDING MUMBAI URBAN INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECT BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT DUE FOR ANSWER ON 12.05.2005.

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b) to (d): The Mumbai Urban Infrastructure Project proposed by the Government of Maharashtra envisages upgradation of roads, construction of flyovers and traffic network in Mumbai with the estimated cost Rs.2648 crore (excluding land acquisition cost) against which the State Government has asked for a special assistance of Rs.648 crore. The Government of India have examined the proposal and advised the State Government to adopt a consortium approach as the infrastructure projects require substantial investments. The bulk of the resources should come from private/institutional sources with minimum budgetary support. The resources available under the related schemes of the Central Ministries should be pooled. After prioritization of the components of the project, the State Government may approach the Planning Commission/Ministry of Urban Development for funding of viability gaps, if any, through the Annual Plan mechanism.

records.qtitle: BRIDGE ON MUMBAI BANGALORE HIGHWAY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the bridge which is under construction on a stream of Kasegaon Village in Sangli district on Mumbai-Bangalore National Highway, which was part of the Golden Quadrilateral Project lately collapsed;

(b) if so, the extent of damage caused and casualties, if any, involved therein; and

(c) Government`s response thereto?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

(SHRI K.H. MUNIYAPPA)


(a) & (b): A part of the deck slab of the above-mentioned bridge collapsed during construction. There was no casualty.

(c ) : The contractor reconstructed the deck slab at his own cost as per the contract agreement.

records.qtitle: SEA CORRIDOR IN MUMBAI .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether there is a proposal for a 22 K.M. Sea Corridor in Mumbai, the Western Free Sea Link from Bandra to Worli to Nariman Point and Cuffe Parade and a harbour link to connect Mumbai with Navi Mumbai;

(b) if so, the details and the estimated cost thereof; and

(c) Government`s response and decision thereon?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

(SHRI K.H. MUNIYAPPA)


(a) to (c) Yes, Sir. Two proposals viz. Mumbai- Trans Harbour link for Rs. 4000 crores and Western Freeway Sea Link Project for Rs. 3960 crores have been received from Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC). In these two proposals MSRDC has requested for grant of Rs. 1600 crores and Rs. 790 crores respectively from the Central Government. However, this Ministry is primarily responsible for the development and maintenance of National Highways only. These two projects do not fall on National Highways and as such Ministry is not directly concerned. Moreover, there is no budgetary provision in the schemes of this Ministry for providing financial assistance to these projects.

records.qtitle: ACQUIRING OF FRENCH SUBMARINES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the cabinet sub-committee on security has sent its approval for acquiring and building French submarines `Scorpene`; and

(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, by when it is likely to give its approval?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRIPRANAB MUKHERJEE)


(a) & (b): Government had approved a long term Perspective Plan for the indigenous construction of submarines and acquisition of national competence in submarine building. No final decision has been taken by the Government on the proposal for the construction of Scorpene submarines under Transfer of Technology.

records.qtitle: INCREASE IN TEA IMPORT .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that due to short-fall in production of tea in the year 2004 the import of tea increased from 98.60 lakhs kg. in the year 2003 to 3.05 crores kg. in the year 2004;

(b) how much foreign exchange was paid for the import of tea in the year 2004, when tea is a major foreign exchange earner for the country; and

(c) what incentives the Ministry proposes to take to increase the production of tea in India?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN )

(a): Although there was an increase in the volume of tea imported during 2004 as compared to 2003, this cannot be attributed solely to the shortfall in tea production during 2004. Tea is mainly imported for the purpose of re-export with value addition. Such imports for re-export increases the price competitiveness of Indian teas in the international market besides catering to the requirements of international buyers.

(b): The value of tea imports during 2004 was US$ 31.13 million as against the earnings from tea exports of US$ 373.64 million.

(c): A number of developmental schemes are being implemented by the Tea Board during the 10th Five Year Plan for enhancing productivity, quality and marketability of tea produced in the country. Financial and technical assistance is being provided for various plantation development activities like replanting, rejuvenation, creation of irrigation facilities etc. It is proposed to take up a programme for replantation and rejuvenation of old tea bushes. The detailed costing and modalities of funding the programme are under examination of the Government.

records.qtitle: DEVELOPMENTAL PLANS OF MUMBAI .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have drawn out plans not only to develop Mumbai into Shanghai of India but also to showcase India as a model and fast developing economy and as an attractive destination of F.DI. with infrastructure favorably comparable to China;

(b) if so, the broad features and details of the plan, indicating phase-wise details and targets Contemplated there under; and

(c) the steps taken and beginning in that direction?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN MINISTRY OF FINANCE SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM

(a) to (c) : Key areas for Mumbai’s transformation, namely, transport infrastructure, housing and other infrastructure have been discussed in various meetings held in Planning Commission. States` proposals in this respect are at an early stage of formulation and the State is yet to develop them into implement able projects with the necessary financial tie up.
The State Government can avail of Central Assistance under National Urban Renewal Mission and other Schemes within the framework of the schemes and subject to the availability of resources, through properly formulated projects.

records.qtitle: REDUCTION IN RATE OF INTEREST ON CENTRAL LOAN TO MAHARASHTRA
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the State Government of Maharashtra had approached the Twelfth Finance Commission to seek relief in respect of the debt-trap State Government found itself in, by various means particularly that by way of reduction in the rate of interest on the Central Government loans; and

(b) if so, the extent of reduction in rate of interest sought by the State Government and the Finance Commission`s recommendation thereon and Government`s response in this regard?
records.ans_text:
Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance SHRI S.S.PALANIMANICKAM
Parts (a) and (b): The State Government had requested the Twelfth Finance Commission (TFC) to recommend reduction in the interest rate on all loans and advances of Central Government and the Financial Institutions (FIs).
T.F.C. recommended consolidation and rescheduling of all Central loans contracted till 31.3.2004 and outstanding as on 31.3.2005 into fresh loans for 20 years carrying 7.5% interest w.e.f, the year of a State enacts the Fiscal Responsibility Legislation, providing for core elements recommended by T.KC.
T.F.C. estimated interest relief of Rs.1217.39 crore and lower repayments by Rs.1133.12 crore for Maharashtra on consolidation of these loans. GOI has accepted this recommendation of the T.F.C.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) CAREER PROGRESSION OF REPUBLIC DAY BRAVERY AWARD WINNING CHILDREN .
records.name: PREMA CARIAPPA
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of the facilities provided to the children, for their career progression, who are awarded for an act of bravery by Government on the occasion of Republic Day; and

(b) the number of the children awarded during the last five years alongwith the details of the facilities being provided to them and the maximum age upto which such facilities would continue? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI ARJUN SINGH)

(a)&(b) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (a) & (b) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 627 FOR 9.5.2005 REGARDING CAREER PROGRESSION OF REPUBLIC DAY BRAVERY AWARD WINNING CHILDREN BY SHRIMATI PREMA CARIAPPA AND SHRI SANJAY RAUT

(a) The National Bravery Awards for children were instituted by the Indian Council for Child Welfare in 1957. The Indian Council for Child Welfare was registered as a non-government organisation under the Societies Registration Act XXI of 1860 on 5th June, 1952. The Awards are presented by the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India prior to Republic Day every year. The Awardees subsequently participate in the Republic Day parade. Prominent social workers, representatives of NGOs and representatives of various Government Departments form part of the Selection Committee.
ICCW has taken the initiative to introduce a number of benefits for the Awardees’ development and career progression with the active support and cooperation of the Government of India. These include the following: 
   
i)   The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare reserves seats
in MBBS (maximum of two in a year)


ii)  The Ministry of Human Resource Development, Department
of Education reserves seats in Diploma and Degree courses in
Engineering (maximum three each in a year) for the Awardees.


iii) The  Ministry of Railways provides free  rail  travel
facilities upto 18 years of age.


	In  addition ICCW provides the following facilities for
	the development of the Awardees.


iv)  Eligible Awardees are granted financial assistance for
their school education under ICCW’s Sponsorship  programme.
The criteria is that the total family income of the Awardee
should not exceed Rs. 2500/- per month.

 
v)   In  the  case  of  posthumous Awardees,  there  is  a
provision to provide Sponsorship assistance to a school
going sibling if eligible under the Sponsorship programme of
ICCW.

 
vi)  Scholarship is provided for higher education such  as
graduation, engineering, medicine.


b)    Number of Awardees from 2000 to 2004 (last five years)
	is  114.   Facilities being provided to them are as detailed
	above   according  to  their  age,  course  of   study   and
	eligibility.
