records.qtitle: PROVISION OF INTERNET CONNECTIONS TO SCHOOLS AND COLLEGES
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
-

(a) whether Government are considering to provide high-speed internet connection to various schools and colleges in every district for accessing the important information and rich educational content in local languages; and

(b) if so, by when it would be made available to schools and colleges?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY(DR.SHAKEEL AHMAD)

(a) and (b): There is no scheme for providing specifically computer internet facility only. Department of Secondary and Higher Education, Ministry of Human Resource Development has launched a scheme of ICT @ Schools during 2004 05, under which financial assistance would be provided to the State / UT for the computer education and training of students. As per the norms of the scheme, an amount of Rs 30,000/- per school would be provided for Internet Connectivity to the State / UTs for Govt. and Govt. aided Secondary and Senior Secondary Schools only in addition to other items like hardware, software, maintenance etc.

records.qtitle: FORMATION OF MILLENNIUM TELECOM COMPANY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether MTNL has formed a subsidiary company known as Millennium Telecom Company;

(b) if so, the projects the company has either installed or marketed and the number of employees in the company;

(c) the profit made by the company since its inception; and

(d) whether the MTNL has formed any other subsidiary company; if so, the name of the company and the status of that company?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

(a) Sir, MTNL has incorporated a 100% subsidiary company in the name of Millennium Telecom Limited (MTL) on 17-02-2002 for carrying out business as Internet Service Provider.

(b) MTL is presently conducting e-tendering work of MTNL. Total income earned by MTL by way of e-tendering work of MTNL during the last three years is Rs.576.82 lakhs. There are no full time employees working in MTL, only four MTNL employees looking after statutory activities of MTL as an additional charge.

(c) Since inception upto 31-03-2004, MTL has made a profit of Rs. 164.9 lacs.

(d) Sir, MTNL has also formed one more 100% subsidiary company with the name of Mahanagar Telephone Mauritius Ltd. (MTML). The MTML is registered in Mauritius and has been licensed by Government of Mauritius to provide telecom services` in Mauritius. Presently, the Company is in the process of setting up infrastructure and the service roll out is expected to start from mid of 2005.

records.qtitle: COMPULSORY MILITARY TRAINING .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is considering any proposal for compulsory military training to all the young citizens so that their services can be utilised during any emergency-crisis in the country;

(b) if so, details thereof; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)


(a) No, Sir.

(b) & (c): Does not arise in view of (a) above.

records.qtitle: FALL IN TEA PRODUCTION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that tea production in the country for the period 1st January to 31st December, 2004 was 82.02 crore kilograms as compared to the tea production for the same period in 2003 which was 85.75 crore kilograms;

(b) if so, what are the reasons for the fall in production of tea;

(c) whether it is true that some Northern States like Jammu and Kashmir, Uttaranchal, Himachal Pradesh, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh have also reported tea production in recent years; and

(d) if so, what incentives the Ministry proposes to give to these States for the production of tea?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN )

(a) & (b): Tea production in the country during 2004 was 820.22 million kg as compared to 857.06 million kg during 2003. The fall in production of tea during 2004 as compared to 2003 was due to unfavorable agro-climatic conditions in North and South India.

(c) & (d): Himachal Pradesh is traditionally a tea-growing State, though in a limited area. In Uttaranchal, the tea areas have been neglected over time, though the State Government has taken steps to revive the industry. New tea gardens have been established in some parts of Bihar.
A number of developmental schemes are being implemented by the Tea Board during the 10th Five Year Plan for enhancing productivity, quality and marketability of tea produced in the country under which financial and technical assistance is being provided for various plantation development activities. Benefits from these schemes are available for the tea gardens located in the various States.

records.qtitle: REQUIREMENT OF PILOTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have visualised the likely growth of air traffic from India in the next five years and the requirement of qualified pilots for the purpose;

(b) whether it is a fact that 70 per cent of the pilots now working with many leading Asian Airlines are Indian because they are offered better salaries and other perks as compared to Air India and Indian Airlines;

(c) if so, Government`s views thereon; and

(d) the total capacity of flying clubs and training academies in India to train qualified pilots per year and whether the Ministry is considering to increase the training centers for pilots?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )
(a), (b), (c) and (d):- A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 553 FOR 03.05.2005 REGARDING REQUIREMENT OF PILOTS. (a): According to Government’s assessment, growth in aviation sector is likely to continue over the next five years and beyond leading to increased demand of qualified pilots. (b) and (c):- No such data is maintained by the Government. However, In view of the expansion in the Middle East and the Indian Sub-Continent, there has been a growing demand for Trained Pilots. Therefore many airlines are offering attractive pay package and perks. Both Air India and Indian Airlines also offer attractive package to the pilots with job security. (d) : There are 30 approved Flying clubs/Training Institute including IGRUA which are producing pilots upto CPL level. The total capacity of these flying clubs / Training institutes including IGRUA is Approx. 500 pilots to be trained in 3 years. Approx. 150 pilots are granted CPL annually and one additional flying training institute is proposed at Gondia, Maharashtra.

records.qtitle: DEVELOPMENT OF TOURISM IN MAHARASHTRA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the State Government of Maharashtra has submitted a special plan for development of tourism m the State to remove regional imbalance;

(b) if so, the salient features and the estimated cost thereof,

(c) the quantum of Central Government aid sought therefore; and

(d) what is Government`s response thereto7
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF TOURISM

(SMT. RENUKA CHOWDHURY)

(a), (b), (c) and (d): Development of tourist places/spots is a continuous process. Ministry of Tourism in collaboration with the State Governments/UT Administrations identifies such places of tourist interest including the State of Maharashtra. Based on project proposals received from the States, Ministry of Tourism provides financial assistance for development of their infrastructure. During 2004-05 projects worth Rs. 16.00 crore were sanctioned for development of tourism in Maharashtra.
Loan assistance was also availed from the Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund of Japan

(now known as the Japan Bank for International Cooperation) for the development of Ajanta - Ellora (Phase I) to the tune of 3745 million Japanese yen. In addition to these completed projects loan has also been approved for the development of Ajanta Ellora Phase II for an amount of 7331 million Japanese Yen and this project is presently under implementation.

records.qtitle: SCHEMES FOR ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT OF SCS STS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are of the opinion that by only reserving certain percentage of jobs in Government and Semi-Government organizations it would not be adequate to uplift the persons belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes; and

(b) if so, the details of concrete plans to improve the economic condition of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes especially the poorest of the poor in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT

(SMT. SUBBULAKSHMI JAGADEESAN)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b): The strategies of Special Component Plan for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and the Tribal Sub Plan for Scheduled Tribes(STs) have been evolved with the objective of ensuring socio economic development of these communities through programmes of land reforms, agriculture, animal husbandry, village and small industries, small business etc. Special Central Assistance (SCA) is also provided to States and UTs implementing Special Component Plan and Tribal Sub-Plan which is meant for giving added thrust to the economic development programmes of these groups. Besides these, three National Finance and Development Corporations for Scheduled Castes (NSFDC), Scheduled Tribes (NSTFDC) and for Safai Karamcharis (NSKFDC) have been set up for financing income generating activities. The Centrally Sponsored Schemes for Assistance to Scheduled Castes Development Corporations (SCDCs) and Scheduled Tribes Development Corporations (TDCs) provide share capital contribution of 49% for the economic development of SCs and STs. The main functions of these Corporations include identification of eligible SC and ST families and motivating them to take up projects for economic development.

records.qtitle: INCENTIVE GRANT TO SSC BOARD .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Government of Maharashtra had in a meeting of Education Minister he had on August 10, 2004, suggested that on the basis of the number of students passing the National Talent Search Examination, conducted by NCERT an incentive grant should be given to SSC Board to improve their quality;

(b) if so, the extent of grant sought and the manner of its utilization; and

(c) Government`s decision thereon?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M.A.A. FATMI)

(a) to (c): A proposal has been received from the Government of Maharashtra for grant to the State SSC Boards for the students qualifying National Talent Search Examination. The proposal is not covered under any of the scheme of the Department of Secondary and Higher Education for providing grants.

records.qtitle: RAILWAY DEPARTMENT S CONTRACT FOR ACCIDENT RELIEF CRANE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Union Government are seriously going to investigate Railway Department’s contract for Accident relief crane (140 tonnes) with two companies i.e. United Kingdom’s Cowans Shelton and Germany’s Gottwald and dealing worth Rs.132 crore during the year 1996-97; and

(b) if so, by when it is going to investigate and whether Government have found anything wrong and unlawful in the contract agreement?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

( SHRI R. VELU )

(a) No, Sir

(b) On allegations of irregularities in the procurement of the above cranes in Parliament, it is stated that the then Minister of Railways Kum. Mamta Banerjee in 2000 had entrusted the detailed investigation into the entire affair to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). CBI after detailed investigations, did not find any irregularity in the procurement.

records.qtitle: RAILWAY SAFETY COMMISSION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Ministry of Railways is free to introduce new train services without the official permission from the Railway Safety Commission for starting new trains;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

(c) whether it is also a fact that the Standing Committee on Railways has insisted that it must be obligatory on the part of the Railway Ministry to receive a regular permission from the Commission of Railways Safety before introducing new train services; and

(d) if so, Government`s response thereto and whether Railway Ministry propose to grant statutory status to the Railway Safety Commission to avoid the increasing number of railway accidents?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R. VELU)


(a) & (b): Permission from Commissioner of Railway Safety is taken in the cases of introduction of trains on new section & gauge converted sections and where new type of rolling stock is to be run.

(c): Standing Committee on Railways(2004) of Fourteenth Lok Sabha has not insisted to take regular permission from the Commission of Railway Safety before introducing new train services. However, vide recommendation No. 18 of 5th Report, the Committee was informed that the Commissioner of Railway Safety is not consulted before announcement of new trains. However all the conditions and recommendations of the Commission are given due consideration by the Ministry of Railways. Before issuing the final sanction to the opening of a new line/ segment, recorded compliance is obtained from the concerned railway and only after getting the satisfactory compliance, the sanction of the Ministry is issued. In very rare cases, where it is not possible to accept some of the recommendations of the Commission, the Ministry issues the sanction by recording the reasons.

(d): Under Chapter III of the Railways Act 1989, the Commission of Railway Safety is a statutory body.

records.qtitle: DEMAND OF WLL GARUDA AND DOLPHIN MOBILE PHONES .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that WLL/Garuda and Dolphin Mobile Phones are not supplied to the consumers in time by the officers of MTNL/BSNL in spite of heavy demand from the people;

(b) whether it is also a fact that due to delay in supply, many of the consumers are going to other private cellular companies; and

(c) if so, the details of the steps taken or proposed to be taken to speed up the supply?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

(a) Sir, Garuda and Dolphin connections, the WLL and GSM post paid connections of MTNL are available on demand and there is no waiting list for both units in MTNL.

(b) In the present Telecom scenario, the consumers are shifting from one operator to another because of options available and suiting to individual requirement.

(c) The following measures are taken to provide connections on the same day:

(i) Use of pre activated handsets in Garuda.

(ii) Enough capacity is available in Dolphin/Garuda network to meet the demand.

(iii) Booking in Sanchar Haat/Call Centre.

(iv) Provision of new subscribers through Billing and Customer Care Service (B & CCS) in case of GSM to cut down delays.

records.qtitle: IMPROVEMENT OF SPEED POST SERVICE .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering to revamp/modernize the postal services in the country by making it people friendly;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether it is a fact that due to failure in efficiency of Postal Department`s Speed Post Services, private courier agencies are gaining day-by-day; and

(d) if so, what steps are taken or proposed to be taken for the improvement of Speed Post Services and make it people friendly?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

(a) & (b) Yes, Sir. Government has taken various steps and initiatives as part of an ongoing process to revamp/modernize the postal services in the country by making it people friendly.
Considering computerization to be a vital tool for the process, efforts are being made to computerize operations relating to booking, sorting and transmission of mails, Saving Bank and Postal Life Insurance. Initiatives are being taken to improve ergonomics and ambience of Post Offices, Railway Mail Offices, Speed Post Centres and other offices.
To give focussed attention to the customer and speedy redressal of public grievances, computerized Customer Care Centres are being established in major cities and towns with inter connectivity through a specially designed software. Government is making efforts to implement its Citizens Charter in more and more post offices.

(c) No, Sir. In fact Speed Post is getting more popular as is evident from sustained growth of traffic and revenue over the years. Traffic and revenue figures of Speed Post for last three years are given in the table below:- 


Year	Traffic (in lakhs)	Revenue (Rs. in Crores)
2001-02	527.97	196.53
2002-03	634.07	243.01
2003-04	826.00	298.35


(d)	A number of value additions, like door to door delivery, free pick
 up, volume based discount, customized packages etc. are provided with Speed
 Post from time to time to make it more people friendly. Internet based track
 and trace facility has been provided in all National Speed Post Centres. 
Efforts are being made to extend tracking facility for State Speed Post Centres
 and other Speed Post booking/delivery offices also . Web based customer 
grievance handling system is put in place in major cities and towns.

records.qtitle: HIGH RETAIL PRICE OF IMPORTED TEA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the retail price charged from users in India is very high while the actual rate of imported tea is only Rs. 45.68 per kg in the year 2004; and

(b) if so, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN )

(a) & (b) : Rs.45.68 per kg was the weighted average unit C.I.F. (Cost, Insurance and Freight) price of tea imported during 2004. Most of the teas imported into the country is for the purpose of re-export and therefore the price of imported tea has little bearing on domestic sales.

records.qtitle: OPERATION OF SMALL AIRSTRIPS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering to enhance and make small airstrips operational in various parts of the country for flying of small passenger and cargo planes;

(b) if so, the details thereof and how many districts will get benefit by air connectivity in the country; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )
(a) Airports Authority of India (AAI) is in constant endeavour to operate and upgrade the airports depending upon the requirements of airlines and traffic. (b) AAI has undertaken the development of Mysore airport in Karnataka and Cooch Behar airport in West Bengal for operation of ATR 42 type of aircraft based on the demand received from Air Deccan and Alliance Air for operation of ATR-42 aircraft. (c) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: PENALTY ON AIRLINES ON CANCELLATION OF FLIGHTS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering to impose heavy penalities on any domestic or international airlines who cancel their scheduled flights without proper intimation except bad climate;

(b) if so, by when it will be started; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )
(a),(b)&(c): There is presently no proposal to impose heavy penalties on any domestic or international airlines in the event of cancellation of flights. The present international air law as established by Warsaw Convention and Montreal Convention,1999 envisage only a measure of facilitation and do not contemplate any punitive action against airlines in case of cancellation/postponement of flights. Most airlines in India already have procedures in place for providing standard passenger facilitation measures in the event of delay/postponement of flights and do everything within their means to ensure that stranded passengers are not inconvenienced. Besides, because of the very nature of the air transportation industry, safety considerations have to be given foremost priority and reasons for delay of the flights are often beyond the control of the airlines. Any punitive provision may also end up increasing the cost of air travel considerably as airlines may be compelled to pass on a part of the financial burden to the passengers.

records.qtitle: MEASURES TO LESSEN LOAN BURDEN OF GOVERNMENT OF MAHARASHTRA
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the State Government of Maharashtra has borrowed loan of around one lakh ten thousand crore rupees from various segments;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the details of corrective steps suggested or proposed so far to the State Government of Maharashtra for lessening the loan amount in the next five years?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE
SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM

(a) & (b) Maharashtra`s outstanding liabilities for the year 2004-05 (BE) were Rs.84114 crore (RBI). The details are enclosed at Annex-A.

(c) Government of India swapped outstanding high cost (13% and above) central debt of Rs.15434.04 crore during 2002-05. Government of India has further accepted the recommendation of Twelfth Finance Commission (TFC) for debt consolidation and waiver of outstanding GoI debts. This Scheme, would benefit the Government of Maharashtra with lower interest of Rs.1217.39 crore, lower repayment of Rs.1133.12 crore and debt waiver of Rs.1953.22 crore over the next five years i.e. 2005-10, if the State meets necessary conditions.

records.qtitle: MINERAL DEPOSITS ON THE COAST OF TAMIL NADU
records.name: Sanjay Raut

(b) how much percentage of Tamil Nadu coast has been reported to have received new mineral deposits; and

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER`S OFFICE (SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN):
(a) There is no substantial enhancement of heavy minerals deposits in the coast of Nagapattanam as a result of the Tsunami.
(b) Along the coastal stretches of Tamil Nadu, it is seen that the deposition of heavy minerals due to Tsunami is patchy, inconsistent and with a maximum thickness of In some instances, the Tsunami waves have destroyed the existing 30-40 cm. In someh instanance thereby relocating the existing concentrations m dunes and deposited them inland, thereby relocating the existing deposits.
(c) It is not practicable to protect these mineral deposits spread over large area. Considering the vast resources of these mineral, the Government of India has in October 1998 notit`md a new policy on Beach Sand Minerals with a view to increase the rate of exploration of the minerals and also to attract more investment in this sector, ~0th private and foreign along with latest technology for value addition within the country .

records.qtitle: LOW COST HOUSING TO MIDDLE CLASS AND POOR PEOPLE
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government propose to chalk out any action plan for providing low cost housing for middle class and poor people by bringing new innovative technology;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and

(d) whether Government`s recent decision of 100 per cent FDI in construction sector would benefit for low-cost housing in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN EMPLOYMENT & POVERTY ALLEVIATION

( KUMARI SELJA )

(a)&(b): Building Materials Technologies Promotion Council,

(BMTPC) an autonomous organization has been set up under the administrative control of this Ministry for a comprehensive and integrated approach towards development, promotion and application of conventional and innovative housing and construction technologies and building materials in the country. Some of the major initiatives to popularize and promote low cost housing are given below:

(i) Incorporation of low cost building technologies into the specifications of Central Public Works Department and State Housing and Building agencies and development of standards through Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) to cover cost effective materials and construction technologies.

(ii) Strengthening of National Network of Building Centres for demonstration and extension of cost effective technologies and training of artisans in innovative low cost techniques at local levels. All materials and components produced at building Centres have been exempted by Government from levy of any excise duty.




(iii) support to research and development organizations for technology development organizations for technology development and transfer for field application.

(iv) Strengthening arrangements for large scale field applications of cost effective technologies and commercializing production of innovative low cost materials and components through BMTPC at national;and regional level and Building Centres at grass-root level.

(v) Providing fiscal incentives for production of cost effective building materials and import of critical machinery and equipments used for production of cost effective technologies and building components particularly based on industrial wastes like flyash, phosophogypsm and red mud.

(vi) Promotion of cost effective technologies in the housing schemes being funded by housing finance institutions like Housing and Urban Development Corporation, etc. In the financial year 2004-05 construction of demonstration houses using low cost housing techniques has been initiated by the BMTPC in 11 States of the country. The BMTPC has developed a number of technologies for low cost housing and several of these have been licensed to entrepreneurs for commercialisation. Similarly, the BMTPC has also developed a number of machines for production of cost effective prefab building components for low cost housing.

(c): Does not arise.

(d): The decision is expected to catalyse investment in construction and development project as on instrument to generate economic activity, create new employment opportunities and add to the available housing stock and built-up infrastructure.

records.qtitle: APPROVAL FOR MRP ON PACKAGED GOODS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware that the Maximum Retail Price (MRP) printed on the packages and packed consumer goods is by and large very high and costlier;

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto;

(c) whether Government are considering to make it mandatory to get the MRP approved by an appropriate agency by safeguarding the interest of consumers; and

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(SHRI TASLIMUDDIN)

(a) & (b): The Standards of Weights and Measures

(Packaged Commodities) Rules, 1977 require declaration of retail sale price of a package in the form MRP …(inclusive of all taxes), for information of consumer. Declaration of MRP on package has to be made by manufacture or packer of the commodity. The Rules have penal provision, which prevent the retail dealer from selling the package at a price higher than the declared MRP. The Government do not have information on the cost of production of commodities in such packages.

(c) & (d): There is no proposal under consideration to make it mandatory to get the MRP approved by an appropriate agency. Competitive market forces would discourage manufacturers/packers from declaring unreasonably high MRP.

records.qtitle: UNPRODUCTIVE LAND IN COUNTRY .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that more than 25 million hectares of land is lying unproductive in the country;

(b) if so, whether Government have revived the various schemes and programmes for the improving wasteland through making it productive to use in the next five years by involving community and private participation in the country;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) if not, reasons therefor ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI A. NARENDRA)

(a) to (c) As per the Wastelands Atlas of India, 2000, brought out by the Department of Land Resources in collaboration with the National Remote Sensing Agency (NRSA), Hyderabad employing Satellite Remote Sensing Technologies, the total extent of Wasteland/degraded lands in the country is 63.85 million hectares of which 36.98 million hectares are treatable wastelands excluding forest wastelands. To revive and develop these areas, the Department of Land Resources has been implementing three area development programmes namely, the Integrated Wastelands Development Programme (IWDP), the Drought Prone Areas Programme (DPAP) and the Desert Development Programme (DDP). These programmes are being implemented on watershed basis since 1995-96. Under these programmes, the watershed works are to be planned, executed and maintained by the local people themselves with necessary technical, financial and managerial inputs and support from the concerned line departments/Zilla Parishad/District Rural Development Agencies.

(d) Question does not arise.

records.qtitle: CUT IN INTEREST RATE FOR ONE YEAR CROP LOAN .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering to curtail interest rate up to six per cent for one -year crop loan for benefiting poor farmers;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and when this is proposed to be implemented; and

(c) ff not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S.PALANIMANICKAM)

(a), (b) and (c): As per the interest rate policy of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), interest rate on loans given by the Commercial Banks are deregulated excepting that interest rate on loans up to Rs. 2 lakh should not exceed the Benchmark Prime Lending Rate(BPLR). Commercial Banks are free to decide their lending rate for Marts above Rs. 2 lakh subject to announcement of their BPLR. However, the Government on 16th July, 2003 had announced reduction in the lending rate for agriculture with a view to extending the full benefit of declining interest rates to agriculture sector, particularly to the small and marginal farmers. Consequent to the announcement, an Public Sector Banks have reduced their lending rate to a single digit rate not more than 9% per annum and in some cases 8.5% per annum on crop loans up to a ceiling of Rs. 50,000/-. This single digit lending rate have benefited most of the crop loan account holders and covered almost all small and marginal farmers.

(b) There is no such proposal. Five hundred scholarships are provided annually to physically disabled students for pursuing Post Matric professional and technical courses. Students with disabilities in Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation, Multiple Disabilities and Profound or Severe Hearing Impaired are provided with scholarship from class IX onwards.
Educational loans are provided to physically disabled students for pursuing professional and technical courses by NHFDC on case to case basis and in accordance with their loaning parameters.

records.qtitle: HEPATITIS C .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are seriously observing and controlling the problems being faced by a number of people due to Hepatitis-C in various parts of the country ; and

(b) if so, the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken by Government for controlling the spread of Hepatitis-C and improving the technique of diagnosis effectively in the country?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

( SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)


(a) & (b) : Hepatitis-C spread through unsafe sex, unsafe blood transmission, unsafe injections and from mother to child etc. This is preventable by ensuring safe blood transmission, safe sex, safe injection practices etc. Vaccine for Hepatitis-C is not available. Measures taken to prevent Hepatitis-C include mandatory testing of blood in all blood banks, promotion of safe sex under National AIDS Control Programme, Health awareness campaigns under this programme, implementation of guidelines by State Health Authorities by using separate syringes and needles for each injection. Also, the Indian Council of Medical Research has envisaged to undertake studies with regard to improvement of therapies to tackle Hepatitis-C in the country.

records.qtitle: RAIDS CONDUCTED BY CBI

(c) whether Government have received any complaints against the CBI officers for their illegal and corruptive nature; and

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTRY AFFAIRS.(SHRI SURESH PACHOURI)

(a) & (b): CBI conducts searches as per the provisions of the law and as a part of investigation depending on the facts and circumstance of the cases. Number of searches conducted in different cases form the part of record of those individual cases and no separate record is maintained about the total number of raids/searches conducted.

(c) & (d): Complaints received are thoroughly verified and appropriate action is taken. Once the allegation is prima-facie substantiated, follow up action is initiated either by registration of cases i.e. Regular Case/Preliminary Enquiry or Regular Departmental Action is initiated for major/minor penalty etc. There is also an in-house surveillance system in CBI to observe the conduct and activities of officers of doubtful integrity.

records.qtitle: HEADQUARTER OF BANNED MILITANT OUTFIT IN J K .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the headquarters of banned militant outfit named as Jaish-e-Mohammed is located in concrete bunkers, deep in the mountains of Tral-dachigam-Dara hills in Jammu and Kashmir;

(b) whether the security forces verified the information given by the captured militant Sajjad Ahmed Butt, that these bunkers were equipped with heavy weaponry including anti-aircraft guns; and ;

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)


(a) & (b): No, Sir. Available reports do not indicate presence of concrete bunkers with heavy weaponry including anti aircraft guns in Tral-Dachigam-Dara Hills in Jammu and Kashmir. However, the presence of terrorists in remote and inaccessible areas of this hilly track cannot be ruled out.

(c): As reported by the State Government of Jammu and Kashmir, the security forces have been laying ambushes and patrolling deep in this hilly terrain regularly. Besides, an additional battalion of Rashtriya Rifles (RR) has been deployed in the area to dominate the ridges and neutralize any terrorist present there.

records.qtitle: DONATIONS BY RELIGIOUS INSTITUTIONS .

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a)to(d): Religious institutions and places of worship are free to manage their activities and Government has no control over the management of their affairs. Action is taken as per law whenever instances of violation of existing laws come to notice.

records.qtitle: STATE LANGUAGES IN SCHOOL CURRICULUM .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that some of the State Governments have made their State language compulsory in the :primary and secondary level school curriculum;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) what would be the impact of such decision if other States also follow;

(d) whether Government have taken any decision in the matter to make State language compulsory in primary and secondary level school`s curriculum; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI ARJUN SINGH)


(a) to (e) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. Statement referred to parts (a) to (e) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 82 by Shri Sanjay Rant due for answer on 7.3.2005 regarding State languages in school curriculum.

(a) to (c) The Government is not aware whether any State Governments have made their respective State languages compulsory in the primary and secondary school curriculum. At the national level, the National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) prepares the curriculum for school education. The Central Board of Secondary Education

(CBSE) adopts/adapts this curriculum for its affiliated schools only. The State Education Boards are not bound to follow the curriculum prepared by the NCERT, They are empowered to prepare their own curriculum for their respective schools. The subject `Education` being on the Concurrent List, information relating to the actions by the State Governments about making State language compulsory in their respective curricula is not centrally available. However, as per Article 350A, it is the responsibility of the State and of every local authority within the State to provide adequate facilities for instructions in the mother- tongue at the primary stage.
The Three Language Formula as advocated in the National Policy on Education was approved by the Parliament. The formula is applicable at the upper primary stage and has to continue upto the end of Secondary stage i.e. Class X. This formula provides for a study of the mother tongue or the regional language compulsorily as the first language. It also requires the study of Hindi, English and a modern Indian language, preferably one of the Southern languages in the Hindi speaking States, Hindi and English in the non- Hindi speaking States. The National Curriculum Framework for School Education (NCFSE) 2000 of the NCERT has also included the provisions of the Three language Formula.
This formula, which flows from a policy decision, is to be reflected in the school curriculum. The role of the Central Government in the matter of the implementation of the formula is recommendatory. The implementation of the Three Language Formula is the sole responsibility of the State Governments. All the States/Union Territories had, accordingly, been urged by the Government from time to time to implement it. While all the schools affiliated to the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) and the Council for the Indian School Certificate Examination (CISCE) have already implemented it, most of the States/UTs, too, are implementing this formula.

(d) No, Sir.

(e) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: SAIL S STATUS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) could not succeed, so far, to recover its sound financial health and is incurring heavy losses, despite Government`s monetary help;

(b) if so, the reasons therefore;

(c) the details of financial help given, so far, by Government for restructuring Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) since February, 2000; and

(d) the present status of SAIL and the steps proposed to be taken in this respect?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS (SHRI RAM VILAS PASWAN) AND MINISTER OF STEEL


(a) & (d) Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) has improved its financial performance and wiped out its entire accumulated losses in 2003-04 itself. It made a net profit of Rs.2,512 crore in 2003-04 as against a loss of Rs.304 crore in 2002-03.

(b) Does not arise in view of (a) & (d) above.

(c) A Business and Financial Restructuring package for SAIL was approved by the Government in February 2000. The financial package provided waiver of a loan of Rs. 5,073 crore advanced to SAIL from the Steel Development Fund (SDF) and Rs. 381 crore from the Government of India. It also provided for Government guarantees for loans to be raised by SAIL from the market. Under this, a guarantee for Rs. 1,500 crore was approved with 50% interest subsidy to finance reduction in manpower through Voluntary Retirement Scheme, and for Rs. 1,500 crore (without interest subsidy) to meet repayment obligation on past loans. No financial help has been given to SAIL since February, 2000.

records.qtitle: SHORTAGE AND BLACK MARKETING OF FERTILIZERS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received any representation/complaints about the shortage, non availability and black marketing of dry ammonia phosphate for Rabi crops in various parts of the country;

(b) if so, the reasons thereof; and

(c) the steps taken or proposed to be taken in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS & MINISTER OF STEEL

(SHRI RAM VILAS PASWAN)

(a) to (c): Di-Ammonium Phosphate (DAP) is a decontrolled fertilizer and its availability depends on market forces of demand and supply. The availability of DAP in Rabi 2004- 05 season was ensured as per assessed requirement. However, there has been an increase of about 16% in the sale of DAP upto 15.2.2005 during the current season due to which some States like Punjab, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal have represented about stress in availability of DAP in some districts/areas within the State. Necessary interventions were made by coordinating with suppliers, states and Railways to make DAP available as per assessed requirement. No reports of Black Marketing of DAP have been received from any State Government during the period.

records.qtitle: PRIOR INTIMATION OF TSUNAMI .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government had received any prior intimation of Tsunami from any Government or international agency;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government are now considering to bring any technology for getting prior intimation of Tsunami and other natural disasters; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?.
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY AND MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF OCEAN DEVELOPME, NT

(SHRI KAPIL SIBAL)

(a) to (d) A statement is laid on the Table of the House. STATEMENT AS REFERRED IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA`S STARRED QUESTION NO. 44 FOR 03.03.2005 RAISED BY SHRI SAN JAY RAUT REGARDING `PRIOR INTIMATION OF TSUNAMI`

(a) & (b): No, Sir. We had not received any prior intimation of Tsunami from any Government or international agency.

(c) & (d): Yes, Sir. It is proposed to set up a multiple hazard monitoring and warning system covering Tsunami, Storm Surges and Cyclones in the Indian Ocean. The envisaged warning system includes, setting up of a dedicated network of seismic stations for earthquake/tsunami monitoring, deployment of pressure sensors, digital tide gauges, Data buoys, radars and ocean current meters for forecasting of the movement of Tsunami, cyclones and ocean surges, modeling of inundation scenarios for the entire Indian coast, bathymetry surveys and establishment of a centre for collection of the information, analysis and dissemination of warnings. Department of Science & Technology, Department of Ocean Development, Department of Space and Council of Scientific and Industrial Research will be the major participating agencies in this endeavour.

records.qtitle: AERIAL SURVEYS CONDUCTED BY SPACE DEPARTMENT
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
:

(a) whether any specific aerial surveys have been conducted by the Space Department or any other agency, recently in the various parts of the Maharashtra ;

(b) if so, the details of the surveys; and

(c) the significant development inputs found by Space Department for various sectors?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER`S OFFICE

(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN):

(a),(b) Yes, Sir. Recently, in April 2004, black and white stereo aerial photography & (c) survey on 1:6000 scale has been carried out over Mumbai and surrounding areas. These photographs are to be used to prepare 1:1000 scale map databases that will be useful for urban applications - municipal administration, utility management, police department, city planning etc. The above maps would be useful for the state Planning and Urban Development Departments, apart from the municipal/metro agencies of Mumbai and other related agencies in the State of Maharashtra.

:-

SHAKEEL AHMAD) (a): As per NASSCOM estimates, the total demand for IT Services and Software professionals in FY 2007-08 is estimated to be 1.1 million. computer aided education to not more than 10 neighboring schools within a radius of 3 to 4 kilometer. records.qtitle: PRODUCTION OF ALTERNATIVE FUELS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the trees like pungan, neem, karanji, ratanjyot or jatropha can be grown to produce oil and this oil can be converted into bio-diesel after esterification and used as fuel in diesel engines;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the steps taken or proposed to be taken for using and producing alternative renewable energy to the petroleum products in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS & PANCHAYATI RAJ

(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR)

(a) to (c) : A statement is laid on the Table of the House
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 12 BY SHRI SANJAY RAUT TO BE ANSWERED ON 1.3.2005 REGARDING PRODUCTION OF ALTERNATIVE FUELS ____________________________________________________________


(a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Bio-diesel, derived from the vegetable oils mentioned in the question can be used as an automotive fuel after mixing with diesel. The process technology for the production of bio-diesel from vegetable oils is available in the country. Under instructions from the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas to the Oil Marketing Companies in the public sector, field trials using bio-diesel and diesel blend in buses are in progress in collaboration with Haryana Roadways and the Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport Undertaking(BEST), Mumbai. Field trials and engine tests on locomotives are also in progress. However, there is no ready domestic market for bio-diesel in India since bio-diesel based on readily available feed-stocks cost much more than diesel. Tackling the cost angle is an essential on-going component of promoting the bio-diesel programme. It is being addressed in consultation with the Ministry of Finance.

(c) The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas is implementing an ethanol blended petrol programme in notified sugar producing States/adjoining States and Union Territories, which envisages supply of 5% ethanol blended petrol if ethanol is available on a sustained basis at reasonable prices for such blending.
A Coal Bed Methane (CBM) policy has been framed to harness the methane hidden in coal beds. So far, 16 CBM blocks have been awarded to different companies. For exploration of gas hydrates, a Steering Committee has been set up under the chairmanship of Secretary, Petroleum and Natural Gas which has prepared a roadmap for such exploration. Five sub-groups on Geo-Science, drilling, production, transportation/pipeline and environment have also been formed to carry out simultaneous activities related to gas hydrates.

(a)&(b): The major problems faced by the small scale industries

(SSI) sector relate to lack of timely and adequate availability of credit, obsolete technology, infrastructure bottlenecks, marketing constraints, etc. For the promotion and development of the SSIs, the Government provides fiscal and credit support, infrastructure development support, incentives for technology upgradation, marketing support, etc. The measures taken to provide adequate credit to the SSI sector include enhancement in composite loan limit from Rs. 50 lakh to Rs. 1 crore, raising of project cost limit under National Equity Fund(NEF) Scheme from Rs. 25 lakh to Rs. 50 lakh, enhancement of eligible loan limit under Credit Guarantee Scheme from Rs. 10 lakh to Rs. 25 lakh, advice to banks to adopt interest rate band of 2% above and below prime lending rates, providing collateral free loan upto Rs. 25 lakh to SSI units having good track record, setting up of Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) Fund of Rs. 10,000 crore under SIDBI, enhancement of credit limit under Laghu Udhyami Credit Card(LUCC) from Rs. 2 lakh to Rs. 10 lakh based on satisfactory track record, etc.

records.qtitle: ONLINE COMPUTERISED LAND INFORMATION SYSTEM .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text: the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for updating of land records, modernization of land record management system and their simultaneous computerization so that online computerized land information system could be developed in the country within a reasonable span of time to eliminate corruption and protecting illiterate farmers from exploitation?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI A. NARENDRA)
Ministry of Rural Development has accorded high priority for improving land records management system in the country. Accordingly, two Centrally sponsored schemes i.e., Strengthening of Revenue Administration & Updating of Land Records (SRA & ULR) and Computerization of Land Records (CLR) are under implementation in States/Union Territories. Under the scheme of SRA & ULR, funds are provided to States on 50:50 sharing basis between Centre and States for carrying out survey/revisional survey with the use of modern technology to keep their records updated. Funds are also provided to States for strengthening of survey & settlement institutions and imparting training to Revenue Officials on latest techniques & tools for modernization of Revenue Administration and regular updation of land records.
The scheme of Computerization of Land Records (CLR) was started in 1988-89 with 100% financial support from Govt. of India with the aim of ensuring accuracy, efficiency, transparency and removing inherent flaws in the existing land records maintenance system. The main objective of the scheme of CLR is that land owners should get updated computerized copies of their Record of Rights on demand from the taluk/tehsil computer centres. The scheme aims to carry out regular updation of land records through automation of mutation workflow. So far the scheme has been sanctioned in 582 districts ~ of the country and it has been extended to 3236 taluks/tehsilslblocks and 471 sub-divisions.

records.qtitle: TASK FORCE ON MICRO IRRIGATION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
to answer to Starred Question 65 given in Rajya Sabha on the 9th July, 2004 and state:

(a) Government`s response to the report submitted by Task Force Committee on micro irrigation;

(b) what are the salient features of the report; and

(c) the steps taken or proposed to be taken for the encouragement of micro irrigation in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a) & (b): The Task Force on Micro Irrigation in its Report submitted to the Central Government has recommended for covering three million ha. under micro irrigation in the country during the Tenth Plan and another 14 million ha. during the Eleventh Plan. According to the Task Force, this would require an investment of Rs.10,500 crores during the Tenth Plan and another Rs. 51,000 crores during the Eleventh Plan. Other salient recommendations of the Task Force are as follows:

(i) The financial assistance to t he farmers for microirrigation should be 50% of unit cost, out of which 40% share should be from Government of India and the balance 10% by the respective State Governments. The States may raise their share through Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) loan from National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD).

(ii) The funds need to be released through NABARD/lead banks.

(iii) There should be tax concessions to make the system affordable by the farmers.

(c): The Department of Agriculture & Cooperation is presently implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme on Macro Management in Agriculture – Supplementation/Complementation of State Efforts through Work Plans under which, among other programmes, assistance is being given to the farmers for promoting drip irrigation and sprinkler irrigation in the country. With a view to give focused attention and for increasing the coverage of area under microirrigation, it is proposed to launch a new Scheme on Microirrigation for implementation during the Xth Plan.

records.qtitle: MITIGATING DROUGHT .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering to formulate comprehensive action plan for eradication/mitigation of drought in the rainfed areas of the country;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) the details of evaluation of programmes launched for drought proofing all these years; and

(d) the special features of New National Policy for drought proofing?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a) & (b): Consistent with provisions of the National Agriculture Policy as given below in reply to part

(d) of the Question, the following programmes being implemented by the Government of India are contributing to the mitigation of drought in the rainfed areas:
A. Ministry of Rural Development

i) Drought Prone Area Programme (DPAP)

ii) Desert Development Programme (DDP)

iii) Integrated Wasteland Development Programme (IWDP)
B. Ministry of Agriculture
i) National Watershed Development Project for Rainfed Areas (NWDPRA)

(c): Different evaluation studies conducted to assess the impact of NWDPRA have concluded that, in the evaluated watersheds, there was general increase in ground water recharge, number of wells and water bodies, cropping intensity, yields of crops, reduction in soil losses and changes in cropping pattern. As regards the impact of DPAP, the evaluation studies show that there is general increase in productivity of land, water table level and availability of fuel wood and fodder.

(d): The National Agriculture Policy being followed in the Government of India since July, 2000 in respect of `Flood and Drought Management` provides:
`In order to reduce risk in agriculture and impart greater resilience to Indian agriculture against droughts and floods, efforts will be made for achieving greater flood proofing of flood prone agriculture and drought proofing of rainfed agriculture for protecting the farmers from vagaries of nature. For this purpose, contingency agriculture planning, development of drought and flood resistant crop varieties, watershed development programmes, drought prone areas and desert development programmes and rural infrastructure development programmes will receive particular attention`.

records.qtitle: DELEGATION FROM CHINA .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether delegation of China visited India in the month of October, 2004;

(b) if so, the subjects of mutual interest which were discussed with them;

(c) the agreements reached during the visit and other details in this regard; and

(d) the assistance expected therefrom?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI E. AHAMED)

(a) Yes,sir.

(b)-(d) During his visit to India from October 18-20, 2004, China`s State Councillor, Mr. Tang Jiaxuan held talks with External Affairs Minister. The Chinese leader also called on Prime Minister and met National Security Advisor. During these meetings, views were exchanged on bilateral, regional and global issues. The two sides agreed to move the relations forward on a constructive agenda and to continuously expand and develop further areas of cooperation, while seeking a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution to outstanding issues, including the boundary question. The Chinese side conveyed that China supports a bigger role for India in the international community, including in the United Nations Security Council.
Another Chinese delegation led by the Governor of China`s Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, Mr. lsmail Tiliwaldi visited India from October 9-15, 2004. During the visit, views were exchanged on prospects for cooperation between India and Xinjiang in the field of trade and commerce, civil aviation, agriculture, tourism and culture.

records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a): whether Government have recently reviewed performance of on- going projects under the Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Yojana in Maharashtra;

(b): if so, the details thereof;

(c): whether his Ministry have set any target for generating more employment opportunities in Maharashtra State under this scheme; and

(d): if so, the details thereof? ANSWER ( SHRI MAHABIR PRASAD )
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES & AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES



(a)&(b): The performance under the Prime Minister`s Rozgar Yojana

(PMRY) in Maharashtra was reviewed in March and May, 2004. During 2001-02 to 2003-04, against the target of 78,350 self-employment units, loans were disbursed to 52,394 self-employment units

(provisional), with estimated employment generation for 78,591 persons in Maharashtra under this Yojana.


(c)&(d): Against the target of 22,800 self-employment units during 2003-04, the target under the PMRY for Maharashtra State during 2004-2005 is 39,000 units.

records.qtitle: OIL EXPLORATION AND PETROLEUM REFINING .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a): whether Government have recently reviewed the perforamnce of oil exploration and petroleum refining;

(b): if so, the details thereof for the last three years by standard indicators along with emerging trends; and

(c): the details of major policy decisions taken/under consideration for attracting FDI in petroleum sector to meet growing requirements?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS AND PANCHAYATI RAJ

(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR)

(a): The performance of Oil Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) under the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas is reviewed continually on a monthly, quarterly and annual basis. In addition, Planning Commission and Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) are also reviewing the performance of Oil PSUs.

(b): Based on the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between the Government and Oil PSUs at the beginning of the year, performance evaluation is done by DPE comprehensively.


(c): With a view to liberalising the Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) regime, Government of India, Ministry of Commerce & Industry have effected the following changes in the FDI Policy in petroleum sector during January, 2004:- 
 

(i)	FDI up to 100 percent is permitted on the automatic route on petroleum product marketing.  FDI for this sector would be permissible subject to the existing sectoral policy and regulatory framework in the oil marketing sector. 

(ii)	FDI up to 100 per cent is permitted on the automatic route in oil exploration in both small and medium sized fields subject to and under the policy of the Government on private participation in : (a) exploration of oil and (b) the discovered fields of national oil companies. 

(iii)	FDI up to 100 per cent is permitted on the automatic route for petroleum product pipelines subject to and under the Government Policy and regulations thereof. 

(iv)	FDI up to 100 per cent is permitted for Natural Gas/LNG Pipelines with prior Government approval.
--

records.qtitle: INCREASE IN CREDIT LOAN FACILITIES TO FARMERS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering to increase credit loan facilities to small, marginal land holding farmers and also woman entrepreneurs in the country; and

(b) if so, the details thereof and the steps taken or proposed to be taken in this regard;
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a) & (b) Yes Sir, The Reserve Bank of India has advised the commercial banks to make efforts to increase their disbursement to small and marginal farmers to 40% of their direct disbursement under the Special Agriculture Credit Plan (SACP) by March,2007. A target of 5% of net bank credit has also been stipulated for lending to women by all public sector banks.
Credit disbursement by public sector banks te small and marginal farmers has increased from 26.73% of agriculture credit disbursement under SACP in 2002-03 to 31.3% during 2003 -04.
As on March, 2004, the net bank credit outstanding to women borrowers constituted 4.71%. in order to further increase the credit flow to women, special efforts are being made through SHG-Bank Linkage programme initiated by NABARD.

records.qtitle: SCRAP DISPOSAL POLICY OF AI .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the scrap disposal policy of Air India as regards aircraft items;

(b) whether it is a fact that the lack of timely raising of scrap notes by the concerned departments for timely disposal of aircraft items results in further deterioration of the obtainable value of scrapped items;

(c) the details of aircraft items pending for disposal due to non-issuance of scrap notes; and

(d) what is Air India`s policy and the plan of action to bring greater accountability in stemming the losses of Air-India on this count?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )
(a): As and when the Engineering Shops scrap a particular part, the same is transfered to Materials Management Department of Air India for disposal. These scrapped parts are disposed of through a tender process, duly categorized as metals, plastics, etc. This tendering is undertaken on behalf of Air India by the Metals Scrap Trading Corporation. (b): No, Sir. Scrap Notes are raised in a timely manner. (c): The issuance of scrappage note is a continuous process. The aircraft items are received in Air India Overhaul Shops which are dismantled, inspected and if found `Beyond economical Repair`, the same are scrapped and necessary scrappage advice is raised. As soon as the Scrap Note is raised, the items are handed over to Materials Management Department for further disposal action. (d): The policy of Air India is to dispose of scrapped material as soon as there is a sizeable lot for the tenderers to bid for the same. So far there has been no accummulation of scrap material awaiting disposal. There is therefore no perceived loss in encashing the obtainable residual value. A computerized Online Materials Management System caled `PROSPER` is already installed in Air India as a result of which the process of scrappage has become more efficient.

records.qtitle: SCARCITY OF WATER
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the level of the ground water is depleting in many parts of the country and also water has become very scare in many cities and towns as a result thereof in recent years;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) what measures Government have taken so far and propose to take, such as using rainwater instead of ground water by popularising the concept of water harvesting; and

(d) how Government propose to take this concept to the grass root level?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD )

(a): Ministry of Water Resources has reported that the ground water levels in certain parts of various districts in the country have shown significant decline. It is one of the factors resulting in scarcity of water in many cities and towns.

(b): State-wise details of districts showing decline in water levels is enclosed at Annexure-I.

(c): Ministry of Water Resources has reported to have taken the following steps for regulating ground water development and augmenting ground water resources:- 
 

(i)   Central  Ground Water Authority (CGWA) has banned drilling
of new tubewells in Delhi, South and South West districts.
Permission  is  being  granted   only  to  the  Government
agencies   responsible   for    drinking   water   supply.
Abstraction  of ground water for sale and supply has  been
banned in the notified area of National Capital Region.


ii)   In  673 over-exploited and 425 dark /critical areas in the
country,  State  Pollution  Control Boards &  Ministry  of
Environment   &  Forests  have  to  obtain  no   objection
certificate   (NOC)  from  CGWA   for  any  new  Industry/
Projects.


iii)  Similarly,  other development projects located in  Coastal
Regulation Zone require NOC from CGWA as pre-requisite for
environmental clearance.
CONTD....2
PA
-  2  -


iv)   CGWA  has  provided  technical   guidance  on   rain-water
harvesting  to  around  1800   agencies  including   State
Government  agencies,  educational  institutions,  private
entrepreneurs and individuals. 
v)    The  Authority  has  issued directions  to  Group  Housing
Societies,  Institutes,  Hotels, Industries, Farm  Houses,
etc.   in the notified areas of Delhi, Faridabad,  Gurgaon
and Ghaziabad to adopt rain water harvesting system. 
vi)   A  Manual on Artificial Recharge of ground water has  been
prepared  and circulated to the States/ Union  Territories
to  enable  them  to formulate  area  specific  Artificial
Recharge  Schemes  to check the declining trend in  ground
water levels.

 
vii)  A  Central  Sector Scheme for Study of Recharge to  Ground
Water in the country has been implemented during the Ninth
Plan.


Ministry   of  Urban  Development   has   circulated   the
literature/guidelines  on  rain-water   harvesting  provided  by
Ministry  of Water Resources / Central Ground Water Board (CGWB)
to  all  States / Union Territories for adoption in those  areas
where  there  has been sharp decline in the ground water  level.
State  Governments have also been advised to make a beginning in
the   existing  Government  offices  /  buildings  and   housing
complexes  and  to  make it mandatory for all new  buildings  by
amending  the  building  bye-laws.  The Ministry  has  issued  a
notification  for  amending  the Unified  Building  Bye-laws  of
Delhi,  1983  on  28.7.01  which makes it  mandatory  for  water
harvesting  through  storing  of runoff  water,  including  rain
water,  in  all  new buildings on plots of 100 sq.   meters  and
above.   Likewise  all  buildings having  minimum  discharge  of
10,000  litres  and  above  per   day  shall  incorporate  water
recycling  system.   The  recycled  water  should  be  used  for
horticultural purpose.


Ministry  of  Water Resources has proposed to implement  a
Centrally  Sponsored  Scheme  on Artificial Recharge  to  Ground
Water  &  Rain Water Harvesting at an estimated cost  of  Rs.175
crores  during the Tenth Plan.  The scheme has a funding pattern
of  75:25  (Centre:  State).  Beneficiaries will contribute  10%
for  O&M.  The scheme will be implemented in identified areas of
various  States, particularly in over-exploited and dark blocks,
drought  prone and water scarcity areas, coastal areas & islands
affected  by  saline  water ingress, areas of  inland  salinity,
urban  areas showing steep decline in ground water levels and in
sub-mountainous/  hilly areas of the country.  It is proposed to
construct  5088  artificial recharge and rain  water  harvesting
structures  on  community  cluster basis.  The  scheme  will  be
implemented through State Govt.  under the technical guidance of
CGWB.


(d):   The  Central Ground Water Authority have  organized  Mass
Awareness  Programmes  on  Rainwater Harvesting  and  Artificial
Recharge  to Ground water throughout the country.  Awareness has
also been created through print and electronic media like films,
advertisements,  posters, incorporation of chapters on Rainwater
harvesting   in  NCERT  text   books,  etc.   Several   training
programmes  have been conducted in various parts of the  country
to develop professional expertise.

records.qtitle: AVAILABILITY OF LIFE SAVING DURGS
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that due to heavy prices of drugs, charged by pharmaceutical companies in India, many people could not afford to purchase life saving drugs;

(b) if so, what steps have been taken or proposed to be taken by Government for ensuring the regular availability of life saving drugs at reasonable prices in the country;

(c) whether Government have undertaken any review of performance of public sector units set up for manufacturing of critical bulk drugs; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS & MINISTER OF STEEL ( SHRI RAM VILAS PASWAN )

(a) & (b): The Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 1995 (DPCO’1995) does not make any distinction between Life Saving drugs and other drugs. In accordance with the provisions of DPCO’1995, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) fixes / revises prices of the drugs listed in the First Schedule of DPCO 1995 and formulations based thereon. In case, there is any violation of the approved/notified price of a Scheduled formulation, action is taken under the provisions of the DPCO’ 1995. Moreover, the Drugs Policies, as announced from time to time, are directed towards ensuring abundant availability of quality drugs at reasonable prices.

(c) & (d): At present, only two central public sector undertakings viz., Hindustan Antibiotics Limited (HAL) and Bengal Chemicals and Pharmaceuticals Limited (BCPL) are engaged in the production of drugs. The performance of these two undertakings are reviewed by the Department on quarterly basis.

records.qtitle: STEPS TO INCREASE EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES IN RURAL AREAS .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) the estimated number of unemployed persons in rural areas of the country particularly in Maharashtra;

(b) whether any evaluation of the Central Government`s programmes to increase employment opportunities in the rural areas in the country has been made by the Union Government; and

(c) if so, the outcome thereof ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(DR. RAGHUVANSH PRASAD SINGH)


(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
Statement referred to in reply to Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 101 due for answer on 08.12.2004. As per the 5th quinquennial round, (1999-2000) of National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO) on employment and unemployment, unemployed persons on Current Daily Status (CDS) are estimated at 19.49 million in rural areas of the country and the number of unemployed persons in rural areas of Maharashtra are estimated at 1.57 million.

2. The Ministry of Rural development has conducted evaluation of the programmes of the Ministry to increase employment opportunities in the rural areas of the country. The various micro and macro level Evaluation and Impact Studies sponsored by the Ministry have revealed that there has been a positive impact of various rural development programmes on employment generation.

3. The findings of the Concurrent Evaluation on Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY) and Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY) have shown that there has been substantial increase in the number of mandays of employment generated under these programmes over the years.

records.qtitle: PROPOSALS FOR RURAL SANITATION .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Union Government has received any proposals from various State Governments relating to sanitation and development of rural areas during the last three years and till date;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the steps taken or proposed to be taken for the improvement of sanitation system in various rural parts of the country ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI A.NARENDRA)

(a) Yes, Sir. During the past three financial years viz, 2001-02, 2002-03, 2003-04 and till date, 465 proposals for implementation of Total Sanitation Campaign in 465 districts of 30 States have been received.

(b) The details of proposals received during the last three years and till date is given in Annexure.

(c) Total Sanitation Campaign (TSC) was launched in 1999 by restructuring the Central Rural Sanitation Programme with the objective of: - 
-	Bringing about an improvement in the general quality of life in the rural areas.
-	Accelerating sanitation coverage in rural areas.
-	Generating felt demand for sanitation facilities through awareness creation and health 
education.
-	Covering schools/Anganwadis in rural areas with sanitation facilities and promote 
hygiene education and sanitary habits among students.
-	Encouraging cost effective and appropriate technologies in sanitation.
-	Eliminating open defecation to minimize risk of contamination of drinking water sources 
and food.
-	Converting dry latrines to pour flush latrines, and eliminate manual scavenging practice, 
wherever in existence in rural areas.
	
TSC gives emphasis on creating awareness through intensive IEC to bring about attitudinal 
and behavioural change for relevant hygiene practices and generate demand of sanitation 
facilities. The demand so generated is met through a wide range of technological choices suited 
to varying requirement of households in different income categories and hydrological conditions.  
Individual Household, Community, School and Anganwadi toilet construction, School Sanitation 
& hygiene education, Women`s dignity are amongst the focus areas of TSC projects.  TSC 
projects have so far been sanctioned for 426 districts.  A reward scheme called Nirmal Gram 
Puraskar for achieving 100% open-defecation-free environment in Panchayati Raj Institution 
areas has also been introduced.

records.qtitle: SEPARATE MINISTRY FOR DISASTER MANAGEMENT .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received any report on Disaster Management, which recommends a separate Ministry for Disaster Management; and

(b) if so, Government`s response thereto and the steps Government have so far taken or propose to take in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI S. REGUPATHY)

(a): The High Powered Committee on Disaster Management had inter-alia recommended that a separate Ministry of Disaster Management be set up for a sustained and focused effort in the area of disaster preparedness, mitigation and management. After the Bhuj earthquake, the High Powered Committee was converted into the working Group of the National Committee on Disaster Management. The Working Group inter-alia recommended that the proposed National Disaster Management Authority should be a full-fledged Department in the Ministry of Home Affairs for effective and holistic management of disasters.

(b): The view taken in the Government is that it will not be appropriate to make the proposed Authority a separate Department as it will need to have close inter-linkages with the Ministry of Home Affairs; it will be headed by a Secretary/Special Secretary in the Ministry with representatives from concerned Ministries/Departments and will function under the overall supervision of Home Secretary.

-

(b) if so, the details of effective steps taken for the benefit of powerloom sector in Maharashtra?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF TEXTILES , (SHRI SHANKERSINH VAGHELA)

(a) & (b): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (b) RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.: 427 FOR 25.8.2004 REGARDING PROBLEMS OF POWERLOOM OWNERS IN MAHARASHTRA
(a) & (b) The Government had been receiving requests from the Maharashtra powedoom industry for removal of CENVAT. In this year`s budget the following important announcements have been made for the textile sector as a whole including the powerloom sector:- o Except for mandatory excise duty on polyester filament yam including texturised yam, synthetic and artificial fibres and synthetic and artificial filament yams, the whole value addition chain has been given excise exemption option. o This excise exemption has been given across the value addition chain. For those, opting to pay duty and avail CENVAT credit, two rates of duty have been given as under:- All textile goods made of pure cotton, not containing any other textile material4%; Other textile goods8%. o Additional Excise Duty on Textiles and Textile Articles (AT&T) and Additional Excise Duty (Goods of Special Importance) Act have been abolished.
Following steps have been taken for modernization of the powerloom sector:- Incentives have been mad~ available under the Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS) whereby the powerloom owner can reduce the cost of borrowing capital either by availing 20% upfront Capital Linked Subsidy or by obtaining 5% interest reimbursement of on the loan availed. Government has announced a Scheme for assistance fbr construction of Group Workshed for powerlooms to create a better working environment and obtain high productivity. Import of shuttleless looms has been allowed under concessional customs duty of 5% without countervailing duly. Excise exemption has also been given on such looms. Accelerated depreciation benefits at the rate of 50% have been extended on the weaving machinery installed under TUFS. Government has taken up modernization and strengthening of powerloom service centers (PSCs), which have been set up to provide technical services of training testing, project preparation etc. Computer Aided Design Centres have been set up to enable small powerloom units to access new designs and upgrade fabric by product development inputs.

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION ( DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH )

(a): The Tenth Plan Working Group on the Public Distribution System and Food Security had recommended introduction of Smart Card system in the form of credit/debit card instead of the existing ration cards in the PDS in the Country.

(b), (c) & (d): Based on the recommendations of the Working Group a Pilot Project on implementation of Smart Cards in PDS, later on renamed as `implementation of Food Credit Cards in PDS` has been formulated for implementation in selected districts/States. The Scheme is being implemented on a pilot basis in Vidisha, Kangra and Ernakulam districts of Madhya Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh and Kerala respectively. The introduction of the Food Credit Cards in the whole country will depend on the outcome of the Pilot Project.

records.name: Sanjay Raut

(b) if so, Government’s response thereto and whether Government’s ‘Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan’ plan is sorting out this problem; and

(c) if so, the details of the progress made through this plan particularly in Maharashtra? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M.A.A FATMI)


(a) According to the estimates for year 2002-03, about 18% of the children in the age group 6 to 14 years and 63% of the children in the age group 14 to 18 years are not attending schools due to various reasons including financial and social conditions.

(i) To bring all 6-14 years age group children in schools/EGS Centres/Bridge courses by 2003
(ii) To ensure that all children in this age group to complete primary education of good quality by 2007 and elementary education by 2010. The progress made so far under SSA in the country and in Maharashtra is given in the Annexure.

records.qtitle: RULES FOR FILM SHOOTING .
records.name: Sanjay Raut
records.qn_text:
(a) whether a film director assistant called Nadia was killed recently on Mumbai Central railway track during a film shooting;

(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor;

(c) the rules set for providing platforms and railway tracks for film shooting; and .ie

(d) whether these rules were violated in the said incident?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

( SHRI R. VELU )

(a)&(b): Yes, Sir. On 25.05.2004, Film Assistant Director called Miss Nadia Khan was knocked down by a fast local train during the com`se of a film shooting near Mahalaxmi Railway Station. As per Government Railway Police, OnL 1.62004, the case was registered by Tardeo Police Station and subsequently transferred to GRP/Mumbai Central who in turn registered the case under CR No.54/2004 u/s 304(A), 182, 201,202, 211, 34 Indian Penal Code.

(c): As per Railway Board`s directives, Railway Administration are empowered to grant permission for Film Shooting in the Railway premises on Wains subject to certain conditions:



1. Submission of Bank Guarantee.

2. Execution of Comprehensive Insurance Cover.

3. Payment of Licence Fee.

4. Charges for rolling stocks, if required.


5. Submission of Indemnity Bond.
6. Observation of safety and security regulations.

(d): Yes, Sir. The permission was granted for shooting at Mahalaxmi Railway Station Platform No. 1 and surrounding area by the Railway Administration. But, as per the version of GRP, the shooting was done by the Film Unit on fast local `UP` tracck thus violating the rules and regulations of Railway Administration.

records.subject: Increase in retirement age of Judges in High Courts
records.extent: A resolution was passed in the Chief Justice Conference held from 13 to 15th September, 2002 in New Delhi to raise the age of retirement of High Court judges.  The resolution has been examined by the Governemnt, the increase of the age of retirement of judges would be effected by amending Article 217 of the Constitution of India in accordance with the procedure laid down in its Article 368(2) .  Since this article is ocvered under Chapter V of the Part VI of the Consstitution  amendment in the aforesaid Article will required ratification by teh Legislatures of atleast one half of the states as per the provison of Artilce 368(2).  So far, no decision has been taken by the Government in this regard.
